26.tq: Use the judicial-review statement as the discriminator among otherwise correct holdings.

26.s: Which recent development revived the debate on the possible misuse of the ordinance-making power and executive overreach?
o: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026
The Inter-State Water Disputes Amendment Ordinance, 2026
26.x: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026 revived the debate on ordinance misuse and executive overreach.
26.tq: Identify the precise recent development instead of being misled by similarly worded legislative titles.

26.s: What is the principal criticism of the frequent promulgation of ordinances?
o: They can be issued only during a financial emergency.
They require prior approval from the Supreme Court.
They transfer all legislative powers to the States.
26.x: Frequent ordinances are criticised because they bypass parliamentary deliberation.
26.tq: Link the institutional criticism to the constitutional function being bypassed.

26.s: With reference to the veto power of the President of the United States, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It is a pocket veto that can be overridden by a simple majority of Congress.
It is a suspensive veto that automatically becomes ineffective after thirty days.
It is a qualified veto that can be overridden by a two-thirds majority of Congress.
It is an absolute veto that cannot be overridden by Congress.
26.x: The US President has only a qualified veto, which can be overridden by a two-thirds majority of Congress.
26.tq: Discriminate between absolute, qualified, suspensive and pocket vetoes by focusing on the override condition.

26.s: The State ordinance concerning organ-transplant committees in Andhra Pradesh was issued under which Article of the Constitution?
26.x: A Governor's ordinance-making power for a State is exercised under Article 213; the Andhra Pradesh ordinance concerned organ-transplant committees.
26.tq: Use the Union ordinance–State ordinance distinction to identify the correct constitutional Article.

27.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the election of the Vice-President of India:
1. The electoral college consists of all members of both Houses of Parliament, elected as well as nominated.
2. Elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies are also part of the electoral college.
3. The election is held by proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and secret ballot.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: Statement 1 is correct: all MPs, elected and nominated, vote (788 when both Houses are full). Statement 2 is wrong: State legislatures have no role in the Vice-President's election. Statement 3 is correct: PR-STV with secret ballot. Hence '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' misses 3, and options with 2 are wrong.
27.tq: VP: all MPs incl. nominated, no MLAs. President: elected MPs + elected MLAs.

27.s: Which one of the following is NOT a qualification for election as Vice-President of India?
o: Qualification for election as a member of the Lok Sabha
Qualification for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha
27.x: The Vice-President must be a citizen of India, at least 35 years old and qualified for election to the Rajya Sabha. Qualification for election to the Lok Sabha is not the prescribed condition.
27.tq: Find the one swapped constitutional qualification among closely related House requirements.

27.s: As Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, the Vice-President ordinarily exercises
o: A casting vote in the event of an equality of votes
A vote only on Money Bills
27.x: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha does not vote in the first instance but has a casting vote when the votes are equally divided.
27.tq: Distinguish an ordinary vote from a casting vote in a presiding-officer question.

27.s: The Vice-President of India is ex officio President of which of the following bodies?
27.x: The Vice-President is also the ex-officio President of the Indian Council of World Affairs (ICWA).
27.tq: Use the exact institutional title to distinguish ICWA from other national bodies.

27.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 64 — Ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
Article 67 — Oath or affirmation of the Vice-President
Article 71 — Election procedure by single transferable vote
27.x: Article 64 provides that the Vice-President shall be the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. Article 67 concerns term and removal, Article 69 concerns oath, and Article 71 concerns election disputes.
27.tq: Match each constitutional Article with its exact subject and reject neighbouring Article swaps.

27.s: All doubts and disputes relating to the election of the President or Vice-President are decided by:
27.x: Article 71 vests the Supreme Court with exclusive authority to decide doubts and disputes concerning Presidential and Vice-Presidential elections.
27.tq: Use the authority-identification method: distinguish the body conducting an election from the body deciding its disputes.

27.s: The 39th Constitutional Amendment and the 44th Constitutional Amendment had what effect on Presidential election disputes?
o: The 39th Amendment vested the disputes in Parliament and the 44th retained that arrangement
The 39th Amendment removed the Supreme Court’s power and the 44th Amendment restored it
The 39th Amendment created the power and the 44th Amendment abolished it
Both Amendments transferred the power to the Election Commission
27.x: The 39th Amendment of 1975 took away the Supreme Court’s jurisdiction over these disputes, while the 44th Amendment of 1978 restored it.
27.tq: Link each Amendment to its opposite constitutional effect instead of relying on the later amendment alone.

27.s:
Consider the following statements about the Vice-President of India:
1. The Vice-President holds office for five years and continues until the successor enters office.
2. The oath of office of the Vice-President is administered by the Chief Justice of India.
3. A resolution for the removal of the Vice-President can be moved only after at least 14 days' notice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: Statement 1 is correct: a five-year term, continuing till the successor takes charge (Art. 67(c)). Statement 2 is wrong: the President administers the Vice-President's oath (Art. 69); the CJI administers the President's oath. Statement 3 is correct: 14 days' notice is needed. Hence '1 and 3 only'; options with 2 are wrong.
27.tq: VP oath by the President; President's oath by the CJI. Removal: 14 days' notice, RS resolution.

27.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Vice-President while acting as President:
1. The Deputy Chairman presides over the Rajya Sabha during that period.
2. The Vice-President continues to draw the salary of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
27.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Vice-President stops functioning as Chairman and the Deputy Chairman presides. Statement 2 is wrong: while acting as President he draws the President's salary, not the Chairman's. Hence '1 only'; '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are wrong.
27.tq: Acting President: stops being RS Chairman, draws the President's salary.

27.s: A vacancy in the office of the Vice-President of India is to be filled
o: Within six months of the vacancy in every case
As soon as possible, without a constitutionally prescribed six-month deadline
Within one year, after approval by the Supreme Court
Only at the next general election to the Lok Sabha
27.x: Article 68 requires an election to fill a vacancy in the office of Vice-President as soon as possible. Unlike the vacancy in the office of President, no six-month deadline is prescribed for this election.
27.tq: Compare the vacancy rules for President and Vice-President, especially the presence or absence of a fixed deadline.

27.s: When the office of the President falls vacant, the Vice-President acts as President until
o: The Council of Ministers elects a successor
The next session of Parliament begins
A new President is elected, which must take place within six months of the vacancy
The remaining term of the previous President expires
27.x: The Vice-President acts as President until a new President is elected. The election to fill the presidential vacancy must be held within six months of the vacancy.
27.tq: Identify the event that ends the acting arrangement and distinguish it from the former President’s remaining term.

27.s:
Consider the following statements about the removal of the Vice-President of India:
1. The resolution must originate in the Rajya Sabha.
2. The resolution requires an effective majority of the Rajya Sabha.
3. The Lok Sabha must agree to the resolution by a simple majority.
4. The Constitution specifies grounds on which the Vice-President may be removed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: Removal is initiated in the Rajya Sabha, requires a majority of all the then members of that House, and must be agreed to by the Lok Sabha by simple majority. The Constitution does not state grounds for this removal.
27.tq: Break the removal procedure into origin, majority, second-House approval and grounds.

27.s: The Vice-President of India may resign his office by writing under his hand addressed to the
27.x: Under Article 67(a) the Vice-President resigns by writing to the President, and the resignation takes effect immediately. The President resigns to the Vice-President; the CJI administers the President's oath; the Speaker is informed of the President's resignation; the Prime Minister receives no constitutional resignation of either office.
27.tq: President resigns to VP; VP resigns to President.

27.s: Which one of the following Vice-Presidents also served two full terms?
27.x: Hamid Ansari served two full terms as Vice-President from 2007 to 2017. Dr. S. Radhakrishnan was the other Vice-President associated with two terms.
27.tq: Distinguish the two-term office-holders from Vice-Presidents who served only one term.

27.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding Vice-Presidents who later became Presidents of India:

List-I
A. S. Radhakrishnan
B. Zakir Husain
C. V.V. Giri
D. K.R. Narayanan

List-II
i. 1962
ii. 1967
iii. 1969
iv. 1997

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
27.x: S. Radhakrishnan became President in 1962, Zakir Husain in 1967, V.V. Giri in 1969 and K.R. Narayanan in 1997.
27.tq: Start with the secure year-office pair and eliminate codes containing a mismatched pair.

27.s: Who is the Vice-President of India elected after the mid-term vacancy created by the resignation of Jagdeep Dhankhar in July 2025?
27.x: C.P. Radhakrishnan was elected Vice-President after the mid-term vacancy caused by Jagdeep Dhankhar’s resignation in July 2025.
27.tq: Use the vacancy event as the identifying clue for the current office-holder.

27.s: Who was the first Vice-President of India?
27.x: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan was the first Vice-President (two terms, 1952-62) and later became President in 1962. Zakir Husain (VP 1962-67) and V.V. Giri (VP 1967-69) came after him, and Hamid Ansari held two full terms from 2007 to 2017.
27.tq: Radhakrishnan = first VP and first President from South India.

27.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the tenure of the Prime Minister?
o: The Prime Minister can be removed only by the Supreme Court.
The Prime Minister holds office for life unless removed by impeachment.
The Prime Minister continues in office while commanding the confidence of the Lok Sabha, subject to the President's pleasure in the constitutional sense.
The Prime Minister has a fixed tenure of five years irrespective of legislative support.
27.x: The Prime Minister has no fixed tenure and ordinarily continues while enjoying the confidence of the Lok Sabha. The Constitution formally states that Ministers hold office during the President's pleasure.
27.tq: Reject the fixed-term trap and connect tenure with legislative confidence.

27.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the President and the Prime Minister in the Indian parliamentary system?
o: The President is the de facto head of government and the Prime Minister is the de jure head of State.
The President is the de jure head of State and the Prime Minister is the de facto head of government.
The Prime Minister is the de jure head of State and the President is only a ceremonial officer of Parliament.
Both the President and the Prime Minister are de facto heads of government.
27.x: The President is the de jure head of the State, while the Prime Minister functions as the de facto head of government.
27.tq: Discriminate the paired constitutional and political roles rather than treating them as identical.

27.s:
Consider the following statements about the Prime Minister of India:
1. He is appointed by the President under Article 75(1).
2. He must be a member of the Lok Sabha at the time of appointment.
3. His oath of office is administered by the President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: Statement 1 is correct: the President appoints the PM under Article 75(1), by convention the leader of the Lok Sabha majority. Statement 2 is wrong: the PM may belong to either House, and a non-member can be PM for six months. Statement 3 is correct: the President administers the oath. Hence '1 and 3 only'; options with 2 are wrong.
27.tq: PM: either House, or none for 6 months.

27.s: Under Article 75(5) of the Constitution of India, a person appointed as a Minister who is not a member of either House of Parliament must become a member within
27.x: Article 75(5) requires a non-member Minister to become a member of either House of Parliament within six consecutive months; otherwise, the person ceases to be a Minister.
27.tq: Use the precise constitutional time limit and distinguish it from other parliamentary periods.

27.s: Which one of the following correctly states the ruling in S.R. Chaudhuri v. State of Punjab (2001)?
o: A non-member cannot be repeatedly reappointed as Minister without getting elected.
Only a member of the Lok Sabha can be appointed as a Minister.
A non-member may be reappointed as Minister indefinitely without election.
A non-member cannot be appointed as Prime Minister under any circumstances.
27.x: The Supreme Court held that the constitutional provision for a non-member Minister cannot be used for repeated reappointments without the person securing election to the legislature.
27.tq: Discriminate the judicial limitation from the general six-month rule.

27.s:
Consider the following statements regarding appointment of Ministers:
1. Any person may be appointed as a Minister, subject to the constitutional six-month rule.
2. A non-member Minister must become a member of either House of Parliament within six months.
3. The six-month rule does not apply to a person appointed as Prime Minister.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the six-month rule applies to the Prime Minister as well.
27.tq: Find the exception that improperly excludes the Prime Minister from a general constitutional rule.

27.s: Article 75(2) was referred to in the acceptance of a Minister's resignation because that Article relates to
o: collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha
the President's pleasure regarding the tenure of Ministers
the Prime Minister's duty to furnish information
27.x: Article 75(2) provides that Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President, which operates in practice on the advice of the Prime Minister.
27.tq: Link a constitutional clause to its operative subject instead of to a neighbouring Article.

27.s: According to Article 75(1A), inserted by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003, the total number of Union Ministers including the Prime Minister shall not exceed
o: 15 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha
12 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha
10 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha
20 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha
27.x: The 91st Amendment inserted Article 75(1A), limiting the Union Council of Ministers including the Prime Minister to 15 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.
27.tq: Match the amendment with its exact percentage limit and constitutional Article.

27.s: If the total strength of the Lok Sabha is 543, the maximum permissible strength of the Union Council of Ministers including the Prime Minister is
27.x: Fifteen per cent of 543 is 81.45; the applicable maximum whole-number limit is 81 ministers, including the Prime Minister.
27.tq: Calculate the constitutional percentage cap and apply the whole-number limit.

27.s: A member of Parliament disqualified for defection under the Tenth Schedule is, by virtue of Article 75(1B),
o: eligible only after approval by the Election Commission
permanently barred from becoming a Union Minister
ineligible to be appointed Union Minister until re-elected to Parliament
eligible to be appointed Union Minister immediately after disqualification
27.x: Article 75(1B), inserted by the 91st Amendment, prevents a member disqualified for defection from being appointed a minister until re-elected to Parliament.
27.tq: Test the duration and condition of disqualification instead of treating it as a permanent bar.

27.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the size of a State Council of Ministers under Article 164(1A):
1. The total number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, shall not exceed 15% of the strength of the Legislative Assembly and shall not be less than 12.
2. This limit was inserted by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.
3. In a State with an Assembly of 294 members, the maximum number of ministers including the Chief Minister is 45.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: Statement 1 is correct: ceiling 15% of the Assembly, floor 12. Statement 2 is correct: the 91st Amendment, 2003 brought in these limits. Statement 3 is wrong: 15% of 294 is 44.1, so the maximum is 44 (e.g. West Bengal), not 45. Hence '1 and 2 only'; options with 3 are wrong and '1 only' misses 2.
27.tq: State: max 15%, min 12 (Art 164(1A), 91st Amdt). 294 seats -> 44.

27.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the classification of Union Ministers:
1. The Constitution itself classifies ministers into Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers.
2. The classification into ranks is based on convention and the choice of the Prime Minister.
3. Deputy Ministers form one of the conventionally recognised ministerial ranks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: The Constitution does not itself classify ministers into ranks. The classification is based on convention and the Prime Minister’s choice, and Deputy Minister is one of the recognised ranks.
27.tq: Separate what the Constitution expressly provides from what operates through convention.

27.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding categories of Ministers:

List-I
A. Cabinet Minister
B. Minister of State with independent charge
C. Minister of State
D. Deputy Minister

List-II
i. Assists a Cabinet Minister or Minister of State
ii. Heads an important ministry and attends Cabinet meetings
iii. Holds a ministry or department on his or her own
iv. Is attached to a Cabinet Minister

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
27.x: A Cabinet Minister heads an important ministry and attends Cabinet meetings; a Minister of State with independent charge heads a ministry independently; a Minister of State is attached to a Cabinet Minister; and a Deputy Minister assists a senior Minister.
27.tq: Start from the distinctive phrase ‘independent charge’ and then complete the remaining role pairs.

27.s: Under Article 74(1), the advice of the Council of Ministers becomes binding on the President after the President
o: secures approval from the Election Commission
refers the matter to the Supreme Court
obtains the consent of the Rajya Sabha
27.x: The President may require the Council of Ministers to reconsider its advice once, but must act in accordance with the advice tendered after such reconsideration.
27.tq: Focus on the one permitted reconsideration rather than an unlimited presidential discretion.

27.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Article)
 a. Article 74(2)
 b. Article 77(1)
 c. Article 77(2)
 d. Article 77(3)

List-II (Provision)
 i. Authentication of orders
 ii. Executive action expressed in the President's name
 iii. Advice not subject to inquiry by any court
 iv. Rules for convenient transaction and allocation of government business

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
27.x: Article 74(2) concerns non-inquiry into ministerial advice; Article 77(1) concerns expression in the President's name; Article 77(2) concerns authentication; and Article 77(3) concerns transaction and allocation of business rules.
27.tq: Start with the sure Article–provision pairs and eliminate codes containing a misplaced constitutional subject.

27.s: Which of the following is NOT a duty of the Prime Minister under Article 78?
o: Furnishing information relating to administration when called for by the President
Submitting for the consideration of the Council any matter decided by an individual Minister when the President requires it
Communicating to the President decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to administration and legislative proposals
Administering the oath of office and secrecy to all Union Ministers
27.x: Options A, B and C are duties of the Prime Minister under Article 78 (communicating Council decisions, furnishing information, and placing a minister's individual decision before the Council when the President requires). Administering the oaths of office and secrecy to Union Ministers is done by the President, not the PM.
27.tq: Find the one function belonging to the President rather than the Prime Minister.

27.s: During a National Emergency, the President of India
o: acquires unrestricted discretion to disregard the advice of the Council of Ministers
continues to be bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers
becomes the real executive in place of the Prime Minister
may dismiss the entire Council without following constitutional advice
27.x: A National Emergency does not confer discretionary power on the President to disregard the binding advice of the Council of Ministers. The parliamentary executive relationship continues.
27.tq: Guard against the emergency-powers trap by checking whether the constitutional advice requirement has been altered.

27.s:
Arrange the following provisions in the order of their appearance in the Constitution:
A. Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President
B. Prime Minister's duties to communicate information to the President
C. All executive action expressed in the President's name
D. Collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha
27.x: The provisions occur in the order Article 74(1), Article 75(3), Article 77(1) and Article 78: advice, collective responsibility, executive expression and Prime Ministerial duties.
27.tq: Use the Article numbers as the sequence: 74, 75, 77 and 78.

27.s: Article 77(1) of the Constitution provides that all executive action of the Government of India shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the
27.x: Article 77(1) requires all executive action of the Government of India to be expressed in the name of the President.
27.tq: Match the constitutional article with the authority in whose name executive action is expressed.

27.s: Under Article 77(3), the President makes rules for the convenient transaction of the business of the Government of India and for its allocation among Ministers. These rules are known as the
o: Union Executive Rules and Ministerial Responsibility Rules
Allocation of Business Rules and Transaction of Business Rules
Conduct of Government Rules and Delegation Rules
Rules of Procedure of Parliament and Cabinet Manual
27.x: Article 77(3) is implemented through the Allocation of Business Rules, 1961 and the Transaction of Business Rules, 1961.
27.tq: Identify the precise official titles associated with a constitutional rule-making power.

27.s:
Consider the following statements about the office of Deputy Prime Minister in India:
1. The office of Deputy Prime Minister is expressly mentioned in the Constitution.
2. A Deputy Prime Minister takes oath as an ordinary Minister.
3. Sardar Patel was the first Deputy Prime Minister.
4. The office is placed at rank 5A in the Table of Precedence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. The office of Deputy Prime Minister is not mentioned in the Constitution; the Deputy Prime Minister takes oath as an ordinary Minister, Sardar Patel was the first, and the office has rank 5A in the Table of Precedence.
27.tq: Identify the constitutional-status trap before checking the factual details of the office.

27.s: The Prime Minister’s Office is best described as a/an
o: parliamentary committee of the Lok Sabha
statutory body headed by the President
extra-constitutional staff agency of the Prime Minister
27.x: The Prime Minister’s Office is not mentioned in the Constitution; it is an extra-constitutional staff agency assisting the Prime Minister.
27.tq: Distinguish constitutional, statutory and extra-constitutional institutions by their legal source.

27.s: Which one of the following is NOT a constitutionally prescribed rank of a Union Minister?
o: Minister of State with Independent Charge
27.x: The Constitution itself does not classify ministers into ranks; by convention the Council comprises Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State (Independent Charge), Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers. Deputy Prime Minister is not one of these ranks and is not mentioned in the Constitution; a Deputy PM takes oath as an ordinary minister.
27.tq: Find the non-standard rank among the established ministerial categories.

27.s:
Consider the following statements about the Leader of the House in the Lok Sabha:
1. It is a constitutional office.
2. The Prime Minister is the Leader of the House if he is a member of the Lok Sabha.
3. If the Prime Minister is not a Lok Sabha member, he nominates a minister as Leader of the House.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is false because the Leader of the House is not a constitutional office; under Manmohan Singh, a Rajya Sabha member, Pranab Mukherjee was named Leader of the House in the Lok Sabha.
27.tq: Not in the Constitution: PM leads if in LS, else his nominee.

27.s: Who was the first Leader of the House in the Lok Sabha?
27.x: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Leader of the House in the Lok Sabha, as the Prime Minister who was a member of that House.
27.tq: First PM, first Leader of the House: Nehru.

27.s: Who was the first Prime Minister of India and also holds the record for the longest overall tenure as Prime Minister?
27.x: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of India and had the maximum aggregate tenure as Prime Minister, from 1947 to 1964.
27.tq: Directly identify the office-holder associated with two linked firsts.

27.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Prime Minister)
A. Gulzarilal Nanda
B. Indira Gandhi
C. A.B. Vajpayee
D. Charan Singh

List-II (Distinction)
1. First Prime Minister from the Rajya Sabha
2. Never faced the Lok Sabha as Prime Minister
3. First acting Prime Minister (twice)
4. Shortest tenure of a regular Prime Minister (13 days)

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
27.x: Gulzarilal Nanda was the first acting PM (1964, 1966); Indira Gandhi was the first PM from the Rajya Sabha (1966); A.B. Vajpayee had the shortest regular tenure (13 days, 1996); Charan Singh (1979) never faced the Lok Sabha. Hence A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2. Option 2 swaps Nanda and Indira and Vajpayee and Charan Singh; option 3 swaps Indira and Vajpayee; option 4 swaps Nanda and Charan Singh.
27.tq: Nanda = acting; Indira = first RS PM; Vajpayee = 13 days; Charan Singh = never faced LS.

27.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Prime Ministers of India:
1. P.V. Narasimha Rao became Prime Minister in 1991 without initially being a Member of Parliament.
2. He subsequently entered the Lok Sabha from Nandyal.
3. He was the first Prime Minister from South India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: All three statements are correct. P.V. Narasimha Rao became Prime Minister in 1991 without initially being an MP, later won from Nandyal, and was the first Prime Minister from South India.
27.tq: Check each linked biographical statement separately before selecting the coded combination.

27.s: Which one of the following was NOT a Prime Minister of India who came from the Rajya Sabha?
27.x: The Prime Ministers from the Rajya Sabha were Indira Gandhi (the first, 1966), H.D. Deve Gowda, I.K. Gujral and Manmohan Singh. Charan Singh was a Lok Sabha member, not a Rajya Sabha PM (he is noted as the PM who never faced the Lok Sabha).
27.tq: Find the odd office-holder by comparing the complete list of Rajya Sabha Prime Ministers.

27.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 130th Constitution Amendment Bill, 2025:
1. A Prime Minister, Chief Minister or Minister detained for 30 consecutive days for an offence punishable with five or more years would be removed on the 31st day.
2. It proposed amendments to Articles 75, 164 and 239AA.
3. It was referred to the Law Commission of India for examination.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
27.x: Statement 1 is correct: 30 consecutive days of detention for an offence punishable with 5+ years leads to removal on the 31st day. Statement 2 is correct: it touches Arts 75, 164 and 239AA. Statement 3 is wrong: the Bill was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee, not the Law Commission. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
27.tq: 130th Bill: 30 days detention, 5+ years offence, out on day 31; Arts 75/164/239AA; sent to a JPC.

27.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the position of the Prime Minister in the United Kingdom from that in India?
o: The UK Prime Minister must belong to the House of Lords, whereas the Indian Prime Minister must belong to the Lok Sabha.
The UK Prime Minister must belong to the House of Commons, whereas the Indian Prime Minister may belong to either House of Parliament.
Both the UK and Indian Prime Ministers must be members of the lower House.
Neither the UK nor the Indian Prime Minister may be a member of the upper House.
27.x: The UK Prime Minister must belong to the House of Commons, while the Indian Prime Minister may be a member of either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha.
27.tq: Use the House-membership distinction to separate the British and Indian parliamentary arrangements.

27.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the tenure of the Prime Minister of India?
o: The Constitution fixes a six-year term for every Prime Minister.
The Constitution fixes a maximum of two terms for the Prime Minister.
The Prime Minister must retire after completing one Lok Sabha term.
There is no constitutional term limit for the Prime Minister.
27.x: The Constitution does not prescribe a term limit for the Prime Minister. The Prime Minister continues in office subject to the parliamentary system and political confidence.
27.tq: Test whether a specific constitutional limitation actually exists rather than assuming a fixed tenure.

27.s: The 1956 Gentlemen’s Agreement relating to the united Andhra Pradesh cabinet provided for the proportion of Andhra and Telangana representation as
27.x: The 1956 Gentlemen’s Agreement fixed the united Andhra Pradesh cabinet proportion at 60% Andhra and 40% Telangana.
27.tq: Retain the direction of the comparison as well as the two percentages.

28.s:
The parliamentary form of government was adopted in India primarily because of which of the following considerations?
1. Experience gained under the Government of India Acts of 1919 and 1935
2. Desire to avoid the emergence of a personality cult
3. Complete separation of the executive from the legislature
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: India adopted the parliamentary form because of experience under the Acts of 1919 and 1935 and to avoid a personality cult. Complete separation of the executive from the legislature is a feature of the presidential system.
28.tq: Identify the historically stated reasons and reject the borrowed presidential-system feature.

28.s: Which one of the following is a feature of the parliamentary system as found in India but not of the presidential system described for the United States?
o: The executive has a fixed term independent of the legislature
The President is both head of the State and head of government
The executive is collectively responsible to the lower House
Secretaries are not members of the legislature
28.x: In India, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. A fixed-term executive, a President as both head of State and government, and non-legislator secretaries are features associated here with the presidential model.
28.tq: Split the options by comparing executive responsibility rather than by focusing on the office of President.

28.s:
Consider the following pairs:

Feature — System
1. Nominal and real executives — Parliamentary system
2. Separation of powers — Presidential system
3. Dissolution of the lower House — Parliamentary system
4. Secretaries as members of Congress — Presidential system

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
28.x: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correctly matched. In the presidential system described, secretaries are not members of Congress, so pair 4 is incorrect.
28.tq: Check each pair against the institutional distinction between parliamentary and presidential executives.

28.s:
Which of the following are necessary features of the parliamentary form of government in India?
1. Majority party rule
2. Collective responsibility
3. Prime Minister as the centre of power
4. Judicial review
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
28.x: Majority party rule, collective responsibility and the Prime Minister as the centre of power are necessary features of India’s parliamentary form. Judicial review is not listed as a necessary feature distinguishing this form.
28.tq: Separate essential features of the system from a general constitutional device.

28.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the feature that most clearly marks India as a parliamentary system?
o: Collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers
28.x: Collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the elected House is the characteristic feature distinguishing the parliamentary system.
28.tq: Identify the defining institutional feature rather than a general constitutional feature.

28.s: The underlying principle of the Cabinet form of government in India is best described as
o: a mechanism for speedy disposal of administrative work
a means of ensuring the supremacy of the President over Parliament
a mechanism of parliamentary democracy for ensuring collective responsibility of the Government to the people
a device for separating the executive completely from the legislature
28.x: UPSC 2017 key: the Cabinet form is a mechanism of parliamentary democracy for ensuring collective responsibility of the Government to the people. Speed of work is not its principle; the President is the nominal head, not supreme over Parliament; complete separation of executive and legislature is a presidential feature.
28.tq: Cabinet form = collective responsibility to the people via Parliament.

28.s: The word ‘Cabinet’ appears in the Constitution of India only in:
28.x: The word ‘Cabinet’ appears only in Article 352, which deals with a Proclamation of Emergency and the written advice of the Union Cabinet.
28.tq: Use the exact Article rather than assuming that the Cabinet is expressly described wherever the Council of Ministers is mentioned.

28.s: The expression ‘Cabinet’ was inserted in Article 352 by the:
28.x: The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1978 inserted the word ‘Cabinet’ in Article 352.
28.tq: Discriminate between closely spaced Constitutional Amendment numbers and years.

28.s: Under Article 352(3), a Proclamation of Emergency can be issued only on the written advice of the:
o: Council of Ministers including Ministers of State
Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home Affairs
28.x: Article 352(3) requires the President to act only on the written advice of the Union Cabinet for a Proclamation of Emergency.
28.tq: Distinguish the constitutionally specified Cabinet from the wider Council of Ministers.

28.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Cabinet from the Council of Ministers?
o: The Council of Ministers consists only of Cabinet Ministers, while the Cabinet includes all ranks of ministers.
The Cabinet is the smaller body of Cabinet Ministers and directs and supervises the Council of Ministers.
The Cabinet is the wider body, while the Council of Ministers is the smaller body.
Both terms refer to precisely the same constitutional body and perform identical functions.
28.x: The Cabinet is the smaller nucleus consisting of Cabinet Ministers; it takes policy decisions and directs and supervises the wider Council of Ministers.
28.tq: Apply the size-and-function distinction instead of treating the two terms as interchangeable.

28.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Council of Ministers is a wider body than the Cabinet.
2. The Council of Ministers is created under Articles 74 and 75.
3. The Council of Ministers normally meets regularly as a single body to take all policy decisions.
4. The Cabinet generally meets regularly and takes policy decisions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The wider Council of Ministers rarely meets as a body; the Cabinet is the body that meets regularly and takes policy decisions.
28.tq: Compare the constitutional status, size and working frequency of the two bodies.

28.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the collective responsibility of the Union Council of Ministers:
1. It is provided under Article 75(3), and the Council is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
2. A minister who is a member of the Rajya Sabha is collectively responsible to the Rajya Sabha.
3. A no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: Statement 1 is correct: Art. 75(3) makes the Council collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. Statement 2 is wrong: ministers from the Rajya Sabha are also collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. Statement 3 is correct: a no-confidence motion lies only in the Lok Sabha. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
28.tq: Collective responsibility = Art 75(3), to the Lok Sabha only, even for RS ministers.

28.s: What is the constitutional consequence of the death or resignation of the Prime Minister?
o: The Rajya Sabha is automatically dissolved.
Only the Cabinet Secretariat is dissolved.
The Council of Ministers as a whole goes out of office.
The President assumes the office of Prime Minister permanently.
28.x: The Prime Minister is the head of the Council of Ministers; therefore, the death or resignation of the Prime Minister results in the Council of Ministers going out of office.
28.tq: Test the institutional consequence of the Prime Minister's departure.

28.s: The oaths of office and secrecy to Union Ministers are administered by the
28.x: The President administers the oaths of office and secrecy to Union Ministers in accordance with the Third Schedule.
28.tq: Identify the constitutional authority associated with administering the oath.

28.s: In the States, the constitutional provision corresponding to Article 75(3) on collective responsibility is:
28.x: Article 164(2) provides that the Council of Ministers in a State is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly.
28.tq: Discriminate between neighbouring constitutional provisions by matching the subject with the exact Article.

28.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Defeat of the Union Government in the Rajya Sabha by itself requires the whole ministry to resign.
2. Passage of a no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha may result in the resignation of the whole ministry.
3. Defeat on a money bill or a major policy measure in the Lok Sabha may lead to the resignation of the whole ministry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct because they indicate loss of Lok Sabha confidence. Defeat in the Rajya Sabha by itself does not compel the ministry to resign.
28.tq: Test the House to which collective responsibility is owed and reject the reversed-House trap.

28.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the expression ‘ministers sink or swim together’ in the Indian parliamentary system?
o: Every minister is personally elected by the Lok Sabha
Ministers may publicly reject Cabinet decisions without consequence
All ministers are required to defend Cabinet decisions or resign
Only Cabinet Ministers are responsible for government policy
28.x: Collective responsibility requires all ministers to support Cabinet decisions publicly. A minister unwilling to defend such a decision must resign.
28.tq: Apply the principle of collective responsibility to the conduct of an individual minister.

28.s: The secrecy of Cabinet deliberations is principally ensured by the:
28.x: The oath of secrecy ensures confidentiality of Cabinet deliberations and supports the public presentation of a united government.
28.tq: Distinguish the oath connected with confidentiality from the general oath of office.

28.s: With reference to individual responsibility of a Union Minister, which of the following statements is correct?
o: A minister holds office during the pleasure of the Lok Sabha under Article 75(3).
A minister holds office during the pleasure of the President under Article 75(2).
A minister holds office during the pleasure of the Chief Justice of India.
A minister can be removed only after a no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha.
28.x: Article 75(2) provides that a Union Minister holds office during the pleasure of the President. In practice, the Prime Minister may ask a minister to resign or advise the President to dismiss the minister.
28.tq: Identify the formal appointing authority and separate individual from collective responsibility.

28.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Department of Personnel:
1. It came into existence in 1970.
2. Its origin was associated with the Administrative Reforms Commission of 1966.
3. It was placed under the Prime Minister.
4. It was created as a recommendation of the N. Gopalaswamy Ayyangar report to provide a minister and secretary solely for administrative reform.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: The Department of Personnel came in 1970, originated from the ARC of 1966 and was placed under the Prime Minister. Statement 4 is false; the Ayyangar report did not suggest a minister and secretary solely for administrative reform.
28.tq: Find the false historical attribution hidden among otherwise precise institutional statements.

28.s:
Which of the following were among the matters associated with the recommendations of the N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar Committee?
1. Grouping of ministries
2. Cabinet Committees
3. Reorganisation of the machinery of government
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: The 1949 report concerned reorganisation of the machinery of government, including grouping ministries and Cabinet Committees.
28.tq: Treat the broad description and its two constituent measures as separate checks.

28.s: The First Schedule to the Allocation of Business Rules, 1961 primarily relates to:
o: Allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha
Distribution of financial grants to local bodies
28.x: The First Schedule to the Allocation of Business Rules, 1961 concerns the allocation of subjects to ministries.
28.tq: Distinguish allocation of executive subjects from constitutional schedules dealing with other matters.

28.s: Which one of the following is a principal staff agency of the Government of India?
28.x: The Cabinet Secretariat is a principal staff agency of the Government of India.
28.tq: Distinguish executive staff agencies from constitutional and statutory bodies.

28.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Cabinet Secretariat:
1. It provides secretarial assistance to the Cabinet and Cabinet Committees.
2. It administers the Allocation of Business Rules and Transaction of Business Rules.
3. It is placed directly under the Vice-President of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Cabinet Secretariat functions directly under the Prime Minister.
28.tq: Split the options by checking the authority attached to the Secretariat.

28.s:
Which of the following correctly represents the wings and associated offices of the Cabinet Secretariat?
1. Civil Wing
2. Military Wing
3. Intelligence Wing
4. Directorate of Public Grievances
5. Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser
28.x: The Cabinet Secretariat has Civil, Military and Intelligence Wings and is associated with the Directorate of Public Grievances and the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser.
28.tq: Use the all-inclusive option only after verifying every listed component.

28.s: Which one of the following statements about the Cabinet Secretary is correct?
o: The Cabinet Secretary is the senior-most civil servant and administrative head of the Cabinet Secretariat.
The Cabinet Secretary is the constitutional head of the Union executive.
The Cabinet Secretary is elected by the Council of States.
The Cabinet Secretary is appointed by the Chief Justice of India.
28.x: The Cabinet Secretary is the senior-most civil servant and the administrative head of the Cabinet Secretariat.
28.tq: Reject options that assign constitutional or electoral roles to a civil servant.

28.s:
Consider the following statements about the Cabinet Secretary:
1. The Cabinet Secretary is described as the first among equals among Secretaries.
2. The Cabinet Secretary occupies the eleventh position in the Table of Precedence.
3. The Cabinet Secretary heads the National Crisis Management Committee.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: All three statements are correct. The Cabinet Secretary is first among equals among Secretaries, is placed eleventh in the Table of Precedence and heads the National Crisis Management Committee.
28.tq: Verify each independent attribute before selecting the combined statement option.

28.s: What is the normal tenure of the Cabinet Secretary, and up to what period may it be extended?
o: Three years, extendable to five years
Two years, extendable to four years
Four years, extendable to six years
One year, extendable to two years
28.x: The Cabinet Secretary has a tenure of two years, which may be extended up to four years.
28.tq: Distinguish the initial tenure from the maximum permissible extension.

28.s: The Cabinet Secretary is appointed by the:
28.x: The Cabinet Secretary is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet.
28.tq: Use the who-would-do-this-job test for senior executive appointments.

28.s: Cabinet Committees in India are best described as:
o: Judicial bodies established by the Supreme Court
Statutory bodies created by Acts of Parliament
Extra-constitutional bodies formed under the Transaction of Business Rules, 1961
Constitutional bodies established by separate Articles of the Constitution
28.x: Cabinet Committees are extra-constitutional bodies formed under the Transaction of Business Rules, 1961, framed under Article 77(3).
28.tq: Separate constitutional, statutory and extra-constitutional institutions.

28.s: How many Cabinet Committees are referred to in the present classification?
28.x: There are eight Cabinet Committees (Apr 2025): Appointments, Security, Political Affairs, Economic Affairs, Parliamentary Affairs, Accommodation, Investment and Growth, and Employment and Skill Development.
28.tq: Use numerical elimination with the closely spaced committee counts.

28.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Cabinet Committee)
A. Appointments Committee
B. Cabinet Committee on Security
C. Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs
D. Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs

List-II (Principal concern)
1. Government business and parliamentary sessions
2. Senior appointments
3. Defence, national security and nuclear doctrine
4. Economic and infrastructure projects

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
28.x: The Appointments Committee deals with senior appointments; the Security Committee with defence and national security; the Economic Affairs Committee with economic and infrastructure projects; and the Parliamentary Affairs Committee with parliamentary business.
28.tq: Start from the sure pairs and eliminate codes with a swapped function.

28.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Cabinet Committee on Employment and Skill Development — Defence and nuclear doctrine
Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs — Centre-State and political issues
Cabinet Committee on Accommodation — Allotment of government accommodation
Cabinet Committee on Investment and Growth — Investment-related decisions
28.x: Defence and nuclear doctrine are dealt with by the Cabinet Committee on Security. The Employment and Skill Development Committee concerns jobs and skilling.
28.tq: Find the wrong function by comparing each committee with its distinctive portfolio.

28.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Cabinet Committees:
1. The Prime Minister chairs the Appointments Committee.
2. The Prime Minister chairs the Cabinet Committee on Security.
3. The Prime Minister chairs the Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs.
4. The Prime Minister chairs the Cabinet Committee on Accommodation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Accommodation Committee is chaired by a senior minister rather than by the Prime Minister.
28.tq: Watch for the swapped chairperson in the otherwise familiar list.

28.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Cabinet Committees:
1. The Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs, which deals with Centre-State and political issues, is described as a 'super cabinet'.
2. The decision on caste enumeration in the Census was taken by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs.
3. The Cabinet Committees on Investment and Growth and on Employment and Skill Development were set up in 2019.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: Statement 1 is correct: the CCPA handles Centre-State and political issues and is called the 'super cabinet'. Statement 2 is wrong: caste enumeration in the Census was decided by the Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs, not the CCEA. Statement 3 is correct: both committees were set up in 2019. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
28.tq: CCPA = super cabinet, caste census; CCEA = economic/infrastructure projects; 2019 = Investment & Growth, Employment & Skills.

28.s: A ‘kitchen cabinet’ refers to:
o: A formal Cabinet Committee established by the Constitution
A permanent secretariat of the Parliament
An informal inner circle of the Prime Minister's trusted colleagues and friends
A group of opposition leaders advising the Speaker
28.x: A kitchen cabinet is an informal inner circle consisting of trusted colleagues and friends of the Prime Minister, including some senior ministers and non-ministers.
28.tq: Distinguish an informal political grouping from a formal constitutional or executive body.

28.s: Which of the following best explains the criticism directed at the kitchen cabinet?
o: It is a constitutional body that cannot advise the Prime Minister.
It is responsible for conducting parliamentary elections.
It consists exclusively of opposition members.
It is an extra-constitutional power centre that may bypass the Cabinet.
28.x: The kitchen cabinet is criticised as an extra-constitutional power centre because it may shape decisions while bypassing the formal Cabinet.
28.tq: Apply the concept to the institutional consequence described in the question.

28.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Groups of Ministers (GoMs) and Empowered Groups of Ministers (EGoMs):
1. They are permanent bodies that replace the Cabinet in decision-making.
2. They have been criticised for causing delay and diluting collective responsibility.
3. The existing GoMs and EGoMs were abolished in 2014.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: Statement 1 is wrong: GoMs/EGoMs are ad hoc groups that examine an issue and report to the Cabinet. Statement 2 is correct: they were criticised for delay and diluting collective responsibility. Statement 3 is correct: the existing GoMs/EGoMs were abolished in 2014. Hence '2 and 3 only'; options with 1 are wrong.
28.tq: GoMs/EGoMs: ad hoc, report to Cabinet, criticised for delay, abolished 2014.

28.s: Which of the following best describes the position of the Union Cabinet during single-party majority eras in India?
o: Collective responsibility is constitutionally suspended during a majority government.
Coalition coordination committees determine all Cabinet decisions.
Parliament invariably exercises complete control over the Cabinet.
The Prime Minister and Cabinet generally exercise strong dominance over Parliament.
28.x: During single-party majority eras, the Prime Minister and Cabinet generally dominate Parliament, leading to the criticism that the system may resemble a ‘cabinet dictatorship’.
28.tq: Distinguish a political tendency from a formal constitutional rule.

28.s: Why did coalition politics tend to weaken Cabinet cohesion and collective responsibility during 1989–2014?
o: Because coordination committees and the demands of alliance partners influenced government functioning
Because the President directly exercised all Cabinet powers
Because Parliament ceased to examine government expenditure
Because the Constitution abolished the office of the Prime Minister during coalition governments
28.x: Coalition governments had to accommodate coordination committees and the demands of alliance partners. This often weakened Cabinet cohesion and the effective operation of collective responsibility.
28.tq: Connect the political condition with its institutional consequence.

28.s: Which of the following statements regarding the resignation of the Attorney General of India is correct?
o: The Attorney General resigns by convention when the government changes.
The Attorney General must resign whenever the Lok Sabha is dissolved.
The Constitution requires resignation at the end of every financial year.
The Attorney General can resign only after approval by the Supreme Court.
28.x: Although the Constitution does not fix the Attorney General’s term, the Attorney General conventionally resigns when the government changes.
28.tq: Distinguish constitutional provisions from conventions governing office-holding.

28.s: Under Article 88 of the Constitution, the Attorney General of India has the right to:
o: Dissolve either House of Parliament with the President’s approval
Participate only in proceedings of the Rajya Sabha
Speak in either House, joint sittings and parliamentary committees without the right to vote
Vote in both Houses of Parliament and their committees
28.x: Article 88 permits the Attorney General to speak and participate in either House, joint sittings and parliamentary committees, but does not confer a right to vote.
28.tq: Test the confusable distinction between participation and voting.

28.s: The parliamentary privileges available to the Attorney General are specifically associated with:
28.x: The Attorney General enjoys the privileges of a Member of Parliament under Article 105(4), even though the Attorney General is not a Member of Parliament.
28.tq: Match the office-related privilege with its constitutional article.

28.s:
Consider the following statements about the professional limitations of the Attorney General of India:
1. The office is not a full-time office.
2. The Attorney General may undertake private practice.
3. The Attorney General may advise or brief against the Government of India in private practice.
4. The Attorney General may become a company director without permission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: The office is not full-time and private practice is permitted. However, the Attorney General cannot advise or brief against the Government of India and cannot become a company director without permission.
28.tq: Use the prohibited activities to eliminate overbroad statements.

28.s: Which one of the following activities is prohibited to the Attorney General of India?
o: Defending an accused person in a criminal case
Speaking in a parliamentary committee without voting
Advising the Government of India on legal matters
Appearing in the Supreme Court for the Government of India
28.x: The Attorney General cannot defend accused persons in criminal cases. Advising the Union Government, appearing in the Supreme Court for it and speaking in committees are recognised functions or rights.
28.tq: Identify the professional restriction hidden among ordinary constitutional functions.

28.s: Who was the first Attorney General of India?
28.x: M.C. Setalvad was the first Attorney General of India. C.K. Daphtary was the first Solicitor General.
28.tq: Discriminate between the first holders of two closely related law offices.

28.s: Which Article, among the following, specifically deals with the Attorney General's right to speak and participate in Parliament without voting rights?
28.x: Article 88 confers the Attorney General's right to speak and take part in parliamentary proceedings without the right to vote. Article 78 concerns the duties of the Prime Minister in relation to the President.
28.tq: Reject the look-alike Article number and identify the precise constitutional provision.

28.s: In the performance of his official duties, the Attorney General of India has the right of audience in
o: the Supreme Court and High Courts only
all courts in the territory of India
all courts in his home State only
28.x: The Attorney General has the right of audience in all courts in the territory of India, not just the Supreme Court or High Courts. The 'State' limitation describes the Advocate General, who has audience in all courts of his State.
28.tq: AG = all courts in India; Advocate General = all courts in the State.

28.s:
Consider the following statements comparing the Attorney General and the Solicitor General of India:
1. The office of the Attorney General is constitutional, whereas that of the Solicitor General is statutory.
2. The Attorney General has a fixed term of three years, whereas the Solicitor General has no fixed term.
3. The Attorney General advises the Government of India, whereas the Solicitor General only appears in courts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: Statement 1 is correct: the AG is constitutional (Art. 76), the SG is statutory. Statement 2 is wrong: it is reversed; the AG's term is not fixed, while the SG has a 3-year term. Statement 3 is correct: the AG advises the government, the SG only appears in courts. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
28.tq: AG: Art 76, no fixed term, advises. SG: statutory, 3 years, courts only.

28.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the appointment of the Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General?
o: They are recommended by the Supreme Court and appointed by the Chief Justice of India.
They are recommended by the Election Commission and appointed by Parliament.
They are recommended by the Attorney General and appointed by the Governor.
They are recommended by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet and appointed by the President.
28.x: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet recommends the Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General, and the President appoints them.
28.tq: Ask which authority performs the recommendation and appointment functions.

28.s: The State-level counterpart of the Attorney General of India is the:
o: State Solicitor General, appointed by the Chief Minister
Legal Secretary, appointed by the President
Public Prosecutor, appointed by the High Court
Advocate General, appointed by the Governor
28.x: The Advocate General is the counterpart of the Attorney General at the State level. The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor under Article 165.
28.tq: Apply the Union–State counterpart method to constitutional law officers.

28.s: The Advocate General of a State has the right to speak in the State Legislature under:
28.x: Article 177 gives the Advocate General the right to speak and participate in the proceedings of the State Legislature, without a right to vote. Article 165 relates to the office itself.
28.tq: Distinguish the article creating the office from the article conferring legislative participation.

28.s: Which one of the following is regarded as a criticism of excessive concentration of power in the Prime Minister’s Office and Cabinet committees?
o: It strengthens independent decision-making by every Cabinet minister.
It dilutes collective decision-making by the Cabinet as a whole.
It transfers all legislative privileges to the Attorney General.
It makes coalition coordination committees constitutionally mandatory.
28.x: Excessive concentration of power in the PMO and Cabinet committees is criticised for diluting collective Cabinet decision-making.
28.tq: Identify the institutional consequence of centralisation within the executive.

28.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Shadow Cabinet:
1. The Shadow Cabinet is associated with the United Kingdom.
2. India has a formal constitutional counterpart of the Shadow Cabinet.
Which of the statements given above is correct?
28.x: The Shadow Cabinet is a feature associated with the United Kingdom. India has no formal counterpart of the Shadow Cabinet.
28.tq: Test the common comparative-politics assumption that similar parliamentary systems have identical institutions.

28.s: In July 2026, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the construction of the third and fourth railway lines on which section?
28.x: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the third and fourth railway lines on the Ballari–Guntakal section at a cost of Rs 1,264 crore.
28.tq: Use the location and project-number combination to identify the correct current-affairs item.

28.s: Who is regarded as the State equivalent of the Cabinet Secretary?
28.x: The Chief Secretary is regarded as the State equivalent of the Cabinet Secretary. G. Sai Prasad took charge as Andhra Pradesh Chief Secretary in February 2026.
28.tq: Apply the Union–State administrative equivalent pairing.

28.s: Who took charge as the Chief Secretary of Andhra Pradesh in February 2026?
28.x: G. Sai Prasad took charge as the Chief Secretary of Andhra Pradesh in February 2026.
28.tq: Distinguish the State appointment from the Union-level administrative appointments.

29.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: United Kingdom — House of Lords and House of Commons
United States of America — Federation Council and State Duma
Japan — Senate and House of Representatives
Russia — House of Councillors and House of Representatives
29.x: The United Kingdom has the House of Lords as its upper house and the House of Commons as its lower house. The other pairs mix the names of houses belonging to different countries.
29.tq: Start from the sure country-house pair and eliminate swapped institutional names.

29.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. USA — Senate and House of Representatives
2. Japan — House of Councillors and House of Representatives
3. Russia — Federation Council and State Duma
4. Australia — Senate and House of Representatives
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
29.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. The Russian Parliament is the Federal Assembly, consisting of the Federation Council as the upper house and the State Duma as the lower house.
29.tq: Check each country against its institutional pair before selecting the inclusive combination.

29.s: The Parliament of Russia is officially known as the
29.x: Russia's Parliament is the Federal Assembly. The Federation Council is its upper house and the State Duma is its lower house.
29.tq: Distinguish the name of the complete legislature from the names of its two chambers.

29.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A legislature consisting of only one House is termed unicameral.
2. India's Parliament is bicameral, consisting of the Rajya Sabha and the Legislative Councils of the States.
3. India's Parliament consists of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
29.x: Statement 1 is correct: unicameral = one House, bicameral = two Houses. Statement 2 is wrong: State Legislative Councils are not part of Parliament. Statement 3 is correct: Parliament = Rajya Sabha + Lok Sabha. Hence 1 and 3 only; options with 2 are wrong and '1 only' misses statement 3.
29.tq: State Legislative Councils belong to State legislatures, never to Parliament.

29.s:
Which of the following countries has a unicameral national legislature?
1. China
2. Israel
3. New Zealand
4. Sweden
5. Denmark
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
29.x: China, Israel, New Zealand, Sweden and Denmark are examples of countries with unicameral national legislatures. Their principal legislative bodies include China's National People's Congress and Israel's Knesset.
29.tq: Treat the complete country list as the tested unit and watch for an omitted member.

29.s: Large and diverse countries generally prefer bicameral legislatures primarily because they
o: ensure that every bill originates in the upper House
represent different sections and regions in the legislative process
prevent the lower House from controlling financial legislation
make direct election unnecessary for both Houses
29.x: Bicameralism is often preferred in large and diverse countries because two Houses can represent different sections, interests and regions.
29.tq: Apply the representational rationale rather than confusing it with a procedural power.

29.s: Which one of the following is NOT an argument advanced in favour of a second chamber?
o: States, regions and diverse interests receive representation.
It necessarily makes the legislative process faster.
Experts can be brought into the legislature through nomination.
Every Bill receives a second examination.
29.x: A second chamber is argued to provide a double check, regional representation and expert participation. Delay and duplication are generally cited as arguments against it, not in its favour.
29.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated advantage into a consequence of bicameral delay.

29.s: The statement, “If it agrees it is superfluous, if it dissents it is mischievous,” is associated with
29.x: The criticism of a second chamber expressed in these words is attributed to Abbé Sieyès.
29.tq: Match the distinctive quotation with its author rather than with a supporter of the institution.

29.s: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar defended the Rajya Sabha as a House intended to provide
o: dignified debate and a check on hasty legislation
29.x: Ayyangar regarded the Rajya Sabha as a forum for dignified debate that could delay legislation passed in the passion of the moment.
29.tq: Identify the purpose attached to the institution by its constitutional defender.

29.s: Jawaharlal Nehru cautioned against the judiciary becoming a
29.x: Nehru cautioned against the judiciary assuming the role of a “third chamber.”
29.tq: Recall the exact constitutional metaphor used in the statement.

29.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the basis of representation in the Rajya Sabha and the US Senate?
o: Rajya Sabha gives two seats to every State, whereas the US Senate is population-based.
Rajya Sabha representation is based on population, whereas the US Senate gives two seats to every State.
Both provide equal representation to every State.
Both allocate seats exclusively through nomination.
29.x: Rajya Sabha seats are allocated broadly according to population under the Fourth Schedule, while every US State has two Senators, making 100 Senators in all.
29.tq: Split the options by comparing the representation principle before considering the numerical detail.

29.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the Rajya Sabha and the US Senate?
1. Rajya Sabha — election by elected MLAs through proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote
2. US Senate — direct election
3. Rajya Sabha — 12 nominated members
4. US Senate — nominated members
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
29.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The US Senate has no nominated members, so statement 4 is false.
29.tq: Use the election and nomination distinctions to reject the swapped-membership statement.

29.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Speaker certifies whether a Bill is a Money Bill.
2. The Speaker presides over a joint sitting of Parliament.
3. The Rajya Sabha can initiate a no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers.
4. The Rajya Sabha has no vote on Demands for Grants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
29.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is false because a no-confidence motion is a device of the Lok Sabha, not the Rajya Sabha.
29.tq: Ask who performs the constitutional job and reject the power assigned to the wrong House.

29.s:
Consider the following statements about the Rajya Sabha:
1. Article 312 relates to the creation of new All-India Services, a role specific to the Rajya Sabha.
2. The Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha within 14 days.
3. Like the US Senate, every State has an equal number of seats in the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
29.x: Statement 1 is correct: Article 312 (creation of new All-India Services) is a special federal role of the Rajya Sabha. Statement 2 is correct: a Money Bill must be returned within 14 days, showing the House is weaker than the Lok Sabha. Statement 3 is wrong: Rajya Sabha seats are allotted broadly by population under the Fourth Schedule (UP 31), unlike the US Senate's 2 per State. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
29.tq: RS: Art 312 power, 14 days on Money Bills, seats by population.

29.s: Under Article 169, a State Legislative Council may be created or abolished by Parliament when the State Legislative Assembly passes a resolution by
o: a majority of the total membership and a two-thirds majority of members present and voting
a two-thirds majority of the total membership alone
a unanimous vote of all members of the Assembly
a simple majority of members present and voting
29.x: The Assembly resolution must be passed by a majority of the total membership and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of members present and voting.
29.tq: Keep the two limbs of the special majority separate: total membership and present-and-voting membership.

29.s:
Consider the following statements about State Legislative Councils:
1. Under Article 169, Parliament creates or abolishes a Legislative Council by law, not by an amendment under Article 368.
2. Under Article 171, a Legislative Council may have up to one-half of the membership of the Legislative Assembly.
3. A Legislative Council must have at least 40 members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
29.x: Statement 1 is correct: Article 169 works through an ordinary law of Parliament after the Assembly resolution. Statement 2 is wrong: the Council cannot exceed one-third of the Assembly. Statement 3 is correct: the minimum is 40. Hence 1 and 3 only; '1 only' misses 3, and options with 2 are wrong.
29.tq: Council size: not more than one-third of the Assembly, not less than 40.

29.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of States with unicameral legislatures?
29.x: Goa, Mizoram and Sikkim have unicameral legislatures. Telangana, Karnataka and Maharashtra each have a Legislative Council, so options B, C and D each include a bicameral State.
29.tq: Identify the common legislative structure and eliminate groups containing a bicameral State.

29.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Legislative Assembly of Delhi is based on Article 239AA, inserted by the 69th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1991.
2. The Legislative Assembly of Puducherry is based on Article 239AA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
29.x: Statement 1 is correct: Delhi's Assembly rests on Article 239AA (69th Amendment, 1991). Statement 2 is wrong: Puducherry's Assembly rests on Article 239A. Hence 1 only; 'Both' and '2 only' wrongly accept statement 2, 'Neither' rejects statement 1.
29.tq: 239A = Puducherry; 239AA (the extra A) = Delhi.

29.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Delhi — 70 Assembly seats
2. Puducherry — 30 elected members and up to 3 nominated members
3. Jammu and Kashmir — 90 elected Assembly seats
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
29.x: Delhi has 70 Assembly seats, Puducherry has 30 elected members and up to 3 nominated members, and Jammu and Kashmir has 90 elected seats.
29.tq: Verify the numerical figures UT by UT, especially the elected-versus-nominated distinction.

29.s: Which Union Territories have elected members in the Rajya Sabha?
o: Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir
Delhi, Daman and Diu and Dadra and Nagar Haveli
29.x: Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir are the three Union Territories having elected members in the Rajya Sabha.
29.tq: Use the complete three-member list and reject Union Territories without elected Rajya Sabha representation.

29.s: The Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 was introduced with the objective of extending women's reservation to the legislatures of
o: All Union Territories having no Legislative Assembly
Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir
29.x: The Bill introduced in 2026 sought to extend women's reservation to the legislatures of Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir.
29.tq: Match the current legislative proposal with the exact set of affected Union Territories.

29.s: In the February 2026 referendum, Bangladesh voted for a bicameral Parliament whose proposed upper House would have
o: 100 members elected according to party vote share
200 members elected equally from every district
50 members elected by direct universal suffrage
100 nominated members appointed by the President
29.x: Bangladesh voted in the February 2026 referendum for a bicameral Parliament with a 100-member upper House elected according to party vote share.
29.tq: Combine the referendum outcome with both the upper-House size and electoral basis.

29.s: Which one of the following statements about Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Its Legislative Council was created in 2020 and abolished in 2021.
It has always had a unicameral legislature since 1956.
Its Legislative Council was abolished in 2007 and revived in 2021.
Its Legislative Council was abolished in 1985, revived in 2007, and the 2020 abolition resolution was withdrawn in 2021.
29.x: Andhra Pradesh's Legislative Council was abolished in 1985, revived in 2007, and the resolution passed in 2020 to abolish it again was withdrawn in 2021.
29.tq: Use the full event sequence to detect reversed years and reversed institutional changes.

29.s: A proposal to increase the size of the Lok Sabha would, in a joint sitting of Parliament, tend to
o: dilute the relative weight of the Rajya Sabha
abolish the Rajya Sabha's nominated membership
increase the relative weight of the Rajya Sabha
give the Rajya Sabha exclusive control over Money Bills
29.x: Since a joint sitting is presided over by the Speaker and voting strength depends on the combined membership, a larger Lok Sabha would dilute the Rajya Sabha's relative weight.
29.tq: Apply the membership relationship in a joint sitting instead of focusing on the separate powers of each House.

30.s: Which of the following correctly represents the composition of Parliament under Article 79?
o: The Prime Minister, the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha
The President, the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha
The President and the Lok Sabha only
The Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha only
30.x: Article 79 provides that Parliament consists of the President and two Houses—the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
30.tq: Recall the constitutional composition rather than the membership of the Houses.

30.s: Articles 79 to 122 of the Constitution occur in
30.x: Parliamentary provisions in Articles 79 to 122 are contained in Part V of the Constitution.
30.tq: Link the article range with the correct constitutional Part.

30.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the President as a component of Parliament:
1. The President is a part of Parliament but is not a member of either House.
2. No Bill passed by Parliament becomes law without the President's assent.
3. The President may summon and prorogue the Houses of Parliament.
4. The President sits in Parliament as a member while addressing the Houses.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
30.x: The President is a component of Parliament but does not sit as a member of either House. Presidential assent is necessary for a Bill to become law, and the President summons and prorogues Parliament.
30.tq: Distinguish being a constitutional component of Parliament from being a member who sits in a House.

30.s: Article 86 of the Constitution empowers the President to
o: Vote in both Houses on an ordinary Bill
Nominate the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Address either House of Parliament or both Houses assembled together
Preside over a joint sitting of Parliament
30.x: Article 86 enables the President to address either House of Parliament or both Houses assembled together and to send messages to them.
30.tq: Discriminate Article 86’s communication power from the powers of the presiding officers.

30.s: The constitutional position of the Indian President in relation to Parliament is most closely comparable to
o: The Governor of a State in relation to its Legislative Assembly only
The President of France in relation to its Senate
The President of the United States in relation to Congress
The Crown-in-Parliament in the United Kingdom
30.x: The inclusion of the President as a component of Parliament resembles the Crown-in-Parliament principle in the United Kingdom. It differs from the United States, where the President is separate from Congress.
30.tq: Apply the comparative constitutional analogy and distinguish the UK model from the US model.

30.s:
Assertion (A): The President is a component of the Parliament of India.
Reason (R): No Bill passed by both Houses of Parliament can become law without the President's assent.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
30.x: Both statements are true. The President’s constitutional role in completing the legislative process is a reason for treating the President as a component of Parliament under Article 79.
30.tq: Test the constitutional relationship between the President’s assent and Parliament’s composition.
