30.s: Under Article 87 of the Constitution, the President's special address to both Houses of Parliament assembled together is made at the commencement of
o: the first session after each general election to the Lok Sabha and the first session of each year
only the Budget session after the Annual Financial Statement is laid
only a joint sitting summoned under Article 108
30.x: Article 87 requires a special address at the first session after each general election to the Lok Sabha and at the first session of each year. It is not made at every session, it is not tied to the Budget being laid, and a joint sitting under Article 108 is a different provision. Article 86 is the general power to address either House at any time.
30.tq: Art. 86 = may address any time; Art. 87 = must address: first session after election + first session of each year.

30.s: Under Article 80 of the Constitution, the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is
30.x: Article 80 fixes the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha at 250, comprising 238 representatives of States and Union Territories and 12 nominated members.
30.tq: Distinguish the constitutional maximum from the present strength.

30.s: The present composition of the Rajya Sabha is correctly represented by which one of the following?
o: 238 representatives of States and Union Territories and 7 nominated members
225 representatives of States, 12 representatives of Union Territories and 8 nominated members
225 representatives of States, 8 representatives of Union Territories and 12 nominated members
233 representatives of States and Union Territories and 12 nominated members
30.x: The present strength is 245: 225 representatives of States, 8 representatives of Union Territories and 12 nominated members.
30.tq: Separate present composition from the constitutional maximum.

30.s:
With reference to the election of representatives of States to the Rajya Sabha, consider the following statements:
1. They are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies.
2. The election is held by proportional representation through the single transferable vote system.
3. Nominated members of State Legislative Assemblies participate in this election.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
30.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct under Article 80(4). Nominated members of State Legislative Assemblies do not participate in this election.
30.tq: Check the elector and the voting method separately; the nominated-member statement is the trap.

30.s:
The Supreme Court decision in Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India (2006) upheld which of the following in relation to Rajya Sabha elections?
1. Removal of the domicile requirement
2. Use of an open ballot
3. Direct election by all citizens of the State
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
30.x: The Supreme Court upheld the removal of the domicile requirement and the open-ballot system. Rajya Sabha members are not directly elected by all citizens of a State.
30.tq: Separate the two holdings of the judgment from the constitutionally prescribed electoral method.

30.s: The present strength of the Lok Sabha is composed of
o: 530 members from States and 13 from Union Territories
524 members from States and 19 from Union Territories
525 members from States and 18 from Union Territories
30.x: The present strength is 543, comprising 524 members from the States and 19 from the Union Territories.
30.tq: Split the total into its State and Union Territory components.

30.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the maximum and present strength of the Lok Sabha?
30.x: The constitutional maximum is 550, while the present strength is 543. The older figure of 552 included two nominated Anglo-Indian members.
30.tq: Compare the current figure with the historical figure instead of treating them as interchangeable.

30.s: The nomination of Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha under Article 331 was discontinued by the
30.x: The 104th Amendment Act, 2019 ended the provision for nomination of up to two Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha, with effect from 25 January 2020.
30.tq: Pair the constitutional provision with the correct amendment and effective date.

30.s: Prior to its discontinuance, Article 331 enabled the President to nominate up to how many Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha?
30.x: Article 331 permitted the President to nominate up to two Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha if the community was not adequately represented.
30.tq: Distinguish the former nomination limit from the present elected strength.

30.s: Members of the Lok Sabha are directly elected on the basis of adult suffrage under Article 326. The voting age for such elections was lowered to 18 years by the
30.x: The 61st Amendment Act, 1987 (in force 1989) lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years under Article 326. The 42nd and 44th Amendments relate to the Emergency-era changes and their reversal, and the 73rd Amendment concerns Panchayati Raj.
30.tq: 61st Amendment = 21 to 18 voting age (Art. 326).

30.s:
The qualification for nomination to the Rajya Sabha includes special knowledge or practical experience in which of the following fields?
1. Literature
2. Science
3. Art
4. Social service
5. Sports
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
30.x: Article 80(3) mentions literature, science, art and social service. Sports is not one of the four constitutionally listed fields.
30.tq: Identify the exact constitutional list and exclude the look-alike addition.

30.s:
Consider the following statements about nominated members of the Rajya Sabha:
1. They can vote in the election of the Vice-President.
2. They can vote in the election of the President.
3. A nominated member may join a political party within six months of taking the seat without being disqualified.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
30.x: Statement 1 is correct: nominated members vote in the Vice-Presidential election. Statement 2 is wrong: they cannot vote in the Presidential election. Statement 3 is correct: joining a party within six months is allowed; after that it attracts disqualification under the Tenth Schedule. Hence 1 and 3 only.
30.tq: Nominated members: VP election yes, President election no.

30.s:
Consider the following statements regarding nominated members of the Rajya Sabha:
1. Sachin Tendulkar was nominated in 2012.
2. Mary Kom was nominated in 2016.
3. Lata Mangeshkar was nominated for her contribution to sport.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
30.x: Sachin Tendulkar was nominated in 2012 and Mary Kom in 2016. Lata Mangeshkar represented the field of art, not sport.
30.tq: Match notable persons with the correct field and avoid the swapped-domain trap.

30.s:
Consider the following statements about the allocation of Rajya Sabha seats:
1. Seats are allotted to the States under the Fourth Schedule.
2. Like the US Senate, every State gets an equal number of seats.
3. Uttar Pradesh has the highest number of Rajya Sabha seats.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
30.x: Statement 1 is correct: seats are allotted under the Fourth Schedule (Arts. 4 and 80(2)). Statement 2 is wrong: seats are allotted by population, unlike the equal representation in the US Senate. Statement 3 is correct: UP has 31 seats, the highest. Hence 1 and 3 only.
30.tq: Rajya Sabha = population-based (Fourth Schedule); US Senate = equal, 2 per State.

30.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (State)
A. Andhra Pradesh
B. Telangana
C. Uttarakhand
D. Tripura

List-II (Rajya Sabha seats)
1. 1
2. 3
3. 7
4. 11

option codes:
30.x: Andhra Pradesh has 11 seats, Telangana 7, Uttarakhand 3 and Tripura 1 in the Rajya Sabha.
30.tq: Start from the sure numerical pair and eliminate codes.

30.s: Which one of the following groups consists only of States having one seat each in the Rajya Sabha?
o: Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Manipur and Tripura
30.x: Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura each have one Rajya Sabha seat. The group in option a contains only such States.
30.tq: Check every member of the group against the single-seat condition.

30.s: The allocation of seats in the Lok Sabha to the States remains frozen on the basis of the 1971 Census until
o: the completion of the 2031 Census only
30.x: The 84th Amendment Act, 2001 froze the allocation of Lok Sabha seats based on the 1971 Census until the first Census after 2026.
30.tq: Read the endpoint of a constitutional freeze precisely.

30.s: Which one of the following statements regarding delimitation of Lok Sabha constituencies is correct?
o: The allocation and constituencies were both permanently frozen by the 84th Amendment.
The constituencies were readjusted on the basis of the 1971 Census by the Election Commission.
The constituencies were readjusted on the basis of the 2001 Census by the Delimitation Commission under Justice Kuldip Singh.
The constituencies were readjusted on the basis of the 2011 Census by Parliament alone.
30.x: The 87th Amendment enabled readjustment of constituencies on the basis of the 2001 Census. This work was undertaken by the Delimitation Commission under Justice Kuldip Singh.
30.tq: Distinguish freezing seat allocation from readjusting constituency boundaries.

30.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched with the number of Lok Sabha seats?
1. Andhra Pradesh — 25
2. Telangana — 17
3. Uttarakhand — 5
4. Jammu and Kashmir — 5
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
30.x: All four pairs are correct: Andhra Pradesh has 25, Telangana 17, Uttarakhand 5 and the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir 5 Lok Sabha seats.
30.tq: Verify each numerical pair independently before choosing the coded combination.

30.s:
Consider the following statements about Lok Sabha seats:
1. Sikkim, Mizoram and Nagaland have one Lok Sabha seat each.
2. Tripura has only one Lok Sabha seat.
3. Ladakh and Lakshadweep have one Lok Sabha seat each.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
30.x: Statement 1 is correct: Sikkim, Mizoram and Nagaland are the single-seat States. Statement 2 is wrong: Tripura has 2 Lok Sabha seats (it has one Rajya Sabha seat). Statement 3 is correct: Ladakh and Lakshadweep, like A&N Islands, Chandigarh and Puducherry, have one seat each. Hence 1 and 3 only.
30.tq: Do not mix single Rajya Sabha seat States (Tripura, Goa...) with single Lok Sabha seat States (Sikkim, Mizoram, Nagaland).

30.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Largest Lok Sabha constituency by number of electors — Malkajgiri
Largest Lok Sabha constituency by area — Ladakh
Smallest Lok Sabha constituency by area — Mumbai South
Smallest Lok Sabha constituency by number of electors — Lakshadweep
30.x: C is wrong: the smallest Lok Sabha constituency by area is Chandni Chowk (Delhi), not Mumbai South. Malkajgiri is the largest and Lakshadweep the smallest by number of electors, and Ladakh is the largest by area.
30.tq: Separate area-based comparisons from elector-based comparisons.

30.s:
Consider the following statements about the term of the Lok Sabha:
1. Under Article 83(2), its five-year term runs from the date of its first meeting.
2. It may be dissolved early by the President on the advice of the Speaker.
3. An early dissolution cannot be challenged in court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
30.x: Statement 1 is correct: the term is reckoned from the first meeting. Statement 2 is wrong: the President dissolves on the Prime Minister's advice, not the Speaker's. Statement 3 is correct: such dissolution cannot be challenged in court. Hence 1 and 3 only.
30.tq: Dissolution = President on PM's advice; term counted from first meeting, not election.

30.s:
With reference to the extension of the term of the Lok Sabha during a National Emergency, consider the following statements:
1. Parliament may extend the term by law for one year at a time.
2. The extension may continue indefinitely after the Emergency ends.
3. No extension can continue beyond six months after the Emergency has ceased.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
30.x: The term may be extended by law for one year at a time during the Emergency, but not beyond six months after the Emergency ends. Statement 2 is therefore false.
30.tq: Split the options by checking the limiting phrase in the constitutional rule.

30.s: Which Lok Sabha was extended during the National Emergency of 1975–1977?
30.x: The Fifth Lok Sabha, constituted for the period 1971–1977, was extended during the 1975–1977 Emergency.
30.tq: Discriminate between closely numbered Lok Sabhas and their distinct events.

30.s: Which one of the following Lok Sabhas was dissolved before completion of its full term?
30.x: The Thirteenth Lok Sabha was dissolved in 2004 before completing its full term. The Fifth Lok Sabha was extended during the Emergency.
30.tq: Find the one item belonging to the stated group by distinguishing dissolution from extension.

30.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Rajya Sabha:
1. It is a permanent and continuing House.
2. It is not subject to dissolution.
3. The whole House is elected together after every six years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
30.x: The Rajya Sabha is permanent and is never dissolved. Its members retire by rotation; the whole House is not elected together.
30.tq: Reject the reversed comparison between the two Houses.

30.s: The term of a member of the Rajya Sabha is six years. This term is fixed by the
o: Rules of Procedure of the Rajya Sabha
30.x: The six-year term of a Rajya Sabha member is fixed by the Representation of the People Act, 1951, and not directly by the Constitution.
30.tq: Use the statutory-versus-constitutional distinction to avoid an authority trap.

30.s: In the first Rajya Sabha constituted in 1952, the members who were to retire first were selected by
o: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
30.x: To initiate the one-third retirement cycle, the terms of the initial members were curtailed and the members retiring first were decided by lottery.
30.tq: Use a precise institutional detail rather than a general feature of rotation.

30.s:
With reference to the qualifications for membership of Parliament, consider the following statements:
1. The minimum age for membership of the Lok Sabha is 25 years.
2. The minimum age for membership of the Rajya Sabha is 30 years.
3. The Constitution prescribes a minimum educational qualification for membership of either House.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
30.x: The minimum ages are 25 years for the Lok Sabha and 30 years for the Rajya Sabha. No minimum educational qualification is prescribed for membership of Parliament.
30.tq: Use the comparison between the two Houses and identify the swapped qualification requirement.

30.s: The oath or affirmation required before a person takes his or her seat in Parliament is made before
o: The Election Commission or a person authorised by it
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha only
The President or a person authorised by him
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha only
30.x: A prospective Member of Parliament makes the prescribed oath or affirmation before the Election Commission or a person authorised by it, in the form given in the Third Schedule.
30.tq: Discriminate between the authority administering the oath and the authority deciding disqualification.

30.s: Which of the following statements regarding electoral qualifications for Parliament is correct?
o: The Constitution requires residence in the concerned State for every Rajya Sabha candidate.
Only a person domiciled in the concerned State can contest a Rajya Sabha election.
A person contesting a reserved Lok Sabha seat need not be an elector.
A person must be a registered elector in a parliamentary constituency to contest a parliamentary election.
30.x: A candidate for Parliament must be a registered elector in a parliamentary constituency. The domicile requirement for Rajya Sabha candidates was removed in 2003, and a candidate for a reserved Lok Sabha seat must belong to the relevant Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe.
30.tq: Separate the continuing elector requirement from the abolished domicile requirement.

30.s: Which one of the following is NOT a ground of disqualification under Article 102 of the Constitution?
o: Being declared of unsound mind by a competent court
Holding an office of profit under the Union or a State, subject to exemptions by law
30.x: Article 102 includes office of profit, unsoundness of mind declared by a court, undischarged insolvency, loss or absence of Indian citizenship and disqualification under a parliamentary law. Lack of a university degree is not a ground of disqualification.
30.tq: Identify the option that is outside the constitutional list of disqualifications.

30.s: Parliament may exempt a particular office from the disqualification relating to office of profit by
o: A notification issued by the President alone
A direction of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
An order of the Election Commission
30.x: Parliament can exempt specified offices from the office-of-profit disqualification by enacting a law.
30.tq: Ask which authority has legislative power rather than merely administrative power.

30.s: A question arises regarding the disqualification of a sitting Member of Parliament under Article 102, other than disqualification under the Tenth Schedule. The constitutional procedure is that the decision is made by the
o: Election Commission, after obtaining the opinion of the President
President, after obtaining and acting according to the opinion of the Election Commission
Speaker or Chairman, without reference to any other authority
Supreme Court, on a reference made by the Prime Minister
30.x: Under Article 103, the President decides the question after obtaining the opinion of the Election Commission and acts in accordance with that opinion.
30.tq: Use the ‘who decides?’ method and distinguish Article 103 from Tenth Schedule proceedings.

30.s:
With reference to disqualification on the ground of defection, consider the following statements:
1. A Member of the Lok Sabha who voluntarily gives up membership of the political party is liable to disqualification.
2. An independent member joining a political party after election is liable to disqualification.
3. A nominated member joining a political party after six months from taking his seat is liable to disqualification.
4. The President decides every question of disqualification under the Tenth Schedule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
30.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 correctly state grounds under the Tenth Schedule. Statement 4 is false: the Speaker of the Lok Sabha or the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha decides such questions, subject to judicial review.
30.tq: Separate Article 103 disqualification from defection decided under the Tenth Schedule.

30.s: A Member of Parliament votes contrary to the direction of the political party without prior permission, but the party condones the action within the prescribed period. In this situation, disqualification on the ground of defection does not arise because the action was condoned within
30.x: A vote or abstention contrary to the party whip may attract disqualification unless the action is permitted or condoned by the party within 15 days.
30.tq: Test the precise statutory time limit rather than the general principle of defection.

30.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Kihoto Hollohan — Judicial review of decisions under the Tenth Schedule
Kuldip Nayar — Introduction of the Tenth Schedule
Thirty-third Amendment — Removal of the office-of-profit disqualification
Article 103 — Decision on defection by the President
30.x: Kihoto Hollohan (1992) recognised that decisions under the Tenth Schedule are subject to judicial review. Kuldip Nayar concerned the Rajya Sabha domicile requirement, the Thirty-third Amendment dealt with resignation procedure, and Article 103 does not govern defection.
30.tq: Match each case or provision with its actual constitutional subject.

30.s:
Consider the following statements about vacation of seats under Article 101:
1. If a person elected to both Houses does not intimate the choice within 10 days, the Lok Sabha seat falls vacant.
2. If a sitting member of one House is elected to the other House, the seat in the first House falls vacant.
3. If a person elected to two seats in the same House does not choose one, both seats fall vacant.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
30.x: Statement 1 is wrong: in that case the Rajya Sabha seat falls vacant. Statement 2 is correct: the first House's seat falls vacant. Statement 3 is correct: both seats fall vacant. Hence 2 and 3 only; options with 1 are wrong and '3 only' misses statement 2.
30.tq: Elected to both Houses and silent for 10 days: lose the Rajya Sabha seat.

30.s: A person is simultaneously elected to Parliament and a State Legislature. Which one of the following is correct?
o: The Parliament seat must be resigned within 10 days, failing which the State seat falls vacant.
The State Legislature seat must be resigned within 14 days, failing which the Parliament seat falls vacant.
The person may retain both seats for the entire term.
Both seats become vacant immediately on election.
30.x: Under the Prohibition of Simultaneous Membership Rules, 1950, the State Legislature seat must be resigned within 14 days; otherwise the seat in Parliament becomes vacant.
30.tq: Use the direction of the consequence and the 14-day time limit to eliminate reversals.

30.s:
With reference to resignation and absence of Members of Parliament, consider the following statements:
1. A resignation must be made in writing to the Speaker or the Chairman, as the case may be.
2. The resignation may be rejected if the presiding officer is satisfied that it is not voluntary or genuine.
3. A House may declare a seat vacant when a member is absent without permission for 60 days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
30.x: All three statements are correct. Resignation is addressed to the Speaker or Chairman, may be rejected when it is not voluntary or genuine, and absence without permission for 60 days can lead the House to declare the seat vacant.
30.tq: Combine the written-resignation rule with the separate 60-day absence rule.

30.s: The provision that the Speaker or Chairman may refuse to accept a member's resignation if satisfied that it is not voluntary or genuine was introduced by the
30.x: The 33rd Amendment Act, 1974 amended Article 101(3)(b) so that a resignation takes effect only on acceptance, and the presiding officer may reject it if it is not voluntary or genuine. The 24th Amendment concerned Parliament's amending power, the 42nd was the 'mini-Constitution' of the Emergency, and the 52nd added the Tenth Schedule (anti-defection).
30.tq: 33rd Amendment (1974) = resignation must be voluntary and genuine; 52nd (1985) = anti-defection.

30.s: Which one of the following is the correct position regarding women’s representation in the 17th Lok Sabha?
o: 94 women members, constituting about 17 per cent
66 women members, constituting about 12 per cent
78 women members, constituting about 14.4 per cent
52 women members, constituting about 9 per cent
30.x: The 17th Lok Sabha, constituted after the 2019 elections, had 78 women members, approximately 14.4 per cent of the House, the highest number at that time.
30.tq: Use the paired figure and percentage to identify the correct Lok Sabha representation.

30.s: Which one of the following statements regarding women’s representation in Parliament is correct?
o: Women constitute less than 5 per cent in both Houses of Parliament.
Women constitute about 15 per cent in the Lok Sabha and about 14 per cent in the Rajya Sabha.
Women constitute more than one-third in both Houses of Parliament.
Women constitute about 14 per cent in the Lok Sabha and about 15 per cent in the Rajya Sabha.
30.x: Women’s representation is approximately 15 per cent in the Lok Sabha and 14 per cent in the Rajya Sabha. These figures are separate from the future constitutional reservation of one-third seats.
30.tq: Compare the two Houses carefully instead of transferring the percentage from one House to the other.

30.s: In which Lok Sabha did women members cross 10 per cent of the total membership for the first time?
30.x: Women members crossed 10 per cent of the total strength of the House for the first time in the 15th Lok Sabha, elected in 2009.
30.tq: Link the threshold event with the correct Lok Sabha number and election period.

30.s: The constitutional provision for reservation of one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies was introduced by the:
30.x: The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023, known as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, provides for reservation of one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
30.tq: Use the familiar amendment-number trap by matching the reservation provision with its exact year.

30.s: Under the constitutional scheme introduced by the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, reservation of one-third seats for women becomes operative:
o: Immediately from the date of Presidential assent
After the next Census followed by delimitation
Only after approval by all State Legislatures
After the next general election, irrespective of delimitation
30.x: The reservation is to become operative after a Census is conducted and the subsequent delimitation exercise is completed. It is not immediately applicable merely upon enactment of the Amendment.
30.tq: Apply the commencement condition instead of assuming that constitutional enactment means immediate operation.

30.s:
Consider the following statements about the reservation of seats for women under the 106th Constitutional Amendment:
1. It applies to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
2. It is provided under Article 334A.
3. It is initially intended to operate for fifteen years and may be extended.
4. It reserves one-half of the seats in the concerned legislatures.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
30.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The reservation is for one-third of the seats, not one-half, and Article 334A governs its operation.
30.tq: Find the changed proportion while retaining the correct Article, institutions and duration.

30.s: Which one of the following is correctly associated with the history of the Women’s Reservation Bill?
o: It was first introduced in 1989 and passed by the Rajya Sabha in 1995.
It was first introduced in 1996 and passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2010.
It was first introduced in 2005 and passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2015.
It was first introduced in 2010 and passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2023.
30.x: The first Women’s Reservation Bill was introduced in 1996 and was passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2010. The constitutional reservation was subsequently enacted through the 106th Amendment in 2023.
30.tq: Distinguish the earlier Bill’s milestones from the later Constitutional Amendment.

30.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: 15th Lok Sabha — 2009 — Women crossed 10 per cent for the first time
30.x: The 106th Constitutional Amendment providing one-third reservation for women was enacted in 2023, not 2010. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
30.tq: Check the year attached to the constitutional amendment against the years of the Lok Sabha milestones.

30.s: Which Lok Sabha had the lowest proportion of women Members among the listed Lok Sabhas?
30.x: The 6th Lok Sabha in 1977 had 19 women MPs, approximately 3.5 per cent, the lowest share among the listed Lok Sabhas.
30.tq: Compare percentages rather than the absolute number of women members alone.

30.s: Under Article 85(1) of the Constitution, each House of Parliament is summoned by the
30.x: Article 85(1) vests the power to summon each House in the President. The two Houses need not be summoned together.
30.tq: Apply the 'wrong authority' trap to distinguish constitutional offices.

30.s: Which one of the following is the normal pattern of parliamentary sessions in India?
o: Winter, Spring and Special sessions only
30.x: There is no fixed constitutional calendar, but Parliament normally has Budget, Monsoon and Winter sessions.
30.tq: Choose the established institutional terminology rather than an invented seasonal sequence.

30.s: Who orders an adjournment sine die of a House of Parliament?
o: The Speaker or Chairman of the concerned House
The Prime Minister after consulting the Cabinet
The President in respect of both Houses
30.x: An adjournment sine die is ordered by the Speaker in the Lok Sabha or the Chairman in the Rajya Sabha, without fixing a date for the next sitting.
30.tq: Use the office-and-function matching method for parliamentary terminology.

30.s: A sitting of a House is suspended for a specified number of hours or days. This parliamentary action is called
30.x: Adjournment suspends a sitting for a specified period. It does not end the session or the life of the Lok Sabha.
30.tq: Apply the definition to a short procedural scenario.

30.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes prorogation from dissolution?
o: Prorogation ends a session, whereas dissolution ends the life of the Lok Sabha only.
Prorogation ends the life of both Houses, whereas dissolution ends only a session.
Dissolution is ordered by the Speaker, whereas prorogation is ordered by the Chairman.
Both prorogation and dissolution end the life of the Rajya Sabha.
30.x: Prorogation ends a session, while dissolution ends the life of the Lok Sabha. The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House and is never dissolved.
30.tq: Compare the effect and authority of two easily confusable parliamentary actions.

30.s:
Arrange the following events in the correct procedural sequence after the conclusion of the business of a sitting:
A. Prorogation by the President
B. Adjournment sine die by the Speaker or Chairman
C. Reassembly in a new session
D. Recess

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
30.x: Normally, the Speaker or Chairman first adjourns the House sine die; the President then prorogues it, followed by a recess and later reassembly in a new session.
30.tq: Use the first-and-last method and distinguish a sitting, session and recess.

30.s: Why is the constitutional requirement that two sessions of Parliament should not have a gap of more than six months significant?
o: It ensures continuing legislative activity and accountability of the government
It makes a fixed number of sitting days compulsory each year
It prescribes a minimum of six months of parliamentary sitting every year
It permits the Rajya Sabha to dissolve the Lok Sabha after six months
30.x: The six-month limit prevents an excessively long interruption and helps maintain legislative business and executive accountability. It does not prescribe a minimum number of sitting days.
30.tq: Distinguish a maximum interval between sessions from a minimum number of sitting days.

30.s: The quorum to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament is:
30.x: Article 100 provides that the quorum for a meeting of either House is one-tenth of its total membership.
30.tq: Recall the fraction attached specifically to quorum and reject nearby fractions.

30.s: Rules of procedure and conduct of business in Parliament are dealt with under:
30.x: Article 118 empowers each House to make rules for regulating its procedure and conduct of business.
30.tq: Link the procedural subject directly to Article 118 and distinguish it from quorum and language provisions.

30.s:
With reference to the language used in Parliament, consider the following statements:
1. The business of Parliament may be transacted in Hindi or English.
2. A member may address the House in his or her mother tongue with the permission of the presiding officer.
3. The Constitution permits parliamentary proceedings only in English.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
30.x: Article 120 recognises Hindi and English for parliamentary business and permits the use of a member's mother tongue with the presiding officer's permission. Proceedings are not restricted exclusively to English.
30.tq: Identify the correct language alternatives and reject the exclusive-language trap.

30.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the administrative control over the secretariats of Parliament?
o: The Lok Sabha Secretariat functions under the Speaker and the Rajya Sabha Secretariat under the Chairman
The Lok Sabha Secretariat functions under the President and the Rajya Sabha Secretariat under the Prime Minister
Both Secretariats function directly under the Union Cabinet
Both Secretariats function under the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs
30.x: The parliamentary Secretariats are independent of the executive. The Lok Sabha Secretariat is under the Speaker, while the Rajya Sabha Secretariat is under the Chairman.
30.tq: Use the House-wise authority comparison to avoid the wrong-ministry and wrong-authority traps.

30.s:
Consider the following statements about the legislative function of Parliament:
1. Parliament makes laws on the Union List and the Concurrent List.
2. An existing law made by Parliament can be changed by a State Legislature.
3. Delegated legislation is subject to review by Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
30.x: Statement 1 is correct: Parliament legislates on the Union and Concurrent Lists (and the State List in special cases). Statement 2 is wrong: only Parliament can change an existing law it made (APPSC-GS 2024). Statement 3 is correct: Parliament reviews delegated legislation. Hence 1 and 3 only.
30.tq: Only the body that made the law can change it.

30.s:
Consider the following statements about the functions of Parliament:
1. Questions and motions are means of parliamentary control over the executive.
2. A no-confidence motion can be moved in either House.
3. No tax can be imposed without the approval of the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
30.x: Statement 1 is correct: questions and motions are tools of executive control. Statement 2 is wrong: a no-confidence motion lies only in the Lok Sabha. Statement 3 is correct: no tax without Lok Sabha approval. Hence 1 and 3 only.
30.tq: No-confidence motion = Lok Sabha only.

30.s:
Which of the following functions belongs to the judicial functions of Parliament?
1. Impeachment of the President
2. Removal of the Vice-President
3. Recommending removal of certain constitutional authorities and judges
4. Punishing breach of privilege
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
30.x: The listed functions are included among the judicial or quasi-judicial functions of Parliament, though their procedures differ according to the office concerned.
30.tq: Treat the list as a classification question and check whether each item is a parliamentary adjudicatory function.

30.s: Which one of the following is NOT an electoral function of Parliament?
o: Participating in the election of the President
Electing the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha
30.x: A is the answer: Parliament's electoral functions are electing the Vice-President, taking part in the President's election and electing its presiding officers (the Lok Sabha elects the Speaker and Deputy Speaker). The Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by the President, not elected by Parliament, so A is not an electoral function.
30.tq: Find the item that is an appointment function rather than an electoral function of Parliament.

30.s:
Which of the following correctly distinguishes the parliamentary electoral colleges for the Vice-President and the President?
1. All members of both Houses elect the Vice-President.
2. Only elected members of both Houses participate in the election of the President.
3. Nominated members of Parliament participate in the election of the President.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
30.x: The Vice-President is elected by all members of both Houses, including nominated members. The President is elected by elected members of both Houses and elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies; nominated members do not participate.
30.tq: Split the two electoral colleges and detect the nominated-member reversal.

30.s:
Which of the following enactments are associated with Parliament's power to make election laws?
1. Representation of the People Act, 1950
2. Representation of the People Act, 1951
3. Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952
4. Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
30.x: The Representation of the People Acts of 1950 and 1951 and the Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952 relate to election law. The Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 concerns inquiry into judges, not election law.
30.tq: Classify statutes by subject and remove the law belonging to the removal procedure.

30.s:
With regard to freedom of speech in Parliament, consider the following statements:
1. Article 105 protects freedom of speech in Parliament.
2. No court proceedings can be instituted against a member for anything said or any vote given in the House or its committees.
3. This immunity applies to every statement made by a member outside Parliament.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
30.x: Article 105 protects speech and votes in Parliament and its committees. It does not provide the same parliamentary immunity for statements made outside Parliament.
30.tq: Reject the overbroad extension of a privilege beyond its constitutional setting.

30.s: A Member of Parliament enjoys freedom from arrest in civil cases during which period?
o: Forty days before and after a session and during the session
Only on the day of voting in the House
The entire term of the Parliament, without exception
Only during the recess between two sessions
30.x: The privilege covers civil arrest during the session and for forty days before and forty days after the session. It does not cover criminal or preventive detention.
30.tq: Test the exact time period and the civil-case limitation together.

30.s: Which one of the following is NOT an individual parliamentary privilege of a member?
o: Freedom from arrest in civil cases during the prescribed period
Freedom of speech in the House
Power to prohibit publication of the House's proceedings
30.x: The power to publish or prohibit publication of the House's reports and proceedings is a collective privilege of the House, not an individual privilege.
30.tq: Find the option that belongs to the opposite classification.

30.s: Under Article 122 of the Constitution, courts cannot inquire into parliamentary proceedings on the ground of
o: The absence of a parliamentary session
30.x: Article 122 bars courts from questioning parliamentary proceedings on the ground of alleged procedural irregularity.
30.tq: Match the constitutional Article with its precise limitation on judicial inquiry.

30.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the present position regarding codification of parliamentary privileges in India?
o: All privileges have been exhaustively codified in a single statute.
Privileges are derived exclusively from judicial decisions.
Only individual privileges are codified under Article 122.
Parliamentary privileges are not codified, but continue under Article 105(3).
30.x: Parliamentary privileges have not been comprehensively codified. They continue under Article 105(3), with their historical basis in the privileges of the British House of Commons.
30.tq: Distinguish an uncodified constitutional position from a supposedly exhaustive statute.

30.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Sita Soren case of 2024:
1. A seven-judge Bench held that parliamentary privilege does not protect a legislator who takes a bribe to vote or speak.
2. The decision overruled the protection recognised in P.V. Narasimha Rao (1998) in this context.
3. The decision held that every speech made by a legislator outside the House is protected by Article 105.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
30.x: The seven-judge Bench in Sita Soren (2024) held that privilege does not protect bribery for voting or speaking and overruled the contrary position in P.V. Narasimha Rao. Statement 3 is false.
30.tq: Use a recent judicial decision while rejecting an overbroad claim about immunity.

30.s: Which one of the following statements about parliamentary privileges is NOT correct?
o: A member may claim exemption from jury service.
The House may exclude strangers and hold secret sittings.
Members are protected from arrest in all criminal and preventive detention cases during a session.
Both collective and individual privileges exist.
30.x: Freedom from arrest applies to civil cases during the prescribed period; it does not extend to criminal or preventive detention cases. The other statements are correct.
30.tq: Look for the overbroad phrase that extends a limited privilege to all cases.

30.s:
Consider the following statements regarding collective privileges of a House:
1. It may exclude strangers and hold secret sittings.
2. It may make its own rules.
3. It may punish members and outsiders for contempt.
4. It must obtain permission from the Governor before publishing its debates.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
30.x: The House may exclude strangers, hold secret sittings, make its own rules and punish for contempt. Permission from the Governor is not required for publishing its debates.
30.tq: Identify the inserted false authority requirement among the established collective privileges of the House.

30.s:
Consider the following statements about parliamentary privileges:
1. No arrest or legal process can take place within the precincts of a House without the Presiding Officer's permission.
2. The right to be informed of a member's arrest, detention or release is an individual privilege of that member.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
30.x: Statement 1 is correct: legal process within the precincts needs the Presiding Officer's permission. Statement 2 is wrong: being informed of a member's arrest, detention or release is a collective privilege of the House. Hence 1 only.
30.tq: Anything the House as a body receives or controls (information, publication, secret sittings, punishment) is collective.

30.s:
Consider the following statements about parliamentary privileges:
1. They are co-terminous with membership of the legislature.
2. They also extend to ministers, the Attorney-General and others who speak in the House.
3. Only individual members enjoy privileges; the House as a whole has none.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
30.x: Statement 1 is correct: privileges last as long as membership. Statement 2 is correct: they extend to ministers, the Attorney-General and others who speak in the House. Statement 3 is wrong (the APPSC-G2 2017 trap): the House has collective privileges as well. Hence 1 and 2 only.
30.tq: Both collective and individual privileges exist; 'only members, not the House' is always false.

30.s: Which one of the following matters is within the equal powers of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha?
o: Initiation of a no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers
Consideration of the report of the Comptroller and Auditor-General
30.x: Both Houses have equal powers in considering the reports of the CAG, UPSC and Finance Commission. The other matters are associated with the superiority of the Lok Sabha.
30.tq: Distinguish an equal parliamentary function from a power exclusively associated with the Lok Sabha.

30.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Demands for grants — Rajya Sabha may vote on them
Money Bill — Rajya Sabha to return it within fourteen days
Joint sitting — Presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
30.x: The Rajya Sabha may discuss the Budget but cannot vote on demands for grants. A Money Bill is returned within fourteen days, a joint sitting is presided over by the Lok Sabha Speaker, and a no-confidence motion is moved in the Lok Sabha.
30.tq: Find the option that reverses the financial or accountability superiority of the Lok Sabha.

30.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Rajya Sabha has equal powers with the Lok Sabha in the election and impeachment of the President.
2. The Rajya Sabha has equal powers with the Lok Sabha in the election of the Vice-President.
3. A resolution for initiating the removal of the Vice-President can be introduced in either House.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
30.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Under Article 67(b), a resolution for initiating the removal of the Vice-President can be moved only in the Rajya Sabha, though the Lok Sabha must agree to it.
30.tq: Test the distinction between equal participation in election and the special initiation power of the Rajya Sabha.

30.s:
Which of the following matters can be dealt with by both Houses of Parliament on an equal footing?
1. Removal of a Judge of the Supreme Court or High Court
2. Approval of an Ordinance promulgated by the President
3. Approval of proclamations of Emergency
4. Passing a resolution to discontinue a National Emergency
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
30.x: The Houses have equal powers in the removal of higher judicial officers, approval of Ordinances and approval of Emergency proclamations. Only the Lok Sabha can pass a resolution to discontinue a National Emergency.
30.tq: Identify the single Lok Sabha-only power among otherwise equal constitutional functions.

30.s: With reference to a Financial Bill of category I, which one of the following is correct?
o: It can be introduced only in the Rajya Sabha and passed by a simple majority there.
It can be introduced in either House, but the Rajya Sabha has no power to amend it.
It can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, but both Houses have equal powers regarding its passage.
It can be introduced only after certification by the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
30.x: A Financial Bill of category I can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha. Unlike a Money Bill, both Houses have equal powers in its passage.
30.tq: Discriminate between a Financial Bill of category I and a Money Bill by comparing introduction and passage.

30.s: If the two Houses of Parliament disagree on a constitutional amendment bill, which one of the following is the consequence?
o: The bill fails because no joint sitting is permitted for such a bill.
The Lok Sabha may pass the bill by a simple majority in a second sitting.
The Supreme Court decides which version of the bill shall prevail.
The President convenes a joint sitting under Article 108.
30.x: There is no provision for a joint sitting in respect of a constitutional amendment bill. Failure to secure the required approval in either House causes the bill to fall.
30.tq: Ask whether the ordinary deadlock mechanism applies; Article 108 does not apply here.

30.s: Which one of the following statements regarding a National Emergency is correct when the Lok Sabha is dissolved?
o: It automatically lapses immediately upon dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
Approval by the Rajya Sabha alone can sustain it permanently.
If approved by the Rajya Sabha, the newly constituted Lok Sabha must approve it within thirty days of its first sitting.
It can continue only after approval by all State Legislatures.
30.x: When the Lok Sabha is dissolved, the Rajya Sabha may approve the Emergency proclamation for the time being. The new Lok Sabha must approve it within thirty days of its first sitting.
30.tq: Apply the special continuity rule for an Emergency during dissolution of the Lok Sabha.

30.s: Which Article empowers the Rajya Sabha to authorise the creation of one or more new All-India Services common to the Union and the States?
30.x: Article 312 enables Parliament to create new All-India Services on the basis of a Rajya Sabha resolution passed by the required two-thirds majority of members present and voting.
30.tq: Match the special Rajya Sabha power with its exact Constitutional Article.

30.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 3:
1. A Bill for formation of a new State or alteration of the area, boundaries or name of an existing State requires the recommendation of the President.
2. The views of the concerned State Legislature are binding on Parliament.
3. Article 3 deals with the formation and alteration of States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
30.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The concerned State Legislature is asked for its views, but those views are not binding on Parliament.
30.tq: Detect the subtle reversal between seeking a State Legislature’s views and being bound by them.

30.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 249, the Rajya Sabha authorises Parliament, and not State Legislatures, to legislate on a State List subject.
2. Under Article 312, the Rajya Sabha can authorise the creation of new All-India Services.
3. Under Article 67(b), the removal of the Vice-President can be initiated only in the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
30.x: All three statements are correct. Articles 249, 312 and 67(b) respectively deal with State List legislation in the national interest, creation of All-India Services and initiation of the Vice-President’s removal.
30.tq: Use article-wise pairing to distinguish the three special powers of the Rajya Sabha.

30.s:
With reference to a Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249, consider the following statements:
1. It must be supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.
2. It remains in force for one year and may be extended one year at a time.
3. It authorises the State Legislatures to make laws on a Union List subject.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
30.x: Statement 1 is correct: the resolution needs two-thirds of members present and voting. Statement 2 is correct: it is valid for one year and can be renewed one year at a time. Statement 3 is wrong: Article 249 lets Parliament legislate on a State List subject in the national interest; it does not authorise State Legislatures. Hence 1 and 2 only.
30.tq: Art. 249: RS (2/3 present and voting) lets PARLIAMENT enter the State List for 1 year at a time.

30.s:
Consider the following statements about the proposal to enlarge the Lok Sabha by about 50% once the 1971 freeze lifts:
1. Its strength would rise to about 815.
2. The Lok Sabha-Rajya Sabha ratio would fall from 3.3:1 to 2.2:1.
3. The 15% ministerial ceiling would rise from 81 to 122 (another source says 133).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
30.x: Statement 1 is correct: about 815 members. Statement 2 is wrong: the ratio would rise from 2.2:1 to 3.3:1, not fall. Statement 3 is correct: the ministerial cap would rise from 81 to 122 (or 133 per another source). Hence 1 and 3 only.
30.tq: A bigger Lok Sabha raises the LS:RS ratio (2.2 -> 3.3) and dilutes the Rajya Sabha.

30.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the proposed expansion of the Lok Sabha:
1. Southern States have expressed apprehension that their relative share would decline.
2. Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan are expected to gain relatively from such an expansion.
3. The debate is linked to the lifting of the freeze based on the 1971 Census.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
30.x: All three statements are correct. The proposed expansion has generated concern in southern States because the relative representation of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan may increase after the 1971-based freeze is lifted.
30.tq: Test the regional comparison and the constitutional background together.

30.s: The Law Commission's 170th Report, submitted in 1999, proposed which of the following alternatives in the context of parliamentary representation?
o: A 50 per cent reduction in Rajya Sabha seats
A 25 per cent increase in seats through a party-list system
Direct election of the President by the people
Abolition of reserved seats in the Lok Sabha
30.x: The Law Commission's 170th Report of 1999 proposed increasing representation by 25 per cent through a party-list system.
30.tq: Link the institutional proposal with the report number and year.

30.s:
Consider the following statements about the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026:
1. It was introduced along with the Delimitation Bill, 2026.
2. It sought to raise the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850.
3. The proposed 850 seats comprised 815 for the States and 35 for the Union Territories.
4. It was passed by the Lok Sabha with the required special majority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
30.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha and therefore did not secure the required special majority.
30.tq: Identify the single false statement by checking the legislative outcome.

30.s: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, was defeated because it failed to secure the special majority required under
30.x: A constitutional amendment Bill must satisfy the special-majority requirement under Article 368; the 2026 Bill fell short of it.
30.tq: Use the article-number association for constitutional amendment procedure.

30.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the resolution adopted by the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly in the debate on Lok Sabha delimitation?
o: It proposed equal representation for every State in both Houses.
It supported increasing the Lok Sabha to 850 seats and a 3.3:1 ratio.
It sought to freeze the Lok Sabha at 543 seats and retain the 2.2:1 Lok Sabha–Rajya Sabha ratio.
It sought to reduce the Lok Sabha to 525 seats and abolish the Rajya Sabha.
30.x: The Tamil Nadu Assembly resolved to retain the Lok Sabha at 543 seats and preserve the approximate 2.2:1 Lok Sabha–Rajya Sabha ratio.
30.tq: Use the precise figures to distinguish the State Assembly's position from the expansion proposal.

30.s: Which one of the following Bills was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee during the 2026 Monsoon Session?
30.x: The FCRA (Amendment) Bill, 2026 was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee during the session.
30.tq: Identify the Bill by linking it with the parliamentary committee action.

30.s: On 11 March 2026, the Lok Sabha rejected by voice vote a resolution seeking removal of the Speaker under
30.x: The resolution seeking removal of Speaker Om Birla was moved under Article 94(c) and was rejected by voice vote on 11 March 2026.
30.tq: Apply the article-number trap by distinguishing the Speaker's removal provision from neighbouring parliamentary provisions.

30.s:
Which of the following proposals has been discussed in relation to limiting the use of party whips in Parliament?
1. Party whips should be limited to confidence votes.
2. Party whips should be limited to money bills.
3. Party whips should be abolished in all legislative business.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
30.x: The proposals discussed were to limit party whips to confidence votes and money bills. A general abolition of whips in all legislative business was not stated.
30.tq: Reject the extreme extension of a limited reform proposal.

30.s: The Andhra State Act of 1953 and the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act of 2014 were enacted under which Article of the Constitution?
30.x: Both the creation of Andhra State in 1953 and the reorganisation of Andhra Pradesh in 2014 were carried out under Article 3, which concerns the formation and alteration of States.
30.tq: Use the common constitutional provision rather than the different years of enactment.

31.s: Which Article provides for the election of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
31.x: Article 93 provides that the House of the People shall choose two members to be Speaker and Deputy Speaker.
31.tq: Match the constitutional article with the office it creates.

31.s: The salary and allowances of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha are charged on the:
31.x: The salaries and allowances of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India under Article 97.
31.tq: Use the constitutional funding source rather than a general parliamentary budget description.

31.s:
Consider the following statements about the Speaker of the Lok Sabha under Article 94:
1. The Speaker vacates office on ceasing to be a member of the Lok Sabha.
2. The Speaker resigns by writing to the President.
3. The Speaker can be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members, after 14 days' notice.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
31.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Speaker resigns to the Deputy Speaker. Statement 3 is correct: removal needs an effective majority and 14 days' notice. Hence 1 and 3 only.
31.tq: Speaker resigns to the Deputy Speaker and vice versa; Deputy Chairman resigns to the Chairman.

31.s: While a resolution for the removal of the Speaker is under consideration, which one of the following is correct?
o: The Speaker cannot speak or vote under any circumstance
The Speaker’s membership of the House automatically terminates
The Speaker cannot preside, but may speak and take part in the proceedings and vote in the first instance, not in the event of a tie
The Speaker may preside but cannot vote
31.x: Article 96 prevents the Speaker from presiding while the removal resolution is under consideration. The Speaker may speak, participate and vote in the first instance, but cannot exercise a casting vote in case of a tie.
31.tq: Separate the restriction on presiding from the retained rights to participate and vote.

31.s: Which of the following pairs of removal motions against Lok Sabha Speakers is correctly matched?
31.x: Removal motions against G. V. Mavalankar in 1954, Hukum Singh in 1966 and Balram Jakhar in 1987 failed. The motion concerning Om Birla was listed for debate in 2026, not 1987.
31.tq: Pair each office-holder with the correct year and reject swapped dates.

31.s:
Consider the following statements about the Speaker when the Lok Sabha is dissolved:
1. The Speaker continues in office until immediately before the first meeting of the new Lok Sabha.
2. The outgoing Speaker presides over the new House as Speaker Pro Tem and conducts the election of the new Speaker.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
31.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Speaker does not vacate office on dissolution. Statement 2 is wrong: the Speaker Pro Tem is the senior-most member, sworn in by the President, not the outgoing Speaker. Hence 1 only.
31.tq: Speaker Pro Tem = senior-most member, sworn in by the President.

31.s: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha exercises a casting vote:
o: Whenever the Council of Ministers advises the Speaker to do so
On every bill passed by the House
Only during a joint sitting of Parliament
Only when there is an equality of votes
31.x: Under Article 100(1), the Speaker normally does not vote in the first instance but has a casting vote when the votes are equally divided.
31.tq: Distinguish the ordinary vote from the casting vote used only to break a tie.

31.s: Who has the final authority to decide whether a bill is a Money Bill?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
31.x: Article 110(3) gives the Speaker of the Lok Sabha the final authority to decide whether a bill is a Money Bill.
31.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ test to identify the constitutionally designated authority.

31.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the powers of the Speaker:
1. The Speaker decides cases under the Tenth Schedule, subject to judicial review.
2. The Speaker recognises the Leader of the Opposition subject to the applicable requirement regarding the strength of the party.
3. The Speaker appoints chairmen of parliamentary committees.
4. Rulings of the Speaker are protected by Article 122.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
31.x: All four statements are correct. The Speaker’s decisions under the Tenth Schedule remain subject to judicial review, and the Speaker also performs the listed recognition, committee and ruling-related functions.
31.tq: Use a multi-function statement set and verify each power independently.

31.s: The party seeking recognition of the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha is required, according to the Speaker’s direction, to have at least:
31.x: Recognition of the Leader of the Opposition requires the party to have at least one-tenth of the strength of the House, according to the Speaker’s direction. The office has statutory status since the 1977 Act.
31.tq: Distinguish the one-tenth threshold from other parliamentary fractions.

31.s: A joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament under Article 108 is presided over by the
o: senior-most member of the Rajya Sabha
31.x: Under Article 118(4), the Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting (the Deputy Speaker in his absence). The President summons the joint sitting but does not preside. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (the Vice-President) does not preside over it, and there is no role for the senior-most Rajya Sabha member.
31.tq: President summons a joint sitting; the Speaker presides (Art. 118(4)).

31.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. The Deputy Speaker is elected by the Lok Sabha after the election of the Speaker.
2. The Deputy Speaker resigns by addressing the resignation to the Speaker.
3. The Deputy Speaker presides over a joint sitting when the Speaker is absent.
4. The Deputy Speaker is subordinate to the Speaker in exercising the office’s constitutional functions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
31.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Deputy Speaker is not subordinate to the Speaker while exercising the office’s functions, so statement 4 is false.
31.tq: Spot the reversed institutional relationship in the final statement.

31.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Panel of Chairpersons of the Lok Sabha is correct?
o: It is nominated by the Deputy Speaker and can preside even when the Speaker’s office is vacant
It is nominated by the President and may contain up to twenty members
It is nominated by the Speaker and may contain up to ten members
It is elected by the Rajya Sabha and contains exactly ten members
31.x: The Speaker nominates a Panel of Chairpersons consisting of up to ten members. A panel member may preside in the absence of both the Speaker and Deputy Speaker, but not when the Speaker’s office is vacant.
31.tq: Check both the nominating authority and the numerical ceiling.

31.s: A member of the Panel of Chairpersons may preside over the Lok Sabha when:
o: The President directs the panel member to preside over a joint sitting
The Speaker’s office is vacant, irrespective of the presence of the Deputy Speaker
The Lok Sabha has been dissolved and no new Speaker has been elected
Both the Speaker and Deputy Speaker are absent, but the Speaker’s office is not vacant
31.x: A panel member may preside in the absence of both the Speaker and Deputy Speaker. The panel member cannot preside when the office of Speaker is vacant.
31.tq: Read the condition cumulatively: absence of both officers is different from vacancy of the office.

31.s: Which of the following statements regarding vacancies of Deputy Speaker offices is correct?
o: The Lok Sabha Deputy Speaker post was filled in June 2019, while the office was vacant in eight State Assemblies in 2025.
The Lok Sabha Deputy Speaker post has been vacant since 2014, and the office was vacant in ten State Assemblies.
The Lok Sabha Deputy Speaker post has been vacant since June 2019, and the office was vacant in eight State Assemblies in 2026.
The Lok Sabha Deputy Speaker post has been vacant since June 2021, and the office was vacant in six State Assemblies.
31.x: The Lok Sabha Deputy Speaker post has been vacant since June 2019. The office was reported vacant in eight State Assemblies, with Jharkhand’s vacancy lasting 21 years.
31.tq: Match the vacancy count and starting date without swapping the two time references.

31.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the conventional relationship between the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Opposition?
o: The Deputy Speaker is appointed by the President on the advice of the Opposition
The Deputy Speaker can belong only to a party represented in the Rajya Sabha
The Deputy Speaker is conventionally chosen from the Opposition, though this is not a constitutional requirement
The Deputy Speaker must always be nominated by the ruling party
31.x: The Deputy Speaker is conventionally chosen from the Opposition. This is a parliamentary convention and not an express constitutional requirement.
31.tq: Distinguish a political convention from a mandatory constitutional qualification.

31.s:
Consider the following statements about the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha:
1. The Deputy Chairman is elected by the Rajya Sabha from among its members.
2. The Deputy Chairman resigns by writing to the President.
3. The Deputy Chairman can be removed by an effective majority after 14 days' notice.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
31.x: Statement 1 is correct (Art. 89(2)). Statement 2 is wrong: the Deputy Chairman resigns to the Chairman. Statement 3 is correct: removal needs an effective majority with 14 days' notice. Hence 1 and 3 only.
31.tq: Deputy Chairman resigns to the Chairman.

31.s: Who was the first Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
31.x: S. Radhakrishnan was the first Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and held the office from 1952 to 1962.
31.tq: Separate the first office-holder from the present office-holders and deputy office-holders.

31.s: In the vacancy of the office of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, the power of the Deputy Chairman to decide on a judge-removal motion under Article 91 was upheld by the Supreme Court in January 2026 in the:
31.x: In January 2026, the Supreme Court upheld, in the Justice Varma case, the Deputy Chairman’s power under Article 91 to decide on a judge-removal motion when the Chairman’s office was vacant.
31.tq: Match the recent judicial ruling with the precise constitutional power and case name.

31.s:
Consider the following statements about the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha:
1. The Vice-President is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
2. While a resolution for his removal is under consideration, he cannot preside but may speak, and he cannot vote.
3. When the Vice-President acts as President, the Deputy Chairman performs the duties of the Chairman.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
31.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Vice-President is ex officio Chairman (Arts. 64 and 89). Statement 2 is correct: unlike the Speaker, who can vote in the first instance during his removal proceedings, the Chairman cannot vote at all while his removal is pending, though he may speak. Statement 3 is correct: under Article 91 the Deputy Chairman presides when the Chairman's office is vacant or the Vice-President is acting as President. Hence all three.
31.tq: Speaker under removal: can vote (first instance). Chairman under removal: cannot vote at all.

31.s: As per the position in 2026, which one of the following is correct regarding the presiding officers of the Rajya Sabha?
o: Harivansh is the Chairman and C.P. Radhakrishnan the Deputy Chairman
C.P. Radhakrishnan is the Chairman, and Harivansh's term as Deputy Chairman ended on 9 April 2026
S. Radhakrishnan is the Chairman and Harivansh the Deputy Chairman
C.P. Radhakrishnan is the Deputy Chairman, and the office of Chairman is vacant
31.x: C.P. Radhakrishnan, as Vice-President, is the present ex officio Chairman, and Harivansh's term as Deputy Chairman ended on 9 April 2026. Harivansh was never Chairman, S. Radhakrishnan was the first Chairman (1952-62), and the Chairman's office is not described as vacant.
31.tq: First Chairman: S. Radhakrishnan; present Chairman: C.P. Radhakrishnan.

31.s: With reference to Article 98 of the Constitution, which one of the following is correct?
o: The President appoints all secretarial staff directly and Parliament has no power to regulate recruitment by law.
The Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha must have identical secretarial establishments without any common posts.
Each House has separate secretarial staff, although posts common to both Houses may be created.
The executive government alone regulates recruitment to the secretariats of both Houses in all circumstances.
31.x: Article 98 establishes separate secretarial staff for each House while permitting the creation of posts common to both Houses.
31.tq: Use the constitutional general rule and its permitted exception to eliminate statements using exclusive powers.

31.s: Until Parliament makes a law regulating recruitment and conditions of service of the secretarial staff of the Houses, rules may be made by the President after consultation with the:
o: Chief Justice of India and Attorney-General of India
Secretary-General of the Lok Sabha and Secretary-General of the Rajya Sabha
Prime Minister and Union Home Minister
Speaker of the Lok Sabha and Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
31.x: In the absence of a law by Parliament, the President may make rules after consulting the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
31.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish the constitutional consultees from parliamentary officials and ministers.

31.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Secretary-General of a House of Parliament is correct?
1. Each House has a Secretary-General as its head of secretarial staff.
2. The Secretary-General is appointed by the presiding officer of the concerned House.
3. The office holds rank equal to that of the Cabinet Secretary.
4. The secretariat is independent of the executive.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
31.x: The secretariat of each House is headed by its Secretary-General, appointed by the concerned presiding officer. The Secretary-General has the rank of Cabinet Secretary, and the parliamentary secretariat is independent of the executive.
31.tq: Test office, appointing authority, rank and institutional independence as separate elements of one constitutional arrangement.

31.s:
Consider the following statements about the sessions of Parliament:
1. The President summons each House.
2. The six-month interval is counted from the last sitting of one session to the first sitting of the next.
3. The Constitution expressly names the Budget, Monsoon and Winter Sessions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
31.x: The President summons each House, and the six-month rule is calculated from the last sitting to the first sitting. Budget, Monsoon and Winter Sessions are conventional names, not sessions expressly named in the Constitution.
31.tq: Separate constitutional requirements from parliamentary conventions.

31.s: The period between prorogation of Parliament and the commencement of its next session is known as:
31.x: The period from prorogation to the next session is called a recess. It is different from adjournment, which interrupts a sitting within a session.
31.tq: Discriminate between a break within a session and the interval between two sessions.

31.s: A quorum in either House of Parliament is ordinarily:
o: One-half of the total membership, including the presiding officer
One-tenth of the total membership, including the presiding officer
One-fourth of the elected membership, excluding nominated members
One-twentieth of the total membership, excluding the presiding officer
31.x: Under Article 100(3), the quorum is one-tenth of the total number of members of the House, including the presiding officer.
31.tq: Check both the fraction and whether the presiding officer is included.

31.s:
Under Article 86 of the Constitution of India, the President may
1. Address either House of Parliament separately or both Houses together.
2. Require the attendance of members for the purpose of the address.
3. Send messages to either House with respect to a pending Bill.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
31.x: Article 86 empowers the President to address either House or both Houses together, require members' attendance and send messages to either House regarding pending Bills.
31.tq: Test the exact scope of Article 86 by separating the President’s powers of addressing, requiring attendance and sending messages.

31.s:
The special address delivered by the President under Article 87 is made at which of the following occasions?
1. The first session after each general election to the Lok Sabha.
2. The first session of Parliament in each year.
3. Every session immediately after prorogation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
31.x: Article 87 provides for the President’s special address at the first session after each general election and at the first session of each year. It is not required after every prorogation.
31.tq: Identify the two constitutionally specified occasions and reject the overbroad time-based statement.

31.s: The address of the President outlining the policies of the Government is debated in Parliament through a:
31.x: The President’s address outlining Government policy is debated through a Motion of Thanks in Parliament.
31.tq: Match the constitutional address with the parliamentary motion that follows it.

31.s:
Consider the following statements about the summoning of Parliament:
1. The President may summon the two Houses separately.
2. The Constitution requires both Houses to be summoned together on every occasion.
3. Each House must meet within six months of its previous sitting.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
31.x: The President need not summon both Houses together, and the maximum interval between sessions is six months. Statement 2 is false.
31.tq: Identify the statement that reverses the constitutional rule on separate summoning.

31.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the usual parliamentary sessions and their periods?
o: Budget—April to July; Monsoon—September to November; Winter—January to February
Budget—February to May; Monsoon—July to August/September; Winter—November to December
Budget—January to March; Monsoon—May to June; Winter—September to October
Budget—March to June; Monsoon—August to October; Winter—December to January
31.x: The usual sessions are the Budget Session from February to May, the Monsoon Session from July to August/September, and the Winter Session from November to December.
31.tq: Match each session with its conventional time period.

31.s: Which one of the following correctly describes adjournment sine die?
o: Termination of the life of the House without fixing a date for reassembly
Suspension of a sitting by the President until the next session
Termination of a session by the Governor without affecting pending notices
Termination of a sitting by the presiding officer without fixing a date for the next sitting
31.x: Adjournment sine die terminates a sitting without fixing a date for the next sitting. It does not terminate the House or the session, and pending bills remain alive.
31.tq: Separate the presiding officer’s power over a sitting from the President’s power over a session.

31.s:
Consider the following statements regarding prorogation:
1. It is ordered by the President in respect of Parliament.
2. It terminates a session.
3. Bills pending before Parliament lapse on prorogation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
31.x: The President prorogues Parliament and prorogation terminates the session. Bills do not lapse on prorogation, although pending notices generally lapse except notices to introduce bills.
31.tq: Test the effect of prorogation separately from the effect of dissolution.

31.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Adjournment sine die — causes bills to lapse
Adjournment — terminates the life of the House
Prorogation — terminates a sitting for a few hours
Dissolution — terminates the life of the Lok Sabha
31.x: Dissolution terminates the life of the Lok Sabha. Adjournment and adjournment sine die affect sittings, while prorogation terminates a session; none of these causes bills to lapse merely by adjournment or prorogation.
31.tq: Use the ‘ends’ column to reject reversed effects.

31.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The office of Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha has remained vacant throughout the 17th Lok Sabha.
2. The office of Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha has remained vacant through the 18th Lok Sabha.
3. The Deputy Speaker’s post has remained continuously occupied in both these Lok Sabhas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
31.x: The Deputy Speaker’s post remained vacant through both the 17th and 18th Lok Sabhas. Therefore, statement 3 is false.
31.tq: Use a present-affairs comparison across two successive Lok Sabhas and reject the directly reversed statement.

31.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Office-holder)
 a. Speaker of the first Andhra Pradesh Assembly
 b. Deputy Speaker of the first Andhra Pradesh Assembly
 c. Chairman of the first Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council

List-II (Person)
 i. Madapati Hanumantha Rao
 ii. Kalluri Subbarao
 iii. Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao

Codes:
 a  b  c
1. iii  ii  i
2. ii   iii i
3. iii  i   ii
4. i    ii  iii
31.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was the Speaker, Kalluri Subbarao was the Deputy Speaker, and Madapati Hanumantha Rao was the first Council Chairman in the first Andhra Pradesh Assembly of 1956.
31.tq: Start from the sure office-holder pair and complete the matching after distinguishing the Assembly offices from the Council office.

31.s: During the Monsoon Session of 2026, the Lok Sabha recorded how many oral answers, according to the cited assessment of legislative scrutiny?
31.x: Only two oral answers were recorded in the Lok Sabha during the Monsoon Session of 2026, a point cited in criticism concerning low scrutiny.
31.tq: Test a precise session-wise figure rather than relying on a general impression about parliamentary scrutiny.

32.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the recognised tools of parliamentary control over the executive?
o: Judicial review by the Supreme Court
32.x: Judicial review is a constitutional function of the judiciary, not a parliamentary device listed among the tools of legislative control over the executive.
32.tq: Separate parliamentary control devices from mechanisms belonging to another constitutional organ.

32.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the devices used by Parliament and State Legislatures for controlling the executive?
o: State Legislatures cannot use Question Hour or motions
Parliament alone uses these devices; State Legislatures use only debates
State Legislatures use the same devices, along with estimates and public accounts committees
State Legislatures use only the no-confidence motion
32.x: State Legislatures use the same parliamentary devices for executive control and also use estimates and public accounts committees.
32.tq: Test the Union–State comparison by identifying the correct extension rather than an exclusive claim.

32.s: Question Hour in the Lok Sabha is generally held during:
o: The first hour of every sitting
Only the first sitting of each week
The hour immediately before the day's adjournment
The last hour of every sitting
