Section 8 of the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003
92.x: The CBI draws its powers from the DSPE Act, 1946, and Section 6 of that Act requires the State's consent. Section 17A PCA is government approval before investigating a public servant's official decisions; Section 19 PCA is sanction before a court takes cognizance; the CVC Act is about the CVC's superintendence, not State consent.
92.tq: CBI in a State = Sec 6 DSPE consent.

92.s: The Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 came into force on:
92.x: The Prevention of Money Laundering Act came into force on 1 July 2005.
92.tq: Distinguish the year of enactment from the date on which the law came into force.

92.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 — Proceedings involving flight from India and confiscation by a Special Court
Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 — Attachment and confiscation of proceeds of corruption
Benami (Amendment) Act, 2016 — Ban on proxy holdings
Benami (Amendment) Act, 2016 — Imprisonment up to ten years as its stated maximum punishment
92.x: The Benami (Amendment) Act, 2016 provides for confiscation and imprisonment up to seven years, not ten years. The other pairings are correctly stated.
92.tq: Find the altered punishment figure while retaining the correct law and subject matter.

92.s:
Which of the following conditions is associated with proceedings under the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018?
1. An arrest warrant has been issued.
2. The value involved is ₹100 crore or more.
3. The person has fled from India.
4. The Enforcement Directorate applies to a Special Court, which may confiscate property before conviction.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
92.x: All four conditions are associated with the FEOA framework: an arrest warrant, an offence value of at least ₹100 crore, flight from India, and an application by the ED to a Special Court empowered to confiscate before conviction.
92.tq: Check whether each statutory condition belongs to the same legal mechanism before selecting the complete combination.

92.s: In the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta framework, the Lokayukta primarily deals with:
o: International relations, while the Upa-Lokayukta deals with public order
Only judicial officers, while the Upa-Lokayukta deals with private citizens
Higher functionaries, while the Upa-Lokayukta deals with the rest
Only Group C and D employees, while the Upa-Lokayukta deals with Ministers
92.x: The Lokayukta has jurisdiction over higher functionaries, whereas the Upa-Lokayukta deals with the remaining categories covered by the state law.
92.tq: Discriminate between two closely related offices by their functional jurisdiction.

92.s: Which State was the first to set up a Lokayukta, and in which year?
92.x: Maharashtra set up the first Lokayukta in 1971. 1983 is the year of the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act, so AP was not first; Karnataka and Kerala came later.
92.tq: First Lokayukta = Maharashtra 1971; AP Act = 1983.

92.s: The 2013 central law on Lokpal and Lokayuktas required every State to set up a Lokayukta within:
92.x: The 2013 Act obliged every State to establish a Lokayukta within one year of its commencement; States then framed widely differing laws. Six months, two years and five years are not the stated period.
92.tq: 2013 Act: Lokayukta in every State within 1 year.

92.s: Citizen Report Cards were pioneered in Bengaluru in the 1990s by the:
o: Central Vigilance Commission associated with K. Santhanam
Public Affairs Centre associated with Samuel Paul
Planning Commission associated with B. R. Ambedkar
Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan associated with Aruna Roy
92.x: Citizen Report Cards were developed by the Public Affairs Centre in Bengaluru in the 1990s under the leadership of Samuel Paul.
92.tq: Recall the institution, person, place and decade as a single civil-society initiative.

92.s: Jan Sunwai, as a method of citizen oversight, is most closely associated with:
o: Lokpal inquiries in Maharashtra during the 2000s
CVC hearings in Delhi during the 1980s
MKSS public hearings in Rajasthan during the 1990s
SSAAT audits in Andhra Pradesh during the 1970s
92.x: Jan Sunwai refers to public hearings associated with the Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan in Rajasthan during the 1990s.
92.tq: Distinguish the similarly public-facing mechanisms by organisation, place and decade.

92.s: The institution of the Ombudsman is generally traced to which country and year?
92.x: The Ombudsman institution began in Sweden in 1809.
92.tq: Recall the origin country and year of the comparative accountability institution.

92.s:
Consider the following statements regarding public accountability and transparency:
1. More than four lakh RTI cases were pending.
2. Bills referred to committees declined from 71% in the 15th Lok Sabha to 16% in the 17th Lok Sabha.
3. More than 100 RTI activists had been killed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: All three statements reflect the reported criticism and debate concerning transparency and legislative scrutiny: over four lakh RTI cases were pending, committee referrals fell from 71% to 16%, and more than 100 RTI activists had been killed.
92.tq: Combine the three separate accountability indicators and verify the direction of the comparative percentage change.

92.s: According to the CVC annual report released in September 2026, the CBI's conviction rate in 2025 was:
92.x: The CVC report (2 Sep 2026) put the CBI conviction rate at 71.71% in 2025, up from 69.14% in 2024. 52.5% and 85.2% are not figures from the report; 69.14% is the 2024 rate, not 2025.

93.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the LPG reforms:
1. Liberalisation means ending licences, quotas and controls and reducing state involvement.
2. Globalisation is the precondition that made liberalisation and privatisation possible.
3. Privatisation means government withdrawal from ownership or management, including outright sale of PSUs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
93.x: Statement 1 is correct: liberalisation ends licences, quotas and controls. Statement 2 is wrong: globalisation is the outcome of liberalisation and privatisation (integration with the world economy), not their precondition. Statement 3 is correct: privatisation is withdrawal from ownership/management or outright sale. So C; A, B and D include the wrong statement 2.
93.tq: L and P are the means; G is the outcome.

93.s: When a private stake exceeding 51 per cent in a public sector undertaking is transferred, the immediate consequence is transfer of:
93.x: A private stake exceeding 51 per cent transfers ownership and management of the public sector undertaking.
93.tq: Use the threshold figure to distinguish disinvestment from control transfer.

93.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Liberalisation — transfer of majority ownership of PSUs
Privatisation — integration with the world economy
Disinvestment — sale of part of PSU equity to the public
93.x: Disinvestment involves sale of part of the equity of a public sector undertaking to the public. The other pairs interchange the meanings of LPG terms.
93.tq: Start from the sure definition and eliminate swapped meanings of paired terms.

93.s: Navratna public sector undertakings were given greater autonomy in:
93.x: Nine PSUs were given Navratna status and greater autonomy in 1997 (NCERT-based sources give 1996). 1991 is the year of the reforms, not of the Navratna scheme.
93.tq: Distinguish the Navratna date and count from nearby PSU reform figures.

93.s: The New PSE Policy for Atmanirbhar Bharat, as stated for 2021, favours:
o: Abolition of all public sector undertakings
Complete nationalisation of all private enterprises
93.x: The New PSE Policy for Atmanirbhar Bharat, 2021, favours strategic disinvestment.
93.tq: Match the policy year with its stated public-enterprise strategy.

93.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's industrial policy resolutions:
1. The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 adopted a mixed economy and placed industries in four categories.
2. Under the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956, Schedule A listed 17 industries for the public sector.
3. Under the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956, Schedule B listed 12 industries reserved exclusively for the private sector.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
93.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 1948 IPR set up a mixed economy with four categories. Statement 2 is correct: Schedule A had 17 public-sector industries. Statement 3 is wrong: Schedule B's 12 industries were mixed (public and private); Schedule C was left to the private sector. So A; B, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
93.tq: 1956 IPR: A = 17 public, B = 12 mixed, C = private.

93.s: The 1977 Industrial Policy Statement is associated with which of the following?
o: Large-scale privatisation and capital account convertibility
Small and cottage industries and District Industries Centres
93.x: The 1977 Industrial Policy Statement of the Janata Government emphasised small and cottage industries and established District Industries Centres.
93.tq: Link the policy statement to its government and distinctive institutional thrust.

93.s: Which of the following was a feature of the 1980 Industrial Policy Statement?
o: Introduction of current account convertibility in 1994
93.x: The 1980 Industrial Policy Statement focused on technology upgrading, export orientation and development of backward areas. It also allowed MRTP firms 25 per cent expansion.
93.tq: Identify the policy thrust rather than a later legal or monetary reform.

93.s: The 1991 Industrial Policy Statement included which combination of measures?
o: De-licensing, restructuring of MRTP provisions, FDI and PSU autonomy through MoUs
Expansion of licensing, prohibition of FDI and abolition of PSU autonomy
Creation of District Industries Centres and reservation of all industries
Replacement of WTO by GATT and introduction of export duties
93.x: The 1991 Industrial Policy Statement emphasised de-licensing, restructuring of MRTP provisions, foreign direct investment and autonomy for PSUs through Memoranda of Understanding.
93.tq: Recognise the reform package while rejecting measures belonging to other periods or fields.

93.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Licence Raj?
o: A system of automatic approval for all FDI
A system of competition regulation introduced in 2002
A system involving licences to start, close or expand firms, SSI reservation and price controls
A system limited to foreign exchange management after 1999
93.x: The Licence Raj involved licensing for starting, closing or expanding firms, reservation for small-scale industries and price controls.
93.tq: Identify the cluster of controls rather than a single isolated feature.

93.s: Which statement regarding the MRTP Act is correct?
o: The MRTP Act was enacted in 1969, relaxed in 1980 and later replaced by the Competition Act, 2002.
The MRTP Act was enacted in 2002 and replaced by the FEMA, 1999.
The MRTP Act was never relaxed and continues as the principal competition law.
The MRTP Act dealt exclusively with insurance reform.
93.x: The Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act was enacted in 1969, relaxed in 1980 and later replaced by the Competition Act, 2002, administered by the CCI.
93.tq: Use the legal sequence of enactment, relaxation and replacement.

93.s: What happened to the asset limits and pre-entry controls under the MRTP framework in 1991?
o: They were expanded to cover all small enterprises.
They were converted into export duties.
They were abolished, including controls on expansion, mergers and acquisitions.
They were transferred to the IMF.
93.x: In 1991, asset limits and pre-entry curbs relating to expansion, mergers and acquisitions under the MRTP framework were abolished.
93.tq: Test the reform's effect on a regulatory restriction, not merely its date.

93.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 1991 balance of payments crisis:
1. Foreign exchange reserves fell to about $975 million by June 1991, enough for roughly two weeks of imports.
2. About 67 tonnes of gold were pledged with the Bank of England and UBS.
3. The rupee was devalued by about 50 per cent in July 1991.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
93.x: Statement 1 is correct: reserves were about $975 million (two weeks of imports). Statement 2 is correct: 67 tonnes of gold were pledged with the Bank of England and UBS. Statement 3 is wrong: the devaluation on 1 and 3 July 1991 was about 20 per cent. So A; B, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
93.tq: 1991: $975 mn reserves, 67 tonnes gold, ~20% devaluation, $7 bn IMF.

93.s: The New Economic Policy of 1991 was led by which combination of Prime Minister and Finance Minister?
o: Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Yashwant Sinha
P.V. Narasimha Rao and Dr. Manmohan Singh
93.x: The 1991 New Economic Policy was led politically by Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and implemented under Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh.
93.tq: Match the reform policy with the correct political and financial leadership.

93.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes stabilisation from structural adjustment?
o: Stabilisation is long-term, whereas structural adjustment is short-term.
Stabilisation is short-term and targets balance of payments, inflation and fiscal deficit, whereas structural adjustment is medium- or long-term and seeks efficiency and competitiveness.
Stabilisation addresses efficiency, whereas structural adjustment addresses only inflation.
Both terms refer exclusively to industrial de-licensing.
93.x: Stabilisation is short-term and deals with macroeconomic imbalances. Structural adjustment is medium- or long-term and aims to improve efficiency and competitiveness.
93.tq: Split the options by comparing time frame, aim and policy instruments.

93.s: Which of the following measures is most appropriately associated with structural adjustment rather than immediate stabilisation?
o: Correction of balance of payments difficulties
93.x: Industrial de-licensing is a structural-adjustment measure intended to improve efficiency. Devaluation, fiscal-deficit reduction and balance of payments correction are associated with stabilisation.
93.tq: Discriminate between short-term stabilisation instruments and structural reforms.

93.s: The New Economic Policy's move in the exchange-rate regime was towards:
o: A complete ban on foreign exchange transactions
A permanently fixed rupee against gold
93.x: The 1991 trade reforms initiated a move towards a market-determined rupee, with the market-determined exchange rate operating from 1993.
93.tq: Identify the policy direction implied by the exchange-rate reform.

93.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 1991 balance of payments crisis:
1. The immediate trigger was a flight of NRI deposits.
2. India approached the IMF for about $7 billion, which came with structural-adjustment conditions.
3. The gold pledged to raise funds was kept with the Reserve Bank of India alone.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
93.x: Statement 1 is correct: NRI deposit flight triggered the crisis. Statement 2 is correct: India approached the IMF for $7 billion with structural-adjustment conditions. Statement 3 is wrong: 67 tonnes of gold were pledged with the Bank of England and UBS. So B; A omits statement 2, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
93.tq: 1991: NRI flight -> $975 mn reserves -> 67 t gold (BoE, UBS) -> IMF $7 bn.

93.s: Which of the following was retained under industrial de-licensing after the 1991 reforms?
o: Every industry employing more than 100 workers
Alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, industrial explosives, electronic aerospace and defence, and drugs
93.x: Industrial licensing was largely abolished, but it was retained for alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, industrial explosives, electronic aerospace and defence, and drugs.
93.tq: Look for the specified exception to a broad reform measure.

93.s: Capital account convertibility in India was:
o: Fully adopted as part of the 1991 reforms
Never fully adopted and examined by the Tarapore Committees
Achieved through the 1994 current account reforms
93.x: Capital account convertibility was not fully adopted. It was examined by the Tarapore Committees, including the committees of 1997 and 2006.
93.tq: Avoid reversing current account convertibility with capital account convertibility.

93.s:
Consider the following statements regarding foreign investment and convertibility after 1991:
1. In 1991, automatic approval was given for FDI up to 51 per cent in 34 priority industries.
2. 100 per cent FDI was later permitted in hotels, infrastructure and software.
3. Current account convertibility was achieved only in 2001.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
93.x: Statement 1 is correct: 51 per cent automatic FDI in 34 priority industries in 1991. Statement 2 is correct: 100 per cent FDI later came in hotels, infrastructure and software. Statement 3 is wrong: current account convertibility was achieved in 1994 (2001 is when quantitative restrictions were fully removed). So A; B, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
93.tq: 51% in 34 industries (1991); current account convertible 1994; capital account never fully.

93.s: The conversion of FERA into FEMA took place in:
93.x: The Foreign Exchange Regulation Act framework was replaced by the Foreign Exchange Management Act in 1999.
93.tq: Distinguish the year of a legal successor from the year of the broader reform package.

93.s: Which statement regarding public-sector reservation after the reforms is correct?
o: The reservation covered only atomic energy and railway operations from the beginning of the reforms.
The reform list included defence, atomic energy and railways; at present, only atomic energy and railway operations remain in the stated list.
All industries were permanently reserved for the public sector.
No public-sector reservation was altered after 1991.
93.x: The reform material lists defence, atomic energy and railways among reserved areas, while the present position stated is limited to atomic energy and railway operations.
93.tq: Track the change in the composition of a reserved-sector list over time.

93.s: Which of the following statements about the trade reforms of 1991 is correct?
o: Import licensing was abolished except for hazardous or environmentally sensitive items.
Quantitative restrictions on imports were fully removed immediately in July 1991.
Export duties were increased as a permanent substitute for licensing.
The reforms restored import substitution as the central trade strategy.
93.x: Import licensing was abolished except for hazardous or environmentally sensitive items. Quantitative restrictions were fully removed later, in April 2001.
93.tq: Distinguish immediate reform measures from the later completion of quantitative-restriction removal.

93.s: The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade was replaced by the World Trade Organization in:
93.x: The WTO replaced GATT in 1995; GATT had been established in 1948.
93.tq: Place the international trade institution in the correct reform-era sequence.

93.s:
Consider the following statements regarding generations of economic reforms in India:
1. First-generation reforms (1991-2000) covered trade and industrial delicensing, tariff cuts, the automatic FDI route and financial-sector reform.
2. Second-generation reforms (2000s) addressed factor markets, fiscal rules, PSU disinvestment and governance.
3. First-generation reforms were mainly concerned with factor markets such as labour, land and power.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
93.x: Statement 1 is correct: it lists the first-generation reforms of 1991-2000. Statement 2 is correct: it lists the second-generation agenda of the 2000s. Statement 3 is wrong: factor markets (labour, land, power) belong to the second generation, not the first. So B; A omits the correct statement 2, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
93.tq: First gen = trade, industry, FDI, finance; second gen = factor markets, fiscal rules, disinvestment, governance.

93.s: The average tariff level is stated to have declined approximately from what level in the late 1980s to what level by the early 2000s?
93.x: Average tariffs declined from about 125 per cent in the late 1980s to about 30 per cent by the early 2000s.
93.tq: Check the direction of a quantitative trend before comparing the two figures.

93.s: Which of the following is included in the current framing of Reforms 2.0?
o: DPI, Aadhaar, UPI, Jan Dhan and DBT from 2014 onwards
93.x: Reforms 2.0 are framed as reforms from 2014 onwards, including digital public infrastructure, Aadhaar, UPI, Jan Dhan and direct benefit transfer.
93.tq: Distinguish the contemporary reform label from the original 1991 LPG package.

93.s: The term ‘Washington Consensus’ is associated with which one of the following economists and years?
93.x: The Washington Consensus was formulated by John Williamson in 1989.
93.tq: Use the direct author–year association without being distracted by economists linked with other economic doctrines.

93.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Washington Consensus:
1. It included fiscal discipline and tax reform.
2. It advocated trade and foreign direct investment liberalisation, privatisation and deregulation.
3. It excluded the protection of property rights from its prescriptions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
93.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because protection of property rights was one of the prescriptions associated with the Washington Consensus.
93.tq: Find the statement that reverses a listed component; the word ‘excluded’ is the key trap.

93.s: Which of the following correctly represents the current characterisation of Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation (LPG) reforms in July 2026?
o: Reforms 2.0, with a case for ending globalisation
Reforms 1.0, with a case for a third wave
Reforms 3.0, with a case for abolishing privatisation
Reforms 1.0, with a case for returning to the License Raj
93.x: LENS (July 2026) describes LPG as ‘Reforms 1.0’ and argues for a third wave of reforms.
93.tq: Match the exact reform label with the associated policy direction instead of choosing an extreme reversal.

93.s:
With reference to the criticisms of the LPG reform framework, consider the following statements:
1. The reforms were associated with IMF structural-adjustment conditions.
2. The uniform application of Washington Consensus prescriptions has been questioned.
3. Contemporary debate accepts that the Washington Consensus is universally suitable without modification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
93.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the one-size-fits-all character of the Washington Consensus is specifically questioned, and the framework is regarded as outdated.
93.tq: Separate the two stated criticisms from the absolute claim that the framework is universally suitable.

94.s: The economic reforms initiated in 1991 shifted the Indian economy from which orientation to which orientation?
94.x: The 1991 crisis and the LPG reforms under Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh shifted the economy from a state-controlled orientation to a market-oriented one.
94.tq: Test the direction of a major policy transition rather than merely recalling its year.

94.s: Which one of the following best describes the shift from Government to Governance after the LPG reforms?
o: The State retained direct control over all services but reduced taxation.
The State transferred all regulatory powers to civil-society organisations.
The State withdrew completely from economic activity.
The State increasingly acted as facilitator, regulator and catalyst for private and civil-society participation.
94.x: The post-reform State moved away from being the direct provider and controller of all services and increasingly became a facilitator, regulator and catalyst for private and civil-society participation.
94.tq: Identify the option that captures the complete institutional shift without using an extreme claim.

94.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Welfare or provider state — Owns and runs production
2. Regulatory state — Sets rules and uses independent regulators to police markets
3. Facilitator or enabler state — Creates conditions for private and civil-society delivery

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
94.x: All three pairs correctly describe the respective roles of the welfare/provider, regulatory and facilitator/enabler states.
94.tq: Match each institutional model with its defining function before selecting the coded combination.

94.s: Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 used the size of the public sector as an indicator of the extent to which the economy was:
94.x: Under the provider-state model, the size of the public sector was treated as a measure of how socialised the economy was.
94.tq: Use a look-alike conceptual option to test the exact official term.

94.s: Which one of the following sets contains only instruments associated with the facilitator or enabler state?
o: Industrial licensing, MRTP controls and public-sector reservation
Capital issue control, tariff fixation and judicial review
Commanding heights, state ownership and production controls
94.x: Public-private partnerships, Direct Benefit Transfer, Government e-Marketplace and UMANG are instruments through which the State enables delivery by private or civil-society actors.
94.tq: Identify the complete cluster of instruments belonging to one State model.

94.s:
Which of the following represents the correct chronological order of the reforms and institutions mentioned below?

A. Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956
B. LPG reforms
C. SEBI becoming a statutory regulator
D. Establishment of TRAI
94.x: Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 preceded the 1991 LPG reforms; SEBI acquired statutory status in 1992 and TRAI was established in 1997.
94.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest dated policy and then place the post-1991 regulators.

94.s: Which statement best explains the change in the financial sector associated with the post-1991 shift towards a facilitator State?
o: Banks were required to obtain prior approval from the RBI for every operational decision.
The RBI began allowing banks to take decisions without consulting it in every matter, facilitating the entry of private and foreign banks.
The RBI nationalised all private and foreign banks after 1991.
The RBI ceased to regulate the banking sector altogether.
94.x: The reforms aimed to shift the RBI from regulator to facilitator, allowing banks greater decision-making freedom and enabling the entry of private and foreign banks. This did not mean that the RBI ceased regulation.
94.tq: Reject absolute interpretations of institutional change and select the precise description of delegated flexibility.

94.s:
Which of the following combinations correctly represents the major forms of market failure that justified the planning-era role of the State?
1. Public goods
2. Externalities
3. Monopoly
4. Information asymmetry
94.x: Public goods, externalities, monopoly and information asymmetry are all identified as market failures that justified an active planning-era State.
94.tq: Use the inclusive list and test whether all listed causes belong to the same conceptual category.

94.s: Which one of the following was NOT cited as an aspect of government failure that justified the economic reforms of 1991?
o: Low efficiency and profitability of public sector undertakings
Complete autonomy of public sector undertakings from political influence
Mounting losses of public sector undertakings
94.x: Lack of autonomy and political interference, rather than complete autonomy, were cited as features of government failure. Low efficiency, losses, labour problems and project delays were also identified.
94.tq: Find the option that reverses the direction of a stated institutional problem.

94.s: The intellectual basis for the argument that government failure necessitated the 1991 reforms was provided by which of the following?
o: Embedded autonomy theory associated with Peter Evans
Developmental-state theory associated with Chalmers Johnson
Public choice theory associated with James Buchanan
Flailing-state theory associated with Lant Pritchett
94.x: Public choice theory, associated here with James Buchanan, supplied the intellectual basis for the government-failure critique of the pre-1991 system.
94.tq: Use the author–theory association to distinguish closely related governance concepts.

94.s:
Which of the following were identified as criticisms of the economic reforms?
1. Fall in public investment in agricultural infrastructure
2. Reduction in revenue available for welfare because of tax incentives
3. Curtailment of growth in social-sector spending
4. Expansion of public investment in agricultural infrastructure
94.x: The criticisms included declining agricultural infrastructure investment, shrinking welfare revenue due to tax incentives and curtailed social-sector spending. Expansion of such investment was not a criticism identified here.
94.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the stated trend while retaining the three linked criticisms.

94.s:
The Washington Consensus referred to a policy package associated with which institutions?
1. International Monetary Fund
2. World Bank
3. United States Treasury
4. World Trade Organization
94.x: The package was associated with the IMF, World Bank and US Treasury. The WTO is not included in the stated formulation.
94.tq: Identify the wrong institutional member in a composition question.

94.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with a Washington Consensus prescription?
o: Fiscal discipline — maintaining fiscal indiscipline to expand demand
Tax reform — broad base and moderate rates
Deregulation — strengthening entry and exit barriers
Property rights — making property rights insecure
94.x: The prescribed tax reform involved a broad tax base and moderate tax rates. Fiscal discipline, deregulation and secure property rights were also prescriptions, but the other descriptions reverse their meaning.
94.tq: Watch for options that reverse the operational meaning of a policy prescription.

94.s:
Which of the following pairs of Washington Consensus prescriptions is correctly matched?
1. Market-determined interest rates — financial liberalisation
2. Competitive exchange rate — exchange-rate policy
3. Trade liberalisation — reduction of trade restrictions
4. Liberalising inward FDI — restricting foreign investment
94.x: The first three statements correctly describe the prescriptions. Liberalising inward FDI means easing, not restricting, foreign investment.
94.tq: Split the options by identifying the statement that reverses a liberalisation measure.

94.s:
Consider the following statements about India's 1991 reform package:
1. Interest-rate deregulation followed the Narasimham Committee.
2. Tax cuts followed the Chelliah Committee.
3. A market-determined exchange rate was adopted in 1993.
4. FERA replaced FEMA in 1999.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
94.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: interest rates were deregulated on the Narasimham Committee line, tax cuts on the Chelliah Committee line, and the exchange rate became market-determined in 1993. Statement 4 is wrong: FEMA (1999) replaced FERA, not the reverse. So 1 and 2 only and 2, 3 and 4 only are wrong, and all four is wrong because of statement 4.
94.tq: Remember the direction: FEMA (management) replaced FERA (regulation) in 1999.

94.s: The later criticism of the Washington Consensus primarily concerned which of the following?
o: Its emphasis on kinship and caste networks
Its rejection of all market-oriented policies
Its use of a single template without sufficient regard to country conditions
Its exclusive focus on agricultural infrastructure
94.x: Critics argued that one uniform template ignored country-specific conditions. Development thinking consequently moved towards more inclusive and context-specific approaches.
94.tq: Distinguish the stated criticism from absolute claims about rejecting markets or focusing on unrelated networks.

94.s: The number of industries reserved for the public sector changed in which sequence?
94.x: The public-sector reservation list was reduced in phases from 17 industries under Schedule A in 1956 to 8 in 1991 and later to 3.
94.tq: Track the direction and stages of numerical reduction instead of treating the figures as isolated facts.

94.s: Which of the following statements regarding goods reserved for small-scale industries is correct?
o: They remained permanently reserved for small-scale industries.
They were transferred exclusively to the public sector in 2015.
They were newly reserved after 1991, with the last items reserved in 2015.
They were progressively de-reserved, and the last items were de-reserved in 2015.
94.x: Goods reserved for small-scale industries were progressively de-reserved, and the last items were de-reserved in 2015.
94.tq: Watch the reversed policy direction: de-reservation, not expansion of reservation, is the correct trend.

94.s: The abolition of asset limits under the MRTP Act removed restrictions relating to which set of activities?
o: Tax collection, monetary policy, public expenditure and budgeting
Citizens’ Charters, RTI, DBT and e-governance
Agricultural land ownership, tenancy and irrigation
Concentration, entry, expansion, mergers and acquisitions
94.x: Abolition of MRTP asset limits removed curbs on concentration, entry, expansion, mergers and acquisitions.
94.tq: Select the option containing the complete policy-effect cluster associated with the MRTP change.

94.s: Public sector enterprises were given greater autonomy through which of the following measures?
o: Transfer of all PSUs to local governments
Industrial licensing and compulsory state ownership
MoUs and Navratna or Maharatna status
94.x: Public sector enterprises received greater autonomy through Memoranda of Understanding and Navratna or Maharatna status.
94.tq: Use the exact institutional instruments rather than a broad but inaccurate description of autonomy.

94.s: Disinvestment in India began in 1991–92 with an initial target of:
94.x: Disinvestment began in 1991–92 with a target of ₹2,500 crore. Initially, the objective was to bridge the fiscal deficit, and later efficiency improvement was also emphasised.
94.tq: Test the exact inaugural target using closely spaced monetary distractors.

94.s: Which of the following was a criticism of the disinvestment process?
o: The proceeds were used exclusively for expanding social infrastructure.
PSU assets were consistently overvalued and no fiscal purpose was served.
Disinvestment prevented all private participation in public enterprises.
PSU assets were undervalued and the proceeds were used to plug revenue gaps rather than develop PSUs or social infrastructure.
94.x: A major criticism was that PSU assets were undervalued and disinvestment proceeds were used to fill revenue gaps instead of funding PSU development or social infrastructure.
94.tq: Identify the criticism containing both the valuation issue and the use-of-proceeds issue.

94.s: Defence production, earlier among the industries reserved for the public sector, was opened to the private sector in which year?
94.x: Defence production was opened to the private sector in 2001, leaving atomic energy and railway operations as the reserved areas in many lists. 1991 is when the reserved list was cut to 8 (defence still in it); 1997 is the Navratna year; 2015 is when the last SSI items were de-reserved.
94.tq: Reserved list 17 -> 8 -> 3 -> 2; defence opened 2001.

94.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Regulator)
A. SEBI
B. TRAI
C. CERC
D. IRDA

List-II (Sector)
I. Insurance
II. Telecom
III. Power tariffs and inter-state transmission
IV. Securities market

Select the correct answer using the code below.
94.x: SEBI regulates the securities market, TRAI telecom, CERC power tariffs and inter-state transmission, and IRDA insurance.
94.tq: Start from the sure regulator-sector pairs and eliminate codes that reverse the institutional domains.

94.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. TRAI was established in 1997 under the TRAI Act, 1997.
2. CERC was established in 1998 under the Electricity Regulatory Commissions Act, 1998.
3. CERC now functions under the Electricity Act, 2003.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
94.x: All three statements are correct. TRAI dates from 1997, CERC from 1998, and CERC now operates under the Electricity Act, 2003.
94.tq: Verify each regulator against both its establishing law and its later legal basis.

94.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
94.x: TRAI was established under the TRAI Act, 1997. The Competition Act, 2002 established the framework for CCI and replaced the MRTP Act.
94.tq: Use the statute-body association and identify the swapped legislation.

94.s: The TV Ratings Policy 2026 made which authority the sole authority over television rating agencies?
94.x: The TV Ratings Policy 2026 made the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting the sole authority over television rating agencies, ending the overlap with TRAI.
94.tq: Test the recent transfer of authority and avoid the familiar-but-displaced regulator trap.

94.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Economic Survey 2025–26:
1. Regulators exercise legislative, executive and judicial powers.
2. It recommended balancing regulatory independence with accountability.
3. It proposed dedicated regulatory careers for younger professionals instead of relying mainly on retired bureaucrats.
4. It suggested statutory timelines for clearances, with penalties for delay.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
94.x: The Economic Survey made all four recommendations or observations: regulators exercise multiple kinds of powers, independence must be balanced with accountability, younger professionals should have dedicated regulatory careers, and delayed clearances should attract penalties.
94.tq: Treat each reform recommendation as an independent statement and check the complete combination.

94.s: Which group of regulators was specifically noted as moving from reactive to anticipatory governance?
94.x: The Economic Survey noted that RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA were moving from reactive to anticipatory governance.
94.tq: Recall the complete institutional grouping rather than selecting a partly familiar list.

94.s: When SEBI was given statutory status under the SEBI Act, 1992, it replaced which earlier authority?
o: Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Commission
Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction
94.x: SEBI (1992) replaced the Controller of Capital Issues as the securities-market authority. The MRTP Commission gave way to the CCI under the Competition Act 2002; the Forward Markets Commission and BIFR are other bodies and were not replaced by SEBI in 1992.
94.tq: SEBI 1992 replaced the Controller of Capital Issues.

94.s: Under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, which pairing of regulator and administrator is correct?
o: Regulated by CERC, administered by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency
Regulated by SEBI, administered by NITI Aayog
Regulated by TRAI, administered by the Ministry of Environment
Regulated by PNGRB, administered by the Central Pollution Control Board
94.x: CERC regulates carbon trading under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, which the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) administers. SEBI regulates securities, TRAI telecom and PNGRB petroleum and gas pipelines, so none of them regulates carbon trading.
94.tq: Carbon trading: CERC regulates, BEE administers.

94.s: The slogan “Minimum Government, Maximum Governance” dates from:
94.x: The slogan “Minimum Government, Maximum Governance” dates from 2014.
94.tq: Use the closest policy-era dates as distractors and identify the slogan’s stated origin year.

94.s: Which of the following best expresses the meaning of “Minimum Government, Maximum Governance”?
o: A leaner State that does less itself but governs better through rules, technology and accountability
A State that directly provides every service through public enterprises
A State that withdraws from all regulation and public accountability
A State that replaces all public institutions with private companies
94.x: The expression refers to a leaner State that performs fewer activities directly but governs more effectively through rules, technology and accountability.
94.tq: Reject extreme interpretations of “minimum government” and select the balanced meaning.

94.s: The Right to Information Act, 2005 is associated with ending which administrative culture?
94.x: The RTI Act, 2005 is described as ending the colonial culture of official secrecy.
94.tq: Associate a landmark statute with its stated governance effect.

94.s: Which of the following is NOT an instrument associated with e-governance for reducing discretion and middlemen?
94.x: Aadhaar, DBT and GeM are e-governance instruments that can reduce discretion and middlemen. Navratna status concerns autonomy for public sector enterprises, not e-governance.
94.tq: Separate digital governance tools from public-enterprise autonomy measures.

94.s: Who used the term “flailing state” in 2009 in relation to India?
94.x: Lant Pritchett used the concept of the “flailing state” in 2009 in relation to India.
94.tq: Test the author–concept–year combination directly.

94.s: The concept of a “flailing state” refers to a situation in which:
o: The field administration works but elite institutions lack direction
The State completely withdraws from industrialisation
The head or elite institutions work, but are not connected to the delivery limbs
The bureaucracy is insulated from business influence but lacks autonomy
94.x: A flailing state has a functioning head—its elite institutions—but weak connection between that head and the field-level delivery limbs.
94.tq: Translate the metaphor into its institutional relationship instead of choosing a general weakness claim.

94.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the developmental-state concept associated with Chalmers Johnson?
o: A strong and autonomous bureaucracy steers industrialisation
A weak bureaucracy allows political mediation to replace administration
Elite institutions function without field-level delivery
A bureaucracy remains insulated from capture but is tied to business
94.x: Chalmers Johnson’s developmental-state concept describes a strong, autonomous bureaucracy steering industrialisation, particularly in the East Asian experience.
94.tq: Discriminate among neighbouring concepts by matching each definition to its author.

94.s: “Embedded autonomy” is associated with which scholar and idea?
o: Peter Evans; a bureaucracy insulated from capture but connected with business
Lant Pritchett; elite institutions disconnected from field delivery
Chalmers Johnson; a bureaucracy directing industrialisation in Japan
John Williamson; a package of fiscal and trade prescriptions
94.x: Peter Evans associated embedded autonomy, in 1995, with a bureaucracy that is protected from capture while remaining connected to business.
94.tq: Match the distinctive definition with the correct author rather than the more familiar developmental-state label.

94.s: Which of the following accurately characterises the position of Indian corporates described in the Economic Survey 2025-26?
o: They are purely Western rules-bound firms
They are exclusively East Asian developmental partners
They operate outside both political mediation and market discipline
They occupy a hybrid equilibrium in which political mediation substitutes for market discipline
94.x: The Economic Survey 2025-26 describes Indian corporates as neither purely East Asian developmental partners nor purely Western rules-bound firms; they occupy a hybrid equilibrium where political mediation substitutes for market discipline.
94.tq: Reject both extreme alternatives and identify the precisely qualified hybrid comparison.

94.s:
Which of the following are cited as criticisms or governance concerns relating to the reform process?
1. Undervaluation of assets sold
2. Shrinking social spending
3. Regulatory overlap, such as between TRAI and MIB on television ratings
4. Complete elimination of regulatory overlap
94.x: Undervalued asset sales, shrinking social spending and regulatory overlap are cited concerns. The claim that regulatory overlap was completely eliminated is false.
94.tq: Identify the extreme reversal in the final statement while retaining the three stated criticisms.

94.s: The Swarna Andhra KPI monitoring framework tracks indicators at which levels?
o: Village, mandal and district levels only
94.x: The Swarna Andhra KPI monitoring framework tracks indicators at the mandal, district and state levels.
94.tq: Test the exact administrative-level sequence rather than replacing one level with a nearby unit.

94.s: Under Deepam-2, BPL families receive which benefit through Direct Benefit Transfer?
o: Three free LPG cylinders a year
Three subsidised kerosene cylinders a year
Unlimited LPG cylinders through in-kind distribution
Two free LPG cylinders a year
94.x: Deepam-2 provides BPL families with three free LPG cylinders per year through DBT.
94.tq: Focus on the precise beneficiary, commodity, annual number and delivery mechanism.

94.s: Deepam-2 illustrates the State’s shift from which role to which role?
94.x: By supporting BPL families through DBT for LPG cylinders, Deepam-2 illustrates a shift from the State as direct provider to the State as enabler.
94.tq: Apply the provider–enabler distinction to a concrete welfare delivery example.

95.s:
Which of the following sets comprises governance reforms aimed at reducing the size and cost of the State?
1. Downsizing the bureaucracy
2. Disinvestment
3. Privatisation of higher educational institutions
4. Encouraging foreign direct investment inflows
95.x: Downsizing, disinvestment and privatisation of higher educational institutions reduce the size or direct role of the State. Encouraging FDI is primarily a growth and external-sector measure, not a downsizing measure.
95.tq: Separate measures that reduce State ownership from broader growth and external-sector measures.

95.s: Disinvestment is best described as
o: the sale of part of a public-sector undertaking's equity to the public
the complete abolition of public-sector enterprises
the transfer of all government employees to private firms
the withdrawal of foreign investment from the economy
95.x: Disinvestment involves selling part of a public-sector undertaking's equity to the public. It need not involve complete transfer of ownership or management.
95.tq: Distinguish partial equity sale from complete privatisation.

95.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Pay Commission)
A. Fifth Pay Commission
B. Sixth Pay Commission
C. Seventh Pay Commission

List-II (Feature)
1. Pay matrix replaced pay bands
2. Group D merged into Group C
3. Staff strength cut by about 30%

Choose the correct answer using the code given below.
95.x: The Fifth Commission was associated with a 30% staff-strength cut, the Sixth with merger of Group D into Group C, and the Seventh with replacement of pay bands by a pay matrix.
95.tq: Start from the distinctive commission-feature pairs and eliminate swapped codes.

95.s:
Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

1. Fifth Pay Commission — Justice S. Ratnavel Pandian — 1997
2. Sixth Pay Commission — Justice B.N. Srikrishna — 2008
3. Seventh Pay Commission — Justice A.K. Mathur — 2015
4. Seventh Pay Commission — effective from 2015
95.x: The Seventh Pay Commission was chaired in 2015 but its recommendations were effective from 2016, not 2015. The other pairs are correctly matched.
95.tq: Check the distinction between the commission year and the year its recommendations became effective.

95.s:
The Sixth Pay Commission is associated with which of the following combinations?
1. Merger of Group D into Group C
2. Introduction of running pay bands
3. Performance Related Incentive Scheme
4. Rationalisation of allowances
95.x: The Sixth Pay Commission introduced the merger of Group D into Group C, running pay bands and the Performance Related Incentive Scheme. Rationalisation of allowances is associated with the Seventh Commission.
95.tq: Separate adjacent commission recommendations by identifying the transferred feature.

95.s:
Which of the following was associated with the Seventh Pay Commission?
1. Pay matrix replacing pay bands
2. Performance-linked pay
3. Rationalisation of allowances
4. Freeze on new posts
95.x: The Seventh Pay Commission introduced a pay matrix in place of pay bands, performance-linked pay and rationalised allowances. The freeze on new posts belonged to the Fifth Commission.
95.tq: Find the one recommendation belonging to an earlier commission.

95.s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 proposed redefining a Government Company in a manner that would permit the State to hold
95.x: The Economic Survey 2025-26 proposed a definition under which the State could hold less than 51%, indicating a new paradigm for disinvestment.
95.tq: Focus on the changed ownership threshold rather than the conventional controlling-share figure.

95.s:
Which of the following are characteristic features of New Public Management?
1. Performance auditing
2. Contracting out non-core services
3. Treating the citizen as a customer
4. Rejection of all performance measures
95.x: NPM promotes performance auditing, contracting out non-core services and a customer-oriented view of citizens. It does not reject performance measurement.
95.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the performance-oriented character of NPM.

95.s: The term ‘New Public Management’ was popularised by
95.x: Christopher Hood popularised the term New Public Management in 1991.
95.tq: Distinguish the originator of the term from authors of related reform theories.

95.s:
Which one of the following sets contains the pioneering countries associated with New Public Management?
1. United Kingdom
2. New Zealand
3. Australia
4. United States of America
95.x: The United Kingdom under Thatcher, New Zealand, Australia and the United States are identified as pioneering countries of NPM.
95.tq: Use the complete country set and avoid excluding a country merely because one is especially prominent.

95.s:
Which of the following is NOT a doctrine associated with Christopher Hood’s New Public Management?
1. Hands-on professional management
2. Explicit standards and performance measures
3. Emphasis on output controls
4. Complete elimination of competition in the public sector
95.x: NPM includes hands-on management, explicit performance standards, output controls and competition in the public sector. It does not call for complete elimination of competition.
95.tq: Locate the statement that directly reverses an NPM doctrine.

95.s: Who authored the book Reinventing Government (1992)?
o: Justice B.N. Srikrishna and Justice A.K. Mathur
95.x: Reinventing Government, published in 1992, was authored by David Osborne and Ted Gaebler.
95.tq: Match the book with its authors, not with theorists of later critiques.

95.s: The catchphrase associated with Reinventing Government is
95.x: Reinventing Government uses the catchphrase “steering, not rowing,” signifying that government should guide rather than directly perform every service function.
95.tq: Discriminate between the similar phrases ‘steering, not rowing’ and ‘serve, not steer’.

95.s:
Match the following principles of Reinventing Government with their meanings:

A. Catalytic
B. Community-owned
C. Competitive
D. Mission-driven

1. Empower rather than serve
2. Inject competition into service delivery
3. Steer rather than row
4. Move from rules to mission

Choose the correct answer using the code given below.
95.x: Catalytic government steers rather than rows; community-owned government empowers; competitive government injects competition; mission-driven government moves from rules to mission.
95.tq: Start with the distinctive ‘steer rather than row’ pair and then resolve the remaining matches.

95.s: In the Reinventing Government framework, moving from hierarchy to participation and teamwork is the meaning of which principle?
95.x: The decentralised principle seeks to move from hierarchy to participation and teamwork.
95.tq: Match the organisational contrast with the corresponding principle.

95.s:
Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?

1. Catalytic — steer rather than row
2. Community-owned — empower rather than serve
3. Customer-driven — fund outcomes, not inputs
4. Anticipatory — prevent rather than cure
95.x: ‘Fund outcomes, not inputs’ is the results-oriented principle. Customer-driven government focuses on meeting the needs of the customer rather than the bureaucracy.
95.tq: Spot the swapped meaning between two neighbouring principles.

95.s: Outsourcing in public administration refers to
o: selling all government-owned land to the public
transferring legislative powers to private companies
hiring regular services from external sources that were earlier performed in-house
appointing only permanent government employees through competitive examinations
95.x: Outsourcing involves hiring external sources for services such as legal, IT, advertising and security work previously performed in-house.
95.tq: Use the distinction between external service procurement and permanent public employment.

95.s:
Which of the following statements regarding unionisation and contract labour is correct?
1. Only 6.3% of the workforce is unionised.
2. Unionisation in the private sector is 1.8%.
3. The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 requires 10% or 100 workers to form a union.
4. Since 1991, all organised-sector workers have maintained a direct relation with their employer.

Select the correct answer using the code below.
95.x: The workforce unionisation rate is 6.3%, the private-sector rate is 1.8%, and the Industrial Relations Code 2020 uses the threshold of 10% or 100 workers. Contractualisation has weakened direct employer relations for many organised-sector workers, so statement 4 is false.
95.tq: Check the numerical thresholds and reject the absolute statement reversing the effect of contractualisation.

95.s:
Which of the following correctly represents the trend in contract labour in manufacturing?
1. It increased from 20% in 1999 to 40.7% in 2022-23.
2. Contract-labour-intensive firms showed 31% lower productivity.
3. The trend indicates a complete disappearance of contractual employment.

Select the correct answer using the code below.
95.x: Contract labour increased from 20% in 1999 to 40.7% in 2022-23, while contract-labour-intensive firms showed 31% lower productivity. It did not disappear; statement 3 is false.
95.tq: Separate the direction of a trend from an extreme and unsupported conclusion.

95.s:
Which of the following correctly describes APCOS?
1. It was set up by the Andhra Pradesh Government in 2020.
2. It recruits outsourced staff.
3. It pays outsourced staff directly.
4. It retains contractor middlemen as the essential link in payment.

Select the correct answer using the code below.
95.x: APCOS was set up by the Andhra Pradesh Government in 2020 to recruit outsourced staff and pay them directly, thereby cutting out contractor middlemen. Statement 4 is therefore false.
95.tq: Identify the institutional purpose and reject the statement that reverses its payment function.

95.s: Which one of the following recommendations is associated with the Second Administrative Reforms Commission (2005–09)?
o: Replacement of all regular services by contractual appointments
Abolition of performance-based promotion in civil services
Lateral entry at the level of Joint Secretary
Transfer of all recruitment powers to private agencies
95.x: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended lateral entry at the Joint Secretary level, along with performance-based appraisal and promotion.
95.tq: Identify the recommendation correctly associated with the named commission.

95.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Action Agenda of NITI Aayog:
1. It calls for transparent recruitment across ministries.
2. It supports wider lateral entry at middle and senior levels.
3. It recommends career pathways and integration with regular services.
4. It advocates shorter and unstable tenures for lateral entrants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Action Agenda calls for longer, stable tenures, not shorter and unstable tenures; hence statement 4 is false.
95.tq: Find the statement that reverses a policy recommendation through a time-related trap.

95.s: At the Centre, the posts of Joint Secretary and Director are ordinarily filled through which arrangement?
o: Recruitment exclusively through state public service commissions
Tenure deputation under the Central Staffing Scheme administered by DoPT
95.x: Joint Secretary and Director posts at the Centre are otherwise filled through tenure deputation under the Central Staffing Scheme of the Department of Personnel and Training.
95.tq: Match the post-filling arrangement with the correct administrative authority.

95.s: The first lateral-entry Joint Secretaries at the Union level joined in:
95.x: The first lateral-entry Joint Secretaries joined in 2019.
95.tq: Recall the exact year from the sequence of lateral-entry developments.

95.s: Which of the following is NOT cited as a debate associated with lateral entry into senior civil services?
o: Automatic enhancement of reservation in every single post
Access to domain expertise and fresh ideas
95.x: The lateral-entry debate weighs domain expertise and fresh ideas against concerns that single posts carry no reservation, possible conflict of interest and demotivation of career officers. Option B inverts the reservation concern: the criticism is the absence of reservation in single-post recruitment, not any automatic enhancement of it.
95.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the stated advantages and concerns.

95.s: In August 2024, the Centre asked the UPSC to cancel an advertisement for lateral-entry posts. Which of the following correctly describes it?
o: 45 posts, cancelled after a debate over reservation
45 posts, cancelled because the Second ARC opposed lateral entry
100 posts, cancelled because of a shortage of applicants
10 posts, cancelled after the Supreme Court struck down lateral entry
95.x: In August 2024 the Centre asked the UPSC to cancel its advertisement for 45 lateral posts after the debate on the absence of reservation in single-post recruitment. The Second ARC actually recommended lateral entry at Joint Secretary level, and neither a shortage of applicants nor a Supreme Court ruling was the reason.
95.tq: Lateral entry: 2nd ARC recommended; first JS 2019; 45 posts cancelled Aug 2024 (reservation).

95.s: The Results Framework Document (RFD) was introduced in 2009 under which system?
95.x: The Results Framework Document was introduced in 2009 under the Performance Monitoring and Evaluation System, associated with the Cabinet Secretariat.
95.tq: Discriminate between a performance tool and the administrative schemes that are related to it.

95.s:
Consider the following statements about a Results Framework Document:
1. It is prepared for each ministry.
2. It lists objectives, success indicators and targets.
3. Its listed targets function as Key Result Areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: An RFD requires each ministry to specify objectives, success indicators and targets; these serve as Key Result Areas. Therefore, all three statements are correct.
95.tq: Confirm all components of an administrative performance document before selecting the complete combination.

95.s:
Consider the following statements about performance management tools in government:
1. Performance-based incentives were recommended by the Second ARC.
2. A Referral Board reviews adverse ACR remarks.
3. 360-degree feedback is a single-source appraisal by the minister.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Second ARC recommended performance-based incentives, and a Referral Board reviews adverse ACR remarks. Statement 3 is wrong: 360-degree feedback is multi-source feedback. So 1 only misses statement 2, and options with statement 3 are wrong.
95.tq: '360 degree' means feedback from all around, i.e. many sources.

95.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Tool)
 a. NeSDA
 b. Good Governance Index
 c. GRAI
 d. Results Framework Document

List-II (Function or feature)
 i. Lists ministry objectives, indicators and targets
 ii. Uniform assessment framework for States and Union Territories
 iii. Assessment of digital services for G2C and G2B
 iv. Ranking of central ministries on CPGRAMS grievance disposal

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
95.x: NeSDA assesses digital services for G2C and G2B; the Good Governance Index provides a uniform framework for States and UTs; GRAI ranks central ministries on CPGRAMS disposal; and the RFD lists objectives, indicators and targets.
95.tq: Start from the distinctive tool-function pairs and eliminate codes containing swapped roles.

95.s: Which of the following statements regarding NeSDA is correct?
o: It was started in 2019 and is modelled on the Online Service Index of the UN e-Government Survey.
It ranks central ministries using 11 indicators in four dimensions.
It was introduced in 2009 to list ministry-level performance targets.
95.x: NeSDA was started in 2019, is modelled on the Online Service Index of the UN e-Government Survey, and covers G2C and G2B services. The other descriptions refer to different tools or incorrectly restrict its coverage.
95.tq: Separate similar benchmarking tools by their year, scope and institutional function.

95.s: India’s rank in the United Nations E-Government Development Index 2024 was:
95.x: India ranked 97th in the UN E-Government Development Index 2024.
95.tq: Recall the exact rank from closely spaced alternatives.

95.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. New Public Service — Denhardt and Denhardt
2. Creating Public Value (1995) — Christopher Hood
3. 'Serve, not steer' — New Public Service
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
95.x: Pair 1 is correct: New Public Service is by Denhardt and Denhardt. Pair 3 is correct: its slogan is 'serve, not steer'. Pair 2 is wrong: Creating Public Value (1995) is by Mark Moore; Christopher Hood popularised NPM. So 1 only misses pair 3, and the options containing pair 2 are wrong.
95.tq: Hood = NPM, Osborne-Gaebler = steer, Denhardts = serve, Moore = public value.

95.s:
Consider the following statements about the New Public Service approach:
1. It emphasises democratic citizenship and community building.
2. It places public interest above market efficiency.
3. Its central prescription is that administrators should serve, not steer.
4. It reduces the citizen to a customer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: New Public Service emphasises democratic citizenship, community building, public interest and serving rather than steering. Reducing the citizen to a customer is a feature criticised by New Public Service, not its own position.
95.tq: Reject the statement that attributes the NPM view of the citizen to its critique.

95.s: Which of the following best expresses the core claim of Public Value theory?
o: Public managers should pursue efficiency alone, irrespective of legitimacy
Government should withdraw entirely from public service delivery
Public managers create value for the public, including legitimacy and trust
Citizens should be treated exclusively as customers of government
95.x: Public Value theory holds that managers create value for the public, including legitimacy and trust, and not merely efficiency.
95.tq: Apply the theory to distinguish public value from narrow market efficiency.

95.s: New Public Service and Public Value theory have in common that they
o: reject legitimacy and trust as administrative concerns
reject the reduction of citizens to customers and the State to a service seller
treat market efficiency as the only public objective
support the complete replacement of government by private firms
95.x: Both approaches critique NPM’s reduction of the citizen to a customer and of the State to a service seller.
95.tq: Identify the shared critique rather than a claim belonging exclusively to one theory.

95.s: New Public Management views the citizen primarily as a customer entitled to:
o: Only purchasing power without public rights
Direct control over every administrative appointment
95.x: NPM applies a customer-oriented approach to administration and holds that citizens deserve quality service. Its instruments include Citizens’ Charters, service standards and grievance redressal.
95.tq: Identify the central principle of the customer-oriented administrative approach.

95.s: Which of the following is NOT an instrument associated with the NPM view of the citizen as customer?
95.x: Citizens’ Charters, service standards and grievance redressal are instruments of the customer-oriented approach. Abolition of accountability requirements is not one of them.
95.tq: Reject the extreme administrative consequence that is not part of the stated model.

95.s:
Consider the following statements regarding criticisms of treating the citizen solely as a customer:
1. A citizen has rights and is not merely a holder of purchasing power.
2. Equity and accountability may suffer if efficiency is treated as the only yardstick.
3. The New Public Service response is expressed as ‘serve, not steer’.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: All three statements are correct. The criticisms emphasise citizenship rights, the importance of equity and accountability, and the New Public Service formulation ‘serve, not steer’.
95.tq: Check whether the statements cover the principle, consequence and alternative formulation together.

95.s: With reference to Registration Service Kendras in Andhra Pradesh, which one of the following is correct?
o: They are modelled on Passport Seva Kendras, while statutory powers remain with Sub-Registrars.
They transfer statutory powers from Sub-Registrars to private companies.
They are exclusively recruitment centres for the registration department.
They abolish the office of the Sub-Registrar throughout the State.
95.x: Registration Service Kendras are based on the Passport Seva Kendra model, but statutory powers remain with Sub-Registrars. The Chief Minister stated that Sub-Registrar Offices were not being privatised.
95.tq: Separate service-delivery redesign from transfer or privatisation of statutory authority.

95.s: The upper age limit for direct recruitment to non-uniform services in Andhra Pradesh was raised from 42 to 44 years up to:
95.x: The upper age limit was raised to 44 years for direct recruitment to non-uniform services until 30 September 2027 under G.O. Ms. No. 187.
95.tq: Combine the revised age with the exact validity date instead of selecting a nearby administrative deadline.

95.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the reach of Andhra Pradesh’s Gram/Ward Sachivalayams?
o: Fewer than 10,000 secretariats offering 500 services only
About 1,000 secretariats offering fewer than 100 services
Over 10,000 secretariats offering more than 500 services
95.x: The Gram/Ward Sachivalayam system comprises over 10,000 secretariats offering more than 500 services.
95.tq: Check both the scale and service-count qualifiers; do not accept a partially altered figure.

95.s: The Civil Services Board in Andhra Pradesh was created primarily to:
o: Regulate online grievance disposal by central ministries
95.x: The Civil Services Board was created to curb political interference in postings.
95.tq: Ask which institutional mechanism addresses the administrative problem described.

95.s: Which of the following consequences is associated with contractualisation in public administration?
o: Automatic improvement in productivity in all departments
Higher job security and stronger unions
Lower job security and weakened unions
95.x: Contractualisation is criticised for lowering job security and weakening unions; it may also adversely affect productivity rather than automatically improving it.
95.tq: Reject the reversed consequences by comparing security, productivity and union strength.

96.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The GST Council is generally regarded as a symbol of cooperative federalism.
2. NITI Aayog is associated with competitive federalism.
3. Delicensing after 1991 reduced competition among States for foreign investment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because delicensing enabled, rather than reduced, competition among States for private and foreign investment.
96.tq: Find the statement that reverses the direction of an economic reform’s impact.

96.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Andhra Pradesh in the Business Reform Action Plan ranking mentioned for 2019?
o: It topped the 2019 ranking released in 2020.
It was excluded from the 2019 ranking.
It topped the ranking released in 2019.
It was ranked first in the 2020 ranking released in 2021.
96.x: Andhra Pradesh topped the 2019 BRAP ranking, which was released in 2020.
96.tq: Separate the reference year of a ranking from its release year.

96.s: The 16th Finance Commission’s introduction of a GDP-contribution criterion is intended to promote which form of federalism?
96.x: The GDP-contribution criterion rewards efficiency and has been described as part of a framework for competitive and accountable federalism.
96.tq: Infer the institutional objective from the stated incentive mechanism.

96.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
96.x: The 15th Finance Commission was chaired by N. K. Singh and recommended a 41% share for States, a one-point reduction from the 14th Finance Commission’s 42%.
96.tq: Start from the sure person-percentage pair.

96.s: Southern States protested in 2024 that population weights in devolution:
o: Rewarded States with better performance disproportionately
96.x: Southern States argued that population weights punish good performance in the devolution formula.
96.tq: Identify the direction of the grievance rather than the existence of the protest.

96.s:
Consider the following statements regarding recent figures on cesses and tax devolution:
1. About 18% of gross tax revenue was in non-shareable cesses in 2025–26.
2. Actual devolution was therefore nearer 31–32%.
3. The 16th Finance Commission kept the devolution share at 41% for 2026–31.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: All three statements are correct: non-shareable cesses were about 18% of gross tax revenue, actual devolution was nearer 31–32%, and the 16th Finance Commission retained a 41% share for 2026–31.
96.tq: Check each numerical statement independently before selecting the combined code.

96.s: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act was enacted in which year?
96.x: The FRBM Act was enacted in 2003 and was amended in 2018.
96.tq: Directly test the date of the fiscal legislation.

96.s:
Consider the following targets under the FRBM Act 2003 (as amended in 2018):
1. Fiscal deficit of not more than 3% of GDP by 31 March 2021.
2. General government debt of not more than 60% of GDP by 31 March 2025.
3. Central government debt of not more than 60% of GDP by 31 March 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: fiscal deficit 3% of GDP by 2021 and general government debt 60% of GDP by 2025. Statement 3 is wrong: the Central government debt target is 40% of GDP. So '1, 2 and 3' and '2 and 3 only' are wrong, and '1 only' leaves out the correct statement 2.
96.tq: Remember 3-60-40: deficit 3%, general debt 60%, Central debt 40%.

96.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the four statements required to be laid in Parliament under the FRBM framework?
96.x: The four statements are the Medium-term Fiscal Policy, Fiscal Policy Strategy, Macro-economic Framework and Medium-term Expenditure Framework statements. An Industrial Licensing Statement is not one of them.
96.tq: Find the unrelated statement among a group of statutory fiscal documents.

96.s:
Consider the following statements regarding fiscal responsibility legislation:
1. The FRBM Act was amended in 2018.
2. Most States have enacted their own FRBM Acts.
3. State FRBM laws completely eliminate the need for Central consent for borrowing.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Article 293(3) requires Central consent when a State is indebted to the Centre and seeks to borrow.
96.tq: Test the constitutional exception to a seemingly general borrowing rule.

96.s: Under Article 293(3) of the Constitution, a State indebted to the Centre requires whose consent to borrow further?
o: Consent of the President acting alone
96.x: A State that is indebted to the Centre requires the consent of the Union Government to borrow under Article 293(3).
96.tq: Ask which authority exercises the borrowing-control power.

96.s: Which of the following combinations is correct regarding the Economic Survey 2025-26?
o: Debt is unsustainable under Bohn’s test and markets price State Development Loans on fiscal health.
Debt is sustainable under Bohn’s fiscal response test and markets do not price State Development Loans on fiscal health.
Debt is sustainable under Bohn’s test and markets price only Central Development Loans on fiscal health.
Debt is unsustainable under Bohn’s test and State Development Loans are priced only by the GST Council.
96.x: The Survey assessed the debt as sustainable on Bohn’s fiscal response test and observed that markets do not price State Development Loans on fiscal health.
96.tq: Match two related findings without reversing either conclusion.

96.s: The Centre steers State capital expenditure through which mechanism mentioned in the Economic Survey 2025-26?
96.x: The Centre steers State capital expenditure through SASCI.
96.tq: Identify the fiscal instrument from a set of nearby scheme acronyms.

96.s: In State of Kerala v. Union of India (2024), Kerala filed a suit under which Article to challenge the Centre's Net Borrowing Ceiling?
96.x: Kerala used the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction in Centre-State disputes under Article 131 to challenge the Net Borrowing Ceiling, which counts off-budget borrowings against the State's cap. Article 32 is for enforcing Fundamental Rights; Article 226 is High Court writ jurisdiction; Article 293 is the borrowing provision itself (293(3) needs Central consent), not the route to sue.
96.tq: Centre-State dispute suit = Art 131; State borrowing = Art 293.

96.s: Which of the following is a recommendation of the 16th Finance Commission on State finances?
o: State fiscal deficits capped at 3% of GSDP and off-budget borrowing ended
State fiscal deficits capped at 6% of GSDP with off-budget borrowing encouraged
All State borrowing to require the consent of the GST Council
State debt to be fully taken over by the Centre
96.x: The 16th FC capped State deficits at 3% of GSDP, ended off-budget borrowing and asked for subsidies to be rationalised. 6% with off-budget borrowing reverses the recommendation; the GST Council has no role in State borrowing; and no Central takeover of State debt was recommended.
96.tq: 16th FC: States 3% of GSDP, no off-budget borrowing.

96.s: Which of the following is included in the ‘core of the core’ category of Centrally Sponsored Schemes?
96.x: MGNREGA is included in the core-of-the-core category, along with NSAP and umbrella schemes for vulnerable groups.
96.tq: Identify a scheme from the correct CSS category.

96.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the Centre–State sharing ratio?
o: PMMVY and ICDS — 90:10 for all States
MGNREGA and NSAP — 60:40 in every component
96.x: PMMVY and ICDS follow a 60:40 Centre–State sharing pattern. The other options either generalise a regional ratio or misclassify the schemes.
96.tq: Use a sure scheme-ratio pair and reject universalising language.

96.s: Which statement best describes the post-2015 trend in Centrally Sponsored Schemes?
o: All schemes became fully funded by the Centre.
Most schemes shifted to lower State shares of funding.
Most schemes shifted to higher State shares of funding.
96.x: After the 2015 reforms, most Centrally Sponsored Schemes moved to higher State shares, increasing the financial burden on States.
96.tq: Identify the direction of change rather than merely the existence of reform.

96.s:
Consider the following statements about Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS):
1. CSS have grown about 26.5% a year since 2016-17.
2. State plan allocations rose by nearly 30% over the same period.
3. Rigid parameters and matching grants of CSS cut into State autonomy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: CSS grew about 26.5% a year since 2016-17, and their rigid parameters and matching grants cut into State autonomy. Statement 2 is wrong: State plan allocations fell by nearly 30%. So any option with statement 2 is wrong, and '3 only' leaves out statement 1.
96.tq: CSS up, State plan money down: that is the autonomy complaint.

96.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 2015 rationalisation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes:
1. It followed the recommendations of a NITI Aayog Sub-Group of Chief Ministers.
2. Schemes were grouped as core of the core, core and optional schemes.
3. Core schemes are funded 90:10 by the Centre and States for all States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: a NITI Aayog Sub-Group of Chief Ministers (2015) grouped CSS into core of the core, core and optional schemes. Statement 3 is wrong: core schemes are mostly 60:40; 90:10 applies only to North-Eastern and Himalayan States. So B; A misses statement 2, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
96.tq: Core CSS 60:40; NE/Himalayan 90:10.

96.s: India’s expenditure on social protection is approximately what percentage of GDP, as stated?
96.x: India spends approximately 4.0% of GDP on social protection, which is lower than the level in most upper-middle-income countries.
96.tq: Recall the stated expenditure ratio and avoid confusing it with policy targets.

96.s: Which pair correctly states the policy targets for public health and education spending?
o: Health 1% of GDP; education 2.5% of GDP
Health 2.5% of GDP; education 6% of GDP
Health 6% of GDP; education 2.5% of GDP
Health 4% of GDP; education 5% of GDP
96.x: The National Health Policy 2017 set a public health spending target of 2.5% of GDP, while NEP 2020 set an education spending target of 6% of GDP.
96.tq: Keep the two sectoral targets in their correct order.

96.s: States bear what share of school education expenditure, according to the stated trend?
96.x: States bear 75.2% of school education spending, showing the increasing burden of social-sector expenditure on States.
96.tq: Test the precise expenditure share rather than a rounded approximation.

96.s: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) was commenced on which date?
