99.x: The National Financial Reporting Authority oversees auditing and accounting standards under the Companies Act, 2013.
99.tq: Match the statutory body with its technical oversight function.

99.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC)?
o: A parliamentary committee chaired by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
A statutory body chaired by the RBI Governor
A non-statutory apex body set up in 2010 and chaired by the Union Finance Minister
A quasi-judicial tribunal chaired by the Chief Justice of India
99.x: FSDC was set up in 2010 as a non-statutory apex body chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
99.tq: Discriminate between the body’s legal status, year of establishment and chairperson.

99.s:
Consider the following functions of the FSDC:
1. Financial stability
2. Inter-regulatory coordination
3. Macro-prudential supervision of large conglomerates
4. Financial literacy and inclusion
Which of the above are functions of the FSDC?
99.x: All four are FSDC roles: the FSDC (2010, non-statutory, chaired by the Union Finance Minister) handles financial stability, inter-regulatory coordination, macro-prudential supervision of large conglomerates, and financial literacy and inclusion. So D; the other options leave out a listed role.
99.tq: Test the full range of functions instead of treating the council as limited to financial stability.

99.s: The sub-committee of the Financial Stability and Development Council is chaired by the:
99.x: The FSDC sub-committee is chaired by the RBI Governor, whereas the main council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
99.tq: Separate the chairperson of the main council from that of its sub-committee.

99.s: The Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission was chaired by:
99.x: The Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission was chaired by Justice B.N. Srikrishna.
99.tq: Test the chairperson of a commission against plausible judicial names.

99.s: Which one of the following was NOT a key proposal of the Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission?
o: A Unified Financial Agency merging SEBI, FMC, IRDA and PFRDA
A separate constitutional court for financial disputes
99.x: The Commission proposed a single Indian Financial Code, a Unified Financial Agency, a Public Debt Management Agency and other reforms, but not a separate constitutional court.
99.tq: Find the proposal that does not belong to the commission’s reform package.

99.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the proposed institutional arrangement of the Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission?
o: SAT — abolished and replaced by the Financial Redress Agency
Resolution Corporation — management of monetary policy
99.x: The proposal retained banking and payments with the RBI. It also proposed a Financial Redress Agency, a Resolution Corporation and expansion of SAT into a Financial Sector Appellate Tribunal.
99.tq: Match each proposed institution with its precise assigned function.

99.s: The proposed expansion of the Securities Appellate Tribunal was to create a:
99.x: The Commission proposed expanding SAT into a Financial Sector Appellate Tribunal.
99.tq: Distinguish the proposed appellate body from existing company-law and insolvency tribunals.

99.s: The Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission (FSLRC) was set up and submitted its report in which years respectively?
99.x: FSLRC, chaired by Justice B.N. Srikrishna, was set up in 2011 and reported in 2013. 2010 is the year the FSDC was set up, so 2010 and 2012 is wrong; the other pairs do not match the Commission's timeline.

99.s: The Economic Survey 2025–26 described RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA as moving towards:
99.x: The Economic Survey 2025–26, under the theme ‘Refining the Regulatory Touch’, stated that these regulators are moving towards anticipatory regulation.
99.tq: Identify the precise policy direction from the stated current-affairs formulation.

99.s: PFRDA’s NPS e-Shramik is intended to extend pension coverage to:
99.x: NPS e-Shramik extends pension coverage to informal workers.
99.tq: Infer the target beneficiary from the scheme’s name and stated purpose.

99.s: Which of the following has been identified as a criticism or debate concerning the financial regulatory framework?
o: Absence of any financial regulator in India
Uniform transfer of all regulatory functions to state governments
Overlapping mandates and mixed evidence regarding a decade of inflation targeting on output and jobs
99.x: The debates include overlapping mandates and mixed evidence on the effect of a decade of inflation targeting on output and jobs.
99.tq: Select the balanced criticism rather than an absolute or exaggerated claim.

100.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. TRAI — Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997
2. CCI — Competition Act, 2002
3. FSSAI — Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
4. AERA — Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India Act, 2008
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
100.x: All four pairs are correct: TRAI comes under the TRAI Act, 1997; CCI under the Competition Act, 2002; FSSAI under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006; and AERA under the AERA Act, 2008. So D.
100.tq: Start from the sure parent-Act pairs and eliminate codes that omit a correctly matched regulator.

100.s: TRAI was established on:
100.x: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India was set up on 20 February 1997 under the TRAI Act, 1997.
100.tq: Discriminate between the establishment dates of different sectoral regulators.

100.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
100.x: CCI was set up on 14 October 2003. FSSAI was set up in 2008, CERC in 1998 and AERA in 2009.
100.tq: Use the establishment year and date to separate closely related regulators.

100.s:
Consider the following statements regarding appointment of chairpersons of regulators:
1. Appointment is made by the Central Government.
2. Appointment is usually based on the recommendation of a search-cum-selection committee.
3. In the case of the CCI, the committee is headed by the Chief Justice of India or the Chief Justice's nominee.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
100.x: Regulatory chairpersons are appointed by the Central Government, usually on committee recommendations. The CCI committee is headed by the CJI or the CJI's nominee.
100.tq: Verify the common appointment rule and the CCI-specific committee detail together.

100.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the removal of a regulator's chairperson?
o: Removal by the Central Government on grounds listed in the parent Act and after a hearing
Removal automatically on completion of half the tenure
Removal by the Supreme Court only after a parliamentary resolution
Removal by the Central Government on any administrative ground without hearing
100.x: Removal is by the Central Government, but only on grounds specified in the parent Act and after the concerned person has been given a hearing.
100.tq: Ask who would perform the removal and whether statutory safeguards apply.

100.s: Which of the following is NOT among the usual grounds for removal of the chairperson of a regulator?
o: Disagreement with a policy decision of the Central Government
Conviction for an offence involving moral turpitude
100.x: The usual grounds include insolvency, conviction for moral turpitude, incapacity and abuse of position. Mere disagreement with a government policy is not listed as a usual ground.
100.tq: Find the non-statutory ground among the recognised removal grounds.

100.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes TRAI from TDSAT?
o: TRAI hears appeals under the DPDP Act, while TDSAT regulates food safety.
TRAI adjudicates disputes, while TDSAT fixes tariffs and quality standards.
TRAI regulates tariffs, interconnection and quality of service, while TDSAT hears disputes and appeals.
Both TRAI and TDSAT perform only adjudicatory functions.
100.x: TRAI performs regulatory functions relating to tariffs, interconnection and quality of service. TDSAT handles disputes and appeals.
100.tq: Separate regulatory and adjudicatory roles instead of treating both bodies as interchangeable.

100.s:
Consider the following statements about TDSAT:
1. It was set up in May 2000.
2. It hears appeals under the Information Technology Act, 2000.
3. It hears appeals under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
100.x: TDSAT was set up in May 2000 and also hears appeals under the IT Act, 2000 and the DPDP Act.
100.tq: Check whether the tribunal’s jurisdiction extends beyond the telecom sector to the two specified digital laws.

100.s: The chairperson of TRAI is:
100.x: Anil Kumar Lahoti is the chairperson of TRAI.
100.tq: Use precise office-holder recall for a statutory regulator.

100.s: The Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT), set up in May 2000, was created by:
100.x: TDSAT was created in May 2000 by the TRAI (Amendment) Act, which separated adjudication from TRAI's regulatory role. There is no separate 'TDSAT Act, 2000'; that is a common trap. The IT Act, 2000 only adds appeals that TDSAT hears, and the Telegraph Act, 1885 is the old telegraph law.
100.tq: TDSAT = TRAI (Amendment) Act; no 'TDSAT Act'.

100.s: The Competition Act, 2002 replaced the:
o: Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 and CCI
Companies Act, 1956 and Company Law Board
100.x: The Competition Act, 2002 replaced the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969 and its MRTP Commission.
100.tq: Match the replacing law with the predecessor law and institution.

100.s: Under the current composition described for the Competition Commission of India, it consists of:
o: A Chairperson and two to six other members appointed by the Central Government
A Chairperson and exactly six members appointed by the Supreme Court
Only a Chairperson and one member appointed by the President
A Chairperson and two to six members appointed by the State Governments
100.x: The current composition is a Chairperson and two to six other members, all appointed by the Central Government.
100.tq: Check both the numerical range and the appointing authority; both are common sources of traps.

100.s:
Consider the following statements about the Competition Commission of India (CCI):
1. Under anti-competitive agreements, it acts against cartels and bid-rigging.
2. Its action against WhatsApp's 2021 privacy policy was taken under its power to review combinations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
100.x: Statement 1 is correct: the CCI acts against cartels, bid-rigging and other agreements that harm competition. Statement 2 is wrong: the WhatsApp privacy-policy case was about abuse of dominant position; combinations means reviewing mergers and acquisitions. So '1 only'; '2 only' and 'Both' wrongly accept statement 2, and 'Neither' rejects a true statement.
100.tq: Three CCI heads: agreements (cartels), dominance (WhatsApp), combinations (mergers).

100.s:
With reference to combinations under competition law, consider the following statements:
1. CCI reviews mergers and acquisitions.
2. A ₹2,000 crore deal-value threshold is intended to address acquisitions of start-ups that may otherwise escape traditional scrutiny.
3. Combinations refer exclusively to cartel agreements.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
100.x: CCI reviews mergers and acquisitions, and the ₹2,000 crore deal-value threshold targets potential ‘killer acquisitions’ of start-ups. Combinations are not exclusively cartel agreements.
100.tq: Reject the extreme word ‘exclusively’ and retain the two statements describing merger scrutiny.

100.s: From 26 May 2017, appeals against orders of the Competition Commission of India lie to the:
o: High Court directly in every case
100.x: NCLAT became the appellate forum for CCI matters from 26 May 2017. Earlier, appeals lay to COMPAT, and a further appeal lies to the Supreme Court.
100.tq: Use the date to distinguish the present appellate forum from its predecessor.

100.s: The proposed Digital Competition Bill seeks to pre-regulate:
o: Digital enterprises registered outside India alone
All online platforms irrespective of their size
100.x: The proposed Digital Competition Bill would pre-regulate Systemically Significant Digital Enterprises.
100.tq: Recall the exact defined category rather than broadening it to all digital platforms.

100.s: Which one of the following organisations has set up a Digital Markets Division?
100.x: The Competition Commission of India has set up a Digital Markets Division.
100.tq: Match the specialised digital-market function with the correct regulator.

100.s: Which one of the following statements about the Competition Commission of India (CCI) is correct?
o: It is a constitutional body under Article 19(1)(g).
It is a statutory body under the Competition Act, 2002, as amended in 2007, under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
It is a statutory body under the MRTP Act, 1969, under the Ministry of Finance.
It is an executive body set up by a Cabinet resolution in 2003.
100.x: The CCI is a statutory body under the Competition Act, 2002, as amended by the Competition (Amendment) Act, 2007, and comes under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs; this was the only true statement in APPSC 2022. It is not a constitutional body, the MRTP Act, 1969 is the law it replaced, and it was set up under a statute, not by Cabinet resolution.
100.tq: CCI: Competition Act 2002 + 2007 amendment; MCA.

100.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: FSSAI — Director General of Health Services as its administrative ministry
FSSAI — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
FSSAI — Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
100.x: FSSAI is administered by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and is not under the Director General of Health Services. Eat Right India was launched in 2018.
100.tq: Find the wrong authority by separating an administrative ministry from an individual health-services office.

100.s: Which one of the following was among the laws or orders consolidated by the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006?
100.x: The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 was among the eight laws and orders consolidated by the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
100.tq: Identify the food-sector predecessor law among statutes belonging to different regulatory fields.

100.s:
From 1 July 2019, food businesses are prohibited from using which of the following for wrapping food?
1. Recycled plastics
2. Newspaper
3. Glass containers
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
100.x: From 1 July 2019, recycled plastics and newspaper may not be used to wrap food. Glass containers are not included in this prohibition.
100.tq: Separate the two prohibited materials from a plausible but unlisted packaging material.

100.s:
Consider the following statements about the 2026 FSSAI licensing reforms:
1. Registration covers food businesses with turnover up to Rs 1.5 crore.
2. A Central licence is needed for turnover above Rs 50 crore.
3. Licences and registrations are now valid for five years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
100.x: Statement 1 is correct: registration now covers turnover up to Rs 1.5 crore (earlier Rs 12 lakh). Statement 2 is correct: the Central licence is for turnover above Rs 50 crore, with a State licence for Rs 1.5-50 crore. Statement 3 is wrong: licences and registrations now have perpetual validity. Hence '1 and 2 only'; the other options either miss statement 2 or include statement 3.
100.tq: FSSAI 2026: perpetual validity; tiers 1.5 crore / 50 crore.

100.s: Which of the following statements regarding PNGRB is correct?
o: It functions under the Ministry of Power and regulates inter-State electricity transmission.
It functions under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and regulates combinations.
It functions under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas and regulates City Gas Distribution networks.
It functions under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and regulates food packaging.
100.x: PNGRB works under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas and regulates City Gas Distribution networks and authorises Geographical Areas.
100.tq: Ask which ministry and sector belong together instead of relying on the regulator’s name alone.

100.s:
Which of the following bodies are statutory bodies under the Ministry of Power?
1. Central Electricity Authority
2. Appellate Tribunal for Electricity
3. Central Electricity Regulatory Commission
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
100.x: CEA, APTEL and CERC are identified as statutory bodies under the Ministry of Power.
100.tq: Check the complete membership of the ministry-wise group rather than selecting only the best-known body.

100.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: APTEL — appeals against CERC and SERC orders
100.x: APTEL hears appeals against orders of CERC and SERCs. CERC deals with inter-State matters, while SERCs deal mainly with intra-State tariffs and consumer protection.
100.tq: Match each electricity body with its level of jurisdiction or appellate role.

100.s: The regulator of carbon trading under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme is:
o: CERC, while BEE administers the scheme
PNGRB, while CCI administers the scheme
SERCs, while APTEL administers the scheme
BEE, while CERC administers the scheme
100.x: CERC is the regulator of carbon trading under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, while the Bureau of Energy Efficiency administers the scheme.
100.tq: Separate the regulator from the body administering the scheme.

100.s: APERC was constituted in 1999 under the:
100.x: The Andhra Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission was constituted in 1999 under the AP Electricity Reform Act, 1998.
100.tq: Distinguish the State reform law establishing APERC from later central and reorganisation laws.

100.s: The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 provided that APERC would continue as a joint regulator for:
100.x: The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 retained APERC as a joint regulator for not more than six months, until separate SERCs were formed.
100.tq: Focus on the limiting phrase ‘not more than’ when interpreting a statutory transition period.

100.s: APTEL was set up on 24 August 2004 under the:
100.x: The Appellate Tribunal for Electricity was set up on 24 August 2004 under the Electricity Act, 2003.
100.tq: Combine the exact date with the correct enabling legislation.

100.s:
Consider the following statements about the Data Protection Board of India (DPBI):
1. It is set up under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.
2. Under the DPDP Rules, 2025, it is a four-member board.
3. Its members are elected by Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
100.x: Statement 1 is correct: the DPBI is an independent adjudicatory body under Sections 18-22 of the DPDP Act, 2023 (enacted August 2023). Statement 2 is correct: the DPDP Rules, 2025 provide for a four-member board with an online complaints portal. Statement 3 is wrong: members are appointed by the Central Government on the recommendation of a Selection Committee. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses statement 2 and the other options include statement 3.
100.tq: DPBI: DPDP Act 2023, Secs 18-22, 4 members, Centre appoints.

100.s: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, the maximum penalty the Data Protection Board can impose is:
o: Rs 50 crore, with imprisonment up to 3 years
Rs 500 crore, with imprisonment up to 7 years
100.x: The Board can impose penalties of up to Rs 250 crore, and the Act provides no imprisonment. So the options with imprisonment are wrong, and Rs 50 crore or Rs 25 crore understate the ceiling.
100.tq: DPDP: up to Rs 250 crore, civil only.

100.s: An order of the Data Protection Board of India can be challenged in appeal before:
o: The TDSAT within 60 days, with a further appeal to the Supreme Court
100.x: Appeals against the Board's orders go to the TDSAT within 60 days, and from there to the Supreme Court. The claim that appeals go directly to the Supreme Court is a known wrong statement. The High Court and NCLAT are not the appellate forums under the DPDP Act.
100.tq: DPBI -> TDSAT (60 days) -> SC.

100.s:
Consider the following statements about the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan (VBSA) Bill, 2025:
1. It is the current form of the proposal for a Higher Education Commission of India.
2. It was introduced in the Rajya Sabha and passed in December 2025.
3. It would repeal the UGC Act 1956, the AICTE Act 1987 and the NCTE Act 1993.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
100.x: Statement 1 is correct: VBSA Bill is the current form of the HECI proposal. Statement 2 is wrong: it was introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2025 and referred to a Joint Committee of Parliament, not passed. Statement 3 is correct: it would repeal the UGC, AICTE and NCTE Acts. Hence '1 and 3 only'; options including statement 2 are wrong and '1 only' misses statement 3.
100.tq: VBSA = HECI's new avatar: Lok Sabha Dec 2025 -> JPC; replaces UGC, AICTE, NCTE.

100.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three councils proposed under the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025?
100.x: The proposed Bill provides for Regulatory, Accreditation and Standards Councils. A Funding Council is not among the three councils listed.
100.tq: Use the complete three-member institutional list to identify the added distractor.

100.s:
Consider the following statements about the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025:
1. It was introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2025.
2. It was referred to a Joint Committee of Parliament.
3. It seeks to repeal the UGC Act, 1956, the AICTE Act, 1987 and the NCTE Act, 1993.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
100.x: The Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2025, referred to a Joint Committee of Parliament and proposes repeal of all three specified higher-education laws.
100.tq: Combine legislative date, parliamentary process and repeal provisions without confusing the three Acts.

100.s: The Competition Commission of India imposed a penalty of ₹213.14 crore on Meta/WhatsApp for:
o: Non-payment of goods and services tax
Failure to obtain a telecom licence
100.x: The CCI fined Meta/WhatsApp ₹213.14 crore for abuse of dominance.
100.tq: Link the exact monetary figure with the regulatory finding rather than the sector of the company.

100.s: The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board approved how many Geographical Areas in Andhra Pradesh for City Gas Distribution?
100.x: The PNGRB approved 10 Geographical Areas in Andhra Pradesh for City Gas Distribution.
100.tq: Test the exact state-level regulatory count using nearby numerical distractors.

100.s: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act has been criticised for amending which provision of the Right to Information Act to widen the exemption relating to personal information?
100.x: The criticism concerns the amendment of Section 8(1)(j) of the Right to Information Act, widening the exemption for personal information.
100.tq: Discriminate among nearby RTI section numbers and identify the provision dealing with personal information.

101.s: The National Green Tribunal’s order relating to rat-hole mining in Meghalaya was principally concerned with:
o: Air pollution caused by diesel vehicles
101.x: The 2014 ban on rat-hole mining in Meghalaya addressed unscientific and unsafe coal mining.
101.tq: Use the issue rather than the date to identify the landmark order.

101.s: The Art of Living was fined by the National Green Tribunal in connection with damage to the:
o: Yamuna floodplain during the World Culture Festival
101.x: The 2016 order concerned damage to the Yamuna floodplain during the World Culture Festival.
101.tq: Link the organisation and event to the affected environmental site.

101.s: The National Green Tribunal’s ban on diesel vehicles older than 10 years in Delhi-NCR was primarily related to:
101.x: The 2015 Delhi-NCR order concerning diesel vehicles older than 10 years addressed air pollution.
101.tq: Identify the environmental issue directly associated with the order.

101.s: The Securities Appellate Tribunal was set up under the:
o: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999
101.x: The Securities Appellate Tribunal was established under the SEBI Act, 1992.
101.tq: Identify the parent statute rather than one of the regulators whose orders it reviews.

101.s:
The Securities Appellate Tribunal hears appeals against orders of:
1. SEBI
2. IRDAI
3. PFRDA
4. CCI
Which of the statements given above are correct?
101.x: SAT hears appeals against orders of SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA. Appeals against CCI orders lie to the NCLAT, not SAT.
101.tq: Distinguish the regulator-wise appellate jurisdiction of SAT from that of NCLAT.

101.s: An appeal against a decision of the Securities Appellate Tribunal to the Supreme Court lies on:
101.x: A SAT decision can be appealed to the Supreme Court on points of law.
101.tq: Identify the legally limited ground of further appeal.

101.s: In the Essel Infraprojects insolvency case, the Supreme Court set aside orders of which bodies because they relied on AI-generated fictitious citations?
101.x: The Supreme Court set aside the NCLT and NCLAT orders in the Essel Infraprojects insolvency case because they relied on AI-generated fictitious citations.
101.tq: Use the wrong-body trap to distinguish the insolvency tribunals from other quasi-judicial bodies.

101.s: The Supreme Court took suo motu cognisance of delays in which tribunal?
101.x: The Supreme Court took suo motu cognisance of delays in the National Company Law Tribunal.

101.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding staffing and infrastructure concerns associated with tribunals?
o: Over 95% of NCLT administrative staff are contractual, and NGT lacks an IT division.
NGT has an IT division but no parent ministry funding.
Over 95% of NGT administrative staff are contractual, and NCLT lacks an IT division.
TDSAT has had 95% permanent staff since 2001.
101.x: Over 95% of NCLT's administrative staff are contractual, while the NGT lacks an IT division.
101.tq: Separate the tribunal, percentage and deficiency instead of accepting swapped institutional details.

102.s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 describes regulators as “mini-states” primarily because they combine which of the following functions?
o: Judicial, electoral and administrative functions only
102.x: Regulators are described as “mini-states” because they combine rule-making, investigation and adjudication, corresponding broadly to legislative, executive and judicial functions.
102.tq: Identify the functions combined by the institution rather than focusing on the metaphor.

102.s: Which one of the following is NOT regarded as a standard safeguard for regulatory independence?
o: Removal only on grounds stated in the statute
Unrestricted removal at the discretion of the parent ministry
102.x: Fixed tenure, selection-committee appointment and statutory grounds for removal are standard safeguards. Unrestricted removal by a parent ministry weakens independence.
102.tq: Find the option that reverses the institutional safeguard.

102.s:
Consider the following statements regarding conflict-of-interest safeguards under the Securities Markets Code Bill, 2025:
1. A board member may be removed if the member acquires an interest that may prejudice official duties.
2. Members are required to disclose direct, indirect and family interests.
3. Disclosure is limited to financial interests held directly by the member.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
102.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The disclosure requirement covers direct, indirect and family interests, not merely direct financial interests.
102.tq: Split the broad disclosure rule from the narrower and false limitation.

102.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. National Green Tribunal — Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2. Railway Claims Tribunal — Zonal Railways
3. AERB — Department of Atomic Energy

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
102.x: The NGT is funded and administered by the MoEFCC, the Railway Claims Tribunal depends on Zonal Railways for its budget, and the AERB works under the DAE through the Atomic Energy Commission.
102.tq: Match each body with its administrative or funding dependency.

102.s:
Consider the following statements about the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB):
1. It was constituted in 1983 under the Atomic Energy Act, 1962.
2. It works under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
3. Because the same department promotes and regulates nuclear power, a Nuclear Safety Regulatory Authority (NSRA) Bill has been proposed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
102.x: Statement 1 is correct: AERB was constituted in 1983 under the Atomic Energy Act, 1962. Statement 2 is wrong: it works under the Department of Atomic Energy through the Atomic Energy Commission. Statement 3 is correct: DAE both promotes and regulates nuclear power, hence the proposed NSRA Bill. So '1 and 3 only'; options with statement 2 are wrong and '1 only' misses statement 3.
102.tq: AERB problem = promoter (DAE) is also regulator -> NSRA Bill.

102.s: Regulatory capture refers to a situation in which:
o: A regulator serves the industry it regulates rather than the public interest
A regulator transfers all functions to a ministry
A regulated industry is controlled directly by the judiciary
A regulator is abolished by the legislature
102.x: Regulatory capture occurs when a regulator comes to serve the interests of the regulated industry instead of the public.
102.tq: Use the precise meaning of the paired term rather than its ordinary meaning.

102.s: The theory of regulatory capture is associated with:
102.x: The theory of regulatory capture is associated with George Stigler, particularly through his 1971 work.
102.tq: Discriminate between theorists and institutional reform figures.

102.s: Annual reports and accounts of regulators are laid before Parliament and examined primarily by:
102.x: Regulators’ annual reports and accounts are laid before Parliament and examined by the Departmentally Related Standing Committees.
102.tq: Identify the parliamentary scrutiny mechanism linked to annual reports and accounts.

102.s:
Which of the following measures were identified as important for regulatory accountability?
1. Periodic parliamentary reviews and publication of orders
2. Accountability of executive management to governing boards
3. Sanctions proportionate to intent, scale and harm

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
102.x: All three measures are part of the accountability framework: parliamentary review and published orders, board oversight of executive management, and proportionate sanctions.
102.tq: Test whether all components of a governance framework are retained together.

102.s: The Standing Committee on Finance sought a regulatory framework for:
102.x: The Standing Committee on Finance sought a regulatory framework for Virtual Digital Assets.
102.tq: Match the parliamentary committee with the subject of its scrutiny.

102.s: The Joint Committee on the VBSA Bill cautioned against:
o: Giving all regulatory powers to state governments
Making parliamentary committees responsible for adjudication
Concentrating power in one central regulator
102.x: The Joint Committee on the VBSA Bill warned against excessive concentration of power in one central regulator.
102.tq: Identify the institutional-risk warning attached to the committee’s observation.

102.s: Which one of the following proposals is associated with the Economic Survey 2025-26 in the context of regulatory capacity?
o: Creation of a National Tribunals Commission
Setting up of an NGT IT division
Conversion of all regulatory staff into permanent employees
Establishment of a School for Regulations
102.x: The Economic Survey 2025-26 proposes a School for Regulations because India has no dedicated cadre trained in regulation.
102.tq: Identify the precise institutional proposal rather than a related tribunal reform.

102.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Railway Claims Tribunal and the National Green Tribunal?
1. The Railway Claims Tribunal provides legal aid at 9 of its 23 benches.
2. The National Green Tribunal has no IT division.
3. The Railway Claims Tribunal provides legal aid at all its benches.
4. The National Green Tribunal has an IT division at every bench.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
102.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Legal aid is available at only 9 of the Railway Claims Tribunal’s 23 benches, while the NGT has no IT division; statements 3 and 4 reverse these facts.
102.tq: Find the two restrictive capacity statements and reject the options that reverse them.

102.s: According to the cited assessment, what proportion of cases under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code exceeded the 330-day limit?
102.x: The assessment stated that 67% of IBC cases exceeded the 330-day limit.
102.tq: Separate the IBC delay figure from the tribunal staffing and Single Desk Portal percentages.

102.s: In the Madras Bar Association case (2025), the Supreme Court gave the government four months to set up which body?
102.x: In Madras Bar Association (2025) the Supreme Court gave the government four months to set up a National Tribunals Commission to address tribunal capacity problems. The School for Regulations is an Economic Survey 2025-26 proposal, and the Unified Financial Agency and Financial Sector Appellate Tribunal are FSLRC proposals.
102.tq: Madras Bar Assn 2025 -> National Tribunals Commission.

102.s:
Consider the following statements about appellate tribunals:
1. TDSAT, set up in May 2000, hears appeals from TRAI and the Data Protection Board.
2. An appeal from SAT lies to the Supreme Court on points of law.
3. APTEL was set up in 2016 to hear appeals against CERC and SERC orders.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
102.x: Statement 1 is correct: TDSAT (May 2000) hears appeals from TRAI, IT Act adjudicating officers and the Data Protection Board. Statement 2 is correct: further appeal from SAT lies to the Supreme Court on points of law. Statement 3 is wrong: APTEL was set up on 24 August 2004 (2016 is NCLAT's year). So '1 and 2 only'; options with statement 3 are wrong and '1 only' misses statement 2.
102.tq: TDSAT 2000, APTEL 2004, NCLAT 2016; SAT -> SC on points of law.

102.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. SAT — SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA
2. APTEL — CERC, SERCs and PNGRB
3. NCLAT — NCLT, IBBI, CCI and NFRA
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
102.x: SAT hears appeals from SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA; APTEL hears appeals from CERC, SERCs and PNGRB; and NCLAT hears appeals from NCLT, IBBI, CCI and NFRA.
102.tq: Use the regulator-to-appellate-tribunal mapping to eliminate swapped forums.

102.s: NCLAT began hearing appeals from the Competition Commission of India from:
102.x: NCLAT acquired the appellate jurisdiction relating to the CCI from 26 May 2017.
102.tq: Use the precise date attached to the transfer of a particular appellate jurisdiction.

102.s: The decision in L. Chandra Kumar (1997) established that:
o: All tribunal decisions are immune from judicial review
Tribunals are superior to constitutional courts
Only the Supreme Court may review tribunal decisions
High Court judicial review of tribunals survives as part of the basic structure
102.x: L. Chandra Kumar held that High Court judicial review of tribunals survives as part of the basic structure of the Constitution.
102.tq: Identify the constitutional consequence rather than confusing judicial review with appellate jurisdiction.

102.s: The 2010 legal arrangement concerning ULIPs:
o: Placed ULIPs under IRDAI and created a joint mechanism for disputes between regulators
Placed ULIPs under PFRDA and barred judicial appeals
Placed ULIPs exclusively under SEBI and abolished inter-regulator coordination
Transferred ULIPs to the CCI for competition adjudication
102.x: The 2010 law placed ULIPs under IRDAI and created a joint mechanism to settle disputes between regulators.
102.tq: Test both the allocation of jurisdiction and the dispute-resolution arrangement.

102.s: The Financial Stability and Development Council primarily performs which role in the context of regulatory overlap?
o: Acts as the appellate tribunal for electricity matters
Replaces all sector regulators with the CCI
102.x: The FSDC coordinates financial regulators and helps address overlap among them.
102.tq: Match the coordinating institution with its governance function.

102.s:
Consider the following statements about regulatory overlap:
1. The CCI penalised WhatsApp for abuse of dominance through data sharing.
2. The DPDP Act separately restricts cross-use of data.
3. The TV Ratings Policy, 2026 made TRAI the sole regulator of rating agencies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
102.x: Statement 1 is correct: the CCI penalised WhatsApp for abuse of dominance via data sharing. Statement 2 is correct: the DPDP Act separately restricts cross-use of data. Statement 3 is wrong: the TV Ratings Policy, 2026 made the MIB, not TRAI, the sole regulator of rating agencies. So '1 and 2 only'; options with statement 3 are wrong and '1 only' misses statement 2.
102.tq: Overlap cases: CCI vs DPDP on data; TRAI vs MIB on TV ratings -> MIB won.

102.s: The Securities Markets Code Bill, 2025 provides for:
o: Exclusive regulation of nuclear safety by SEBI
A complete prohibition on multiple financial regulators
Inter-regulatory coordination on instruments overseen by several regulators
102.x: The Bill provides for coordination among regulators where financial instruments fall within the oversight of several regulators.
102.tq: Identify the coordination solution to overlapping jurisdiction.

102.s: Virtual Digital Assets are presently described as being in a regulatory grey area because they are covered only for:
o: Consumer complaints and nuclear safety purposes
102.x: Virtual Digital Assets remain in a regulatory grey area and are covered only for anti-money-laundering and tax purposes.
102.tq: Use the exact limited scope of regulation to distinguish it from comprehensive regulation.

102.s: The FSLRC reported with a draft Indian Financial Code in:
102.x: The FSLRC reported in 2013 and proposed a draft Indian Financial Code.
102.tq: Distinguish the reform-commission year from the later code and bill years.

102.s: Which of the following was NOT a proposal of the FSLRC’s draft Indian Financial Code?
o: A Unified Financial Agency for core regulatory tasks
Moving from area-based to task-based regulation
A Financial Redressal Agency for consumer complaints
Abolishing the Financial Sector Appellate Tribunal
102.x: The FSLRC proposed a Financial Sector Appellate Tribunal for appeals; it did not propose abolishing such a tribunal.
102.tq: Find the option that reverses a specific reform proposal.

102.s: The Regulatory Reform Bill, 2013 was a draft prepared by the:
102.x: The Regulatory Reform Bill, 2013 was a Planning Commission draft intended to provide a common framework for infrastructure regulators.
102.tq: Match the reform bill with its drafting institution and intended regulatory field.

102.s: The VBSA Bill, 2025 proposes:
o: One nuclear regulator replacing the AERB, DAE and AEC
Three independent regulators replacing the CCI, SEBI and IRDAI
One higher-education regulator with three councils, replacing UGC, AICTE and NCTE
A tribunal replacing all Departmentally Related Standing Committees
102.x: The VBSA Bill, 2025 proposes one higher-education regulator with three councils, replacing the UGC, AICTE and NCTE.
102.tq: Test the proposed institutional merger and the bodies affected by it.

102.s: The Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission, which proposed moving from area-based to task-based financial regulation, was headed by:
102.x: FSLRC was headed by Justice B.N. Srikrishna and reported in 2013 with a draft Indian Financial Code. Y.V. Reddy was an RBI Governor, Urjit Patel headed the committee on inflation targeting, and R.N. Malhotra headed the committee on insurance reforms.
102.tq: FSLRC = Srikrishna = Indian Financial Code.

102.s:
Assertion (A): Regulatory capacity is an important component of State capacity.
Reason (R): Regulation is one of the important points where the State meets the economy.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
102.x: Both statements are true, and the State’s interface with the economy through regulation explains why regulatory capacity forms part of overall State capacity.
102.tq: Check whether the reason directly explains the relationship stated in the assertion.

102.s: The Joint Committee’s draft report on the VBSA Bill flagged risks relating primarily to:
o: The number of NCLT contractual staff
The number of Railway Claims Tribunal benches
102.x: The Joint Committee’s draft report on the VBSA Bill flagged risks to institutional autonomy.
102.tq: Separate the current institutional-autonomy concern from operational capacity indicators of tribunals.

103.s: Civil society organisations are described as development partners and democratic watchdogs forming the:
o: First sector alongside the judiciary and legislature
Fourth sector alongside government and courts
Third sector alongside government and market
Second sector alongside government and market
103.x: Civil society organisations are described as the third sector, alongside government and the market, while functioning as development partners and democratic watchdogs.
103.tq: Discriminate among sector classifications by using the government-market comparison.

103.s: The focus of NGOs in India has shifted from welfare delivery towards:
103.x: The stated shift is from welfare delivery to rights and empowerment.
103.tq: Identify the direction of institutional change rather than the earlier role.

103.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Legal form)
 a. Society
 b. Private trust
 c. Public charitable trust
 d. Not-for-profit company

List-II (Registration law)
 i. Section 8, Companies Act, 2013
 ii. Societies Registration Act, 1860
 iii. Indian Trusts Act, 1882
 iv. State public trust law, such as the Bombay Public Trusts Act, 1950

Codes:
103.x: Societies are registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860; private trusts under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882; public charitable trusts under State laws; and not-for-profit companies under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013.
103.tq: Start from the sure pair of Section 8 and eliminate the codes that misplace the trust laws.

103.s: An NGO receiving foreign funds must, in addition to its applicable legal-form registration, also register under:
o: The Representation of the People Act, 1951
103.x: Any NGO receiving foreign funds must also register under the FCRA.
103.tq: Apply the additional-registration rule to the condition of receiving foreign funds.

103.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the groups covered by the World Bank's broad understanding of civil society?
103.x: The broad definition includes NGOs, unions, faith-based groups, professional associations and foundations. Central banks are not included in this classification.
103.tq: Find the institution outside the recognised civil-society grouping.

103.s: In the context of development programmes, NGOs were described by the APPSC 2019 key as:
103.x: The APPSC 2019 key described NGOs in development programmes as “observationalists in development”.
103.tq: Recall the exact descriptive phrase used for the role of NGOs.

103.s: The National Policy on the Voluntary Sector was adopted in which year by the Planning Commission?
103.x: The National Policy on the Voluntary Sector was adopted in 2007 by the Planning Commission.
103.tq: Test the policy year against nearby legislation and policy years.

103.s:
Which of the following are objectives of the National Policy on the Voluntary Sector, 2007?
1. Creation of an enabling environment for voluntary organisations
2. Easier mobilisation of resources
3. Partnership between voluntary organisations and government
4. Complete subordination of voluntary organisations to government departments
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
103.x: The policy seeks an enabling environment, easier resource mobilisation and partnership with government. It does not seek complete subordination of voluntary organisations to government departments.
103.tq: Reject the extreme control-based statement and retain the partnership objectives.

103.s: With regard to accountability of voluntary organisations, the National Policy on the Voluntary Sector, 2007 gives preference to:
o: Transparency, self-regulation and codes of conduct
Direct management by the Planning Commission
Confidentiality and exemption from public scrutiny
103.x: The policy favours transparency, self-regulation and codes of conduct rather than tight government control.
103.tq: Identify the policy approach by contrasting self-regulation with state control.

103.s: The Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) was first enacted in which year?
103.x: The FCRA was first enacted in 1976 and was later replaced by the FCRA, 2010.
103.tq: Use the direct year-recall method for a foundational statute.

103.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the administration of FCRA from FEMA?
o: FCRA is administered by MHA, whereas FEMA is administered by RBI and ED.
FCRA is administered by RBI and ED, whereas FEMA is administered by MHA.
Both FCRA and FEMA are administered exclusively by MHA.
Both FCRA and FEMA are administered exclusively by RBI.
103.x: The Ministry of Home Affairs administers FCRA, while FEMA, 1999 is administered by the Reserve Bank of India and the Enforcement Directorate.
103.tq: Discriminate between two related laws by identifying the correct administering authorities.

103.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 2016 amendment to the FCRA:
1. It had retrospective effect.
2. Indian subsidiaries of foreign companies were no longer treated as foreign sources.
3. It followed the Delhi High Court's 2014 ruling relating to donations received by the BJP and Congress.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: All three statements are correct. The retrospective 2016 amendment followed the Delhi High Court's 2014 Vedanta-donations ruling and excluded Indian subsidiaries of foreign firms from the definition of foreign sources.
103.tq: Check each statement against the amendment's date, effect and judicial background.

103.s:
With reference to the FCRA 2020 amendment, consider the following statements:
1. The ceiling on administrative expenses was reduced from 50 per cent to 20 per cent.
2. Sub-granting of foreign contributions to other NGOs was prohibited.
3. Foreign contributions could first be received in any bank account selected by the NGO.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because contributions must first be received in the designated FCRA account at SBI, New Delhi.
103.tq: Find the false statement by checking the changed percentage, sub-granting rule and designated-account requirement.

103.s: An FCRA registration is ordinarily valid for:
103.x: FCRA registration is valid for five years.
103.tq: Recall the statutory validity period using the distinct year options.

103.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated ground or administrative basis associated with cancellation of FCRA registration?
o: Failure to file returns or seek renewal on time
Breach of the Act, rules or registration conditions
Having a registered office in a State other than New Delhi
103.x: Cancellation may arise from breach of the law or conditions, non-functioning, or administrative defaults such as non-filing of returns or delayed renewal. Location of the registered office in another State is not a stated ground.
103.tq: Find the unrelated location-based option among genuine cancellation grounds.

103.s: The Public Health Foundation of India was placed under the FCRA prior-permission category in 2017 primarily on the ground of:
o: Failure to maintain a designated SBI account
Employing foreign citizens as key functionaries
103.x: The Public Health Foundation of India was placed under the FCRA prior-permission category in 2017 for lobbying with parliamentarians.
103.tq: Apply the who-and-why trap by linking the organisation with the specific cancellation reason.

103.s: The FCRA Amendment Bill, 2026, introduced in the Lok Sabha on 25 March 2026, proposed to:
o: Create an authority to take over assets of NGOs whose registration is cancelled or suspended
Transfer FCRA administration from MHA to RBI
Abolish FCRA registration for all NGOs
103.x: The Bill proposed an authority empowered to take over the assets of NGOs whose registration was cancelled or suspended. Its passage was deferred after protests.
103.tq: Identify the proposed institutional power rather than confusing it with existing FCRA rules.

103.s:
Consider the following statements about the FCRA Amendment Rules, 2026:
1. Registration is under five categories, with separate fees for each category and each State/UT of work.
2. An NGO with a Person of Indian Origin as a key functionary is ineligible.
3. At least 75% of an instalment must be used before the next is sought, and foreign funds cannot be used for proselytisation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
103.x: Statement 1 is correct: five categories (social, economic, educational, cultural, religious) with separate fees per category and per State/UT. Statement 2 is wrong: ineligibility applies to foreign citizens other than PIOs as key functionaries; PIOs are excluded from it. Statement 3 is correct: 75% utilisation before the next instalment and no funding for proselytisation. So '1 and 3 only'.
103.tq: FCRA Rules 2026: foreign citizens bar, but PIOs are exempt.

103.s: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh functions primarily through which lending model?
o: It lends to intermediary NGOs and microfinance bodies, which on-lend to poor women and SHGs.
It lends only to trade unions for industrial welfare.
It lends directly to every individual borrower without intermediaries.
It provides grants exclusively to municipal bodies for urban infrastructure.
103.x: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh follows a quasi-wholesale model: it lends to intermediary NGOs and microfinance bodies, which lend onward to poor women and SHGs.
103.tq: Identify the intermediary chain in the lending arrangement.

103.s: Under which law was Rashtriya Mahila Kosh registered as a society?
o: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969
103.x: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh is registered as a society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
103.tq: Distinguish the legal form and governing statute from company and cooperative legislation.

103.s: Since which year has NABARD been fully owned by the Government of India?
103.x: NABARD has been fully owned by the Government of India since 2019.
103.tq: Distinguish the ownership date from the establishment and SHG-pilot dates.

103.s: The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme, for which NABARD is known, was piloted in:
103.x: The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme was piloted in 1992 and encourages banks to lend to SHGs of poor women.
103.tq: Use the sequence of NABARD-related dates to separate the 1992 pilot from its 1982 establishment.

103.s: DAY-NRLM is best characterised as a:
103.x: DAY-NRLM is community-driven and develops SHG members as community resource persons.
103.tq: Identify the defining institutional character of the programme.

103.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the community resource-person roles associated with DAY-NRLM?
103.x: The listed roles are Pashu Sakhi, Krishi Sakhi, Bank Sakhi, Bima Sakhi and Poshan Sakhi. Nyaya Sakhi is not included in the stated list.
103.tq: Identify the odd term by recalling the complete set of community resource-person roles.

103.s: Which umbrella initiative is run under DAY-NRLM for village enterprises?
103.x: DAY-NRLM runs the SVEP umbrella for village enterprises.
103.tq: Match the programme with its specific enterprise-support initiative.

103.s: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh, which provides microcredit to poor women through intermediary organisations, was set up in:
o: 1993 under the Ministry of Women and Child Development
2011 under the Ministry of Rural Development
1982 under the Reserve Bank of India
103.x: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh was set up in 1993 under the Ministry of Women and Child Development as a society. 1992 is when NABARD piloted the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme; the Ministry of Rural Development runs DAY-NRLM; and 1982 is NABARD's year, not RMK's, and RMK is not under the RBI.
103.tq: RMK 1993, WCD; SHG-BLP 1992, NABARD.

103.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the role of civil society organisations:
1. They have helped secure rights relating to work, education, food and information.
2. Their role has remained confined to service delivery.
3. They increasingly undertake advocacy, policy formulation and watchdog functions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Civil society organisations have moved beyond service delivery to advocacy, policy formulation and watchdog functions; statement 2 is false.
103.tq: Separate the continuing role from the expanded functions of civil society organisations.

103.s: The Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan (MKSS) is associated with which one of the following combinations?
103.x: MKSS emerged in Rajasthan in 1990 and is associated with Aruna Roy. Its campaign contributed to the enactment of the Right to Information Act, 2005.
103.tq: Match the organisation with its year, location and associated personality.

103.s: The Anti-arrack movement of 1992 began at which place?
103.x: The Anti-arrack movement began in 1992 at Dubagunta village in Nellore. It resulted in an arrack ban and later prohibition in Andhra Pradesh.
103.tq: Test the exact place associated with a regional movement.

103.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: India Against Corruption — Anna Hazare — Jan Lokpal
MKSS — Medha Patkar — Sardar Sarovar dam
Narmada Bachao Andolan — Anna Hazare — Right to Information
103.x: India Against Corruption was led by Anna Hazare and demanded a Jan Lokpal. MKSS is associated with Aruna Roy and Nikhil Dey, while the Narmada movement is associated with Medha Patkar and Baba Amte.
103.tq: Match each movement with its own leader and demand before eliminating swapped pairs.

103.s: The Narmada Bachao Andolan was primarily associated with opposition to:
o: The use of information technology in elections
The Sardar Sarovar dam and displacement
103.x: The Narmada Bachao Andolan opposed the Sardar Sarovar dam and the displacement associated with it.
103.tq: Link the movement to its specific project and affected issue.

103.s: Which of the following demands is associated with the MKSS movement?
o: Minimum wages and the right to information through jan sunwai
Immediate formation of a political party
103.x: MKSS raised issues of minimum wages and the right to information, using the public hearing or jan sunwai process.
103.tq: Identify the distinctive demand and method associated with MKSS.

103.s: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act followed the India Against Corruption movement in:
103.x: The India Against Corruption movement (2011, Anna Hazare) demanded a Jan Lokpal, which resulted in the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013. 2011 is the year of the movement, not of the Act.
103.tq: Distinguish the movement year from the year of the resulting legislation.

103.s: The Chipko Movement is correctly associated with which of the following combinations?
o: Uttarakhand, formerly Uttar Pradesh — Sunderlal Bahuguna, Chandi Prasad Bhatt and Gaura Devi — 1973
103.x: The Chipko Movement is associated with Uttarakhand, then part of Uttar Pradesh, and with Sunderlal Bahuguna, Chandi Prasad Bhatt and Gaura Devi in 1973.
103.tq: Match the movement with its state, leaders and year; reject the swapped movement details.

103.s: Which one of the following best describes a pressure group?
o: A constitutional body that supervises the conduct of elections
A temporary administrative committee constituted by the government
An organised group that seeks to influence public policy without contesting elections or seeking office
An organised group that contests elections to capture political power
103.x: A pressure group seeks to influence public policy but does not contest elections or seek governmental office.
103.tq: Distinguish influence on policy from contesting elections and holding office.

103.s: Which of the following is NOT generally regarded as a pressure group?
o: A group of Members of Parliament acting in their legislative capacity
103.x: Trade unions, NGOs and business associations may function as pressure groups. MPs acting as legislators are not classified as pressure groups.
103.tq: Find the institutional actor that does not belong to the pressure-group category.

103.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Type of pressure group)
A. Business
B. Trade union
C. Professional
D. Peasant

List-II (Example)
1. Indian Medical Association
2. Bharatiya Kisan Union
3. FICCI
4. AITUC
103.x: FICCI is a business group, AITUC is a trade union, the Indian Medical Association is a professional group, and Bharatiya Kisan Union is a peasant organisation.
103.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with mismatched group types.

103.s: Almond and Powell classify pressure groups into which of the following categories?
o: State, market, civil society and electoral
103.x: Almond and Powell classify pressure groups as institutional, associational, non-associational and anomic.
103.tq: Recall the exact classification associated with the named scholars.

103.s: Pressure groups are also referred to as the:
103.x: Pressure groups are described as the 'Anonymous Empire' because they influence public policy without directly seeking governmental office.
103.tq: Recall the distinctive descriptive phrase associated with pressure groups.

103.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes a political party from a pressure group?
o: A political party seeks to capture power and govern, whereas a pressure group seeks to influence those in power.
A political party never contests elections, whereas a pressure group contests all elections.
A pressure group seeks to govern the entire country, whereas a political party represents only one sectional interest.
Both are answerable only to government departments.
103.x: Political parties seek to capture power and govern. Pressure groups seek to influence those in power without seeking governmental office.
103.tq: Compare the central aim of each organisation rather than its methods alone.

103.s:
Consider the following statements about pressure groups:
1. They generally do not contest elections.
2. They are answerable primarily to their members.
3. They usually represent a specific sectional interest.
4. They necessarily seek to form the government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: Pressure groups generally do not contest elections, are answerable to their members and represent sectional interests. Seeking to form the government is the characteristic of a political party, not a pressure group.
103.tq: Use the election, accountability and scope distinctions to reject the party-related statement.

103.s: Which one of the following correctly matches a pressure-group technique with its meaning?
o: Propaganda — helping sympathetic candidates win elections
Electioneering — shaping public opinion through media and campaigns
Lobbying — dealing with legislators and officials regarding legislation and regulation
Propaganda — directly contesting elections to form the government
103.x: Lobbying means dealing with legislators and officials to promote or defeat legislation and regulation. Propaganda shapes public opinion, while electioneering assists sympathetic candidates.
103.tq: Separate the meanings of lobbying, propaganda and electioneering.

103.s: Written demands or memoranda submitted to authorities constitute which technique of influencing public policy?
103.x: Petitioning involves submitting written demands or memoranda to authorities.
103.tq: Distinguish written representation from lobbying, litigation and direct action.

103.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Dharna — Written memorandum to an authority
Litigation — Public Interest Litigations and court cases
Petitioning — Direct action to disrupt public life
Media campaign — Filing electoral cases in courts
103.x: Litigation includes PILs and court cases, such as electoral cases filed by ADR. Direct disruption is associated with strikes, bandhs and dharnas, while written memoranda constitute petitioning.
103.tq: Find the correctly matched technique after separating legal, written and direct-action methods.

103.s: Strikes, bandhs and dharnas are examples of:
o: Direct action to disrupt and force attention
103.x: Strikes, bandhs and dharnas are forms of direct action intended to disrupt normal activity and force public or governmental attention.
103.tq: Identify the common purpose shared by the listed forms of protest.

103.s:
Consider the following statements about the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC):
1. The APPSC answer key identifies it as the most powerful pressure group in India.
2. It was founded in 1947.
3. N.M. Joshi was one of its co-founders.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
103.x: Statement 1 is correct: the APPSC key (2007) names AITUC as the most powerful pressure group, though standard texts usually rank business groups like FICCI higher. Statement 2 is wrong: AITUC, India's oldest central trade union, was founded in 1920 (1947 is INTUC). Statement 3 is correct: N.M. Joshi was a co-founder. So '1 and 3 only'.
103.tq: AITUC 1920 (CPI), INTUC 1947 (Congress) - don't swap the years.

103.s:
Match the following trade unions with their affiliations:

List-I (Trade union)
 a. AITUC
 b. INTUC
 c. HMS
 d. BMS

List-II (Affiliation)
 i. Indian National Congress
 ii. Socialists
 iii. CPI
 iv. BJP/Sangh Parivar

Codes:
103.x: AITUC is affiliated with CPI, INTUC with the Indian National Congress, HMS with the Socialists, and BMS with the BJP/Sangh Parivar.
103.tq: Start with the clear INTUC-Congress or BMS-BJP pair and eliminate the remaining codes.

103.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
103.x: HMS was founded in 1948, not 1955. BMS was founded in 1955, while AITUC, INTUC and CITU were founded in 1920, 1947 and 1970 respectively.
103.tq: Check the year against the adjacent union-year entries and locate the swapped year.

103.s:
Which of the following statements regarding trade unions is correct?
1. BMS was founded in 1955.
2. BMS is affiliated with RSS/BJP.
3. Legal recognition of trade unions came through the Trade Unions Act, 1926, after five years of pressure.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
103.x: All three statements are correct. BMS was founded in 1955, is associated with RSS/BJP, and legal recognition came through the Trade Unions Act, 1926 after five years of pressure.
103.tq: Verify the union's year, affiliation and legal-recognition history before selecting the combined option.

103.s:
Consider the following statements about media in a democracy:
1. Press freedom is read into Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution.
2. A free press is necessary for a vibrant democracy.
3. New media technologies have made communication more participatory.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: All three statements are correct. Freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a) includes press freedom, while new media has increased participatory communication.
103.tq: Use the constitutional provision and the two stated democratic functions together.

103.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a problem associated with the contemporary media environment?
103.x: Dependence on government advertisements is identified as a problem. Universal independence from government advertising is not a characteristic of the media environment described.
103.tq: Identify the reversed statement that converts a reported problem into its opposite.

103.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents issues that may be associated with misuse against media or journalists?
o: FCRA, Census Act and Finance Act
RTI Act, RTE Act and MGNREGA
UAPA, IT Rules and defamation law
Forest Rights Act, Motor Vehicles Act and GST Act
103.x: The misuse of UAPA, IT Rules and defamation law is identified as a concern affecting media freedom.
103.tq: Match the relevant legal instruments with the issue of media regulation and misuse.

103.s: India is placed in which category in the Reporters Without Borders classification of press freedom?
103.x: India is placed in the 'very serious' category in the Reporters Without Borders classification mentioned here.
103.tq: Distinguish the exact category from adjacent press-freedom classifications.

103.s: The Press Council of India was first set up in 1966 under which legislation?
o: Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867
103.x: The Press Council was first set up in 1966 under the Press Council Act, 1965. Its present statutory framework is associated with the Press Council Act, 1978.
103.tq: Separate the original establishment year and Act from the later statutory framework.

103.s: The Press Council of India consists of:
103.x: The composition of the Press Council of India is a Chairman plus 28 members.
103.tq: Test the exact statutory composition using nearby numerical distractors.

103.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Press Council of India:
1. It can warn newspapers and journalists.
2. It can admonish or censure newspapers and journalists.
3. It possesses punitive powers to impose criminal punishment.
4. Its jurisdiction covers print media only.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: The Press Council can warn, admonish or censure newspapers and journalists and covers print media only. It lacks punitive powers, so statement 3 is false.
103.tq: Separate moral or regulatory sanctions from punitive powers.

103.s:
Consider the following statements about the Press Council of India:
1. It is a statutory, quasi-judicial body under the Press Council Act, 1978.
2. Its Chairman is by convention a retired Supreme Court judge.
3. The Chairman is chosen by the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
103.x: Statement 1 is correct: the PCI is a statutory, quasi-judicial body under the Press Council Act, 1978 (first set up in 1966 under the 1965 Act). Statement 2 is correct: the Chairman is by convention a retired Supreme Court judge. Statement 3 is wrong: the Chairman is chosen by the Rajya Sabha Chairman, the Lok Sabha Speaker and a member elected by the PCI. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
103.tq: PCI chair: RS Chairman + LS Speaker + PCI member.

103.s: The Amaravati farmers' agitation began in December 2019 primarily in opposition to:
o: The introduction of the Right to Information Act
The construction of the Sardar Sarovar dam
The establishment of the Press Council of India
103.x: Farmers involved in land pooling in Amaravati protested from December 2019 against the three-capitals plan.
103.tq: Link the regional agitation with its immediate policy trigger and date.

103.s:
Which of the following are examples of pressure groups in Andhra Pradesh?
1. AP NGOs' Association
2. Rythu sanghams
3. Election Commission of India
4. Farmers' associations
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
103.x: The AP NGOs' Association and farmers' associations, including rythu sanghams, are examples of pressure groups. The Election Commission is a constitutional authority, not a pressure group.
103.tq: Identify civil-society associations while excluding a constitutional body.

103.s: In July 2026, the Andhra Pradesh Cabinet asked the police to constitute a task force against:
o: Fake news and defamatory social-media content
Displacement caused by the Sardar Sarovar dam
Irregularities in the appointment of Press Council members
103.x: The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet asked the police for a task force to address fake news and defamatory content on social media.
103.tq: Match the state-level administrative response with the specific contemporary media problem.

103.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the debate over the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA):
1. Critics argue that the FCRA has shifted from regulating foreign funds towards State control of civil society.
2. The government justifies its position on the grounds of transparency and national security.
3. The debate is unrelated to the civic space available to non-governmental organisations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because FCRA curbs and NGO funding regulations are specifically debated in relation to shrinking civic space.
103.tq: Find the statement that reverses the central criticism before selecting the coded combination.

103.s: Which of the following statements best describes a criticism of pressure groups in governance?
o: They can capture policy-making for narrow interests.
They are constitutionally empowered to exercise judicial review.
They are required to represent every social group equally.
They eliminate the need for civil-society participation in governance.
103.x: A recognised criticism is that pressure groups may capture policy for narrow interests. The other statements assign them powers or obligations not stated in the context.
103.tq: Apply the concept to a governance situation and distinguish criticism from an institutional power.

103.s: The FCRA Amendment Rules, 2026, which drew opposition letters seeking their withdrawal, were notified in which month and year?
103.x: The FCRA Amendment Rules, 2026 were notified on 22 June 2026. They brought in five registration categories, fees for each category and each State, and other conditions, and drew opposition letters from K.C. Venugopal and John Brittas seeking their withdrawal.
103.tq: Use the precise date instead of being distracted by nearby current-affairs months.

103.s: Who among the following wrote opposition letters seeking withdrawal of the FCRA Amendment Rules, 2026?
103.x: The opposition letters were written by K.C. Venugopal and John Brittas, seeking withdrawal of the FCRA Amendment Rules, 2026.
103.tq: Discriminate between closely associated political names rather than relying on general familiarity.

103.s: The NEET paper-leak protests received solidarity from civil society in which country, as reported in July 2026?
103.x: The NEET paper-leak protests drew solidarity from Sri Lankan civil society in July 2026.
103.tq: Identify the cross-border civil-society connection rather than the location of the domestic protest.

103.s: Which one of the following developments was associated with civil-society activity in July 2026?
o: The notification of the FCRA Amendment Rules, 2025
The introduction of the Lokpal Bill, 2011
The launch of an AP social-media task force
The establishment of the Press Council of India
103.x: An AP social-media task force was asked for by the AP Cabinet in July 2026, and it is among the July 2026 developments. The FCRA Amendment Rules are of 2026 (notified June 2026), not 2025. The Jan Lokpal agitation was in 2011, and the Press Council dates from 1966/1978.
103.tq: Match the event with its correct month and jurisdiction while rejecting unrelated institutional events.

104.s: Which one of the following best describes acculturation?
o: Absorption of a minority culture into the dominant culture with loss of its identity
Convergence of all cultures towards a single global pattern
Mixing of global and local elements into a new blended form
Exchange of cultural traits between two cultures in contact, with both changing while remaining distinct
104.x: Acculturation involves mutual exchange of traits between cultures in contact. Both cultures change, but each retains its distinct identity.
104.tq: Distinguish closely related cultural-change terms by checking whether identities are retained.

104.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Term)
 a. Glocalisation
 b. Homogenisation
 c. Hybridisation
 d. McDonaldisation

List-II (Meaning)
 i. Blending of global and local elements
 ii. Spread of fast-food principles through society
 iii. Adaptation of global ideas to local tastes
 iv. Convergence towards one global cultural pattern

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
104.x: Glocalisation means local adaptation, homogenisation means convergence, hybridisation means blending, and McDonaldisation means the spread of fast-food principles.
104.tq: Start from the sure pair of McDonaldisation with fast-food principles and eliminate codes.

104.s: A minority culture is absorbed into the dominant culture and loses its distinct identity. This process is known as:
104.x: Assimilation occurs when a minority culture is absorbed into the dominant culture and loses its distinct identity.
104.tq: Use the identity-loss clue to distinguish assimilation from acculturation.

104.s: The spread of the principles of efficiency, calculability, predictability and control from fast-food restaurants to wider society is termed:
104.x: McDonaldisation refers to the spread of fast-food principles such as efficiency, calculability, predictability and control across society.
104.tq: Match the distinctive four-principle formulation with the exact sociological term.

104.s: Globalisation is best described as:
o: Liberalisation of trade in goods alone, with restrictions on capital flows
Free flow of goods, services, capital, technology, ideas and people across borders
Nationalisation of foreign enterprises to protect domestic industry
Free movement of people while restricting trade in goods and services
104.x: Globalisation means the free flow of goods, services, capital, technology, ideas and people across national borders.
104.tq: Globalisation lets everything flow: goods, money, ideas and people.

104.s: The spread of cultural traits from one society to another is known as:
104.x: Diffusion is the spread of cultural traits from one society to another. Assimilation is absorption into a dominant culture, homogenisation is convergence to one pattern, and glocalisation is local adaptation of global products.
104.tq: Diffusion: traits spread like ink in water.

104.s:
Consider the following statements about globalisation theorists:
1. Anthony Giddens described globalisation as time-space distanciation and spoke of a 'runaway world'.
2. Roland Robertson is associated with the concept of the 'space of flows'.
3. Manuel Castells is associated with the idea of the network society.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
104.x: Statement 1 is correct: Giddens - time-space distanciation, 'runaway world'. Statement 2 is wrong: 'space of flows' is Castells'; Robertson gave glocalisation and 'the world as a single place'. Statement 3 is correct: Castells - network society. Hence 1 and 3 only; options with 2 are wrong.
104.tq: Pair each theorist with one tag: Giddens-runaway world, Robertson-glocalisation, Castells-network/flows.

104.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
104.x: George Ritzer developed the concept of McDonaldisation of society. The five scapes belong to Arjun Appadurai, space of flows to Manuel Castells, and runaway world to Anthony Giddens.
104.tq: Check the scholar-concept pair and reject the swapped theorist names.

104.s: Which of the following is NOT one of Arjun Appadurai’s five ‘scapes’?
104.x: Appadurai’s five scapes are ethnoscapes, mediascapes, technoscapes, financescapes and ideoscapes. ‘Politiscapes’ is not included in this list.
104.tq: Find the item outside the memorised five-member list.

104.s: Immanuel Wallerstein’s world-systems theory classifies the global system into:
o: Developed, developing and least developed regions only
104.x: Wallerstein’s world-systems theory divides the global system into core, semi-periphery and periphery.
104.tq: Recall the exact three-part classification and reject near-synonymous substitutions.

104.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as an effect of global integration on consumption and media?
o: Complete elimination of local cultural influences
104.x: Global integration is associated with wider consumer choice, global brands, media expansion and cultural fusion. It does not imply the complete elimination of local cultural influences.
104.tq: Find the absolute statement that goes beyond the stated effects.

104.s: The expression ‘mindless aping’ in discussions of globalisation refers primarily to:
o: The rejection of all foreign media
The movement of skilled labour to rural areas
104.x: ‘Mindless aping’ refers to the uncritical imitation of Western lifestyles, identified as a cultural risk accompanying global integration.
104.tq: Identify the exact meaning of a critical phrase rather than its broad cultural context.

104.s: What proportion of tertiary-educated youth was unemployed in 2023–24, indicating a skills-job mismatch?
104.x: About 29% of tertiary-educated youth were unemployed in 2023–24, reflecting a skills-job mismatch.
104.tq: Separate the youth unemployment figure from the migration and coffee-sector percentages.

104.s: The World Migration Report is published by the IOM and has been issued biennially since:
104.x: The International Organization for Migration publishes the World Migration Report, which has been issued biennially since 2000.
104.tq: Link the institutional publisher with the starting year of the recurring report.

104.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India has the largest diaspora in the world.
2. The India-UAE migration corridor ranks fifth among the top migration corridors.
3. The India-US migration corridor ranks sixth among the top migration corridors.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
104.x: All three statements are correct. India has the world’s largest diaspora, while India-UAE and India-US are ranked fifth and sixth respectively among the stated top migration corridors.
104.tq: Keep the two corridor ranks in sequence while checking the broader diaspora statement.

104.s: The Gulf labour force is described as the backbone of India’s:
104.x: Gulf labour is described as the backbone of India’s remittance economy.
104.tq: Identify the economic channel directly associated with overseas Gulf employment.

104.s: Which institution signs Migration and Mobility Partnerships and conducts Pre-Departure Orientation Training under the Pravasi Kaushal Vikas Yojana?
o: Ministry of Labour and Employment alone
104.x: The Ministry of External Affairs signs Migration and Mobility Partnerships and runs Pre-Departure Orientation Training under the Pravasi Kaushal Vikas Yojana.
104.tq: Apply the ‘who performs this job?’ method to distinguish the responsible authority.

104.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s migration data:
