129.x: Free legal aid is provided through the Legal Services Authorities. Courts and police desks may support access to justice but are not the institution identified for providing free legal aid.
129.tq: Distinguish the institution providing legal aid from institutions providing emergency, police or judicial support.

129.s: Which institution provides medical, legal, counselling and shelter support to women under one roof?
o: Women Help Desk in police stations
129.x: One Stop Centres (Sakhi) bring medical, legal, counselling and shelter support under one roof, and they exist in every AP district. Women Helpline 181 gives emergency help and counselling by phone, Fast Track Special Courts try cases, and Women Help Desks sit in police stations.
129.tq: Sakhi = One Stop Centre; 181 = helpline.

129.s: According to UNODC trafficking findings, which one of the following countries is identified as both a high origin country and a high destination country?
129.x: Bangladesh, India, Nepal and Pakistan are identified as high origin countries, while India and Pakistan are also identified as high destination countries.
129.tq: Separate the overlapping origin-and-destination category from countries listed only as origins.

129.s: The GLOTIP 2016 finding that traffickers and victims often share the same national or ethnic background relates to which aspect of trafficking?
o: The compulsory involvement of only foreign nationals
The classification of countries into US TIP tiers
The social and demographic relationship between traffickers and victims
The exclusive role of state agencies in trafficking
129.x: GLOTIP 2016 highlighted that traffickers and victims often come from the same national or ethnic background. This is a finding about the relationship between perpetrators and victims, not about TIP classification.
129.tq: Identify the precise subject of the finding instead of confusing it with country ranking or tier classification.

129.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the US Trafficking in Persons Report tiers:

List-I
 a. Tier 1
 b. Tier 2
 c. Tier 2 Watch List
 d. Tier 3

List-II
 i. Does not fully meet minimum standards but is making significant efforts
 ii. Not making significant efforts
 iii. Fully meets the minimum standards
 iv. Special watch-list category associated with Tier 2

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
129.x: Tier 1 fully meets the minimum standards; Tier 2 does not fully meet them but is making significant efforts; Tier 2 Watch List is the watch-list category; and Tier 3 represents countries not making significant efforts.
129.tq: Start with the sure pair Tier 1–fully meets standards and eliminate codes that disturb it.

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the definition of trafficking under the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013:
1. It covers forms such as sex trafficking, forced labour and organ removal.
2. It applies only where the victim did not consent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
129.x: Statement 1 is correct: the forms include sex trafficking, forced/bonded labour, child trafficking, slavery and organ removal. Statement 2 is wrong: the CLA 2013 definition covers all forms irrespective of consent. Hence 1 only (A); B, C and D are wrong.
129.tq: Consent is irrelevant under the CLA 2013 trafficking definition.

129.s: Which one of the following statements regarding India’s international obligations is correct?
o: India has ratified only the US Trafficking in Persons Report.
India has rejected all protocols concerning transnational organised crime.
India has ratified the UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime and its protocols.
India has ratified only conventions relating to domestic labour and not transnational crime.
129.x: India has ratified the UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime and its protocols.
129.tq: Distinguish a binding international convention and its protocols from an assessment report or domestic law.

129.s: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 was originally known as the:
o: Protection of Women from Traffic Act
129.x: The law originally started as the Suppression of Immoral Traffic Act, commonly abbreviated as SITA, and was later renamed the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act.
129.tq: Test the original title directly, a common law-name confusion point.

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956:
1. It gives effect to the 1950 UN Convention.
2. Protective homes under it are run by the Central Government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
129.x: Statement 1 is correct: ITPA gives effect to the 1950 UN Convention. Statement 2 is wrong: protective homes are run by the States. Hence 1 only (A); B, C and D are wrong.
129.tq: ITPA: 1950 UN Convention; protective homes by States.

129.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the scope of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956?
o: It penalises activities such as brothel-keeping, living on the earnings of prostitution, soliciting, detaining persons and clients, but does not criminalise prostitution itself.
It regulates only the registration of protective homes and does not prescribe offences.
It deals exclusively with child trafficking and has no application to brothel-keeping.
It criminalises prostitution itself in every circumstance.
129.x: The Act does not criminalise prostitution itself. It penalises specified activities including brothel-keeping, living on prostitution earnings, soliciting, detaining people and clients.
129.tq: Separate the underlying activity from the exploitative or facilitating activities made punishable by the law.

129.s: The Victim Protection Plan is intended to provide which of the following through a common protocol?
o: Legal aid, education, skills and livelihood support for rescued victims
129.x: The Victim Protection Plan provides a common protocol for legal aid, education, skills and livelihood support to rescued victims.
129.tq: Select the option containing the complete rehabilitation-support package.

129.s: Ujjawala, launched in 2007, covered which combination of activities?
o: Only prosecution and conviction of traffickers
Prevention, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of trafficking victims
129.x: Ujjawala covered prevention, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of trafficking victims.
129.tq: Recall the four-part programme design instead of reducing the scheme to rescue alone.

129.s: Ujjawala is now part of which institutional framework under Mission Shakti?
o: Legal Services Authorities, through Women Helpline 181
129.x: Ujjawala is now part of Shakti Sadan under the Samarthya component of Mission Shakti, providing integrated relief homes for trafficked and destitute women.
129.tq: Distinguish the rehabilitation framework from emergency response, judicial and legal-aid mechanisms.

129.s: Which information system shares real-time alerts on trafficking across States?
129.x: Cri-MAC is the Ministry of Home Affairs information technology initiative that shares real-time crime and trafficking alerts across States and supports inter-State coordination.
129.tq: Use the function-based distinction between an alert-sharing system, an emergency number and a global report.

129.s: What minimum compensation was directed for victims of acid attacks in Laxmi v. Union of India?
129.x: Victims of acid attacks were directed to receive compensation of at least ₹3 lakh.
129.tq: Use the statutory minimum rather than confusing it with a higher discretionary amount.

129.s: Apart from compensation, victims of acid attacks are entitled to:
o: Automatic government employment in every case
129.x: The directions associated with Laxmi v. Union of India provide free treatment for acid-attack victims in addition to compensation.
129.tq: Identify the immediate medical remedy linked with the compensation direction.

129.s: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 treats acid-attack injuries as:
o: A form of temporary unemployment only
A disability eligible for disability benefits
129.x: The RPwD Act, 2016 lists acid-attack injuries as a disability, thereby enabling victims to receive disability benefits.
129.tq: Distinguish the disability-law consequence from the criminal-law punishment for the same harm.

129.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the directions relating to the sale of acid in Laxmi v Union of India?
o: Maintenance of a register by sellers
No sale to persons below 18 years
Sale without recording the purchaser’s purpose
129.x: The purchaser’s stated purpose had to be recorded; sale without recording it was not permitted. The directions also included photo identification, a register and prohibition of sale to persons below 18 years.
129.tq: Find the option that reverses a specific regulatory safeguard.

129.s: Which of the following is correctly matched under the law relating to acid attacks?
o: BNS Section 124 — minimum ten years to life imprisonment; attempt — five to seven years
BNS Section 103 — acid attack; attempt — one year
BNS Section 143 — acid attack; attempt — death penalty only
BNS Section 124 — maximum punishment three years; attempt — seven to ten years
129.x: BNS Section 124 provides a minimum punishment of ten years extending to life imprisonment for acid attack, while attempt attracts five to seven years.
129.tq: Keep the principal offence, section number and attempt punishment aligned.

129.s: According to the current assessment cited, approximately how many dowry deaths occur in India per day?
129.x: The assessment places the incidence at approximately 20 dowry deaths per day.
129.tq: Use the precise numerical figure rather than an approximate distractor.

129.s: Which of the following States are identified as leading in the incidence of dowry deaths?
o: Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh
Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan
Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand
129.x: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan are identified as the leading States in the cited assessment.
129.tq: Test the exact membership of a named group rather than a single State.

129.s: A film chamber makes submission of an Internal Complaints Committee report compulsory before granting publicity clearance to a film. This measure is most directly associated with which legislation?
o: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
129.x: The compulsory Internal Complaints Committee report is linked to compliance under the POSH Act, 2013.
129.tq: Identify the governing law from the institutional mechanism involved.

129.s: Which of the following has been identified as a reason for the continuing ineffectiveness of anti-dowry laws?
o: Poor enforcement, faulty FIRs and disguising cases as accidents or suicides
Excessive conviction rates and compulsory mediation in every case
Absence of any statutory prohibition of dowry
129.x: Poor enforcement, faulty First Information Reports, and presenting dowry-death cases as accidents or suicides are identified as major reasons for ineffectiveness.
129.tq: Select the option containing the complete cause-effect chain rather than an absolute claim.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about the debates surrounding laws concerning women:
1. The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act involves an overlap between prostitution and trafficking concerns.
2. Section 498A has been associated with both claims of misuse and heavy under-reporting.
3. The debate on Section 498A is limited exclusively to the question of conviction rates.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the debate includes misuse claims as well as heavy under-reporting, not only conviction rates.
129.tq: Reject the extreme word 'exclusively' when the issue has two stated dimensions.

130.s: In the 2023 NCRB break-up of crimes against women, which category accounted for 29.8% of the cases?
o: Assault with intent to outrage modesty
130.x: Cruelty by husband or relatives was the largest category, accounting for 29.8% of crimes against women in 2023.
130.tq: Match the exact percentage with the highest-ranked crime head.

130.s:
Arrange the following crime heads in descending order of their share among crimes against women in 2023:
A. Assault with intent to outrage modesty
B. Cruelty by husband or relatives
C. Kidnapping and abduction
130.x: The descending order is cruelty by husband or relatives at 29.8%, kidnapping and abduction at 19.8%, and assault with intent to outrage modesty at 18.7%.
130.tq: Rank the items by the numerical values before reading the sequence options.

130.s: Which of the following is classified under Special and Local Laws rather than under the IPC/BNS heads listed?
130.x: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 is an SLL head. Rape, attempt to rape and acid attack are included among the IPC/BNS heads listed.
130.tq: Separate offences under the general criminal code from offences under a special statute.

130.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Crime or legal area)
a. Cruelty by husband or relatives
b. Kidnapping and abduction of women
c. Protection of women from domestic violence
d. Indecent representation of women

List-II (Classification)
i. Special and Local Law
 ii. IPC/BNS head

Select the correct answer using the code below.
130.x: Cruelty by husband or relatives and kidnapping or abduction of women are IPC/BNS heads. The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 and the Indecent Representation of Women Act are SLL heads.
130.tq: Start with the sure statutory-law pairs and then eliminate codes.

130.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the social-violence categories identified in the cited classification?
130.x: Foeticide, sati and eve-teasing are classified as social violence. Rape is classified under criminal violence.
130.tq: Identify the category by grouping the listed examples rather than by severity.

130.s: In the NCRB Crime in India 2024 data, which crime head was dominant, accounting for about 42% of crimes against women?
o: Assault with intent to outrage modesty
130.x: Cruelty by husband or relatives was the dominant head in NCRB 2024, at about 42% of crimes against women; it was also the top head in 2023 (29.8%). Kidnapping and abduction (19.8%) and assault on modesty (18.7%) ranked below it in 2023.
130.tq: Cruelty by husband = No.1 head (29.8% in 2023; ~42% in 2024).

130.s:
Consider the following statements about the causes of crimes against women:
1. Patriarchal norms and son preference reinforce unequal power relations.
2. Dowry demands may escalate into bride burning.
3. Alcoholism and aggression among partners or parents may contribute to violence.
4. Some aggressors were themselves abused as children.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: All four are listed causes: patriarchal norms and son preference create unequal power relations, dowry demands escalate into bride burning, and partner or parental alcoholism and aggression contribute, with many aggressors having been abused as children themselves.
130.tq: Treat each causal pathway independently before selecting the combined code.

130.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a factor contributing to under-reporting of violence against women?
130.x: Stigma, fear, lack of awareness and economic dependence contribute to under-reporting. High conviction rates are not a cause of under-reporting; conviction rates are described as low.
130.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated relationship.

130.s: Why is marital rape considered inadequately captured in NCRB data?
o: Under-reporting and the limited visibility of such incidents reduce its capture in official crime data.
It is always classified as a cybercrime.
It is included exclusively in violent-crime data from Odisha.
It is recorded only under the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act.
130.x: Marital rape is not captured well in NCRB data because such incidents are substantially under-reported and remain insufficiently visible in official reporting systems.
130.tq: Apply the reporting-barrier concept rather than confusing legal categories.

130.s: Which combination best reflects the institutional weaknesses identified in the justice response to crimes against women?
o: Court pendency is below 10%, while conviction rates have steadily reached 42%.
More than 90% of police are women, conviction rates are high and pendency is negligible.
Only 11.7% of police are women, but rape conviction rates exceed 90%.
Only 11.7% of police are women, rape conviction rates are low and court pendency exceeds 90%.
130.x: The cited weaknesses are that women constitute only 11.7% of the police, rape conviction rates are low, and pendency in courts for crimes against women is over 90%.
130.tq: Combine the institutional indicators and reject reversals of percentage and trend.

130.s: Which State recorded the highest crime rate against women in 2023?
130.x: Telangana had the highest crime rate against women in 2023, whereas Uttar Pradesh had the highest number of cases.
130.tq: Use the number-versus-rate distinction as the key discriminator.

130.s:
Which of the following statements about the Crime in India 2024 report is correct?
1. It recorded 58.86 lakh cognisable crimes.
2. It was the first report to include BNS data alongside IPC data.
3. It was released in May 2026.
4. Odisha had the highest violent-crime rate.
130.x: All four statements are correct. The 2024 report recorded 58.86 lakh cognisable crimes, incorporated BNS data for the first time alongside IPC data, was released in May 2026, and reported Odisha as having the highest violent-crime rate.
130.tq: Verify the date, novelty, total and State-specific finding separately.

130.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pendency of cases involving crimes against women — over 90%
130.x: The rape conviction rate in 2023 was 22.7%, not 42%. About 42% refers to the share of cruelty by husband as a dominant category in 2024.
130.tq: Identify the swapped percentage by matching each figure to its subject.

130.s: The rape conviction rate in 2023 was 22.7%, compared with approximately what range during 2018–2022?
130.x: The rape conviction rate was 22.7% in 2023, down from approximately 27–28% during 2018–2022.
130.tq: Compare the current value with the stated earlier range.

130.s: Which institution is responsible for the National Crime Records Bureau, and where is the Bureau headquartered?
o: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation; New Delhi
Ministry of Law and Justice; Mumbai
Ministry of Home Affairs; New Delhi
Ministry of Women and Child Development; Hyderabad
130.x: The National Crime Records Bureau works under the Ministry of Home Affairs and is headquartered in New Delhi. It maintains the Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems (CCTNS).
130.tq: Apply the ‘who controls this body?’ method to identify the ministry and headquarters.

130.s: The National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal and the 1930 helpline function under which organisation for reporting cybercrime?
o: CERT-In under the Ministry of Communications
Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre under the Ministry of Home Affairs
National Commission for Women under the Ministry of Women and Child Development
National Crime Records Bureau under the Ministry of Law and Justice
130.x: The National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal and the 1930 helpline operate under the Ministry of Home Affairs’ Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C). The portal particularly facilitates reporting of crimes such as CSAM and non-consensual imagery against women and children.
130.tq: Use the institutional-authority clue to distinguish I4C from other cyber bodies.

130.s: Cybercrimes against women increased by approximately what percentage between 2017 and 2022?
130.x: Cybercrimes against women rose by 239% between 2017 and 2022.
130.tq: Distinguish the long-term increase from the separate rise in trafficking cases under ITPA.

130.s: According to the Crime in India 2023 data, which State recorded the highest number of crimes against women?
130.x: Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest number of crimes against women in 2023. Telangana recorded the highest crime rate, which is a different measure.
130.tq: Separate absolute number from crime rate before selecting the State.

130.s:
With reference to cybercrime in NCRB Crime in India 2024, consider the following statements:
1. Cybercrime cases crossed 1 lakh for the first time.
2. Fraud accounted for about 72.6% of cybercrime cases.
3. Sexual exploitation accounted for more than half of cybercrime cases.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: cybercrime reached 1,01,928 cases in 2024, the first time above 1 lakh, and 72.6% was fraud. Statement 3 is wrong because sexual exploitation was only 3.1% (3,190 cases). So options with statement 3 fail.
130.tq: Cybercrime 2024: 1,01,928 (first time > 1 lakh); 72.6% fraud, 3.1% sexual exploitation.

130.s: Which group of States accounted for most dowry-death cases according to the cited data?
o: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan
Odisha, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala
West Bengal, Assam, Sikkim and Tripura
130.x: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan accounted for most dowry-death cases in the cited data.
130.tq: Recognise the complete State cluster rather than selecting a single high-population State.

130.s: What percentage of women were married before attaining 18 years according to NFHS-5?
130.x: NFHS-5 reported that 23.3% of women were married before the age of 18. NFHS-4 had recorded 26.8%.
130.tq: Distinguish the later NFHS-5 value from the earlier NFHS-4 value.

130.s: According to NFHS-5, what proportion of ever-married women have faced spousal violence?
130.x: NFHS-5 reported that 32% of ever-married women had faced spousal violence.
130.tq: Distinguish the denominator—ever-married women—from the separate age-group indicator.

130.s: Which one of the following correctly states the NFHS-5 figure for women aged 18–49 who have faced physical violence?
130.x: NFHS-5 reported that 29% of women aged 18–49 had faced physical violence.
130.tq: Match the percentage with the precise population category given in the question.

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding marital rape and spousal violence:
1. NFHS-4 reported that 5.4% of women reported marital rape.
2. The marital rape exception in rape law remains in force.
3. The Delhi High Court gave a split verdict on the marital rape exception.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: All three statements are correct: the NFHS-4 figure was 5.4%, the exception remains, and the Delhi High Court delivered a split verdict on it.
130.tq: Combine a survey figure with the legal position and judicial outcome without conflating them.

130.s: According to Census 2011, what was the Child Sex Ratio of India and Andhra Pradesh respectively?
130.x: The Child Sex Ratio was 918 in India and 944 in Andhra Pradesh according to Census 2011.
130.tq: Separate closely related national and State figures before selecting the pair.

130.s: The Child Sex Ratio in India declined from which figure in 2001 to 918 in 2011?
130.x: India's Child Sex Ratio declined from 927 in 2001 to 918 in 2011.
130.tq: Use the direction of change and distinguish the earlier value from the provisional 2011 figure.

130.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the Adult Sex Ratio of India and Andhra Pradesh in Census 2011?
130.x: The Adult Sex Ratio was 943 for India and 996 for Andhra Pradesh in Census 2011.
130.tq: Match the indicator with the correct geographical unit instead of reversing the two figures.

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding NFHS-5 sex-ratio indicators:
1. The overall sex ratio was 1,020.
2. The rural sex ratio was higher than the urban sex ratio.
3. The sex ratio at birth was 929.
4. The overall sex ratio declined from the NFHS-4 figure of 991.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the figures were 1,020 overall, 1,037 rural, 985 urban and 929 at birth. Statement 4 is false because the overall figure increased from 991 in NFHS-4.
130.tq: Spot the reversed trend in the final statement while retaining the correct numerical set.

130.s: Under the Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act, 1994, prenatal diagnostic techniques are permitted primarily for detecting:
o: The future educational needs of the child
The economic status of the family
The sex of the foetus for parental choice
130.x: The PCPNDT Act permits diagnostic procedures for detecting genetic abnormalities, while prohibiting sex selection and prenatal sex determination.
130.tq: Identify the legally permitted purpose rather than the prohibited use of diagnosis.

130.s: Approximately how many girls are stated to go “missing” every year in the context of sex-selective discrimination?
130.x: The estimated number is about 3 million girls every year.
130.tq: Convert the stated magnitude carefully and avoid confusing lakh and million scales.

130.s: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched in 2015 primarily to address the decline in the:
130.x: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched in 2015 to address the declining Child Sex Ratio and related discrimination against girls. It now covers all districts.
130.tq: Link the scheme to its specifically stated demographic target.

130.s: The PCPNDT law prohibits
o: collection of census data on sex ratio
130.x: The PCPNDT law bans advertising sex determination as part of the legal response to sex-selective practices.
130.tq: Apply the statutory objective to a concrete prohibited practice.

130.s: The Supreme Court judgment in Shakti Vahini v Union of India (2018) dealt primarily with:
o: interference by khaps in marriages of consenting adults
the two-finger test in rape cases
130.x: Shakti Vahini addressed honour crimes and held that khap interference in marriages of consenting adults is illegal, while prescribing preventive, remedial and punitive measures.
130.tq: Match the case with its subject matter and distinguish it from other rights-related judgments.

130.s: Which earlier Supreme Court decision affirmed the right of adults to marry?
130.x: Lata Singh (2006) affirmed the right of consenting adults to marry.
130.tq: Arrange the judicial authorities by subject and year to identify the earlier precedent.

130.s: The Law Commission’s 242nd Report, submitted in 2012, proposed a draft law concerning:
o: abolition of the National Investigation Agency
interference in matrimonial alliances in the name of honour
recognition of trafficking victims as offenders
regulation of private hospitals treating acid victims
130.x: The 242nd Law Commission Report proposed a draft law against interference in matrimonial alliances in the name of honour.
130.tq: Identify the report’s exact subject rather than a broadly related women’s-rights issue.

130.s:
Honour killings violate which of the following Fundamental Rights provisions?
1. Article 14
2. Article 15
3. Article 19
4. Article 21
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: Honour killings violate Articles 14, 15, 19 and 21, which respectively protect equality, prohibit discrimination, protect freedoms and safeguard life and personal liberty.
130.tq: Check the complete constitutional grouping instead of selecting only the most familiar right.

130.s: Honour killings are prosecuted as murder under which provision of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita?
130.x: Honour killings are prosecuted as murder under Section 103 of the BNS.
130.tq: Discriminate among nearby BNS section numbers by matching the offence category.

130.s: Protective homes under the ITPA are run by
130.x: States run protective homes under the framework of the ITPA.
130.tq: Identify the responsible level of government rather than the central coordinating body.

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Palermo Protocol:
1. It supplements the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime.
2. India has ratified it.
3. It deals specifically with trafficking in persons, especially women and children.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: All three statements are correct. The Palermo Protocol supplements the UNTOC and addresses trafficking in persons, particularly women and children; India has ratified it.
130.tq: Check each statement against the instrument’s purpose, legal relationship and ratification status.

130.s: Under the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956, which of the following is correct?
o: Prostitution itself is treated as a crime in every circumstance.
Only trafficking of children is punishable.
Brothel-keeping, pimping, soliciting and living on the earnings of prostitution are punishable acts.
The Act abolishes protective homes maintained by State Governments.
130.x: The ITPA does not treat prostitution per se as a crime, but penalises activities such as brothel-keeping, pimping, soliciting and living on prostitution earnings.
130.tq: Use the distinction between the activity itself and associated exploitative activities.

130.s: Under Section 143 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which principle applies to trafficking?
o: Consent is relevant only if the trafficking is inter-State.
The victim’s consent is always a complete defence.
Consent matters only when the victim is an adult male.
130.x: Section 143 of the BNS treats the victim’s consent as immaterial in determining the offence of trafficking.
130.tq: Discriminate between consent as a defence and the statutory rule that consent is immaterial.

130.s: Which of the following was a feature of the Trafficking of Persons Bill, 2018?
o: It limited shelters to private institutions only.
It was enacted by both Houses without lapse.
It removed all provisions relating to rehabilitation.
It proposed aggravated trafficking and aiding trafficking as new offences.
130.x: The 2018 Bill proposed new offences including aggravated trafficking and aiding trafficking, and also provided for shelters and rehabilitation. It was passed by the Lok Sabha but later lapsed.
130.tq: Test the bill’s substantive provisions separately from its legislative status.

130.s:
With reference to the Trafficking of Persons Bill, 2018, consider the following statements:
1. It was passed by the Lok Sabha.
2. It subsequently lapsed.
3. It proposed the National Investigation Agency as the national investigating agency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: The 2018 Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha and later lapsed. The proposal to designate the NIA as the national investigating agency belonged to the 2021 draft Bill.
130.tq: Separate closely related legislative proposals by year and avoid transferring a feature from one draft to another.

130.s: The 2021 draft Bill relating to trafficking proposed which agency as the national investigating agency?
130.x: The 2021 draft Bill proposed the National Investigation Agency (NIA) as the national investigating agency for trafficking-related matters.
130.tq: Use the agency-name trap among bodies with overlapping law-enforcement roles.

130.s: The UNODC Global Report on Trafficking in Persons, 2016, observed that victims and traffickers often:
o: have no prior social relationship of any kind
belong to entirely different regions and social backgrounds
belong only to organised international networks
130.x: The 2016 UNODC report noted that victims and traffickers often share the same background.
130.tq: Recall the precise relationship highlighted in the report without substituting a stronger generalisation.

130.s: Which State was reported to have the most trafficking cases in the NCRB 2024 data cited?
130.x: Telangana was reported as having the most trafficking cases in the cited NCRB 2024 data.
130.tq: Test the location-specific conclusion rather than the total case figure.

130.s: Trafficking cases registered under the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act increased by approximately what percentage between 2022 and 2023?
130.x: Trafficking cases under the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act rose by about 44.7% between 2022 and 2023.
130.tq: Match the percentage to the correct subject and time period.

130.s: Anti-Human Trafficking Units are best described as:
o: Judicial tribunals that exclusively decide marital disputes
Central police units dealing only with cybercrime
District-level task forces funded by MHA for trafficking intelligence, rescue and prosecution
Village-level bodies responsible only for issuing identity documents
130.x: AHTUs are district-level task forces funded by the Ministry of Home Affairs for trafficking intelligence, rescue and prosecution.
130.tq: Identify the body by its level, funding authority and complete operational functions.

130.s: Which provision of the Constitution of India prohibits traffic in human beings?
130.x: Article 23(1) prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour. Article 21A is the right to education, Article 24 bars child labour in hazardous employment, and Article 39(f) is a Directive Principle on protecting children from exploitation.
130.tq: Trafficking = Art. 23(1); BNS s.143.

130.s: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 was enacted in the immediate aftermath of the:
130.x: The 2013 amendment followed the December 2012 Delhi gang rape, commonly referred to as the Nirbhaya case.
130.tq: Use the event-year association and distinguish the context of the 2013 and 2018 amendments.

130.s:
The Justice J.S. Verma Committee report led to amendments to which of the following laws in 2013?
1. Indian Penal Code
2. Code of Criminal Procedure
3. Indian Evidence Act
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 amended the IPC, CrPC and Indian Evidence Act following the Justice J.S. Verma Committee report.
130.tq: Check the full legislative set instead of stopping at the most familiar statute.

130.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched under the 2013 criminal law amendments?
130.x: Disrobing was provided under Section 354B IPC, not Section 354E. Sections 354A, 354C and 354D relate respectively to sexual harassment, voyeurism and stalking.
130.tq: Find the wrong statutory pairing among closely numbered provisions.

130.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (IPC provision)
a. Section 326A
b. Section 326B
c. Section 354C
d. Section 376E

List-II (offence or punishment)
i. Voyeurism
ii. Death for repeat rapists
iii. Acid attack
iv. Attempt to acid attack

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
130.x: Section 326A concerns acid attack, Section 326B attempt to acid attack, Section 354C voyeurism and Section 376E death for repeat rapists.
130.tq: Start with the sure statutory pairs and eliminate codes containing a swapped offence.

130.s: Which one of the following statements regarding rape under the 2013 amendment is correct?
o: Rape was confined to penile-vaginal penetration.
Penetration by objects or body parts and oral acts were included, with a minimum punishment of seven years.
The minimum punishment was reduced to five years.
Only consensual acts involving adults were covered.
130.x: The 2013 amendment widened the definition of rape to include penetration by objects or body parts and oral acts, while keeping the minimum punishment at seven years (it was raised to ten years in 2018).
130.tq: Test the expanded definition together with the associated minimum punishment.

130.s: The Supreme Court struck down the two-finger test in which case?
o: Lata Singh v State of Uttar Pradesh
Shakti Vahini v Union of India
130.x: The Supreme Court struck down the two-finger test in Lillu v State in 2013.
130.tq: Match the judicial directive with the correct case name.

130.s:
Which of the following was recommended by the Justice J.S. Verma Committee but not adopted in the same form by Parliament?
1. Criminalisation of marital rape
2. No death penalty for rape
3. Keeping the age of consent at 16 years
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: The Verma Committee recommended criminalising marital rape, opposed the death penalty for rape and recommended retaining the age of consent at 16. Parliament raised the age of consent to 18 years.
130.tq: Separate committee recommendations from the final legislative choices.

130.s: Who among the following was NOT a member of the Justice J.S. Verma Committee as listed?
130.x: The listed members were Justice J.S. Verma, Justice Leila Seth and Gopal Subramanium. Justice Ranjana Desai was not among them.
130.tq: Use the committee-membership trap by identifying the outsider in a closely related judicial group.

130.s: Which of the following was NOT a principal policy outcome associated with the December 2012 Nirbhaya case?
130.x: The principal listed outcomes were the Justice Verma Committee, the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 2013, the Nirbhaya Fund and the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015. The BNS was not among those immediate policy outcomes.
130.tq: Use the event’s immediate policy timeline to eliminate a later legal enactment.

130.s: The Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 permits 16–18-year-olds to be tried as adults in cases involving:
130.x: The Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 permits 16–18-year-olds to be tried as adults for heinous crimes, subject to the statutory process.
130.tq: Reject the extreme “all offences” formulation and apply the age-and-offence condition together.

130.s: Nirbhay Raho is an initiative of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj undertaken with which partners and supported under which fund?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development and NLSIU; Nirbhaya Fund
Ministry of Home Affairs and WHO; Central Victim Compensation Fund
Ministry of Law and Finance Commission; Union Consolidated Fund only
Ministry of Education and UNICEF; PM CARES Fund
130.x: Nirbhay Raho is a Ministry of Panchayati Raj initiative with the Ministry of Women and Child Development and NLSIU, under the Nirbhaya Fund.
130.tq: Match the implementing ministry, partner institutions and funding source without swapping neighbouring bodies.

130.s: Which of the following correctly lists the three components of the Nirbhay Raho initiative?
o: Nirbhay Netri, Nirbhay Chetna and Nirbhay Drishti
130.x: The three components are Nirbhay Netri, Nirbhay Chetna and Nirbhay Drishti.
130.tq: Separate the initiative’s component names from the related Mission Shakti and Nirbhaya Fund programmes.

130.s:
Match the offence introduced by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 with its corresponding section in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita:
a. Acid attack (IPC 326A)
b. Sexual harassment (IPC 354A)
c. Stalking (IPC 354D)
d. Death for repeat rapists (IPC 376E)
i. Section 75
ii. Section 71
iii. Section 124(1)
iv. Section 78
130.x: Acid attack (326A) is now BNS 124(1), sexual harassment (354A) is BNS 75, stalking (354D) is BNS 78, and death for repeat rapists (376E) is BNS 71. The other codes swap these pairs.

130.s: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018 was enacted in the context of which cases?
130.x: The 2018 amendment followed public concern arising from the Kathua and Unnao cases and was associated with the fast-track court response.
130.tq: Link the amendment to its immediate factual context without confusing it with the 2013 background.

130.s: Which time-limit combination is associated with the 2018 criminal law changes?
o: Investigation two months, trial two months and appeals six months
Investigation one month, trial six months and appeals one year
Investigation two months, trial six months and appeals one month
Investigation six months, trial two months and appeals two months
130.x: The stated timelines were two months for investigation, two months for trial and six months for appeals.
130.tq: Match each procedural stage with its specific time limit instead of relying on one familiar figure.

130.s: In the cases covered by the 2018 amendment, anticipatory bail was barred in relation to rape of a girl:
130.x: The 2018 amendment barred anticipatory bail in cases involving rape of a girl below 16 years.
130.tq: Distinguish the specific statutory age threshold from broader child-protection categories.

130.s: Which of the following punishment changes was made by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018?
o: Anticipatory bail became mandatory in rape cases involving minors.
All offences against children were made compoundable.
The minimum punishment for rape was reduced from seven to five years.
The minimum punishment for rape was raised from seven to ten years.
130.x: The 2018 amendment raised the minimum punishment for rape from seven years to ten years.
130.tq: Test the direction and magnitude of the statutory change rather than the offence name alone.

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018:
1. Rape of a girl below 16 years attracted a minimum punishment of 20 years.
2. Rape of a girl below 12 years could attract imprisonment for 20 years to life or the death penalty.
3. Gang rape of a girl below 12 years could attract life imprisonment or the death penalty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: All three are 2018 changes. Rape of a girl under 16 carries a minimum of 20 years. Rape of a girl under 12 carries 20 years to life or death, and gang rape of a girl under 12 carries life or death.
130.tq: Separate age thresholds and punishment ranges carefully; do not merge the under-16 and under-12 categories.

130.s: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the new offence relating to sexual intercourse by deceitful means, including a false promise of marriage or job and identity fraud, is contained in Section:
130.x: Section 69 of the BNS addresses sexual intercourse by deceitful means, including a false promise of marriage or job and identity fraud.
130.tq: Match the specific offence with its provision number, separating it from trafficking and minor-sale provisions.

130.s:
With reference to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, consider the following statements:
1. It retains the IPC provisions relating to rape, stalking and voyeurism.
2. It raises the age for the gang-rape provision from 16 to 18 years.
3. It treats consent as material for establishing trafficking in every case.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because consent is immaterial for the trafficking offence under Section 143.
130.tq: Identify the deliberate reversal of the legal rule concerning consent in trafficking.

130.s: Safe City Projects and ERSS-112 are funded from the:
130.x: Safe City Projects and ERSS-112 receive funding from the Nirbhaya Fund, which is dedicated to women’s-safety projects.
130.tq: Match the safety initiative with its dedicated funding source.

130.s: The One Stop Centre (Sakhi) Scheme has been in operation since:
130.x: One Stop Centres have operated since 2015.
130.tq: Separate the launch year of the mechanism from the year of the Nirbhaya case and later laws.

130.s:
Which of the following mechanisms is funded by the Nirbhaya Fund?
1. One Stop Centres
2. Women Helpline 181
3. ERSS 112
4. Central Victim Compensation Fund
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
130.x: The One Stop Centres, Women Helpline 181 and ERSS 112 are funded by the Nirbhaya Fund. The Central Victim Compensation Fund receives a one-time grant from that Fund.
130.tq: Track the common funding source across the institutional mechanisms rather than confusing it with the Union Budget source.

130.s: The Women Helpline 181 was universalised from 2015 and is being integrated with:
130.x: Women Helpline 181 was universalised from 2015 and is being integrated with ERSS-112.
130.tq: Distinguish the emergency-response integration from other legal and oversight institutions.

130.s: The Central Victim Compensation Fund supports State victim-compensation schemes and receives:
o: Annual grants only from municipal bodies
Funds exclusively from the Central Vigilance Commission
A one-time grant from the Nirbhaya Fund
A loan from the World Bank
130.x: The Central Victim Compensation Fund supports State schemes through a one-time grant from the Nirbhaya Fund.
130.tq: Identify the specific source of a grant rather than the body associated with the word “Central.”

130.s:
Which of the following is correctly classified under Mission Shakti?
1. Sambal includes One Stop Centres, Women Helpline 181 and Nari Adalat.
2. Samarthya includes Shakti Sadan and PMMVY.
3. Sambal is the empowerment component, whereas Samarthya is the safety component.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
130.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 reverses the classification: Sambal concerns safety, while Samarthya concerns empowerment.
130.tq: Watch for the reversed comparison between the two Mission Shakti components.

130.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) uses the single emergency number 112.
2. The Nirbhaya Fund is a non-lapsable corpus created after the 2012 Delhi case.
3. Women Helpline 181 is being replaced by the Witness Protection Scheme.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: ERSS works on the single number 112 (asked in APPSC 2018), and the Nirbhaya Fund is a non-lapsable corpus set up after the 2012 case. Statement 3 is wrong: 181 is being integrated with ERSS-112, not replaced by the Witness Protection Scheme.
130.tq: ERSS = 112; Nirbhaya Fund = non-lapsable corpus (2013).

130.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) ITSSO
(b) NDSO
(c) CCTNS
(d) Cri-MAC

List-II
(i) Links police stations
(ii) National database of convicted sexual offenders
(iii) Tracks time-bound investigation of sexual offences
(iv) Real-time sharing of information on significant crimes

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
130.x: ITSSO tracks investigation timelines; NDSO is the database of convicted sexual offenders; CCTNS links police stations; Cri-MAC enables real-time crime information sharing.
130.tq: Start with the distinctive purpose of each database and then eliminate codes.

130.s: The National Database on Sexual Offenders (NDSO) is best described as:
o: A police-only database of convicted sexual offenders
A public database of all persons accused of any offence
A database linking all State police stations
A database of missing children maintained by courts
130.x: NDSO, established by the NCRB in 2018, is a police-only national database of convicted sexual offenders.
130.tq: Distinguish convicted offenders from accused persons and identify the user group.

130.s: Safe City Projects include:
o: A national database of convicted sexual offenders
Free transport for women stranded at night in rural areas
CCTV and AI-based public safety measures for women in eight major cities
Only the construction of women’s prisons in every district
130.x: Safe City Projects use CCTV and artificial intelligence-based public-safety measures for women in eight major cities.
130.tq: Distinguish an urban technology project from databases, courts and transport schemes.

130.s: The Fast Track Special Courts (FTSC) scheme is a centrally sponsored scheme funded from the Nirbhaya Fund and primarily deals with:
o: Only cases under the Dowry Prohibition Act
130.x: The FTSC scheme is a centrally sponsored scheme funded from the Nirbhaya Fund for cases involving rape and offences under POCSO.
130.tq: Combine the scheme’s funding source with its subject-matter jurisdiction.

130.s: The FTSC scheme, which followed the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018, was extended up to:
130.x: The FTSC scheme was extended up to March 2026 and covered 790 courts under the stated extension.
130.tq: Separate the scheme’s extension date from later reported court-functioning figures.

130.s: Under the POCSO Act, a special court may be designated by:
o: A Sessions Court in each district
A Magistrate’s Court in each village
A High Court only for the entire State
The Union Cabinet for every Union Territory
130.x: The POCSO Act permits a Sessions Court to be designated as a special court in each district. Pendency remains a major challenge.
130.tq: Identify the judicial level and territorial unit specified in the provision.

130.s: The Nirbhaya Fund was established in:
130.x: The Nirbhaya Fund was established in 2013 as a dedicated corpus for projects related to women’s safety.
130.tq: Link the fund’s establishment year with its purpose, not with a later scheme.

130.s: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 provided for:
o: The designation of every Sessions Court as a POCSO court
The establishment of Safe City Projects in eight cities
Death penalty for repeat rape offenders (Section 376E IPC)
130.x: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 inserted Section 376E IPC, allowing death or life imprisonment for repeat rape offenders. Special POCSO courts come from the POCSO Act 2012, Safe City Projects and NDSO (2018) are later administrative measures, and the FTSC scheme (2019) followed the 2018 Act.
130.tq: Distinguish a statutory provision from later administrative schemes and databases.

130.s: In which State was India's first women's court set up?
130.x: The first women's court was set up in West Bengal (APPSC-GS 2019). Kerala had the first all-women police station (Kozhikode, 1973), Odisha announced 45 fast-track courts in 2019, and Andhra Pradesh is linked to the Disha model, so those options are traps.
130.tq: First women's court = West Bengal; first all-women police station = Kozhikode.

130.s: In 2025, Fast Track Special Courts disposed of 87,754 POCSO cases against 80,320 cases registered. What disposal rate does this give?
130.x: 87,754 disposals against 80,320 registrations is a disposal rate of about 109%, meaning FTSCs disposed of more cases than were newly registered. The other figures do not match this ratio.
130.tq: FTSC 2025: 109% disposal rate (87,754 vs 80,320).

130.s: What percentage of India’s police force was reported to be women?
130.x: Women constituted only 11.7% of India’s police force according to the cited figure.
130.tq: Distinguish the police representation figure from the violence-related survey percentages.

130.s: The first all-women police station in India was established at:
130.x: The first all-women police station was established at Kozhikode in Kerala in 1973.
130.tq: Use the exact place and year rather than substituting a prominent State capital.

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding gender sensitisation of the police:
1. Women Help Desks are established in police stations.
2. Mahila Police Volunteers are a measure associated with the Ministry of Women and Child Development and the Ministry of Home Affairs.
3. Mahila Police Volunteers are funded exclusively through the Union Budget, 2013 Nirbhaya corpus.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Women Help Desks are set up in police stations, and Mahila Police Volunteers are a joint MWCD-MHA measure. Statement 3 is wrong because MPVs only drew on the Nirbhaya Fund; they were not funded 'exclusively' from it.
130.tq: Reject the unsupported exclusive funding claim while retaining the stated institutional measures.

130.s: The Witness Protection Scheme, 2018 is enforced under Article 141 until:
o: All States adopt separate constitutional amendments
The Supreme Court withdraws every protection order
130.x: The Witness Protection Scheme, 2018 operates under Article 141 until Parliament enacts a law on the subject.
130.tq: Identify the stated constitutional interim basis and its legislative endpoint.

130.s: The Disha Bill of Andhra Pradesh was introduced primarily as a response to:
130.x: The Disha Bill was Andhra Pradesh’s legislative response to the 2019 Hyderabad veterinarian rape-murder case.
130.tq: Match the legislation with the immediate triggering event.

130.s: Under the Disha Act, the prescribed time structure for investigation and trial of rape cases is:
o: Investigation in 14 days and trial in 7 days
Investigation in 14 days and trial in 21 days
Investigation in 7 days and trial in 14 days
Investigation in 21 days and trial in 14 days
130.x: The Disha Act specifies seven days for investigation and fourteen days for trial, making a total of twenty-one days.
130.tq: Separate the two components of the total time limit.

130.s: Which one of the following is NOT associated with the provisions of the Disha Act?
o: Mandatory forensic evidence in relevant cases
Death sentence for rape and gang rape
Penalties for cyber-stalking and deepfake misuse
A special court only at the State capital
130.x: The Disha Act provides for a special court in every district, not merely one special court at the State capital.
130.tq: Find the option that reverses the scope of a stated institutional provision.

130.s: Why does the Disha Act require the assent of the President of India?
o: It seeks to amend the Constitution.
It deals with subjects exclusively placed in the Union List.
It creates a new High Court in Andhra Pradesh.
Criminal law is included in the Concurrent List.
130.x: The Disha Act requires Presidential assent because criminal law falls in the Concurrent List. It has not come into force as passed.
130.tq: Ask which constitutional distribution of legislative power explains the requirement.

130.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Disha App — SOS alerts for women in distress or danger
2. Abhayam — Chittoor police awareness campaign for the safety of women and children
3. Abhay pilot — Free pick-up and drop for women stranded between 9 p.m. and 5 a.m.
4. Mahila Samrakshana Karyadarsi — Women-protection functionaries in village and ward secretariats
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
130.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Abhayam was associated with Chittoor, while the Abhay pilot was implemented by Prakasam police at Ongole.
130.tq: Verify the purpose and location attached to each similarly named initiative.

130.s: Which of the following statements about recent Andhra Pradesh measures is correct?
o: Shakti Teams are used along with Sexual Offender Sheets of repeat offenders.
Sexual Offender Sheets are maintained only for first-time offenders.
Shakti Teams are special courts under the Disha Act.
Trishul committees deal exclusively with cybercrime.
130.x: Shakti Teams are used along with Sexual Offender Sheets for repeat offenders. Trishul committees have a broader three-part zero-tolerance mandate.
130.tq: Use the institutional-function distinction to reject swapped roles.

130.s:
The Trishul committees in Andhra Pradesh are associated with which of the following objectives?
1. Zero drugs
2. Zero tolerance to atrocities against women
3. Zero road accidents
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
130.x: Trishul committees are described as state and district panels pursuing zero drugs, zero tolerance to atrocities against women and zero road accidents.
130.tq: Treat a three-part slogan as three separate testable components.

130.s:
The further 4.4% decline in crimes against women in Andhra Pradesh was credited to which of the following?
1. Shakti Teams
2. Women’s Safety Week rallies
3. Sexual Offender Sheets
4. Replacement of all police stations by women police stations
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
130.x: The decline was credited to Shakti Teams, Women’s Safety Week rallies and Sexual Offender Sheets. There is no record that all police stations were replaced by women police stations.
130.tq: Reject the absolute institutional claim and retain the three specifically cited measures.

130.s: The APSES 2024–25 objective concerning crimes against women is to achieve:
o: A uniform conviction rate of 100% in every district
The highest crime rate in the country with ordinary courts only
One of the lowest crime rates and special courts for atrocity cases
130.x: APSES 2024–25 aims for one of the lowest crime rates and provides for special courts for atrocity cases.
130.tq: Select the measured policy objective and avoid an absolute numerical claim not stated.

130.s: The number of crimes against women reported in Andhra Pradesh declined from 25,503 in 2022 to 22,418 in 2023 and to how many in 2024?
130.x: Crimes against women in Andhra Pradesh fell to 19,952 in 2024, from 22,418 in 2023 and 25,503 in 2022. 17,149 is the number of arrests, not cases.
130.tq: Follow the year-wise sequence and avoid confusing cases with arrests.

130.s: According to Crime in India 2024, which one of the following statements is correct regarding overall crime and cybercrime in India?
o: Total crime declined by 6%, while cybercrime increased by 17.9%.
Total crime increased by 6%, while cybercrime declined by 17.9%.
Both total crime and cybercrime declined by 6%.
Both total crime and cybercrime increased by 17.9%.
130.x: Crime in India 2024 recorded a 6% fall in total crime, whereas cybercrime increased by 17.9%.
130.tq: Use the reversed-trend trap by separately checking the direction of change for total crime and cybercrime.

130.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Women, Peace and Security Index 2023 is correct?
130.x: The comparative position cited for the Women, Peace and Security Index 2023 was 128 out of 177. A later publication printed 131, creating a reported variation in the cited figure.
130.tq: Resolve a close-number confusion by matching the rank with the correct total number of countries.

130.s:
Consider the following statements about crimes against women in India:
1. Cases involving crimes against women have been reported to have more than 90% pendency.
2. The opposition, citing Crime in India 2024, stated that crimes against women had risen by 42.6% since 2013.
3. The reported 42.6% increase refers to cybercrime alone.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the 42.6% claim concerned crimes against women overall, not cybercrime alone.
130.tq: Separate an overall crime-against-women claim from the distinct cybercrime trend.

130.s: Which one of the following is a major criticism of the death penalty in cases involving sexual offences?
o: It makes rape laws completely gender-neutral.
It may discourage victims from reporting offences.
It necessarily eliminates delays in criminal trials.
It prevents all cases from reaching fast-track courts.
130.x: A stated criticism is that the death penalty may discourage reporting by victims or affected families. It does not automatically eliminate trial delays or make rape law gender-neutral.
130.tq: Identify the policy criticism rather than assuming that a severe punishment solves every procedural problem.

130.s: With reference to debates on rape law in India, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Rape law has been criticised for not being gender-neutral.
Gender neutrality has eliminated all criticism of rape law.
The debate concerns only the speed of investigation and not the scope of the law.
Rape law is universally regarded as gender-neutral.
130.x: The non-gender-neutral character of rape law is a criticism. The debate is not confined only to investigation speed.
130.tq: Avoid the absolute-word trap in statements claiming that a legal debate has been completely settled.

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding fast-track justice and related concerns:
1. Trials may remain prolonged despite the existence of fast-track courts.
2. Rising disposals can coexist with falling POCSO conviction rates.
3. Fast-track courts, by themselves, guarantee a 100% conviction rate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because fast-track courts do not guarantee a 100% conviction rate.
130.tq: Reject the absolute claim that an institutional mechanism automatically guarantees a particular outcome.

130.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Model or initiative)
 a. Disha model
 b. Nirbhaya Act
 c. Shakti Teams
 d. SHe-Box 2.0

List-II (Associated feature)
 i. Single-window portal for workplace harassment complaints
 ii. Two-month probe
 iii. Twenty-one-day verdict model
 iv. Current Andhra Pradesh policing model

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
130.x: The Disha model is associated with a 21-day verdict, the Nirbhaya Act with a two-month probe, Shakti Teams with the current Andhra Pradesh policing model, and SHe-Box 2.0 with the workplace-harassment complaint portal.
130.tq: Start with the sure pair and then eliminate codes using the distinctive time limits and institutional roles.

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding sex-ratio figures:
1. Andhra Pradesh has a higher adult sex ratio than India.
2. Andhra Pradesh has a higher child sex ratio than India.
3. India’s adult sex ratio and child sex ratio are 996 and 944, respectively.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Andhra Pradesh records 996 and 944 against India’s 943 and 918. Statement 3 reverses the State and national figures.
130.tq: Compare both rows of a paired State–India table before selecting the coded option.

130.s: Which of the following measures was ordered by Chief Minister Naidu in relation to crimes against women in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Replacement of Shakti Teams by a two-month investigation period
A uniform 21-day verdict for every criminal case in the State
Formation of Trishul committees and a police response time of 30 minutes
Abolition of Sexual Offender Sheets and withdrawal of conviction targets
130.x: The measures included Trishul committees, a police response time of 30 minutes, and an emphasis on improving conviction rates.
130.tq: Match the executive direction with the correct State-level institutional measures, not with unrelated time limits.

130.s: SHe-Box 2.0, associated with the Ministry of Women and Child Development, is primarily:
o: A police database containing Sexual Offender Sheets in 22 States
A judicial platform for issuing 21-day verdicts in sexual-offence cases
A single-window portal for workplace harassment complaints available in 22 languages
A portal exclusively for reporting cybercrime against children in 30 languages
130.x: SHe-Box 2.0 is a Ministry of Women and Child Development single-window portal for workplace harassment complaints and is available in 22 languages.
130.tq: Use the body-function-language combination to distinguish the portal from policing and judicial mechanisms.

131.s: Which Articles of the Constitution provide for equal franchise in the context of women voters?
131.x: Articles 325 and 326 provide the constitutional basis for equal electoral franchise.
131.tq: Distinguish voting rights provisions from provisions concerning eligibility to contest elections.

131.s: Articles 84 and 173 are relevant to women in elections because they concern:
o: The ability of women to contest elections
The delimitation of constituencies for women voters
The reservation of seats for women in local bodies
The appointment of women as Election Commissioners
131.x: Articles 84 and 173 relate to qualifications for membership of Parliament and State Legislatures, respectively, and thereby permit women to contest elections when the qualifications are met.
131.tq: Separate contesting eligibility from the constitutional provisions governing the franchise.

131.s:
Consider the following statements regarding women's electoral participation:
1. Women's turnout exceeded men's for the first time in 2019.
2. Women's turnout again exceeded men's in 2024.
3. The ECI's SVEEP programme targets women voters.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
131.x: Women's turnout first exceeded men's in 2019, did so again in 2024, and women voters are among the targets of the ECI's SVEEP programme.
131.tq: Combine the trend, repetition of the trend and the relevant voter-awareness programme.

131.s: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam is associated with the
131.x: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam is the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, receiving assent in 2023.
131.tq: Match the popular name of the amendment with its constitutional number and assent year.

131.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to women's reservation in chronological order:
A. Constitution (106th Amendment) Act enacted
B. 108th Amendment Bill passed by the Rajya Sabha
C. 81st Amendment Bill introduced
D. 108th Amendment Bill lapsed with the 15th Lok Sabha
131.x: The 81st Amendment Bill was introduced in 1996, the 108th Bill was passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2010, it lapsed in 2014, and the 106th Amendment was enacted in 2023.
131.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest Bill and the final enacted amendment.

131.s: The Women's Reservation Bill introduced in 1996 was known as the:
131.x: The Bill introduced in 1996 during the Deve Gowda government was the 81st Amendment Bill.
131.tq: Use the year-Bill number association to distinguish earlier attempts from later versions.

131.s:
Consider the following statements about the 108th Amendment Bill:
1. It was introduced in the Rajya Sabha in 2008.
2. It was passed by the Rajya Sabha on 9 March 2010.
3. It lapsed with the 15th Lok Sabha in 2014.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
131.x: The 108th Amendment Bill was introduced in the Rajya Sabha in 2008, passed there on 9 March 2010, and lapsed with the 15th Lok Sabha in 2014.
131.tq: Verify the legislative history as a sequence of introduction, passage and lapse.

131.s: Which of the following correctly states the relationship between the 2023 Women's Reservation Bill and the Constitution?
o: The 108th Amendment Bill was enacted as the 106th Amendment Act in 2023.
The 106th Amendment Bill was enacted as the 128th Amendment Act.
The 81st Amendment Bill was revived and enacted without modification.
The 128th Amendment Bill was enacted as the 106th Amendment Act.
131.x: The 2023 Bill was introduced as the 128th Amendment Bill and was enacted as the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023.
131.tq: Keep the Bill number and enacted Amendment number distinct.

131.s: Which of the following measures came first in empowering women politically in India?
o: Setting up the National Commission for Women
Reserving seats for women in local bodies
Introducing the Women's Reservation Bill for legislatures
131.x: Reserving seats for women in local bodies came first (73rd/74th Amendments) and is the APPSC 2007 key. The NCW, SHGs and a Reservation Bill for legislatures came after, so they are not the answer.
131.tq: Local-body reservation first; legislature quota (106th) came much later.

131.s: Which one of the following statements about the 106th Constitutional Amendment is NOT correct?
o: It came into operation immediately upon assent without any delimitation condition.
It covers the Delhi Legislative Assembly through an amendment to Article 239AA.
131.x: The Amendment does not operate immediately upon assent; commencement depends on delimitation based on the first Census after the Act. The other three statements are correct.
131.tq: Identify the false immediate-effect claim by checking the commencement condition.

131.s: Under Article 334A, the reservation of seats for women is to be rotated:
o: Every five years irrespective of delimitation
131.x: Article 334A provides for rotation of the reserved seats after each delimitation.
131.tq: Distinguish the constitutional trigger for rotation from the ordinary election cycle.

131.s: Under the current law described for the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, the quota is linked to the 2027 Census and is therefore not enforceable before approximately:
131.x: Because commencement depends on the Census and subsequent delimitation, the quota is linked to the 2027 Census and is not expected to be enforceable before 2034 under the current law.
131.tq: Track the sequence of Census, delimitation and implementation rather than selecting the first relevant year.

131.s: Implementation of the women’s reservation under the 106th Amendment is linked to delimitation based on:
o: The first Census conducted after the Act, namely the 2027 Census
131.x: The reservation is to commence only after delimitation based on the first Census after the Act, i.e. the 2027 Census.
131.tq: Connect commencement with the specified future Census and delimitation condition.

131.s: The Constitution (106th Amendment) Act provides reservation for women of:
o: One-third of the seats in the Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and Delhi Assembly, including within SC/ST seats
One-fourth of the seats in the Lok Sabha only
One-third of seats only in State Assemblies and municipalities
One-half of the seats in all legislatures, excluding SC/ST seats
131.x: The amendment provides reservation of one-third of seats in the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly, including one-third within the seats reserved for SCs and STs.
131.tq: Check the institutions covered and whether sub-reservation within SC/ST seats is included.

131.s: From 17 April 2026, the women's reservation under the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act was stated to be in force for the Assemblies of:
131.x: The reservation was stated to be in force for the Jammu and Kashmir and Puducherry Assemblies from 17 April 2026.
131.tq: Match the effective date with the exact pair of Assemblies named.

131.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the reservation provided under the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023:
1. It provides one-third reservation in the Lok Sabha.
2. It provides one-third reservation in State Legislative Assemblies.
3. It includes one-third of the seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
4. It provides reservation in the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
131.x: The Act provides one-third reservation in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies, including one-third of SC/ST-reserved seats. It does not provide reservation in the Rajya Sabha.
131.tq: Find the excluded chamber while retaining the correct scope of the quota.

131.s: Which of the following is NOT provided under the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023?
o: An OBC or BC sub-quota within the women's reservation
One-third reservation in the Delhi Legislative Assembly
Rotation of reserved seats after delimitation
One-third reservation in State Legislative Assemblies
131.x: The Act does not provide an OBC or BC sub-quota. It provides reservation in the specified legislatures and provides for rotation after delimitation.
131.tq: Look for the specific exclusion among otherwise correct features of the amendment.

131.s: The duration of reservation under the 106th Amendment is:
o: 20 years, extendable only by the Election Commission
131.x: The reservation is provided for 15 years and may be extended by Parliament.
131.tq: Distinguish a fixed constitutional duration from permanent or election-cycle arrangements.

131.s:
Match the Article inserted by the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 with its subject:
a. Article 330A
b. Article 332A
c. Article 239AA(2)(ba)
d. Article 334A
i. Delhi Legislative Assembly
ii. Commencement and duration of the reservation
iii. Lok Sabha
iv. State Legislative Assemblies
131.x: Article 330A is the Lok Sabha quota, 332A the State Assemblies quota, 239AA(2)(ba) the Delhi Assembly quota, and 334A deals with commencement, duration and rotation. The other codes swap these pairs.
131.tq: 330A LS, 332A States, 239AA Delhi, 334A commencement/duration.

131.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the proposed 131st Constitutional Amendment Bill, 2026 is correct?
o: It proposed increasing the Lok Sabha strength from 550 to 850 on the basis of the 2011 Census.
It introduced the GST Council into Article 279A.
It restored the nomination of Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha.
It proposed increasing the Rajya Sabha strength from 250 to 550 on the basis of the 2021 Census.
131.x: The 131st Amendment Bill, 2026, sought to expand the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850 seats using the 2011 Census as the basis for delimitation.
131.tq: Use the paired numerical figures and the stated Census basis to identify the proposal.

131.s: The 131st Constitutional Amendment Bill, 2026, was
o: referred to the JPC on 17 December 2024
131.x: The 131st Amendment Bill, 2026 was defeated (negatived) in the Lok Sabha on 17 April 2026. It got 298 votes for and 230 against, short of the 352 needed for the Article 368 special majority. It was not enacted.
131.tq: Separate the fate and date of the amendment proposal from the separately withdrawn delimitation Bill.

131.s: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 was defeated in the Lok Sabha on 17 April 2026 because:
o: It got fewer votes in favour than against
It got 298 votes in favour against 230, short of the 352 needed for the Article 368 special majority
The Rajya Sabha had rejected it first
It needed ratification by half the States, which was refused
131.x: It won a simple majority (298 for, 230 against, of 528 present and voting) but fell short of the 352 votes needed for the special majority under Article 368. It was not defeated on a simple vote, the Rajya Sabha did not vote first, and State ratification was not the reason.
131.tq: 131st Bill: 298-230, needed 352 (Art 368) -> defeated 17 Apr 2026.

131.s: Which State is exempt from reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes in Panchayats because it has no Scheduled Caste population?
131.x: Arunachal Pradesh is exempt from SC reservation because it has no Scheduled Caste population.
131.tq: Test the specific constitutional exception rather than the general reservation rule.

131.s: The constitutional provision corresponding to the one-third reservation of seats for women in Municipalities is:
131.x: Article 243T(3) provides for reservation of not less than one-third of directly elected seats in Municipalities for women.
131.tq: Use the D–T distinction to separate Panchayat and Municipality provisions.

131.s:
Which of the following statements regarding reservation in local bodies is correct?
1. Reservation of seats and chairperson offices for SCs and STs is proportionate to population.
2. Chairperson offices are reserved as provided by State law and allotted by rotation.
3. Reservation of seats for backward classes is constitutionally compulsory in every State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
131.x: SC/ST reservation is proportionate to population, and chairperson offices are arranged under State law and rotation. Reservation for backward classes is voluntary, not compulsory in every State.
131.tq: Spot the reversal of a compulsory SC/ST rule and a voluntary backward-class provision.

131.s: Reservation of seats and chairperson offices for SCs and STs in Panchayats is linked to the sunset provision contained in:
131.x: Article 243D(5) links the duration of SC/ST reservation in Panchayats to the period specified under Article 334. The current period is stated as extending to 2030 under the 104th Amendment.
131.tq: Match the local-government reservation rule with the constitutional sunset article.

131.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the duration of reservations in local bodies?
o: Women's reservation has no such sunset provision, whereas SC/ST reservation is linked to the Article 334 period.
All local-body reservations are permanently fixed by the 73rd Amendment.
SC/ST reservation has no constitutional time limit, but women's reservation ends in 2030.
Women's reservation and SC/ST reservation both automatically end in 2030.
131.x: Women's reservation in local bodies has no equivalent sunset provision. SC/ST reservation is linked to Article 334, whose current period extends to 2030 under the 104th Amendment.
131.tq: Compare the duration clauses instead of assuming that all reservation categories have the same limit.

131.s: Under Article 243D(3) of the Constitution, the minimum reservation for women in seats of Panchayats is:
o: One-half of the total seats, excluding SC/ST seats
One-third of the total seats, including one-third of the seats reserved for SCs and STs
131.x: Article 243D(3) provides that not less than one-third of the total seats in every Panchayat, including one-third of the seats reserved for SCs and STs, shall be reserved for women.
131.tq: Test the constitutional minimum against the higher reservation adopted by some States.

131.s: Which provision of the Constitution reserves not less than one-third of the offices of chairpersons in Panchayats at each level for women?
131.x: Article 243D(4) reserves at least one-third of chairperson offices in Panchayats for women. Article 243D(3) covers seats (not chairpersons), 243T(3) covers seats in Municipalities, and 243D(5) links SC/ST reservation to the Article 334 period.
131.tq: Seats 243D(3); chairpersons 243D(4); municipal = 243T.

131.s: The Constitution (73rd Amendment) Act, which introduced one-third reservation for women in Panchayats, came into force on:
131.x: The 73rd Amendment came into force on 24 April 1993, which is why 24 April is National Panchayati Raj Day. The other dates are not its commencement date.
131.tq: 73rd in force 24 April 1993 (Panchayati Raj Day).

131.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the constitutional position regarding reservation for women in Panchayats and Municipalities?
o: The Constitution leaves women's reservation entirely to State legislatures.
The Constitution prescribes a ceiling of one-third and prohibits States from increasing it.
The Constitution prescribes a floor of one-third, and States may provide a higher proportion such as one-half.
The Constitution provides one-half reservation in every local body throughout India.
131.x: The constitutional one-third requirement is a floor, not a ceiling. States may increase women's reservation, and several States provide one-half reservation.
131.tq: Apply the floor-versus-ceiling distinction to a State reservation policy.

131.s: Bokkasam Palem, located in Srikalahasti mandal of Tirupati, is associated with which achievement?
o: It received the first national award for tribal self-governance
It became the first girls’ Panchayat in India
It was ranked first nationally among women-friendly Panchayats
It was the first Panchayat to introduce a BC-women sub-quota
131.x: Bokkasam Palem in Srikalahasti mandal of Tirupati ranked first nationally among women-friendly Panchayats under the Deendayal Upadhyay Panchayat Satat Vikas Awards.
131.tq: Link the place, administrative location and award-related achievement precisely.

131.s: What percentage of seats is reserved for women in Andhra Pradesh local bodies, as specified in the context of women-led Panchayats?
131.x: Andhra Pradesh provides 50 per cent reservation for women in local bodies.
131.tq: Distinguish the State-level local-body figure from the constitutional one-third floor.

131.s: Which was the first State to raise the reservation for women in Panchayati Raj Institutions to 50%, and in which year?
131.x: Bihar was the first State to give women 50% in PRIs, in 2006. Many States followed, and 19 States/UTs now give 50%, including Andhra Pradesh. The other pairs are not the first.
131.tq: 50% for women in PRIs: Bihar first (2006).

131.s: The Balika Panchayat initiative, India's first of its kind, was launched in June 2022 in which of the following places?
131.x: The first Balika Panchayat was established in villages of Kutch, Gujarat, in June 2022.
