131.tq: Use the state-location association to distinguish the initiative from other grassroots programmes.

131.s: The primary purpose of the Balika Panchayat is to:
o: Provide vocational training exclusively to adolescent boys
Conduct elections to State Legislative Assemblies
Monitor implementation of central taxation schemes
131.x: Balika Panchayat is a girls' panchayat intended to train girls in local governance.
131.tq: Match the named initiative with its precise purpose rather than its broad social objective.

131.s: Mahila Sabha is best described as:
o: A meeting of women officers of the Election Commission
A statutory committee of the National Commission for Women
A meeting of women members of Parliament before a joint sitting
A women-only meeting held before the Gram Sabha
131.x: Mahila Sabha refers to a women-only meeting conducted before the Gram Sabha, as exemplified in Maharashtra.
131.tq: Discriminate between a grassroots women-only forum and statutory or parliamentary bodies.

131.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the ministry associated with the Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
131.x: The Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan is associated with the Ministry of Panchayati Raj.
131.tq: Apply the 'which ministry' test, using neighbouring ministries as distractors.

131.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan:
1. It provides leadership training to Women Elected Representatives.
2. It includes legal-awareness and gender-justice modules.
3. It includes modules on gender-based violence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
131.x: The Abhiyan provides leadership, legal-awareness and gender-justice training, including modules on gender-based violence, for Women Elected Representatives.
131.tq: Check whether all listed components belong to the same capacity-building programme.

131.s:
With reference to Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats, consider the following statements:
1. At least one such panchayat is envisaged per district.
2. They are intended to provide safe spaces and gender-responsive governance.
3. Their approach includes alignment with Self-Help Groups.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
131.x: Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats are intended to be established at least one per district, promote safe spaces and gender-responsive governance, and align with SHGs.
131.tq: Use a three-part programme-description question and verify each stated feature.

131.s: The initiative 'Nirbhay Raho - Nirbhay Chetna' is associated with which of the following objectives?
o: Training girls exclusively for urban municipal administration
Providing legal aid only to women prisoners
Increasing women's turnout through electronic voting
131.x: Nirbhay Raho - Nirbhay Chetna gender-sensitises male panchayat representatives.
131.tq: Identify the programme from its target group and objective.

131.s: Self-Help Groups have been described as involving approximately:
o: Nearly 1 crore women in over 9 lakh SHGs
Nearly 90 lakh women in 10 crore SHGs
Nearly 10 crore women in over 90 lakh SHGs
131.x: Nearly 10 crore women are associated with more than 90 lakh Self-Help Groups, which contribute to grassroots leadership.
131.tq: Match each numerical magnitude with the correct unit: women and SHGs.

131.s: Which one of the following statements about the National Commission for Women is correct?
o: It is a constitutional body set up under Article 338
It is a statutory body set up in 1992 under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990
It was created by an executive resolution in 2001
It is a statutory body under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
131.x: The NCW was set up in 1992 as a statutory body under the NCW Act, 1990. It reviews safeguards, recommends measures and handles grievances. It is not a constitutional body (Article 338 is the SC Commission), not an executive creation, and not set up under the DV Act.
131.tq: NCW: Act 1990, set up 1992, statutory.

131.s: The study by Chattopadhyay and Duflo (2004) examined the effect of women’s leadership in village governance by using which method?
o: Random reservation of pradhan posts in West Bengal and Rajasthan
Rotation of Lok Sabha constituencies reserved for women
Census-based selection of women sarpanches in Andhra Pradesh
Nomination of women pradhans by the Union Government in all States
131.x: Chattopadhyay and Duflo used the random reservation of pradhan posts in West Bengal and Rajasthan to study the effects of women’s political leadership.
131.tq: Identify the distinctive research design and the two States attached to it.

131.s: According to the findings associated with the Chattopadhyay-Duflo study, women leaders invested more in which of the following?
o: Military infrastructure and border roads exclusively
Goods and facilities requested by women, including drinking water and roads
Only administrative buildings and police infrastructure
131.x: Women leaders invested more in public goods that women specifically requested, notably drinking water and roads.
131.tq: Apply the study’s finding to the type of public goods selected by women leaders.

131.s: The term “sarpanch-pati” refers to a situation in which:
o: A male relative exercises the office elected to a woman representative
The husband of a male sarpanch receives a reserved Panchayat post
A woman sarpanch is appointed by the District Collector instead of being elected
A former sarpanch automatically becomes the adviser to every woman sarpanch
131.x: “Sarpanch-pati” denotes proxy representation in which a male relative exercises the office formally held by an elected woman.
131.tq: Discriminate between the elected office-holder and the person informally exercising the office.

131.s:
Consider the following statements regarding proxy representation in women-led Panchayats:

1. Evaluation studies find that proxy representation declines markedly in a second term.
2. Proxies, intimidation and online trolling continue to be barriers.
3. Proxy representation means that the elected woman is legally replaced by a male relative.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
131.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because proxy representation is an informal exercise of the office by a male relative; it does not legally replace the elected woman.
131.tq: Separate the empirical finding from the legally incorrect extreme claim.

131.s: Which of the following pairs of laws constitutes the principal legal shield specifically mentioned for protection against atrocities and discrimination involving Dalit and tribal communities?
o: The SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
The Representation of the People Act, 1951 and the Panchayats Act, 1992
The National Commission for Women Act, 1990 and the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961
The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 and the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015
131.x: The relevant legal safeguards identified are the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955.
131.tq: Match each law with the rights-protection issue it directly addresses.

131.s: Which organisation publishes the Gender Development Index (GDI) as part of its Human Development Report?
o: Georgetown Institute for Women, Peace and Security
131.x: The Gender Development Index is published by the United Nations Development Programme through its Human Development Report.
131.tq: Match the index with its publisher rather than with a similar global gender report.

131.s: The Gender Development Index primarily measures the ratio of female to male achievement in which of the following dimensions?
o: Economic participation, educational attainment, health and political empowerment
Reproductive health, political empowerment and labour market participation
Health, education and command over economic resources
131.x: GDI compares female and male HDI achievements in life expectancy, education and earned income or command over economic resources.
131.tq: Distinguish the dimensions of GDI from the sub-indices of GII and GGGI.

131.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Gender Development Index:
1. It is read in terms of parity between female and male human development.
2. A value close to 1 indicates near parity between women and men.
3. A scale in which 1 represents the worst position for women is the defining scale of the GDI.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
131.x: GDI is interpreted through female-to-male parity, with a value near 1 indicating parity. The 0-to-1 loss scale in which 1 denotes the worst position belongs to the GII, not the GDI.
131.tq: Separate two closely related indices by identifying the reversed scale and its meaning.

131.s: The Gender Inequality Index (GII) was introduced by the United Nations Development Programme in which year?
131.x: The GII was introduced by UNDP in 2010.
131.tq: Use the year-specific numerical clue to distinguish GII from the other gender indices.

131.s: Which of the following indicators is included under the reproductive health dimension of the Gender Inequality Index?
o: Maternal mortality ratio and adolescent birth rate
Mean years of schooling and earned income
Share of women in parliamentary seats only
131.x: The reproductive health dimension of GII includes maternal mortality ratio and adolescent birth rate.
131.tq: Link each indicator to the correct index dimension.

131.s: The Global Gender Gap Index is published by the:
131.x: The Global Gender Gap Index is published by the World Economic Forum.
131.tq: Use publisher-index matching to avoid confusing GGGI with UNDP indices.

131.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the four sub-indices of the Global Gender Gap Index?
131.x: The four GGGI sub-indices are Economic Participation and Opportunity, Educational Attainment, Health and Survival, and Political Empowerment. Reproductive Health is associated with GII.
131.tq: Eliminate the GII dimension inserted into the GGGI list.

131.s: The Women, Peace and Security Index is associated with which of the following organisations?
o: Georgetown Institute for Women, Peace and Security with PRIO
UN Women and International Labour Organization
131.x: The Women, Peace and Security Index is associated with the Georgetown Institute for Women, Peace and Security and PRIO.
131.tq: Identify the less familiar publisher rather than choosing the better-known gender-index institution.

131.s: India's rank in the Global Gender Gap Index was 135th in 2022 and 127th out of 146 countries in 2023. Which conclusion follows from these figures?
o: India was ranked first among the 146 countries in 2023.
India remained at the same rank in both years.
131.x: A lower numerical rank represents a better position; therefore, India improved from 135th in 2022 to 127th of 146 in 2023.
131.tq: Read ranking changes in the correct direction instead of treating a larger number as improvement.

131.s: India's Global Gender Gap Index rank in 2018 was:
131.x: India was ranked 108th among 149 countries in the 2018 Global Gender Gap Index.
131.tq: Match the rank with the correct year and denominator.

131.s: Which one of the following statements about India's performance in the 2023 Global Gender Gap Index is correct?
o: Political empowerment parity was 36.7%, while economic participation parity was complete.
Economic participation parity exceeded 75%, while enrolment parity was absent at all levels.
Economic participation parity was 36.7%, while enrolment parity had been achieved at all educational levels.
India ranked 108th out of 149 countries in 2023.
131.x: In 2023, India's economic participation parity was only 36.7%, whereas parity in enrolment had been achieved at all education levels.
131.tq: Separate the education achievement from the continuing economic participation gap.

131.s: India's lower position in the Gender Inequality Index relative to its overall Human Development Index rank is attributed particularly to:
o: Low female labour-force participation and low political representation
High female labour-force participation and high political representation
Low male literacy and high maternal mortality alone
High educational enrolment and low life expectancy of men
131.x: India's GII position is pulled down especially by low female labour-force participation and low political representation.
131.tq: Identify the stated cause-effect relationship rather than substituting unrelated development indicators.

131.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Post)

a. President of India
b. Speaker of the Lok Sabha
c. Chief Minister
 d. Governor

List-II (First woman to hold the post)

i. Sarojini Naidu
 ii. Sucheta Kripalani
 iii. Pratibha Patil
 iv. Meira Kumar

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
131.x: Pratibha Patil was the first woman President, Meira Kumar the first woman Lok Sabha Speaker, Sucheta Kripalani the first woman Chief Minister, and Sarojini Naidu the first woman Governor.
131.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing a swapped office-holder.

131.s: Who was the first woman Speaker of the (undivided) Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly?
131.x: Pratibha Bharati became the first woman Speaker of the undivided AP Assembly in 2004. Meira Kumar was the first woman Lok Sabha Speaker, Sucheta Kripalani the first woman Chief Minister (UP), and Sarojini Naidu the first woman Governor (UP).
131.tq: AP Assembly first woman Speaker = Pratibha Bharati (2004).

131.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Pratibha Patil — President of India — 2007
2. Meira Kumar — Lok Sabha Speaker — 2009
3. Sucheta Kripalani — Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh — 1963
4. Sarojini Naidu — Governor of Uttar Pradesh — 1947

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
131.x: All four pairs are correct: Pratibha Patil became the first woman President in 2007 and Meira Kumar the first woman Lok Sabha Speaker in 2009. Sucheta Kripalani became the first woman Chief Minister (UP, 1963) and Sarojini Naidu the first woman Governor (UP, 1947).
131.tq: Check each office-year pair independently before selecting the combination.

131.s:
Consider the following statements regarding reservation and representation in local bodies and legislatures:

1. Local bodies have a constitutional one-third floor for women’s reservation.
2. Half reservation for women exists in 19 States and Union Territories.
3. In legislatures, one-third reservation for women is to operate only after delimitation.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
131.x: All three statements are correct: local bodies have a one-third floor, half reservation operates in 19 States and Union Territories, and legislative reservation is linked to post-delimitation operation.
131.tq: Compare the different commencement conditions for local-body and legislative reservation.

131.s: Local-body quotas are described as the working model for which constitutional amendment concerning women’s representation?
131.x: The existing experience of local-body quotas is described as the working model for the 106th Amendment concerning women’s representation in legislatures.
131.tq: Distinguish the earlier local-governance amendments from the later legislative-reservation amendment.

131.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the representation of women among Panchayat members?
o: Women constitute more than three-fourths of all Panchayat members.
Women constitute nearly half of all Panchayat members.
Women constitute nearly one-fourth of all Panchayat members.
Women constitute nearly one-third of all Panchayat members.
131.x: Women are nearly half of all Panchayat members, reflecting the effect of local-body reservation.
131.tq: Use the approximate share carefully; do not convert “nearly half” into an exact percentage.

131.s: Women’s groups demanded the removal of which condition attached to women’s legislative reservation?
o: The condition of reservation only in urban local bodies
The condition of approval by all State Legislatures
The condition of prior approval by the Election Commission
131.x: Women’s groups demanded removal of the Census-delimitation condition, including during the Monsoon Session.
131.tq: Identify the specific procedural condition under debate rather than a general approval requirement.

131.s: The criticism that bundling women’s quota with delimitation may provide political cover relates principally to:
o: Replacing elected representatives with nominated members
131.x: The criticism is that linking the quota with delimitation may serve as political cover for reallocating seats.
131.tq: Connect the criticism to its stated institutional consequence—seat reallocation.

131.s: Which of the following demands has been raised by the Andhra Pradesh Congress and BC groups in relation to women’s reservation?
o: A complete abolition of local-body reservation
A reduction of women’s reservation to one-third in Andhra Pradesh
Reservation exclusively for women from Scheduled Tribes
131.x: The Andhra Pradesh Congress and BC groups have demanded a sub-quota for BC women.
131.tq: Identify the specific sub-quota demand rather than the general reservation percentage.

131.s: The Gender Budget for 2026–27 was stated to be approximately:
131.x: The Gender Budget for 2026–27 was ₹5.01 lakh crore, amounting to 9.37 per cent.
131.tq: Match the amount and percentage as a pair; changing either figure makes the option incorrect.

131.s: Which of the following is identified as a criticism of the present framework of women’s political representation?
o: It delays women’s legislative quota until post-Census delimitation and does not provide an OBC-women sub-quota.
It provides an OBC-women sub-quota in every legislature.
It excludes women from all Panchayat institutions.
It permits proxy representation only in Parliament.
131.x: The criticisms include delay of the women’s quota until post-Census delimitation, proxy representation, and the absence of an OBC-women sub-quota.
131.tq: Find the option combining the stated criticisms and reject claims that reverse the position.

132.s: From 1 April 2022, the schemes of the Ministry of Women and Child Development were placed under how many umbrella missions?
132.x: From 1 April 2022, MWCD schemes were organised under three umbrella missions: Mission Shakti, Mission Vatsalya, and Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0.
132.tq: Use the exact count and identify the three umbrella missions together.

132.s: From 1 April 2022, which component is included under Mission Poshan 2.0?
o: One Stop Centre and Women Helpline 181
Anganwadi Services, Poshan Abhiyaan and Scheme for Adolescent Girls
Shakti Sadan, Sakhi Niwas and PMMVY
Child Protection Services and the Juvenile Justice system
132.x: Mission Poshan 2.0 comprises Anganwadi Services, Poshan Abhiyaan and the Scheme for Adolescent Girls.
132.tq: Identify the umbrella mission from its component-scheme cluster.

132.s:
Consider the following statements about Mission Vatsalya:
1. It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
2. Its implementation period cited is 2021–22 to 2025–26.
3. It is aligned with the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015.
4. It is concerned with child protection, happy childhood and Sustainable Development Goals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
132.x: All four are correct: Mission Vatsalya is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for 2021-22 to 2025-26 (₹10,916 crore). It is aligned to the JJ Act 2015 and aims at child protection, a happy childhood and the SDG goals.
132.tq: When all statements belong to the same consistent scheme profile, test whether the complete combination is valid.

132.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?
1. Sambal — Women’s safety
2. Samarthya — Women’s empowerment
3. Mission Vatsalya — Women’s economic empowerment
4. Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0 — One of the three MWCD umbrella missions
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
132.x: Sambal concerns women’s safety, Samarthya concerns empowerment, and Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0 is one of the three umbrella missions. Mission Vatsalya is not the women’s economic-empowerment vertical.
132.tq: Detect the swapped description of Mission Vatsalya before selecting the combination.

132.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the Sambal sub-scheme?
132.x: One Stop Centre, Women Helpline 181 and Nari Adalat are components of Sambal. Palna is a component of Samarthya.
132.tq: Separate the safety components of Sambal from the empowerment components of Samarthya.

132.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched with Samarthya?
A. Shakti Sadan
B. Sakhi Niwas
C. Palna
D. SANKALP-Hub for Empowerment of Women
132.x: Samarthya includes Shakti Sadan, Sakhi Niwas, Palna, PMMVY, SANKALP-Hub for Empowerment of Women and Gap Funding for Economic Empowerment.
132.tq: Recognise the complete empowerment cluster rather than isolating one component.

132.s: Shakti Sadan was formed by merging which two earlier schemes?
o: Working Women Hostel and National Creche Scheme
132.x: Shakti Sadan was created by merging Swadhar Greh and Ujjawala under Samarthya.
132.tq: Test the merger relationship while distinguishing it from renamed or reclassified schemes.

132.s: Which pair is correctly matched under Samarthya?
o: Sakhi Niwas — former Working Women Hostel; Palna — former National Creche Scheme
Sakhi Niwas — former Ujjawala; Palna — former Swadhar Greh
Sakhi Niwas — former Mahila Police Volunteers; Palna — former Mahila Shakti Kendra
Sakhi Niwas — former Nari Adalat; Palna — former One Stop Centre
132.x: Sakhi Niwas is the successor to Working Women Hostel, while Palna is the successor to the National Creche Scheme.
132.tq: Discriminate between renamed schemes by pairing each with its former title.

132.s: One Stop Centre, also known as Sakhi, provides which combination of services under one roof?
o: Medical, legal, counselling and shelter support
Antenatal care, LPG connection and pension services
Only vocational training and hostel accommodation
Only financial credit and marketing support
132.x: One Stop Centre provides medical, legal, counselling and shelter support under one roof. It is funded from the Nirbhaya Fund.
132.tq: Select the option that combines all the core services of an integrated support centre.

132.s: Nari Adalat under Mission Shakti is intended primarily for:
o: Alternative grievance redressal in petty cases such as harassment and denial of entitlements
Selection of beneficiaries for LPG connections
Distribution of maternity benefits to government employees
Trial of serious criminal offences by regular courts
132.x: Nari Adalat provides an alternative grievance-redressal mechanism for petty cases, including harassment and denial of entitlements.
132.tq: Distinguish alternative local grievance redressal from formal criminal adjudication.

132.s: Which of the following initiatives has been discontinued?
o: Mahila Shakti Kendra and Mahila Police Volunteers
One Stop Centre and Women Helpline 181
132.x: Mahila Shakti Kendra and Mahila Police Volunteers have been discontinued. The other options refer to continuing schemes or sub-schemes.
132.tq: Identify the discontinued pair rather than choosing active Mission Shakti components.

132.s: Stree Mano Raksha, launched in March 2022 for the mental health of women, is a project of the Ministry of Women and Child Development with:
132.x: Stree Mano Raksha is an MWCD project with NIMHANS, Bengaluru for the mental health of women (APPSC 2021 key). AIIMS and ICMR are not the partners, and NLSIU is the partner in Nirbhay Raho, not this project.
132.tq: Stree Mano Raksha = MWCD + NIMHANS (mental health).

132.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Beti Bachao Beti Padhao:
1. It is 100% centrally funded.
2. It initially covered 100 gender-critical districts.
3. It currently covers all districts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
132.x: All three statements are correct. The scheme is fully centrally funded, began in 100 districts with low Child Sex Ratio, and has subsequently expanded to all districts.
132.tq: Check the sequence from initial district coverage to nationwide expansion.

132.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective of Beti Bachao Beti Padhao?
o: Ensuring the survival, protection and education of the girl child
Arresting the decline in Child Sex Ratio
Providing legal assistance as its principal objective
132.x: The scheme focuses on Child Sex Ratio, prevention of gender-biased sex selection, and the survival, protection and education of girls. Providing legal assistance is not its stated principal objective.
132.tq: Find the option that belongs to a neighbouring women-protection function rather than the scheme’s stated objectives.

132.s: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao operates under which vertical of Mission Shakti?
132.x: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao is included under the Sambal vertical, which deals with women’s safety.
132.tq: Match the scheme with the correct Mission Shakti vertical.

132.s: Which one of the following statements about Beti Bachao Beti Padhao is correct?
o: It was launched in 2015 and initially focused on gender-critical districts with low Child Sex Ratio.
It was launched in 2006 and later renamed in 2015.
It was launched in 2010 only for urban districts.
It was launched in 2022 under Mission Vatsalya.
132.x: The scheme was launched in 2015 and initially targeted 100 gender-critical districts with low Child Sex Ratio. The claim that it began in 2006 is incorrect.
132.tq: Discriminate between the correct launch year and the misleading year 2006.

132.s: Which of the following Ministries is NOT involved in implementing Beti Bachao Beti Padhao?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
132.x: BBBP is a joint scheme of MWCD (nodal), Health and Family Welfare, and Education (then HRD). Social Justice and Empowerment is not involved, which was the APPSC 2022 key.
132.tq: BBBP: MWCD (nodal) + Health + Education; NOT Social Justice.

132.s: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana, introduced in 2015 under Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao, is associated with which of the following?
o: An annual pension for women above 60 years of age
Vocational training for adolescent girls in aspirational districts
A post-birth grant exclusively for girls of BPL families
A small-savings account for a girl below 10 years of age for education and marriage
132.x: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana was introduced in 2015 under BBBP as a small-savings account scheme for girls below 10 years, primarily supporting education and marriage expenses.
132.tq: Distinguish the precise objective of a scheme from the objectives of nearby girl-child programmes.

132.s: Balika Samriddhi Yojana, launched in 1997, provides which of the following benefits?
o: A savings account for girls below 10 years of age
Post-birth grants and annual scholarships for girls belonging to BPL families
Nutrition and life-skills training for adolescent girls under ICDS
Conditional cash transfers for immunisation and delayed marriage
132.x: Balika Samriddhi Yojana provides a post-birth grant and annual scholarships to girls from families living below the poverty line.
132.tq: Use the scheme-year and benefit together to avoid confusing similar girl-child schemes.

132.s: Dhanalakshmi scheme is correctly associated with which one of the following combinations?
o: 2008 — conditional cash transfer linked to birth registration, immunisation, schooling and postponement of marriage beyond 18
1997 — post-birth grant and annual scholarships for BPL girls
2015 — small-savings account for education and marriage
132.x: Dhanalakshmi was introduced in 2008 as a conditional cash-transfer scheme linked to birth registration, immunisation, schooling and delaying marriage beyond 18 years.
132.tq: Match the year with the distinctive conditions attached to the scheme.

132.s:
With reference to Kishori Shakti Yojana, consider the following statements:
1. It was introduced in 2000.
2. It is based on the Integrated Child Development Services framework.
3. It focuses on nutrition, health and life-skills for adolescent girls.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
132.x: All three statements are correct. Kishori Shakti Yojana was introduced in 2000 under the ICDS framework for the nutrition, health and life-skills development of adolescent girls.
132.tq: Check all components of a programme rather than relying only on its target group.

132.s:
Consider the following statements about SABLA (Scheme for Adolescent Girls):
1. It provides nutrition, life-skills and health support to adolescent girls.
2. It is now part of the Samarthya sub-scheme of Mission Shakti.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
132.x: Statement 1 is correct: SABLA covers nutrition, life-skills and health of adolescent girls. Statement 2 is wrong: SABLA is now part of Poshan 2.0, not Mission Shakti's Samarthya. So '1 only' is right; '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' fail because statement 2 is false and statement 1 is true.
132.tq: Adolescent-girl nutrition schemes sit under Poshan 2.0; Samarthya is women's empowerment (Shakti Sadan, Sakhi Niwas, Palna, PMMVY).

132.s:
Consider the following statements about NAVYA (2025-26):
1. It is run by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship with the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
2. It gives vocational training to girls aged 16-18 through PMKVY 4.0.
3. It covers all districts of every State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
132.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: NAVYA is an MSDE-MWCD initiative training girls aged 16-18 via PMKVY 4.0. Statement 3 is wrong: it covers 27 aspirational districts in 19 States, not all districts. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' misses statement 2, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include statement 3.
132.tq: NAVYA = MSDE + MWCD, girls 16-18, PMKVY 4.0, 27 aspirational districts in 19 States.

132.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Scheme)
A. IGMSY
B. PMMVY
C. PMSMA
D. JSY

List-II (Feature)
I. Institutional-delivery cash assistance under NHM
II. Free antenatal check-up on the ninth of every month
III. Pilot conditional maternity benefit and forerunner of PMMVY
IV. Partial wage-loss compensation for the first living child

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
132.x: IGMSY was the pilot maternity-benefit scheme; PMMVY provides partial wage-loss compensation; PMSMA provides monthly antenatal check-ups; and JSY supports institutional delivery.
132.tq: Start with the distinctive PMSMA and JSY features, then complete the remaining pairs.

132.s: The Indira Gandhi Matritva Sahyog Yojana was introduced in which year?
132.x: IGMSY was introduced in 2010 as a pilot conditional maternity-benefit scheme and later served as the forerunner of PMMVY.
132.tq: Distinguish the pilot scheme’s year from the later PMMVY year.

132.s: Which statement correctly describes PMMVY 2.0?
o: It provides ₹5,000 for the first child and ₹6,000 for a second child if the second child is a girl.
It provides ₹5,000 only to regular government employees.
It was introduced from 2016 under Mission Vatsalya.
It provides ₹6,000 for every second child irrespective of sex.
132.x: PMMVY 2.0, implemented from 2022 under Mission Shakti, provides ₹5,000 for the first child and ₹6,000 for a second child if the second child is a girl. Regular government employees are excluded.
132.tq: Separate the first-child benefit, the conditional second-child benefit and the exclusion condition.

132.s: Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan provides free antenatal check-ups on:
o: The first day of every month
The fifteenth day of every month
The fifth day of every month
The ninth day of every month
132.x: PMSMA provides free antenatal check-ups for all pregnant women on the ninth day of every month.
132.tq: Recall the fixed monthly date associated with PMSMA.

132.s: Swadhar Greh is intended primarily for which target group?
132.x: Swadhar Greh is meant for women in difficult circumstances and has now been brought within Shakti Sadan.
132.tq: Identify the target group before considering the scheme’s institutional location.

132.s: STEP, introduced during 1986–87, was designed to promote which of the following?
o: Fast-track trials of crimes against women
Skills for gainful employment of women
132.x: STEP, or Support to Training and Employment Programme for Women, was introduced in 1986–87 to develop skills for women’s gainful employment.
132.tq: Link the programme’s historical period with its employment-oriented purpose.

132.s: Swayam Siddha is best described as a scheme for which of the following?
o: Rescue and rehabilitation of trafficking victims
Conditional cash transfers for girls’ schooling
132.x: Swayam Siddha, introduced in 2001, promotes holistic women’s empowerment through self-help groups.
132.tq: Distinguish an empowerment model based on SHGs from schemes providing a single benefit.

132.s: Mahila Samriddhi Yojana, introduced in 1993, seeks to promote which one of the following among rural women?
132.x: Mahila Samriddhi Yojana was introduced in 1993 to encourage the savings habit among rural women.
132.tq: Use the beneficiary group and the single core objective to avoid scheme substitution.

132.s: Working Women Hostel, introduced during 1972–73, is now known as which of the following?
132.x: The Working Women Hostel scheme, introduced during 1972–73 for working women, is now known as Sakhi Niwas.
132.tq: Distinguish a renamed accommodation facility from shelter and crisis-support institutions.

132.s: Ujjawala, the women’s welfare scheme, primarily dealt with:
o: Deposit-free LPG connections for poor households
Prevention of trafficking, rescue and rehabilitation
132.x: Ujjawala was concerned with prevention of trafficking, rescue and rehabilitation. Deposit-free LPG connections belong to PM Ujjwala Yojana, a separate scheme.
132.tq: Separate two look-alike scheme names by comparing their ministry purpose and beneficiary service.

132.s: Which one of the following statements about DWCRA is correct?
o: It was a sub-scheme of IRDP for groups of rural women, initiated in 1982-83.
It was an urban poverty mission launched in 2007.
It was an interest subsidy programme introduced in 2004.
It was a World Bank-aided project implemented only in municipalities.
132.x: DWCRA was a sub-scheme of the Integrated Rural Development Programme for groups of rural women and began in 1982-83.
132.tq: Combine the programme's origin, target group and administrative relationship.

132.s: Mahila e-Haat is best described as:
o: A credit scheme exclusively for SC/ST entrepreneurs
An online marketing platform for women entrepreneurs and Self-Help Groups
A maternity cash-transfer programme for pregnant women
A residential shelter for women in distress
132.x: Mahila e-Haat is an MWCD online marketing platform for women entrepreneurs and Self-Help Groups. It was started in 2016 and is run by Rashtriya Mahila Kosh.
132.tq: Identify the function of the platform before associating it with its implementing institution.

132.s: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh was established in 1993 as a registered society under which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
132.x: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh was established in 1993 as a registered society under the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
132.tq: Use the ministry-organisation relationship as the identifying feature.

132.s: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh provides credit mainly by:
o: Directly distributing grants to all women households
Lending to intermediary NGOs and MFIs, which on-lend micro-credit to poor women
Providing only crop loans to women farmers through state governments
132.x: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh lends to intermediary NGOs and micro-finance institutions, which in turn provide micro-credit to poor women.
132.tq: Follow the intermediary-credit chain instead of choosing a direct-beneficiary description.

132.s:
With reference to Stand-Up India, consider the following statements:
1. It is associated with the Ministry of Finance.
2. It provides bank loans from ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore for greenfield enterprises.
3. Each bank branch is required to support at least one SC/ST borrower and one woman borrower.
4. It is restricted to existing enterprises only.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
132.x: Stand-Up India is a Ministry of Finance scheme for greenfield enterprises, with loans of ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore and the stated SC/ST and women borrower requirement. Statement 4 is false because the scheme concerns new, or greenfield, enterprises.
132.tq: Reject the reversed existing-versus-greenfield enterprise description.

132.s: DAY-NRLM is administered by which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Ministry of Women and Child Development
132.x: DAY-NRLM is a Ministry of Rural Development programme. It was launched as Aajeevika in 2011 and renamed in 2016.
132.tq: Identify the implementing ministry from the rural livelihoods character of the programme.

132.s: A woman who is an SHG member and earns at least ₹1 lakh in a year is described under DAY-NRLM as a:
132.x: Under DAY-NRLM, an SHG member earning at least ₹1 lakh annually is termed a Lakhpati Didi.
132.tq: Use the income threshold and SHG membership to identify the programme label.

132.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Mahila Samman Savings Certificate?
o: A two-year certificate with deposits from ₹1,000 to ₹2 lakh and 7.5% interest
A five-year certificate with 6% interest and no upper limit
A one-year certificate available only to SHG members
A ten-year certificate administered exclusively by SIDBI
132.x: The Mahila Samman Savings Certificate is offered through the Ministry of Finance and India Post, has a two-year tenure, permits deposits from ₹1,000 to ₹2 lakh, and carries 7.5% interest.
132.tq: Check tenure, deposit range and interest together to avoid mixing it with other savings products.

132.s:
Which of the following combinations is correct regarding women’s economic indicators?
1. Women hold over 55% of PM Jan Dhan accounts.
2. About 70% of MUDRA loans go to women.
3. Female Labour Force Participation Rate is near 37%.
4. Women hold less than 10% of PM Jan Dhan accounts.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
132.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: women hold over 55% of PM Jan Dhan accounts, about 70% of MUDRA loans go to women, and female LFPR is near 37%. Statement 4 reverses the account-share figure.
132.tq: Reject the reversed percentage and retain the three consistent quantitative indicators.

132.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched regarding Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana?
1. Ministry — Petroleum and Natural Gas
2. Launch date — 1 May 2016
3. Launch place — Ballia, Uttar Pradesh
4. Beneficiaries — Women of BPL households
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
132.x: All four particulars are correct: PMUY is under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, was launched on 1 May 2016 at Ballia, and provides LPG connections to women of BPL households.
132.tq: Combine ministry, date, place and beneficiary details to avoid confusing PMUY with other welfare schemes.

132.s: Ujjwala 2.0, launched in August 2021 at Mahoba, provided which additional features?
o: Antenatal care and maternity cash assistance
Free second LPG cylinder and permanent housing for migrants
Free first refill and hotplate, with self-declaration of address for migrant families
Interest-free loans for LPG distributors only
132.x: Ujjwala 2.0 provided a free first refill and hotplate. Migrant families were permitted to self-declare their address.
132.tq: Use the launch location and the two distinctive benefits to identify Ujjwala 2.0.

132.s: The reported reach of Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana is:
132.x: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana has reached over 10.5 crore households.
132.tq: Recall the scale of coverage without confusing household reach with the number of beneficiaries in a different scheme.

132.s: Which one of the following is correctly associated with Talliki Vandanam?
o: Marriage assistance for poor SC/ST/BC/minority brides
₹15,000 per year and 75 per cent attendance condition
₹18,750 per year without any attendance condition
Four instalments for reimbursement of SHG loans
132.x: Talliki Vandanam provides ₹15,000 annually to eligible mothers, with a 75 per cent attendance condition, and was described as a restructured form of Amma Vodi.
132.tq: Compare the benefit amount and eligibility condition with those of neighbouring AP schemes.

132.s: YSR Cheyutha provides annual assistance of ₹18,750 to which group?
o: Rural BPL women organised under DWCRA
BC, SC, ST and minority women aged 45–60 years
All women students in Classes 1 to 10
132.x: YSR Cheyutha, introduced in 2020, provides ₹18,750 annually to BC, SC, ST and minority women in the 45–60 age group.
132.tq: Use the combined social-category and age filter to identify the scheme.

132.s:
Consider the following statements regarding YSR Kalyanamasthu/Shaadi Tohfa:
1. It was introduced in 2022.
2. It provides marriage assistance.
3. Its beneficiaries include poor SC, ST, BC and minority brides.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
132.x: YSR Kalyanamasthu/Shaadi Tohfa was introduced in 2022 and provides marriage assistance to poor brides belonging to SC, ST, BC and minority communities.
132.tq: Test the year, nature of assistance and beneficiary categories separately.

132.s: Which one of the following statements about the Disha Bill is correct?
o: It was withdrawn after receiving assent under the former IPC.
It never received Presidential assent; the IPC and CrPC provisions it sought to amend were replaced by the BNS and BNSS from 1 July 2024.
It was enacted by Parliament and amended only the CrPC.
It received Presidential assent and came into force in 2019.
132.x: The Disha Bill never received Presidential assent. The IPC and CrPC, which it sought to amend, were replaced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita from 1 July 2024.
132.tq: Watch for the false legislative-status claim attached to an otherwise familiar law-and-order measure.

132.s: The One Stop Centres in Andhra Pradesh are intended to provide services to women through which administrative coverage?
132.x: One Stop Centres are functioning in all 26 districts of Andhra Pradesh.
132.tq: Use the exact administrative count instead of an older or reduced district figure.

132.s: The reported rape conviction rate in 2018 and 2019 was approximately within which range, leading to calls for extending fast-track courts?
132.x: NCRB put the rape conviction rate at 27.2% in 2018 and 27.8% in 2019, prompting demands for more fast-track courts and stronger standards. It fell to 22.7% in 2023.
132.tq: Use the narrow reported range rather than a rounded or exaggerated percentage.

132.s: Which of the following reforms has been demanded in relation to One Stop Centres and shelters?
o: Extension of fast-track courts and national minimum standards for OSCs and shelters
Abolition of fast-track courts and decentralisation of shelters
Replacement of OSCs by SHGs in every district
Restriction of shelters to women above 45 years
132.x: The stated demands include extending fast-track courts and establishing national minimum standards for One Stop Centres and shelters.
132.tq: Connect the identified institutional shortcomings with the specific reform proposals.

132.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Andhra Pradesh demographic and policy context mentioned in relation to women’s welfare?
o: Talliki Vandanam is a hostel scheme and the total fertility rate is approximately 0.7.
Talliki Vandanam is an anti-trafficking scheme and the total fertility rate is approximately 2.7.
Talliki Vandanam is an unconditional pension and Andhra Pradesh’s total fertility rate is approximately 3.7.
Talliki Vandanam is a conditional cash transfer and Andhra Pradesh’s total fertility rate is approximately 1.7.
132.x: Talliki Vandanam is described as a conditional cash transfer, while Andhra Pradesh’s total fertility rate is approximately 1.7.
132.tq: Match the welfare instrument with the correct demographic indicator instead of a similar-sounding scheme.

133.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 17:
1. Untouchability is expressly defined in the Constitution.
2. Article 17 operates against private persons also.
3. Article 17 belongs to the Right to Equality group.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: The Constitution does not define ‘untouchability’. Article 17 is a Fundamental Right within the Right to Equality group and can operate against private persons as well.
133.tq: Reject the precise-sounding but false claim that the Constitution defines untouchability.

133.s: Who is associated with ensuring that Article 17 made untouchability a punishable offence?
133.x: B.R. Ambedkar ensured that Article 17 constitutionally treated untouchability as a punishable offence.
133.tq: Match the constitutional contribution with the principal figure associated with it.

133.s: Under Article 35(a)(ii) of the Constitution of India, the power to prescribe punishment for offences under Article 17 belongs to
o: Both Parliament and State Legislatures concurrently
133.x: Article 35(a)(ii) gives Parliament, and not the State Legislatures, the power to prescribe punishment for offences relating to Article 17.
133.tq: Ask which authority would do this job, while distinguishing Parliament from State Legislatures.

133.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Mysore High Court's interpretation of 'untouchability' under Article 17:
1. It covers the practice as it developed historically, not the literal sense of the word.
2. Social boycott of a few individuals falls within its scope.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
133.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Mysore HC read 'untouchability' as the historically developed practice, not its literal meaning. Statement 2 is wrong: the same reading excludes social boycott of a few individuals. Hence A; B and C wrongly accept statement 2, and D wrongly rejects statement 1.
133.tq: Historical practice - yes; boycott of a few individuals - excluded.

133.s: Which one of the following does NOT represent a form of untouchability mentioned in the constitutional context?
o: The two-tumbler system in tea shops
Election of representatives through universal adult franchise
133.x: The two-tumbler system, denial of temple entry and residential segregation are listed forms of untouchability. Universal adult franchise is unrelated to such a practice.
133.tq: Identify the odd item by grouping concrete discriminatory practices together.

133.s: The concept of “structural violence”, in the context of untouchability, refers to
o: violence caused exclusively by international conflict
violence committed only by armed forces
133.x: Structural violence is harm built into social structures. The concept is associated with Johan Galtung.
133.tq: Choose the precise conceptual definition rather than a literal or unrelated form of violence.

133.s: The two principal angles from which untouchability may be understood are
o: ritual pollution attached to people and practices used by society to protect itself from it
133.x: Untouchability involves both the stigma of ritual pollution attached to people and the practices adopted by the rest of society to protect itself from that supposed pollution.
133.tq: Recall the paired analytical dimensions rather than selecting broad social issues.

133.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Article — Subject
o: Article 46 — Educational and economic interests of SCs and STs
Article 342 — National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
133.x: Article 46 concerns the educational and economic interests of SCs and STs. Article 342 concerns notification of STs, Article 338A establishes the NCST, and Article 275(1) concerns grants-in-aid.
133.tq: Start with the sure Article–subject pair and eliminate swapped constitutional provisions.

133.s:
Which of the following combinations is correctly matched?

1. Article 15(4) and Article 16(4) — Special provisions and reservation in posts
2. Article 244(1) — Fifth Schedule administration
3. Article 244(2) — Sixth Schedule administration
4. Article 244A — Autonomous State within Assam
133.x: All four pairings are correct. Article 244A provides for an Autonomous State within Assam and was inserted by the 22nd Amendment in 1969.
133.tq: Test a sequence of closely numbered Articles by matching each with its subject.

133.s: The provision for grants-in-aid for ST welfare and for raising the level of administration of Scheduled Areas is contained in:
133.x: Article 275(1) provides grants-in-aid for ST welfare and for raising the level of administration of Scheduled Areas, including funds associated with the Tribal Sub-Plan.
133.tq: Identify the exact Article associated with a financial and administrative support function.

133.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Articles 15 and 16 of the Constitution:
1. Article 15(4) provides for special provisions for the advancement of SEBCs, SCs and STs.
2. Article 16(4) concerns reservation of appointments or posts for backward classes that are not adequately represented in State services.
3. Article 15(5) permits admission quotas in private educational institutions, including minority educational institutions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Article 15(5) excludes minority educational institutions from its scope.
133.tq: Separate the similar-looking reservation provisions by their beneficiaries and institutional coverage.

133.s:
With reference to Article 16(4B), consider the following statements:
1. It permits unfilled reserved vacancies of a year to be carried forward as a separate class.
2. Such carried-forward vacancies are not counted against the 50 per cent ceiling for that particular year.
3. It was introduced by the Eighty-First Constitutional Amendment Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: All three statements are correct. Article 16(4B), introduced by the Eighty-First Amendment, deals with carry-forward reserved vacancies and their treatment outside the annual 50 per cent ceiling.
133.tq: Check the clause, its numerical effect and the amendment together.

133.s:
Consider the following statements regarding reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes:
1. Article 330 relates to reservation of seats in the Lok Sabha.
2. Article 332 relates to reservation of seats in State Legislative Assemblies.
3. The Constitution provides reservation of SC/ST seats in the Rajya Sabha under Article 332.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Article 332 concerns State Legislative Assemblies, and there is no constitutional reservation of SC/ST seats in the Rajya Sabha.
133.tq: Reject the reversed chamber trap by comparing Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and Rajya Sabha.

133.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 334 of the Constitution:
1. It originally prescribed the reservation of seats for SCs and STs for a period of 10 years.
2. The 104th Constitutional Amendment (2019) extended this reservation up to 2035.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
133.x: Statement 1 is correct: Article 334 originally fixed a 10-year time limit, later extended by amendments. Statement 2 is wrong: the 104th Amendment (2019) extended the reservation up to 2030, not 2035. Hence '1 only' (A); B, C and D all wrongly accept the 2035 date or reject the 10-year original period.
133.tq: Original period 10 years; latest extension (104th, 2019) runs to 2030.

133.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes Article 335 of the Constitution?
o: It provides grants-in-aid for Scheduled Areas from the Consolidated Fund of India.
It empowers State Legislatures to alter the list of Scheduled Castes.
It requires SC/ST claims in services to be considered consistently with administrative efficiency.
It establishes the National Commission for Scheduled Castes.
133.x: Article 335 requires that the claims of SCs and STs in appointments and posts be considered consistently with the maintenance of efficiency of administration.
133.tq: Match the service-related article with its governing principle.

133.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 339 provides for Union control over the administration of Scheduled Areas and the welfare of Scheduled Tribes.
2. Article 339(1) provides for a Commission to report on such administration and welfare.
3. Scheduled Areas are declared under Article 339 rather than under the Fifth Schedule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: Scheduled Areas are declared under paragraph 6 of the Fifth Schedule, not under Article 339.
133.tq: Spot the wrong constitutional location while retaining the correct Union-control provision.

133.s: With reference to Articles 341 and 342, which one of the following is correct?
o: State Legislatures alone specify and alter the lists of SCs and STs.
The Governor specifies the lists and the President alters them by executive order.
The President specifies SCs and STs for each State or Union Territory, while Parliament alone can alter the notified lists by law.
The Supreme Court specifies the lists, while Parliament only advises the President.
133.x: Under Articles 341 and 342, the President specifies the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes for a State or Union Territory, and only Parliament can include or exclude groups from those lists by law.
133.tq: Ask which authority specifies a list and which authority can legally alter it.

133.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 366(24) — Scheduled Castes; Article 366(25) — Scheduled Tribes
Article 366(24) — Scheduled Tribes; Article 366(25) — Scheduled Castes
Article 366(24) — Scheduled Areas; Article 366(25) — Tribal Areas
133.x: Article 366(24) defines Scheduled Castes, while Article 366(25) defines Scheduled Tribes.
133.tq: Use the adjacent constitutional definitions as a paired memory unit.

133.s: Which of the following constitutional provisions deals with reservation of seats and chairperson posts for SCs and STs in local bodies?
133.x: Articles 243D and 243T provide for reservation of seats and chairperson posts for SCs and STs in Panchayats and Municipalities, respectively.
133.tq: Distinguish local-body reservations from Parliament and State Assembly reservations.

133.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 16(4A) — Reservation in promotion for SCs and STs
Article 244 — Administration of Scheduled Areas and Tribal Areas
Article 275(1) — Specification of Scheduled Castes by the President
Article 15(4) — Special provisions for advancement of SEBCs, SCs and STs
133.x: Article 275(1) concerns grants-in-aid for ST welfare and Scheduled Areas. The President’s power to specify Scheduled Castes is dealt with under Article 341.
133.tq: Find the option that assigns a list-specification power to a financial provision.

133.s: The provision relating to women's reservation in legislatures is associated with which one of the following constitutional provisions and amendments?
133.x: Article 334A was inserted in connection with women's reservation by the 106th Constitutional Amendment of 2023.
133.tq: Separate the provisions for existing SC/ST reservation from the newer provision for women's reservation.

133.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional provisions concerning the lists of certain classes?
o: Articles 341 and 342 concern SC and ST lists, while Article 342A concerns SEBC lists
Articles 338 and 338A concern SC and ST lists, while Article 342 concerns SEBC lists
Articles 339 and 340 concern SC and ST lists, while Article 341 concerns SEBC lists
Articles 330 and 332 concern SC and ST lists, while Article 342A concerns Anglo-Indian lists
133.x: Article 341 concerns the list of Scheduled Castes, Article 342 the list of Scheduled Tribes, and Article 342A concerns socially and educationally backward classes.
133.tq: Compare the neighbouring list-related articles and reject the commission and reservation provisions.

133.s: Which one of the following is the principal directive contained in Article 46?
o: To notify Scheduled Castes for each State and Union Territory
To abolish untouchability through criminal law alone
To promote the educational and economic interests of weaker sections, especially SCs and STs, and protect them from social injustice and exploitation
To reserve all public offices exclusively for SCs and STs
133.x: Article 46, a Directive Principle of State Policy, directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of weaker sections, especially SCs and STs, and protect them from social injustice and exploitation.
133.tq: Match the Article with its precise function instead of confusing it with notification, abolition or reservation provisions.

133.s: With reference to the specification of Scheduled Castes in a State or Union Territory, which one of the following is correct?
o: The Governor specifies them, subject to approval by the State Legislature.
The State Legislature specifies the Scheduled Castes by resolution.
The National Commission for Scheduled Castes specifies them by order.
The President specifies them by public notification after consulting the Governor, and Parliament alone can subsequently alter the list by law.
133.x: Under Article 341, the President specifies the Scheduled Castes for a State or Union Territory after consulting the Governor. Subsequent inclusion or exclusion can be made only by Parliament by law.
133.tq: Ask who would do this job and distinguish the initial authority from the authority competent to make later changes.

133.s: In Chinthada Anand v. State of Andhra Pradesh, the Supreme Court held that a person who has converted to Christianity from a Scheduled Caste community—
o: automatically retains Scheduled Caste status after conversion
can claim Scheduled Caste status on the recommendation of the State Government alone
can claim Scheduled Caste status only with proof of original status, bona fide reconversion and acceptance by the community
can claim Scheduled Caste status because religion is irrelevant to the SC list
133.x: The judgment held that a Christian convert cannot claim Scheduled Caste status merely on the basis of earlier caste identity. Reconversion requires proof of original SC status, bona fide reconversion and acceptance by the community.
133.tq: Use a legal scenario to test the exact conditions rather than relying on a broad generalisation.

133.s: The Supreme Court struck down Bihar's 2015 notification merging Tanti-Tantwa into an entry in the Scheduled Caste list in—
133.x: The Supreme Court struck down Bihar's 2015 notification in July 2024, reaffirming that a State cannot alter the Scheduled Caste list.
133.tq: Use the year-and-event pair and eliminate adjacent-year distractors.

133.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to the recognition of Scheduled Castes in chronological order:
A. The term 'Scheduled Castes' was first used by the Simon Commission.
B. The Government of India Act, 1935 gave shape to the term.
C. The first official Scheduled Caste list was prepared.
D. The earlier expression 'Depressed Classes' was replaced in official usage.
133.x: The term was first used by the Simon Commission, given statutory shape in the Government of India Act, 1935, and the first official SC list followed in 1936, after which 'Scheduled Castes' replaced the earlier 'Depressed Classes' in official usage. Hence A, B, C, D.
133.tq: Start with the earliest institutional reference and then place the statutory development and list in sequence.

133.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 344 — Addition of castes to the Scheduled Caste list
Article 341 — Scheduled Tribes in States and Union Territories
Article 342 — Scheduled Castes in States and Union Territories
Article 341 — Scheduled Castes in States and Union Territories
133.x: Article 341 deals with Scheduled Castes, while Article 342 deals with Scheduled Tribes. Article 344 concerns the Official Language Commission and is not the provision for adding castes to the SC list.
133.tq: Separate the adjacent Article numbers and reject the look-alike Article 344 trap.

133.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional position regarding Scheduled Tribes?
o: Scheduled Tribe status is decided exclusively by the State Legislature.
Scheduled Tribe status is religion-neutral and the list for a State or Union Territory is specified under Article 342.
Scheduled Tribe status is confined to Hindus, Sikhs and Buddhists.
Scheduled Tribe status is determined by the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes without Presidential notification.
133.x: Article 342 concerns the specification of Scheduled Tribes, and ST status is not restricted by religion.
133.tq: Combine the correct Article with the key SC–ST distinction instead of choosing a familiar but misplaced authority.

133.s: The first list of Scheduled Castes was issued through the:
133.x: The first list was issued through the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950. The term ‘Scheduled Castes’ itself had appeared earlier in the Government of India Act, 1935.
133.tq: Separate the origin of the term from the constitutional instrument that issued the first list.

133.s: According to Census 2011, approximately how many caste groups were notified as Scheduled Castes across the States and Union Territories of India?
133.x: Census 2011 records 1,241 caste groups notified as Scheduled Castes across States/UTs. 2,399 is the number of castes listed by the Kaka Kalelkar Commission (OBCs); 705 and 3,743 are distractors and not the SC count.
133.tq: SC groups notified (Census 2011) = 1,241.

133.s: The K.G. Balakrishnan Commission, whose term was extended till 10 June 2026, examines which of the following issues?
o: Sub-classification of OBCs in the Central List
Grant of Scheduled Caste status to Dalits who converted to Christianity and Islam
Reservation of seats for SCs in the Rajya Sabha
133.x: The K.G. Balakrishnan Commission examines SC status for Dalit converts to Christianity and Islam; its term was extended to 10 June 2026. OBC sub-categorisation is the Justice G. Rohini Commission's task; there is no ST creamy-layer commission or Rajya Sabha SC reservation.
133.tq: Balakrishnan = Dalit Christians/Muslims SC status; Rohini = OBC sub-categorisation.

133.s: Which sequence correctly represents the successive extensions of SC/ST reservation in legislatures under Article 334?
133.x: The listed extensions were made through the 8th, 23rd, 45th, 62nd, 79th, 95th and 104th Amendments; the 104th extended the reservation up to 2030.
133.tq: Track the reservation-extension series separately from promotion and service-related amendments.

133.s:
With reference to reservation of seats for SCs and STs in legislatures, consider the following statements:
1. The number of reserved seats is related to the population of the respective communities.
2. Separate electorates are provided for SC and ST voters.
3. All voters in the constituency elect the representative.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: Reserved seats are provided in proportion to population, but there are no separate electorates. All voters in the constituency participate in electing the representative.
133.tq: Trap the reversal between reserved seats and separate electorates.

133.s: The number of seats reserved for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha was refixed on the basis of the
o: 1971 Census and 1981 Census through the 42nd and 44th Amendments
1981 Census and 1991 Census through the 73rd and 74th Amendments
1991 Census and 2001 Census through the 84th and 87th Amendments
2001 Census and 2011 Census through the 87th and 91st Amendments
133.x: The 84th Amendment refixed the seat numbers on the basis of the 1991 Census, and the 87th Amendment did so on the basis of the 2001 Census.
133.tq: Match the Census years with the corresponding amendment numbers.

133.s:
Consider the following statements regarding reserved seats in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Of AP's 25 Lok Sabha seats, 4 are reserved for SCs and 1 for STs.
2. Of AP's 175 Assembly seats, 7 are reserved for SCs and 29 for STs.
3. Araku is the ST-reserved Lok Sabha constituency of AP.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: Statement 1 is correct: 4 SC + 1 ST of 25 Lok Sabha seats. Statement 2 is wrong: the Assembly has 29 SC and 7 ST seats of 175 (the numbers are reversed). Statement 3 is correct: Araku is the ST seat. Hence B; A omits statement 3, while C and D wrongly include statement 2.
133.tq: AP: Lok Sabha 4+1 (Araku); Assembly 29 SC + 7 ST - watch for reversed numbers.

133.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding extensions under Article 334?
1. 8th Amendment — extension up to 1970
2. 45th Amendment — extension up to 1990
3. 79th Amendment — extension up to 2010
4. 95th Amendment — extension up to 2020
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
133.x: All four pairs are correct: the 8th Amendment extended the period to 1970, the 45th to 1990, the 79th to 2010 and the 95th to 2020.
133.tq: Verify each amendment-year endpoint pair before choosing the comprehensive code.

133.s: The number of reserved seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha rose from 79 and 41 respectively to what figures after the 2001-Census delimitation?
133.x: The reserved Lok Sabha seats increased from 79 for Scheduled Castes and 41 for Scheduled Tribes to 84 and 47, respectively, after the 2001-Census delimitation.
133.tq: Treat the paired figures as two separate columns and avoid reversing the SC and ST numbers.

133.s: The 51st Constitutional Amendment, 1984, provided for ST seats in the Lok Sabha for
o: Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram
133.x: The 51st Amendment, 1984, provided ST representation in the Lok Sabha for Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram.
133.tq: Test the exact four-State grouping and avoid substituting neighbouring north-eastern States.

133.s: The proviso to Article 335 relating to relaxation of qualifying marks in promotion was enabled by which Constitutional Amendment?
133.x: The Eighty-Second Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000 inserted the proviso to Article 335 permitting relaxation of qualifying marks and standards in promotion for SCs and STs.
133.tq: Separate the closely placed reservation amendments by their precise subject.

133.s: The 85th Constitutional Amendment is associated with
o: relaxation in qualifying marks under Article 335
backlog vacancies being treated as a separate class
consequential seniority in promotion under Article 16(4A), with effect from 17 June 1995
reservation of seats for STs in the Lok Sabha
133.x: The 85th Amendment provided consequential seniority in promotion under Article 16(4A), with effect from 17 June 1995.
133.tq: Use the effective date and the phrase “consequential seniority” as the decisive identifiers.

133.s: Article 16(4A), permitting reservation in promotion for SCs and STs, was inserted by the 77th Amendment (1995) mainly in response to which judicial position?
o: Indra Sawhney (1992) confining reservation under Article 16(4) to initial appointment
E.V. Chinnaiah (2004) treating SCs as a homogeneous class
133.x: Indra Sawhney (1992) held that reservation under Article 16(4) applies only at initial appointment, not promotion; the 77th Amendment (1995) responded by inserting Article 16(4A). M. Nagaraj came later and upheld the 77th; Chinnaiah concerns SC sub-classification; Janhit Abhiyan concerns EWS.
133.tq: 77th = 16(4A) promotion, answer to Indra Sawhney.

133.s:
Consider the following statements about the Madiga Reservation Porata Samithi (MRPS):
1. It was founded in 1994 by Manda Krishna Madiga.
2. It was founded at Karamchedu in Guntur district.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
133.x: Statement 1 is correct: Manda Krishna Madiga founded the MRPS in 1994. Statement 2 is wrong: it was founded at Eedumudi in Prakasam district, not Karamchedu. Hence A; B and C wrongly accept Karamchedu, and D wrongly rejects statement 1.
133.tq: MRPS: 1994, Manda Krishna Madiga, Eedumudi (Prakasam).

133.s: What was the principal demand of the Madiga Dandora movement?
o: Categorisation of Scheduled Caste reservations into A–B–C–D groups
133.x: Madiga Dandora demanded categorisation of Scheduled Caste reservations into A–B–C–D groups, or reservation within reservation.
133.tq: Distinguish reservation sub-categorisation from general reservation demands.

133.s: The Madiga Dandora movement alleged that which community dominated the 15 per cent Scheduled Caste quota?
133.x: The movement alleged that the Mala community disproportionately dominated the 15 per cent Scheduled Caste quota, leading to the demand for a separate share.
133.tq: Discriminate between closely related communities in a reservation controversy.

133.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Justice P. Ramachandra Raju Commission:
1. It recommended grouping the Scheduled Castes of Andhra Pradesh into four categories.
2. The four categories were designated A, B, C and D.
3. It recommended grouping Madigas under Category B and Malas under Category C.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: All three statements are correct. The Commission recommended four groups: A comprising Relli and others, B Madiga, C Mala and D Adi-Andhra.
133.tq: Check the complete composition of a classification rather than recognising only its headline.

133.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the sequence associated with Scheduled Caste sub-classification in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Justice Ramachandra Raju Commission — 1996; AP SC Rationalisation Act — 2000
Justice Ramachandra Raju Commission — 2000; AP SC Rationalisation Act — 1996
Usha Mehra Commission — 1996; AP SC Rationalisation Act — 2004
Davinder Singh judgment — 2000; AP SC Rationalisation Act — 2024
133.x: The Justice P. Ramachandra Raju Commission made its recommendation in 1996, and the AP SC (Rationalisation of Reservations) Act was enacted in 2000.
133.tq: Use the date sequence to separate a commission recommendation from the later legislation.

133.s: Which State was the first to sub-categorise Scheduled Castes by legislation, after the Justice Ramachandra Raju Commission process?
133.x: Andhra Pradesh became the first State to sub-categorise Scheduled Castes by statute, through the AP SC (Rationalisation of Reservations) Act, 2000 (Punjab had done so earlier, in 1975, only by an executive circular).
133.tq: Test a superlative linked to a specific legislative milestone.

133.s:
With reference to E.V. Chinnaiah v. State of Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court treated Scheduled Castes as a single homogeneous class under Article 341.
2. It struck down the Andhra Pradesh Scheduled Caste (Rationalisation of Reservations) Act, 2000.
3. It held that sub-classification did not interfere with the Presidential list under Article 341.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Chinnaiah treated Scheduled Castes as a homogeneous class and struck down the State Act; it regarded sub-classification as interfering with the Article 341 list, so statement 3 is false.
133.tq: Find the statement that reverses the court’s holding.

133.s: The Usha Mehra Commission, constituted in 2007–08, recommended which of the following?
o: Amending Article 341 to enable States to sub-categorise Scheduled Castes
Including all Other Backward Classes in the Scheduled Caste list
133.x: The Usha Mehra Commission recommended amendment of Article 341 so that States could undertake sub-categorisation of Scheduled Castes.
133.tq: Match a commission with its specific recommendation.

133.s: In State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024), the seven-judge Bench held that sub-classification within Scheduled Castes is permissible when the class is not homogeneous. What was the majority ratio?
133.x: The seven-judge Bench permitted sub-classification by a majority of 6:1, overruling the position taken in E.V. Chinnaiah.
133.tq: Test the exact judicial majority using closely spaced numerical distractors.

133.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Usha Mehra Commission — Amendment of Article 341 recommended
Davinder Singh case — Sub-classification within Scheduled Castes permitted
Indra Sawhney case — Sub-classification of Scheduled Castes in Andhra Pradesh upheld
E.V. Chinnaiah case — Scheduled Castes treated as a homogeneous class
133.x: Indra Sawhney dealt principally with reservation under Article 16(4), the 50 per cent ceiling and reservation at initial appointment; it did not uphold Andhra Pradesh’s Scheduled Caste sub-classification.
133.tq: Eliminate the option that assigns a later State-specific issue to an unrelated case.

133.s: Which case upheld the 77th, 81st, 82nd and 85th Constitutional Amendments, subject to the State showing quantifiable data on specified conditions?
o: State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh
Jarnail Singh v. Lachhmi Narain Gupta
M. Nagaraj v. Union of India
E.V. Chinnaiah v. State of Andhra Pradesh
133.x: M. Nagaraj upheld the four constitutional amendments but required quantifiable data concerning backwardness, inadequate representation and administrative efficiency.
133.tq: Associate a cluster of constitutional amendments with the case that examined them.

133.s: Which State became the first to implement Scheduled Caste sub-categorisation after the Davinder Singh judgment?
133.x: Telangana became the first State to implement Scheduled Caste sub-categorisation after Davinder Singh, with three groups in April 2025.
133.tq: Distinguish the State that enacted the earlier framework from the State that implemented the post-2024 classification.

133.s: The original form of Article 338 provided for—
o: a non-statutory multi-member commission appointed by the State Governments
a Special Officer designated as the Commissioner for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
a Parliamentary committee for monitoring reservations
a separate National Commission for Scheduled Castes and a separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
133.x: Originally, Article 338 provided for a Special Officer, known as the Commissioner for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, to investigate safeguards and report to the President.
133.tq: Track institutional evolution by identifying the original arrangement before later commissions were created.

133.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched regarding the status of office-bearers of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
133.x: The Chairperson of the NCST has Cabinet rank, the Vice-Chairperson has Minister of State rank, and members have Secretary rank. Therefore, describing the Chairperson as having Minister of State rank is incorrect.
133.tq: Find the single reversed rank in a hierarchy-based matching question.

133.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the National Commission for Scheduled Castes from the State-level commission functioning in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The Andhra Pradesh commission alone has civil-court powers under Article 338.
The Andhra Pradesh commission is a non-statutory body and the National Commission is an executive body.
The Andhra Pradesh commission is a statutory State commission, whereas the National Commission for Scheduled Castes is a constitutional body.
Both are constitutional bodies established directly under Article 338.
133.x: Andhra Pradesh has a statutory State Commission for Scheduled Castes, whereas the National Commission for Scheduled Castes is a constitutional body under Article 338.
133.tq: Compare constitutional and statutory status instead of assuming that similarly named bodies have identical legal foundations.

133.s: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes began functioning as a separate Commission from—
133.x: The 89th Constitutional Amendment created the separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under Article 338A, and it began functioning from 19 February 2004.
133.tq: Distinguish the amendment year from the date on which the separate institution actually began functioning.

133.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Commissions for SCs and STs:
1. In 1990 the joint national commission for SCs and STs became a constitutional body under Article 338.
2. The 89th Amendment (2003) bifurcated it into the NCSC (Article 338) and the NCST (Article 338A).
3. The Commissions submit their reports to the Prime Minister, who lays them before Parliament.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the joint commission became constitutional in 1990, and the 89th Amendment (2003) split it into the NCSC under Article 338 and the NCST under new Article 338A. Statement 3 is wrong: the Commissions report to the President, and the reports are laid before Parliament. Hence A; B, C and D wrongly include statement 3 or drop statement 1.
133.tq: 89th = bifurcation; reports go to the President.

133.s: What does Article 338(9) of the Constitution provide?
o: It empowers the President to create State Commissions for Scheduled Castes
It requires the Union and every State to consult the National Commission for Scheduled Castes on all major policy matters affecting SCs
It gives the NCSC power to amend the Scheduled Caste list
It provides grants-in-aid to State SC Commissions
133.x: Article 338(9) obliges the Union and State Governments to consult the NCSC on major policy matters affecting SCs. It does not empower the President to create State commissions (a trap in CDCA); State SC Commissions are created by State law. The SC list is altered only by Parliament under Article 341, and grants-in-aid are under Article 275(1) for ST welfare.
133.tq: 338(9) = duty to consult NCSC; State SC Commissions come from State law.

133.s: Which of the following is NOT an offence covered by the Protection of Civil Rights law in relation to untouchability?
o: Providing reservation in public employment to an eligible Scheduled Caste candidate
Denying access to shops, hotels and places of entertainment
Barring entry to a place of public worship
Justifying untouchability on religious or traditional grounds
133.x: The Protection of Civil Rights law covers practices such as denial of temple entry, justification of untouchability and denial of access to public facilities. Providing reservation in public employment is not one of the listed offences.
133.tq: Find the item outside the statutory list rather than choosing a familiar Scheduled Caste-related provision.

133.s: A conviction for an offence relating to untouchability results in disqualification from contesting elections under
o: Section 7 of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1976
Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
133.x: Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides disqualification from contesting elections upon conviction for untouchability offences.
