138.tq: Keep the two jurisdictions, age thresholds and legal provisions separate.

138.s: Which pair correctly represents the two policy options discussed in the debate over consensual adolescent relationships?
o: Close-in-age exemption; or retaining the age of consent at 18 with judicial discretion
Replacing POCSO with the Mines Act; or removing judicial review
Abolition of the age of consent; or compulsory imprisonment in every case
Lowering the age of consent to 12; or excluding all adolescents from POCSO
138.x: The two options discussed are a close-in-age exemption or retaining the age of consent at 18 while allowing judicial discretion.
138.tq: Identify the balanced alternatives rather than absolute positions.

139.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Launch of ICDS
B. Universalisation of ICDS
C. Introduction of the Mid-Day Meal Scheme
D. Introduction of Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0
Select the correct sequence.
139.x: ICDS was launched in 1975, the Mid-Day Meal Scheme was introduced in 1995, ICDS was universalised in 2006, and Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 was introduced in 2021.
139.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place universalisation and the school-meal launch between them.

139.s: Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) was universalised in which year?
139.x: ICDS was launched in 1975 and universalised in 2006.
139.tq: Distinguish the launch year from the later year of universalisation.

139.s: The principal beneficiaries of ICDS are:
o: Children below six months only and school-going adolescents
Children aged six months to six years, pregnant women and lactating mothers
Children aged six to fourteen years and elderly persons
139.x: ICDS primarily covers children from six months to six years, pregnant women and lactating mothers.
139.tq: Separate the age group and maternal categories from school-age and adolescent beneficiaries.

139.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding ICDS services:
List-I (Service)
a. Supplementary Nutrition
b. Immunisation
c. Health check-up
d. Referral services
List-II (Delivery system)
i. Health system
 ii. Anganwadi Centre
Which of the following is the correct code?
139.x: Supplementary Nutrition is delivered through the Anganwadi Centre, whereas immunisation, health check-up and referral services are delivered through the health system.
139.tq: Start with the sure pair—supplementary nutrition and Anganwadi Centre—and then complete the repeated health-system pairs.

139.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the six ICDS services?
139.x: Cash maternity benefit is provided under PMMVY, now associated with Mission Shakti, and is not one of the six ICDS services.
139.tq: Use the scheme-boundary test to distinguish ICDS services from a related maternity-benefit programme.

139.s:
Which of the following statements correctly describes the role of an Anganwadi Worker?
1. She runs the Anganwadi Centre.
2. She is an honorary worker.
3. The Anganwadi Helper cooks and serves meals and brings children to the centre.
4. AWWs and ASHAs jointly undertake HBYC home visits.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
139.x: All four statements correctly describe the Anganwadi Worker, Anganwadi Helper and the joint AWW-ASHAs role in HBYC home visits.
139.tq: Verify the function, employment status and linked field responsibilities separately.

139.s: An Anganwadi Worker (AWW), an honorary worker who runs the Anganwadi Centre, is a functionary of which scheme?
139.x: The Anganwadi Worker is the ICDS functionary who runs the Anganwadi Centre (APPSC-G2 2025 key). The ANM and ASHA belong to the health system (NHM), PM POSHAN is the school-meal scheme and Samagra Shiksha is the school-education scheme.
139.tq: AWW = ICDS (MWCD); ANM/ASHA = NHM.

139.s:
Consider the following statements about ICDS:
1. It is administered by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
2. It is now run as Anganwadi Services under Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0.
3. It is a Central Sector Scheme implemented directly by the Union without the States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: Statement 1 is correct: MWCD is the ministry. Statement 2 is correct: ICDS now runs as Anganwadi Services under Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0. Statement 3 is wrong: it is centrally sponsored and implemented by States/UTs. So '1 and 2 only'; options with 3 are wrong.
139.tq: ICDS = MWCD, CSS, implemented by States/UTs.

139.s: The Scheme for Adolescent Girls under Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 covers which group?
o: Girls aged 14-18 years in Aspirational Districts and the North-Eastern Region
All boys and girls aged 6-14 years
Girls aged 10-14 years in all districts
Girls aged 15-19 years only in urban areas
139.x: The Scheme for Adolescent Girls covers girls aged 14-18 years in Aspirational Districts and the North-Eastern Region.
139.tq: Check both the age band and the geographical qualification; changing either creates a false option.

139.s: One Nation One Anganwadi primarily enables migrant families to:
o: Use Anganwadi services only after obtaining a new ration card
Continue receiving Anganwadi benefits after moving to another State
Claim only cash maternity benefits from any State
139.x: One Nation One Anganwadi enables migrant families to continue receiving benefits for children below six years and pregnant or lactating women after migration to another State.
139.tq: Apply the portability principle to a migrant-family situation instead of confusing it with cash or school benefits.

139.s: Which one of the following statements about One Nation One Anganwadi is correct?
o: Services are open on demand and child Aadhaar is not mandatory.
It is available only within the State where the child was originally registered.
The facility is limited to pregnant women and excludes children below six years.
Services are available only through prior appointment and child Aadhaar is compulsory.
139.x: Under One Nation One Anganwadi, services are open on demand and a child’s Aadhaar is not mandatory.
139.tq: Separate the portability and access conditions from commonly assumed documentation requirements.

139.s:
Consider the following statements about Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0:
1. It was introduced in 2021.
2. Its nodal ministry is the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
3. It is a Central Sector Scheme with no State contribution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: Statement 1 is correct: it was introduced in 2021. Statement 2 is correct: MWCD is the nodal ministry. Statement 3 is wrong: it is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with 60:40 sharing (90:10 for NE/Himalayan States and J&K). So '1 and 2 only' is right; options with 3 are wrong.
139.tq: A Centre-State ratio like 60:40 means Centrally Sponsored, not Central Sector.

139.s: Which one of the following funding patterns is correctly matched under Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0?
o: North-Eastern and Himalayan States and Jammu and Kashmir — 90:10
139.x: North-Eastern and Himalayan States and Jammu and Kashmir receive funding in the 90:10 pattern. Union Territories without legislature are funded 100 percent by the Centre.
139.tq: Check the category-specific ratio and reject reversed funding patterns.

139.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three verticals of Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0?
o: Universal secondary education for all adolescents
Nutrition support, including for adolescent girls
Early Childhood Care and Education for children aged 3–6 years
139.x: The three verticals are nutrition support, ECCE for children aged 3–6 years, and Anganwadi infrastructure. Universal secondary education is not one of them.
139.tq: Find the option outside the scheme's three-part structure.

139.s:
Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, introduced in 2021, merges which of the following?
1. Anganwadi Services/Supplementary Nutrition Programme
2. POSHAN Abhiyaan
3. Scheme for Adolescent Girls
4. PM POSHAN
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
139.x: Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 merges Anganwadi Services/SNP, POSHAN Abhiyaan and the Scheme for Adolescent Girls. PM POSHAN is a separate school-meal scheme.
139.tq: Reject the neighbouring but separate school-meal scheme before selecting the merged components.

139.s: POSHAN Abhiyaan was launched on which occasion and at which place?
139.x: POSHAN Abhiyaan was launched on 8 March 2018 at Jhunjhunu in Rajasthan.
139.tq: Use the date-place combination to distinguish the launch from later campaign events.

139.s: POSHAN Abhiyaan is the abbreviated name of which of the following?
o: Prime Minister's Organisation for School Health and Nutrition
Programme for Overcoming Social Hardship and Nutrition
Public Scheme for Holistic Nutrition and Education
Prime Minister's Overarching Scheme for Holistic Nourishment
139.x: POSHAN stands for Prime Minister's Overarching Scheme for Holistic Nourishment.
139.tq: Test the exact expansion of an official programme name rather than its broad objective.

139.s: Which one of the following is NOT a target associated with POSHAN Abhiyaan?
139.x: POSHAN Abhiyaan targets stunting, undernutrition or underweight, anaemia and low birth weight. Universal elimination of communicable diseases is not stated as its target.
139.tq: Find the option outside the programme's nutrition-specific target group.

139.s:
Consider the following statements regarding POSHAN Abhiyaan:
1. Its mission goal included reducing stunting to 25 percent by 2022.
2. It seeks to build a Suposhit Bharat.
3. It is intended to function as a Jan Andolan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: All three statements are correct. POSHAN Abhiyaan envisages a Suposhit Bharat and a Jan Andolan, with the stated goal of reducing stunting to 25 percent by 2022.
139.tq: Check whether all statements describe the mission goal and implementation approach.

139.s:
Consider the following statements about the 9th edition of Rashtriya Poshan Maah (2026):
1. It was launched at Varanasi.
2. Its theme was "Hamari Anganwadi Hamari Jimmedari".
3. Ten years of PM-KISAN was one of its pillars.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 9th edition was launched at Varanasi. Statement 2 is correct: the theme was 'Hamari Anganwadi Hamari Jimmedari'. Statement 3 is wrong: the pillar was 10 years of PMMVY, not PM-KISAN. So '1 and 2 only' is right; every option containing 3 is wrong.
139.tq: Poshan Maah 2026 marks 10 years of PMMVY - a maternity scheme fits a nutrition month; PM-KISAN does not.

139.s:
With reference to Poshan Pakhwada, consider the following statements:
1. It is observed as a fortnight-long campaign.
2. Its 8th edition in 2026 focused on brain development during the first six years.
3. It is conducted exclusively for adolescent girls.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: Poshan Pakhwada is a fortnight-long campaign, and its 8th edition in 2026 focused on brain development in the first six years. It is not exclusively for adolescent girls.
139.tq: Reject the exclusive-beneficiary trap and retain the duration and focus supported by the programme description.

139.s: Why should Poshan Tracker data not be treated as strictly comparable with NFHS survey data?
o: NFHS records only adult nutrition, whereas Poshan Tracker records only income.
Poshan Tracker covers only urban children, whereas NFHS covers only rural households.
Poshan Tracker is a census of children at Anganwadi centres, whereas NFHS is a survey.
Both datasets are collected exclusively through laboratory testing.
139.x: Poshan Tracker data represents a census of children enrolled or covered at Anganwadi centres, while NFHS data is survey-based; therefore, the two are not strictly comparable.
139.tq: Distinguish a census-type administrative dataset from a sample survey.

139.s: Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi primarily seeks to:
o: Bring early childhood care and education into Anganwadis through play-based pedagogy
Replace all Anganwadi workers with digital instructors
Introduce higher education in rural schools
139.x: Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi integrates ECCE into Anganwadis and promotes play-based pedagogy, effectively developing them as pre-schools.
139.tq: Identify the educational intervention from the age group and institutional setting involved.

139.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Initiative)
 a. Poshan Tracker
 b. Poshan Vatika
 c. Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi
 d. Poshan Pakhwada

List-II (Feature)
 i. Nutrition gardens at Anganwadi centres
 ii. Brain development in the first six years
 iii. Real-time monitoring of Anganwadi services
 iv. ECCE and play-based pedagogy

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
139.x: Poshan Tracker relates to real-time monitoring, Poshan Vatika to nutrition gardens, Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi to ECCE and play-based pedagogy, and Poshan Pakhwada to brain development in the first six years.
139.tq: Start with the sure pair Poshan Vatika–nutrition gardens and eliminate codes.

139.s: Which of the following statements regarding nutrition support is correct?
o: Poshan Vatikas are exclusively urban nutrition laboratories.
Millets are supplied only during Poshan Pakhwada.
There are 43,500 Poshan Vatikas, and millets are prohibited in supplementary nutrition.
There are 4.35 lakh Poshan Vatikas, and millets are included in supplementary nutrition at least once a week.
139.x: The programme has 4.35 lakh Poshan Vatikas, and millets are provided at least once a week in supplementary nutrition.
139.tq: Combine the numerical figure with the precise frequency of millet inclusion.

139.s:
Consider the following statements about Vigilance Awareness Week:
1. It is associated with the Central Vigilance Commission.
2. It is observed in the week that includes 2 October.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
139.x: Statement 1 is correct: the week is associated with the Central Vigilance Commission. Statement 2 is wrong: it is the week that includes 31 October, Sardar Patel's birth anniversary, not 2 October. So '1 only' is right; '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are wrong.
139.tq: Vigilance links to Sardar Patel, the Iron Man - his birthday, 31 October.

139.s: The National Early Childhood Care and Education Policy was formulated in which year?
139.x: The National ECCE Policy was formulated in 2013.
139.tq: Distinguish the ECCE policy year from the later NEP year.

139.s: The foundational stage under the National Education Policy, 2020 comprises which of the following?
o: Ages 3–6, excluding the first two years of school
Ages 3–8, including three years of Anganwadi/pre-school and Classes 1–2
139.x: The NEP 2020 foundational stage covers ages 3–8: three years of Anganwadi or preschool followed by Classes 1 and 2.
139.tq: Break a composite age band into its preschool and school components.

139.s: Which of the following pairs relating to ECCE initiatives in Andhra Pradesh is correctly matched?
o: Hub Anganwadi Centres — 1,030, with ITC and Pratham
Anganwadi workers trained under Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi — 17,000 only
Bal Vatika — Excluded from PM POSHAN
139.x: Andhra Pradesh has 1,030 Hub Anganwadi Centres associated with ITC and Pratham. The State also reported training 55,607 Anganwadi workers under Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi; Bal Vatika was brought under PM POSHAN.
139.tq: Use the distinctive institutional partnership and number as the sure pair.

139.s: Bal Vatika has been brought under which programme?
139.x: Bal Vatika was brought under PM POSHAN as part of the school nutrition framework.
139.tq: Identify the programme linkage rather than confusing education and maternal-health schemes.

139.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years?
139.x: Article 45 provides for ECCE for children up to six years. Article 21A is the right to education for 6-14 years; Article 39(f) concerns healthy development of children as a directive; Article 51A(k) is the parents' fundamental duty to provide education opportunities to children aged 6-14.
139.tq: Art 45 = ECCE (0-6); Art 21A = RTE (6-14).

139.s: The Mid-Day Meal Scheme was introduced on 15 August 1995 under which name?
o: National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education
139.x: The scheme was introduced on 15 August 1995 as the National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education (NP-NSPE).
139.tq: Distinguish the original name from the later name PM POSHAN.

139.s: PM POSHAN is implemented as a rights-based Centrally Sponsored Scheme under which legislation?
139.x: PM POSHAN is a rights-based Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented under the National Food Security Act, 2013.
139.tq: Use the legal-basis trap by separating the governing legislation from related education and food institutions.

139.s:
With reference to PM POSHAN, consider the following statements:
1. It covers children studying in Bal Vatika and Classes I to VIII.
2. It provides one hot cooked meal.
3. It is restricted to unaided private schools.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: PM POSHAN covers Bal Vatika and Classes I to VIII in government and government-aided schools and provides one hot cooked meal. It is not restricted to unaided private schools.
139.tq: Find the wrong coverage category by checking the type of school included.

139.s:
Consider the following statements about the nutritional norms under PM POSHAN:
1. At the primary level, the norm is 450 kcal and 12 g protein per child.
2. At the upper-primary level, the norm is 700 kcal and 12 g protein per child.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
139.x: Statement 1 is correct: the primary norm is 450 kcal and 12 g protein. Statement 2 is wrong: the upper-primary norm is 700 kcal and 20 g protein, not 12 g. So '1 only' is right; '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are wrong.
139.tq: Primary 450/12, upper primary 700/20 - both calories and protein rise with the stage.

139.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective beyond the provision of nutrition under PM POSHAN?
o: Enhancing retention and concentration among disadvantaged children
Providing universal cash transfers to school children
139.x: PM POSHAN aims to address classroom hunger and improve enrolment, attendance, retention and concentration. Universal cash transfers are not one of its stated aims.
139.tq: Identify the option that changes a nutrition-and-schooling intervention into a cash-transfer scheme.

139.s: Tithi Bhojan, associated with community participation in PM POSHAN, was first introduced by which State?
139.x: Tithi Bhojan, under which communities contribute meals on special occasions, was first introduced by Gujarat.
139.tq: Test the origin State of a named community-participation practice.

139.s: The Centre-State sharing pattern generally applicable to PM POSHAN is:
139.x: The general Centre-State sharing ratio under PM POSHAN is 60:40.
139.tq: Distinguish the general financing ratio from the special ratio applicable to certain regions under other schemes.

139.s: Which Ministry is the nodal Ministry for PM POSHAN?
o: Ministry of Education, Department of School Education and Literacy
Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
139.x: PM POSHAN is administered by the Ministry of Education through the Department of School Education and Literacy.
139.tq: Apply the 'who would do this job?' test to identify the nodal ministry.

139.s:
Consider the following statements regarding PM POSHAN:
1. Social audit is mandatory in every district.
2. School nutrition gardens are among its features.
3. Additional nutrition is provided in aspirational and high-anaemia districts.
4. Farmer Producer Organisations and Self-Help Groups may participate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: All four statements describe features of PM POSHAN: mandatory district-level social audits, school nutrition gardens, additional nutrition in specified districts, and participation of FPOs and SHGs.
139.tq: Check each programme feature independently before selecting the complete combination.

139.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Akshaya Patra Foundation—largest NGO partner in the mid-day meal programme
Tithi Bhojan—introduced first by Tamil Nadu
PM POSHAN—administered by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
139.x: The Akshaya Patra Foundation, based in Bengaluru, is identified as the largest NGO partner in the mid-day meal programme. The other pairings contain incorrect State, Ministry or year associations.
139.tq: Use the wrong-person or wrong-ministry trap to identify the only correctly matched pair.

139.s: Akshaya Patra Foundation, identified as the largest NGO mid-day meal provider, was established in Bengaluru in 2000 under the leadership of:
139.x: The Akshaya Patra Foundation was established in Bengaluru in 2000 under the leadership of Madhu Pandit Dasa.
139.tq: Link the organisation with its founder and place instead of confusing it with other social-sector figures.

139.s: Under the Dokka Seethamma Mid-Day Meal programme in Andhra Pradesh during 2024-25, which combination is correct?
o: Classes XI-XII; 27.97 lakh students; milk and fruit daily
Classes IX-X; 20 lakh students; 5 eggs and 3 chikkis weekly
Classes I-VIII; 11.8 lakh students; 3 eggs and 5 chikkis weekly
Classes XI-XII; 27.97 lakh students; 5 eggs, 3 chikkis and ragi java weekly
139.x: In Andhra Pradesh, the Dokka Seethamma Mid-Day Meal was extended to Intermediate Classes XI-XII in 2024-25, covering 27.97 lakh students and providing five eggs, three chikkis and ragi java per week.
139.tq: Combine class range, beneficiary count and weekly nutrition items to defeat partial-match options.

139.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Mid-Day Meal Scheme:
1. The mid-day meal was first started in Tamil Nadu.
2. The national scheme was renamed PM POSHAN (Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman) in 2021.
3. PM POSHAN is administered by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: Statement 1 is correct: the mid-day meal first started in Tamil Nadu. Statement 2 is correct: it was renamed PM POSHAN in 2021. Statement 3 is wrong: the nodal ministry is the Ministry of Education (Dept of School Education and Literacy); MWCD runs ICDS. So '1 and 2 only'.
139.tq: MDM: TN first, NP-NSPE 1995, PM POSHAN 2021, Ministry of Education.

139.s: Janani Suraksha Yojana was launched in 2005 under which framework and ministry?
o: National Food Security Act and Ministry of Women and Child Development
Samarthya and Ministry of Women and Child Development
Mission Vatsalya and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
National Rural Health Mission and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
139.x: JSY was launched in 2005 under the National Rural Health Mission and is administered by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. It is a 100% Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
139.tq: Separate JSY’s ministry and framework from PMMVY’s institutional arrangement.

139.s: Which of the following services is covered under Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram?
o: A cash incentive exclusively for home delivery
A Rs.10 lakh corpus payable to a child at age 23
Free delivery, drugs, diagnostics, blood, diet and transport without out-of-pocket expenditure
A monthly take-home ration of 2.5 kg for infants
139.x: JSSK, launched in 2011 under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, provides pregnant women and sick newborns with free delivery, medicines, diagnostics, blood, diet and transport.
139.tq: Match a maternal-health scheme with its service package rather than a cash transfer.

139.s: The legal basis cited for the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana is which provision?
o: Section 4 of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015
Section 4 of the National Food Security Act, 2013
139.x: PMMVY has its legal basis in Section 4 of the National Food Security Act, 2013.
139.tq: Distinguish a statutory basis from constitutional provisions and unrelated legislation.

139.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: PMMVY — Matru Shakti Rashtra Shakti; helpline 1515
PMSMA — Breastfeeding within one hour; helpline 1098
MAA — Free transport for institutional delivery; helpline 112
JSY — High-risk pregnancy screening on the ninth of every month; helpline 1515
139.x: PMMVY carries the tagline ‘Matru Shakti Rashtra Shakti’ and its helpline is 1515. PMSMA concerns antenatal check-ups on the ninth of every month, while MAA promotes early breastfeeding.
139.tq: Match each scheme with its distinctive tagline or service and reject cross-swapped details.

139.s: Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan is associated with which of the following?
o: Promotion of breastfeeding within one hour of birth
Free treatment exclusively for sick newborns
Free antenatal check-up on the ninth of every month and identification of high-risk pregnancies
Cash assistance for institutional delivery at rural and urban rates
139.x: PMSMA, launched in 2016 under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, provides free antenatal check-ups on the 9th of every month and helps identify high-risk pregnancies.
139.tq: Use the fixed monthly date and service purpose as identifying clues.

139.s: Mothers’ Absolute Affection (MAA) primarily promotes which practice?
o: Breastfeeding within one hour of birth
Foster care for children without parental support
Supplementary nutrition for children aged 6–36 months
139.x: MAA is a Ministry of Health and Family Welfare initiative launched in 2016 to promote breastfeeding within one hour of birth.
139.tq: Distinguish breastfeeding promotion from delivery and nutrition-transfer schemes.

139.s:
Arrange the following maternal-health schemes in chronological order of launch:
A. PMMVY
B. Janani Suraksha Yojana
C. PMSMA
D. Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram
139.x: JSY was launched in 2005, JSSK in 2011, PMSMA in 2016 and PMMVY on 1 January 2017. Therefore, B, D, C, A is the correct sequence.
139.tq: Fix the earliest and latest schemes first, then place the two middle years.

139.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with its nodal ministry?
o: JSSK — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
PMSMA — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
JSY — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
PMMVY — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
139.x: PMMVY is administered by the Ministry of Women and Child Development. JSY, JSSK and PMSMA are associated with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
139.tq: Apply the ministry-swapping trap, especially between JSY and PMMVY.

139.s: Under PMMVY 2.0 (from April 2022), which of the following correctly describes the maternity benefit?
o: Rs 5,000 for the first child, and Rs 6,000 if the second child is a girl
Rs 5,000 in three instalments for the first two children irrespective of sex
Rs 6,000 for every live birth irrespective of birth order
Rs 1,400 for institutional delivery in rural areas
139.x: PMMVY 2.0 gives Rs 5,000 for the first child and Rs 6,000 if the second child is a girl. Rs 5,000 in three instalments was the old PMMVY 1.0 design (a trap). It does not cover every birth. Rs 1,400 for rural institutional delivery is the JSY benefit.
139.tq: PMMVY 2.0: 5,000 (1st) + 6,000 (2nd girl); '3 instalments' = old 1.0.

139.s: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) is presently implemented under which component of Mission Shakti?
139.x: BBBP is implemented under Sambal, the safety component of Mission Shakti.
139.tq: Identify the correct umbrella mission by matching the scheme with its present administrative component.

139.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the funding and geographical coverage of Beti Bachao Beti Padhao?
o: It is fully funded by the Centre and covers all districts.
It is jointly funded by the Centre and States and covers only selected districts.
It is funded through direct benefit transfers in rural districts only.
It is financed through district-level private contributions and covers aspirational districts only.
139.x: BBBP has 100% central funding and covers all districts.
139.tq: Test the pair of funding pattern and coverage together; avoid confusing central funding with shared funding.

139.s:
With reference to Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, consider the following statements:
1. It is primarily a behaviour-change campaign.
2. It provides direct benefit transfers to every girl child.
3. It involves no asset creation.
4. Funds for each district vary with its Sex Ratio at Birth.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: BBBP is a behaviour-change campaign with no DBT and no asset creation. Funds for each district vary with its Sex Ratio at Birth. Statement 2 is false.
139.tq: Find the false policy-feature statement; direct transfers and asset creation are common traps in scheme questions.

139.s: The Sex Ratio at Birth under the indicators cited for Beti Bachao Beti Padhao improved from 918 in 2014–15 to which figure in 2024–25?
139.x: The cited Sex Ratio at Birth increased from 918 in 2014–15 to 929 in 2024–25.
139.tq: Distinguish closely spaced numerical options by retaining both the base year and terminal year.

139.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana:
1. It is associated with the Ministry of Finance.
2. A family may open accounts for at most two girls.
3. The annual deposit range is ₹250 to ₹1.5 lakh.
4. The account matures after 15 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: The scheme is under the Ministry of Finance, permits accounts for at most two girls per family, and allows annual deposits from ₹250 to ₹1.5 lakh. It matures at 21 years, not 15 years.
139.tq: Separate the deposit period from the maturity period; the reversed time period is the trap.

139.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Scheme)
a. Balika Samriddhi Yojana
b. Dhanalakshmi
c. Beti Bachao Beti Padhao

d. Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana

List-II (Feature)
i. Behaviour-change campaign for survival and education of the girl child
ii. Conditional cash transfer linked with birth registration, immunisation and schooling
iii. Cash grant at birth and scholarships for girls of BPL families
iv. Savings scheme with maturity at 21 years
139.x: Balika Samriddhi provides a birth grant and scholarships; Dhanalakshmi is a conditional cash-transfer pilot; BBBP is a behaviour-change campaign; Sukanya Samriddhi matures at 21 years.
139.tq: Start from the sure scheme-objective pair and eliminate codes containing swapped girl-child schemes.

139.s: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched at which place on 22 January 2015?
139.x: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched on 22 January 2015 at Panipat in Haryana.
139.tq: Use the place-date pair to distinguish the scheme from other women-centric initiatives.

139.s:
Consider the following statements about Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP):
1. The Ministry of Women and Child Development is the nodal ministry, with the Health and Education ministries.
2. It aims to reverse the falling Child Sex Ratio and secure the girl child's survival and education.
3. It is administered by the Ministry of Finance as a savings scheme.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: MWCD is nodal (with Health and Education) and BBBP aims to reverse the falling Child Sex Ratio. Statement 3 is wrong: the Ministry of Finance savings scheme is Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
139.tq: BBBP = MWCD + Health + Education; SSY = Finance.

139.s: Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, the minimum legal age for marriage is:
o: 21 years for both girls and boys
18 years for girls and 21 years for boys
18 years for girls and 18 years for boys
21 years for girls and 18 years for boys
139.x: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 prescribes 18 years for girls and 21 years for boys.
139.tq: Directly discriminate between the two age thresholds in a commonly confused pair.

139.s: An adult male who contracts, conducts or promotes a child marriage under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 may be punished with:
o: Rigorous imprisonment up to two years and fine up to Rs. 1 lakh
Fine up to Rs. 10 lakh only
Simple imprisonment up to five years without fine
Imprisonment up to one year and fine up to Rs. 50,000
139.x: The punishment may extend to two years of rigorous imprisonment and a fine up to Rs. 1 lakh.
139.tq: Retain both components of the penalty instead of selecting a partially correct punishment.

139.s: Who appoints the Child Marriage Prohibition Officers?
o: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
139.x: Child Marriage Prohibition Officers are appointed by State Governments.
139.tq: Ask which authority performs the appointment to avoid confusing it with a national commission's role.

139.s: The Prohibition of Child Marriage (Amendment) Bill, 2021 proposed to raise the minimum marriageable age of women to 21 years. What happened to the Bill?
o: It was withdrawn after being passed by both Houses.
It was rejected by the Supreme Court.
It was enacted as an Act in 2022.
It was referred to a Standing Committee and lapsed with the 17th Lok Sabha.
139.x: The Bill was sent to a Standing Committee and subsequently lapsed with the 17th Lok Sabha.
139.tq: Track the legislative stage and final status rather than only the proposed reform.

139.s: Which group of States was identified as having the highest levels of child marriage in the cited NFHS-5 data?
o: Tamil Nadu, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh
139.x: West Bengal, Bihar and Tripura were identified among the States with the highest child-marriage levels in the cited NFHS-5 data.
139.tq: Recall the complete three-State grouping rather than a single State.

139.s: ALIVA, a data-driven approach to addressing child marriage, originated in which district?
139.x: ALIVA is a data-driven approach from Nayagarh district of Odisha.
139.tq: Check both the district and the State rather than relying on the district name alone.

139.s: Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, the legal status of a child marriage is that it is:
o: Void ab initio in all cases
Voidable at the option of the party who was a minor at the time of marriage
Voidable only at the option of the State Government
139.x: Under PCMA 2006 a child marriage is voidable at the option of the minor party, not automatically void. It is not fully valid and unchallengeable, and the option lies with the minor party, not the State Government.
139.tq: Child marriage = voidable at minor party's option.

139.s:
Consider the following statements regarding child marriage:
1. NFHS-5 found that 23.3% of women aged 20-24 were married before 18.
2. The '100-Day Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat' campaign was launched by the Ministry of Women and Child Development in December 2025.
3. The ALIVA model to end child marriage originated in Ganjam district of Odisha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: Statement 1 is correct (NFHS-5: 23.3%). Statement 2 is correct: MWCD launched the 100-day campaign in December 2025. Statement 3 is wrong: ALIVA is from Nayagarh district, Odisha. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
139.tq: NFHS-5 23.3%; ALIVA = Nayagarh.

139.s: CHILDLINE 1098 has been integrated with ERSS-112 in 36 States and Union Territories under
139.x: Under Mission Vatsalya, CHILDLINE 1098 has been integrated with ERSS-112 in 36 States and Union Territories.
139.tq: Match the helpline integration with the correct child-protection mission.

139.s: Mission Vatsalya, introduced in 2021–22, subsumed the
139.x: Mission Vatsalya subsumed the Integrated Child Protection Scheme, or ICPS.
139.tq: Distinguish the child-protection scheme absorbed by Mission Vatsalya from education schemes.

139.s: Mission Vatsalya, introduced during 2021–22, is primarily concerned with which of the following?
o: Child protection and promotion of a happy childhood
Nutrition support exclusively for adolescent girls
Employment of women in rural areas
Universal health insurance for senior citizens
139.x: Mission Vatsalya was introduced in 2021–22 for child protection and the promotion of a happy childhood, in alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals.
139.tq: Identify the scheme from its distinctive purpose.

139.s: Under Mission Vatsalya, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: JJB and CWC — One in every State only
Sponsorship and foster care — Rs.4,000 per child per month
Institutional care — Rs.4,000 per child per month
Aftercare — Available only up to 18 years
139.x: Mission Vatsalya provides Rs.4,000 per child per month for non-institutional care through sponsorship and foster care. JJBs and CWCs are to be established in every district; institutional care is Rs.3,000 per month and aftercare extends beyond 18 years.
139.tq: Start with the distinctive monetary norm and eliminate reversed amounts or age limits.

139.s:
With reference to institutional and aftercare provisions under Mission Vatsalya, consider the following statements:
1. Child Care Institution maintenance is fixed at Rs.3,000 per month.
2. The normal capacity of a Child Care Institution is 50 children.
3. The capacity norm is 25 children in North-Eastern and hilly areas.
4. Aftercare is available from 18 to 21 years and may be extended up to 23 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: All four statements correctly state the Mission Vatsalya norms for Child Care Institutions and aftercare.
139.tq: Test several numerical and age norms in one coded statement question.

139.s: Palna, the National Creche Scheme, is intended for children in which age group?
139.x: Palna covers children from 6 months to 6 years. Its creches may function whether or not the mother is employed, and 17,000 Anganwadi-cum-Creches were targeted.
139.tq: Use the exact age range to distinguish Palna from preschool and school-age programmes.

139.s: Which of the following is a feature of PM CARES for Children?
o: It provides a corpus of Rs.10 lakh at the age of 23 to eligible COVID-19 orphaned children.
It provides support only to children who lost one parent before 2020.
It provides only free school meals and no health support.
It is restricted to children below six years receiving Anganwadi services.
139.x: PM CARES for Children was launched in 2021 for children who lost parents or specified guardians to COVID-19 and provides a corpus of Rs.10 lakh at 23, along with education and health support.
139.tq: Find the option that preserves the scheme’s beneficiary, amount and age details.

139.s: Under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Amendment Act, 2021, who has been made the focal point for adoption matters in a district?
139.x: The JJ Amendment Act 2021 made the District Magistrate the focal point for adoption. The CWC is a statutory body for children in need of care, but not the designated focal point; the District Judge and SP are not given this role.
139.tq: JJ Amendment 2021 -> DM handles adoption.

139.s: Which scheme is described as one of the world’s largest SHG-based rural livelihood programmes?
139.x: DAY-NRLM, launched in 2011, is an SHG-based rural livelihoods programme described as one of the world’s largest.
139.tq: Identify the scheme from its distinctive scale and SHG-based livelihood feature.

139.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Swavalambini — 2022 — entrepreneurship programme for women students in the North-East
139.x: Swavalambini was associated with 2022 and promoted entrepreneurship among women students in the North-East through MSDE and NITI Aayog. The other pairs mix up the years and objectives of different schemes.
139.tq: Match the less familiar scheme with its distinctive target group, geography and institutional partners.

139.s: PM Ujjwala Yojana was launched in May 2016 by which Ministry and provides what principal benefit?
o: Ministry of Rural Development; SHG loans to rural women
Ministry of Women and Child Development; free maternity benefits
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas; deposit-free LPG connections to adult women of poor households
Ministry of Finance; girl-child savings accounts
139.x: PM Ujjwala Yojana was launched in May 2016 by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas to provide deposit-free LPG connections to adult women of poor households.
139.tq: Use the ministry-benefit pairing to distinguish PM Ujjwala from the similarly named anti-trafficking scheme.

139.s: The targeted subsidy under PM Ujjwala Yojana is cited as ₹300 per cylinder for up to:
139.x: The cited targeted subsidy is ₹300 per cylinder for up to 12 refills.
139.tq: Test the exact ceiling attached to a subsidy rather than confusing it with the per-cylinder amount.

139.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Swadhar, which provides shelter to women in difficult circumstances, is now part of Shakti Sadan.
2. Ujjawala is the scheme that provides deposit-free LPG connections to women of poor households.
3. PM Ujjwala Yojana was launched by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: Statement 1 is correct: Swadhar now sits inside Shakti Sadan. Statement 2 is wrong: Ujjawala deals with trafficking; LPG connections come under PM Ujjwala Yojana. Statement 3 is correct: PMUY (May 2016) is run by MoPNG. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
139.tq: Ujjawala = trafficking; Ujjwala = LPG (MoPNG).

139.s: The Allahabad High Court held on 1 July 2026 that the age limits under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act apply:
o: Only to persons governed by personal laws without exceptions
To all citizens irrespective of religion
Only to persons below the age of 18 who reside in Uttar Pradesh
139.x: The Allahabad High Court held that the PCMA age limits apply to all citizens irrespective of religion.
139.tq: Test the constitutional-law scope of a statute by focusing on the phrase that removes the religious distinction.

139.s: Poshan Pakhwada 2026 was launched in Andhra Pradesh at:
139.x: The Andhra Pradesh launch of Poshan Pakhwada 2026 took place at Gajuwaka in Visakhapatnam.
139.tq: Use the precise launch location to distinguish an Andhra Pradesh angle from the national BBBP launch location.

139.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Andhra Pradesh take-home ration package?
o: 2.5 kg Balamrutham, eggs and milk, with 200 ml milk in the richer tribal package
5 kg rice, pulses and oil, with no separate tribal provision
2.5 kg Balamrutham and fruit juice, with 100 ml milk in tribal areas
Only eggs and milk, without Balamrutham
139.x: The package includes 2.5 kg of Balamrutham, eggs and milk; the tribal package is richer and provides 200 ml of milk.
139.tq: Apply the service description to a field-level scenario and identify the enhanced tribal provision.

139.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the Andhra Pradesh women and child welfare data cited?
o: Sakhi One Stop Centres — all 26 districts
139.x: Sakhi One Stop Centres are present in all 26 districts. The cited figures are 28 Shakti Sadans, 1,02,000 women reached by PMMVY, and Women Helpline 181 since 2016.
139.tq: Find the correctly matched administrative figure while rejecting altered counts and dates.

139.s: Which of the following statements best reflects the criticism of the women and child welfare schemes cited?
o: They continue to focus on survival rather than full child development, and last-mile gaps remain in tribal and Rayalaseema hamlets.
They focus mainly on full child development and have no survival-oriented component.
They have eliminated all implementation gaps in tribal areas.
They are limited exclusively to urban women and children.
139.x: The criticism is that the schemes still emphasise survival rather than complete child development, while last-mile gaps persist in tribal and Rayalaseema hamlets.
139.tq: Choose the balanced evaluative statement; absolute claims such as “all” and “eliminated” are traps.

139.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the cited ‘first’ or unique feature?
o: BBBP — first launched at Varanasi; PMMVY — only nutrition scheme under NFSA
Tithi Bhojan — first began in Gujarat; PMMVY — only cash maternity benefit written into the NFSA
Poshan Maah — first began in Gajuwaka; PMMVY — only LPG subsidy under NFSA
Ujjawala — first began in Panipat; PMMVY — only SHG scheme under NFSA
139.x: Tithi Bhojan began in Gujarat, and PMMVY is identified as the only cash maternity benefit written into the National Food Security Act.
139.tq: Match each unique descriptor with the correct programme and avoid swapping launch locations or policy sectors.

140.s: The Cabinet approval of an MoU on cooperation in the disability sector referred to cooperation between India and:
140.x: The Cabinet approved an MoU between India and South Africa on cooperation in the disability sector.
140.tq: Recall the partner country in the disability-sector MoU without substituting a familiar bilateral partner.

140.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. India ratified the UNCRPD.
B. The UN General Assembly adopted the UNCRPD.
C. The RPwD Act, 2016, was enacted.
D. The RPwD Act, 2016, came into force.
140.x: The UNCRPD was adopted on 13 December 2006, India ratified it in October 2007, the RPwD Act was enacted in 2016, and it came into force on 19 April 2017.
140.tq: Fix the first two international dates before placing enactment and commencement.

140.s: Which of the following correctly describes India's position regarding the Optional Protocol to the UNCRPD?
o: India has replaced it with the National Trust Act, 1999.
India has not ratified it, and it provides an individual complaints mechanism.
India has signed and ratified it but has excluded all complaints relating to education.
India has ratified it and accepted compulsory individual complaints jurisdiction.
140.x: India has not ratified the Optional Protocol to the UNCRPD. The Protocol provides an individual complaints mechanism.
140.tq: Separate the Convention ratification from the unratified Optional Protocol and its complaints mechanism.

140.s: The International Year of Disabled Persons was observed in:
140.x: The International Year of Disabled Persons was observed in 1981.
140.tq: Distinguish an international year from an annual observance or statutory enactment year.

140.s: In the Seventh Schedule, ‘Relief of the disabled and unemployable’ is placed under which entry of the State List?
140.x: ‘Relief of the disabled and unemployable’ is State List Entry 9.
140.tq: Test the exact List entry number against nearby constitutional entry numbers.

140.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Article 41 — Public assistance in disablement
2. Article 46 — Interests of weaker sections
3. State List Entry 9 — Relief of the disabled and unemployable
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
140.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Article 41 concerns public assistance in disablement, Article 46 concerns weaker sections, and State List Entry 9 concerns relief of the disabled and unemployable.
140.tq: Match each constitutional provision with its exact subject before checking the code.

140.s: A proposal for a national minimum disability pension of Rs 8,000 per month has been linked with which constitutional provision?
140.x: The proposal for a national minimum disability pension of Rs 8,000 per month has been linked with Article 41, which refers to public assistance in cases of disablement.
140.tq: Apply the constitutional principle of public assistance to the proposed pension floor.

140.s: The International Day of Persons with Disabilities is observed every year on:
140.x: 3 December is the International Day of Persons with Disabilities (the Accessible India Campaign was also launched on 3 December 2015). 1 October is the International Day of Older Persons, 10 December is Human Rights Day and 15 June is World Elder Abuse Awareness Day.
140.tq: 3 Dec = PwD Day; 1 Oct = Older Persons.

140.s:
Assertion (A): The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, is regarded as a rights-based law.
Reason (R): It replaced the PwD (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995, which was welfare-based.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
140.x: Both statements are true. The 2016 Act replaced the welfare-based 1995 law with a rights-based framework, which explains the assertion.
140.tq: Test whether the earlier law and the change in legislative approach explain the assertion.

140.s: Section 2(s) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, defines a person with disability as one having a long-term:
o: Physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairment which, in interaction with barriers, hinders full and effective participation
Sensory impairment certified exclusively by a Central institution
Physical impairment only, irrespective of social or environmental barriers
Temporary illness that prevents employment for more than six months
140.x: Section 2(s) covers long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairment which, in interaction with barriers, hinders full participation in society.
140.tq: Use the precise statutory wording and reject narrower or substituted definitions.

140.s:
With reference to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, consider the following statements:
1. The number of specified disabilities increased from 7 to 21.
2. Autism, acid attack victims and sickle cell disease are among the examples included.
3. The Central Government may add further disabilities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
140.x: The Act increased specified disabilities from 7 to 21, includes conditions such as autism, acid attack victims and sickle cell disease, and permits the Central Government to add more disabilities.
140.tq: Verify the count, examples and delegated power together.

140.s:
With reference to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, consider the following statements:
1. Benchmark disability means at least 40% of a specified disability.
2. It provides 5% reservation in government jobs and 4% in higher education seats.
3. Children with benchmark disabilities are entitled to free education from 6 to 18 years of age.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
140.x: Statement 1 is correct: benchmark disability is at least 40%. Statement 2 is wrong: the figures are reversed - 4% in government jobs and 5% in higher education. Statement 3 is correct: free education for ages 6-18. So '1 and 3 only' is right; options containing 2 are wrong.
140.tq: Jobs 4, colleges 5 - watch for the swapped-figures trap.

140.s: Which of the following statements regarding the RPwD Act, 2016, is correct?
o: It was passed in 2018 and came into force in 2019.
It was enacted in 2016 and came into force on 3 December 2016.
It was enacted in 1995 and came into force on 19 April 2017.
It was enacted in 2016 and came into force on 19 April 2017.
140.x: The Act was enacted in 2016 and came into force on 19 April 2017. The description of it as a law passed in 2018 is incorrect.
140.tq: Separate the year of enactment from the date of commencement and reject the famous-year trap.

140.s:
Assertion (A): A person with 40% disability cannot automatically be denied consideration for a government job merely because the disability exceeds an administratively fixed upper ceiling.
Reason (R): The Supreme Court has treated 40% as the floor for benchmark disability, while suitability must be assessed with reference to functional ability and reasonable accommodation.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
140.x: Both the assertion and reason are correct. The Supreme Court held in March 2026 that 40% is a floor, not an upper ceiling, and that functional ability with reasonable accommodation is relevant to suitability.
140.tq: Test the distinction between a minimum threshold and an impermissible upper ceiling.

140.s: Survivors of forcible acid ingestion were recognised as acid attack victims under the RPwD Act after:
o: The adoption of the UNCRPD in 2006
The enactment of the National Trust Act in 1999
The ratification of the UNCRPD by India in 2007
140.x: After a Supreme Court interpretation in 2026, survivors of forcible acid ingestion were recognised as acid attack victims under the Act.
140.tq: Link the later judicial interpretation to the legal recognition it produced.

140.s: The Inclusive India initiative is primarily aimed at:
o: Providing legal guardianship to persons with multiple disabilities
Providing concessional loans to persons with disabilities for self-employment
Bringing persons with intellectual and developmental disabilities into the mainstream
Regulating the training of rehabilitation professionals
140.x: The Inclusive India initiative of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, associated with the National Trust, seeks to bring persons with intellectual and developmental disabilities into the mainstream.
140.tq: Match the initiative with its distinctive target group and purpose.

140.s: Which of the following bodies is a statutory authority under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, empowered to monitor implementation and take up complaints?
o: Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities
140.x: The Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities is the statutory authority under the RPwD Act, 2016, responsible for monitoring implementation and taking up complaints.
140.tq: Identify the authority from its statutory monitoring and complaint-handling role.

140.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Trust:
1. It functions under the National Trust Act, 1999.
2. It covers persons with autism, cerebral palsy, mental retardation and multiple disabilities.
3. It regulates the Central Rehabilitation Register.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
140.x: The National Trust Act, 1999 covers autism, cerebral palsy, mental retardation and multiple disabilities and provides for welfare and legal guardianship. The Central Rehabilitation Register is maintained by the Rehabilitation Council of India.
140.tq: Use the wrong-body trap by separating National Trust functions from RCI functions.

140.s: Which one of the following is NOT a scheme associated with the National Trust?
140.x: Niramaya, Disha, Vikas, Samarth and Gharaunda are schemes associated with the National Trust. PRASHAST is not a National Trust scheme.
140.tq: Find the odd scheme by checking which option belongs outside the National Trust group.

140.s: Niramaya, a scheme of the National Trust, provides:
o: Five per cent reservation in higher education
Health insurance up to Rs. 1 lakh per year
140.x: Niramaya provides health insurance coverage of up to Rs. 1 lakh per year. Travel concessions and loans are associated with other initiatives or institutions.
140.tq: Link the scheme to its specific monetary entitlement rather than a general disability benefit.

140.s: The principal function of the Rehabilitation Council of India is to:
o: Provide legal guardianship under the National Trust Act
Monitor implementation of the RPwD Act through State Commissioners
Regulate the training of rehabilitation and special-education professionals and maintain the Central Rehabilitation Register
140.x: The Rehabilitation Council of India regulates training of rehabilitation and special-education professionals and maintains the Central Rehabilitation Register.
140.tq: Associate the professional regulator with training standards and the register it maintains.

140.s: Which of the following statements about the Rehabilitation Council of India is correct?
o: It was established under the RCI Act, 1992, became statutory in 1993 and was amended in 2000.
It was established under the National Trust Act, 1999, and amended in 2016.
It was created under the RPwD Act, 2016, and became statutory in 2017.
It was established under the PwD Act, 1995, and amended in 2006.
140.x: The RCI is associated with the RCI Act, 1992; it became statutory in 1993 and was amended in 2000.
140.tq: Track the legal basis and amendments without confusing RCI with the National Trust or RPwD Acts.

140.s:
Consider the following pairs (National Institute / body - location or field):
1. National Institute for locomotor disability - Kolkata
2. SVNIRTAR - Dehradun
3. NIEPID - Secunderabad, intellectual disabilities
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
140.x: Pair 1 is correct: the locomotor-disability institute is at Kolkata. Pair 2 is wrong: SVNIRTAR is at Cuttack; Dehradun hosts the visual-disability institute. Pair 3 is correct: NIEPID, Secunderabad, is for intellectual disabilities. So '1 and 3 only' is right; options containing 2 are wrong.
140.tq: Kolkata-locomotor, Dehradun-visual, Cuttack-SVNIRTAR, Secunderabad-intellectual, Gwalior-para-sports.

140.s: The Accessible India Campaign was launched on which date?
140.x: The Accessible India Campaign was launched on 3 December 2015 as a flagship initiative for universal accessibility.
140.tq: Use the exact launch date rather than confusing it with an observance date.

140.s: Which of the following correctly represents the three verticals of the Accessible India Campaign?
o: Transport system, social security and vocational training
Built environment, transport system and ICT ecosystem
Built environment, electoral reforms and digital payments
Health services, education system and rural housing
140.x: The three verticals are accessibility in the built environment, transport system and ICT ecosystem.
140.tq: Identify the complete official triad and reject neighbouring disability-welfare activities.

140.s: The Sugamya Bharat App is primarily a platform for which of the following?
o: Providing monthly pensions to persons with disabilities
140.x: The Sugamya Bharat App functions as a crowdsourcing platform through which accessibility gaps can be reported.
140.tq: Match the digital application with its operational function, not with another disability service.

140.s:
Which of the following statements regarding accessible elections is correct?
1. Accessible elections include accessible polling booths.
2. Braille-enabled EVMs are associated with accessible elections.
3. Accessible elections are one of the three verticals of the Accessible India Campaign.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
140.x: Accessible booths and Braille-enabled EVMs are measures for accessible elections. Accessible elections are not listed as one of the three campaign verticals; the verticals are built environment, transport and ICT.
140.tq: Separate a related accessibility measure from the officially listed campaign verticals.

140.s: The Supreme Court recognised safe footpaths as a fundamental right under which Article, along with a minimum footpath width of 1.8 metres?
140.x: The Supreme Court recognised safe footpaths as part of the right to life under Article 21 and specified a minimum width of 1.8 metres.
140.tq: Link the judicially recognised right with the correct constitutional Article and measurement.

140.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: UDID — single national disability ID and certificate
SIPDA — monthly pension to BPL households
140.x: UDID provides a single national disability identity and certificate. SIPDA, DDRS and PM-DAKSH have different functions.
140.tq: Use the exact institutional function to distinguish identity, grants and training schemes.

140.s: Which scheme provides free aids and appliances to eligible persons below a monthly income of Rs 22,500 and subsidised assistance up to Rs 30,000?
140.x: The ADIP scheme provides free aids and appliances to persons below the stated income limit and subsidised assistance up to Rs 30,000.
140.tq: Match the income ceiling and assistance limit with the correct scheme.

140.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: PM-DAKSH — skill training and job linkage
IGNDPS — monthly pension to severely disabled persons from BPL households
SIPDA — free aids and appliances below a specified income ceiling
DDRS — grants to NGOs for rehabilitation and vocational training
140.x: SIPDA provides grant-in-aid for implementing the RPwD Act. Free aids and appliances are associated with ADIP.
140.tq: Find the scheme whose benefit has been swapped with that of ADIP.

140.s:
Which of the following is NOT a component of the Scholarships for Students with Disabilities scheme?
1. Pre-matric scholarship
2. Post-matric scholarship
3. National Fellowship
4. Monthly disability pension
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
140.x: Monthly disability pension is not one of the six scholarship components. The listed components include pre-matric, post-matric and National Fellowship, along with Top Class, Overseas and Free Coaching.
140.tq: Find the welfare benefit that does not belong to a scholarship-component list.

140.s:
Which of the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh welfare measures is correct?
1. Inclusive education assistance is Rs 3,500 per child with special needs.
2. Andhra Pradesh has 679 Bhavitha Centres.
3. The Andhra Pradesh Samagra Shiksha programme received the national award for Best State in implementing the RPwD Act for 2024-25.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
140.x: All three statements are correct: the assistance is Rs 3,500 per child, there are 679 Bhavitha Centres, and AP received the stated national award for 2024-25.
140.tq: Combine the monetary, institutional and award facts without confusing them with national scheme data.

140.s: Special education under the cited framework primarily targets:
o: All adult learners undertaking vocational training
140.x: The target group for special education is children with disabilities, or CwSN; it is not a programme exclusively for gifted groups.
140.tq: Discriminate between children with disabilities and the misleading alternative of gifted children.

140.s:
Which of the following services is covered under Samagra Shiksha’s inclusive education component for RPwD-listed disabilities?
1. Assessment
2. Aids and assistive technology
3. Therapy
4. Exclusive education of gifted children
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
140.x: Samagra Shiksha covers assessment, aids, assistive technology and therapy for children with disabilities. Exclusive education of gifted children is not its stated target.
140.tq: Find the unrelated target group while retaining the complete inclusive-education service package.

140.s: Samagra Shiksha’s inclusive education component took over which earlier programme?
140.x: The inclusive education component of Samagra Shiksha took over the earlier IEDSS programme.
140.tq: Distinguish the predecessor education programme from disability rehabilitation and pension schemes.

140.s: EKAM Fest is associated with which of the following objectives?
o: Providing free education to children with benchmark disabilities
Providing cultural training exclusively to government employees with disabilities
Promoting entrepreneurship among Divyangjan and creating awareness of the potential of persons with disabilities
140.x: EKAM stands for Entrepreneurship, Knowledge, Awareness and Marketing. It promotes entrepreneurship among Divyangjan and awareness of the potential of persons with disabilities; it is organised by NDFDC.
140.tq: Expand the acronym through the activity naturally associated with the event.

140.s: Divya Kala Shakti is best described as:
o: A health-insurance scheme of the National Trust
A cultural showcase of the artistic talent of persons with disabilities
A loan programme for self-employment of persons with disabilities
A programme for appointing legal guardians
140.x: Divya Kala Shakti showcases the artistic talent of persons with disabilities and is associated with the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities.
140.tq: Distinguish a cultural showcase from welfare, finance and guardianship programmes.

140.s: NHFDC, now known as the National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation, is primarily concerned with:
o: Legal guardianship for persons with multiple disabilities
Concessional loans for self-employment of persons with disabilities
140.x: NHFDC, now NDFDC, provides concessional loans to persons with disabilities for self-employment. It functions under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities.
140.tq: Identify the institution from its finance-related mandate and reject nearby welfare functions.

140.s: The National Handicapped Finance and Development Corporation (NHFDC), now known as the National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation, functions under which department and ministry?
o: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Department of Rural Development, Ministry of Rural Development
Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education
Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
140.x: NHFDC, now the National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation, is under the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities in the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
140.tq: Use the ‘who administers the scheme?’ method to distinguish the correct department and ministry.

140.s: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a channel for disbursing or facilitating NHFDC loans?
140.x: NHFDC loan channels include State Channelising Agencies, Public Sector Banks and Regional Rural Banks. District Legal Services Authorities are not listed as a loan channel.
140.tq: Find the institution that does not belong to the financing-channel group.

140.s: The PM-DAKSH-DEPwD portal, introduced in 2023, combines which of the following features?
o: UDID-based skilling and Divyangjan Rozgar Setu for jobs
Disability pension disbursement and prison accessibility audits
Census enumeration and international treaty ratification
Artificial-limb production and national award selection
140.x: The PM-DAKSH-DEPwD portal provides UDID-based skilling and the Divyangjan Rozgar Setu for employment opportunities.
140.tq: Match the portal with its two stated digital functions and reject unrelated disability measures.

140.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes ALIMCO?
o: It is a portal for UDID-based skilling and job matching.
It is a UN body responsible for implementing the UNCRPD.
It is a Central Public Sector Enterprise set up in 1972 that makes aids and artificial limbs.
It is a State Channelising Agency set up in 2023 to provide employment loans.
140.x: ALIMCO is a Central Public Sector Enterprise established in 1972 and manufactures aids and artificial limbs.
140.tq: Use the institution–year–function combination to distinguish ALIMCO from a portal or financing agency.

140.s:
Match the following cases with the issue involved:
 a. Jeeja Ghosh v. Union of India
 b. Vikash Kumar v. UPSC
 c. Rajive Raturi v. Union of India

 i. Scribe as reasonable accommodation without benchmark disability
 ii. Mandatory accessibility standards under the RPwD Act
 iii. Deplaning of a woman with cerebral palsy and right to dignity

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
140.x: Jeeja Ghosh concerned deplaning and dignity; Vikash Kumar recognised a scribe as reasonable accommodation; Rajive Raturi concerned mandatory accessibility standards.
140.tq: Start with the distinctive case issue and then eliminate the codes with swapped judgments.

140.s: In Jeeja Ghosh v. Union of India, the principal issue concerned:
o: The maintenance of the Central Rehabilitation Register
A candidate’s entitlement to a scribe without benchmark disability
The framing of mandatory accessibility standards under the RPwD Act
A woman with cerebral palsy being deplaned by an airline and her right to dignity
140.x: Jeeja Ghosh concerned the deplaning of a woman with cerebral palsy by an airline, raising the right to dignity and resulting in compensation.
140.tq: Associate the case with its distinctive factual incident rather than a general accessibility principle.

140.s: Which case recognised a scribe as a form of reasonable accommodation even in the absence of benchmark disability?
o: Jeeja Ghosh v. Union of India
Rajive Raturi v. Union of India
140.x: Vikash Kumar v. UPSC (2021) recognised the availability of a scribe as reasonable accommodation even without benchmark disability.
140.tq: Use the specific accommodation to distinguish the case from dignity and accessibility-standard cases.

140.s: Rajive Raturi v. Union of India (2024) was associated with which issue?
o: Compensation for deplaning a passenger with cerebral palsy
Recognition of an International Year of Disabled Persons
Mandatory accessibility standards to be framed under the RPwD Act
140.x: The case concerned mandatory accessibility standards to be framed under the RPwD Act.
140.tq: Match the judicial direction with the subject-specific accessibility issue.

140.s: Which of the following correctly compares the Census 2011 figure for India with the approximate global estimate mentioned for persons with disabilities?
o: India: 2.21 percent; global estimate: about 16 percent
India: about 16 percent; global estimate: 2.21 percent
140.x: India’s Census 2011 figure was 2.21 percent, whereas the approximate global estimate was about 16 percent; the difference suggests under-reporting in India.
140.tq: Keep national census data separate from the international estimate and disability-type percentages.

140.s: Among the following categories, which was the largest disability group in India according to the cited Census 2011 distribution?
140.x: Movement disability was the largest among the cited categories at 20.3 percent, followed by hearing at 18.9 percent and seeing at 18.8 percent.
140.tq: Compare the three close percentages rather than relying on a broad category impression.

140.s: Which one of the following is the correct descending order of the cited disability categories in Andhra Pradesh?
140.x: The figures are orthopaedic 3.13 lakh, hearing 2.90 lakh, visual 2.03 lakh, multiple 1.96 lakh and mental 1.02 lakh.
140.tq: Use the descending numerical order to test the complete AP category ranking.

140.s:
With reference to Divyang Shakti in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. It was introduced in 2026.
2. It provides completely free travel for persons with disabilities in APSRTC buses.
3. It provides concessional loans for self-employment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
140.x: Divyang Shakti was introduced in Andhra Pradesh in 2026 and provides 100% free travel for persons with disabilities in APSRTC buses. Concessional self-employment loans are associated with NDFDC, not Divyang Shakti.
140.tq: Separate a transport entitlement from the nearby finance-related initiative.

140.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh initiative named ‘Indra Dhanassu’, free APSRTC bus travel is available to persons with disabilities having at least what percentage of disability?
140.x: From 18 March 2026, free APSRTC bus travel is available in the specified categories to persons with 40 percent or more disability.
140.tq: Focus on the eligibility threshold rather than the separate escort concession.

140.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Divyang Shakti free bus travel arrangement, disability certification is carried out through:
140.x: The cited Andhra Pradesh arrangement uses SADAREM for disability certification.
140.tq: Distinguish the state certification system from national identity, training and screening platforms.

140.s: The Andhra Pradesh Differently Abled and Senior Citizens Assistance Corporation primarily performs which functions?
o: Supplying aids and appliances and running economic-rehabilitation schemes
Conducting the Census and issuing national disability cards
Providing only international scholarships to persons with disabilities
Regulating rehabilitation professionals and maintaining the Central Rehabilitation Register
140.x: The Corporation supplies aids and appliances and runs economic-rehabilitation schemes for persons with disabilities and senior citizens.
140.tq: Identify the state welfare corporation by its paired functions rather than by a statutory regulatory role.

140.s: With reference to the comparison of disability-welfare expenditure, which one of the following is correct?
o: India spends about 0.12–0.15 per cent of GDP, whereas South Africa spends about 0.02 per cent.
India spends about 1.2 per cent of GDP, whereas South Africa spends about 0.12 per cent.
India spends about 0.02 per cent of GDP, whereas South Africa spends about 0.12–0.15 per cent.
Both India and South Africa spend about 0.02 per cent of GDP.
140.x: The stated comparison is approximately 0.02 per cent of GDP for India and 0.12–0.15 per cent for South Africa.
140.tq: Check the direction of the comparison and retain the correct range for the second country.

140.s: The Supreme Court’s direction concerning prisoners with disabilities included which of the following?
o: Replacing the RPwD Act with the 1995 disability law
Ensuring prison accessibility and revising prison manuals in line with the RPwD Act
Limiting accessibility measures to courts and tribunals
Transferring all prison administration to the Union Government
140.x: The Supreme Court directed attention to prison accessibility and revision of prison manuals in accordance with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016.
140.tq: Identify the operative judicial direction rather than selecting a broad institutional change not stated.

140.s: The Supreme Court’s recognition of digital access as part of Article 21 was made with reference to which international convention?
o: Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women
United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights
United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child
140.x: The Supreme Court recognised digital access as part of Article 21 while citing the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.
140.tq: Link the judicially recognised right with the specific international disability convention cited.

140.s:
Consider the following statements regarding disability legislation and enumeration:
1. The 1995 disability law recognised seven disabilities.
2. The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 recognises 21 disabilities.
3. The Census 2027 categories are described as narrower than the 21 categories in the 2016 Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
140.x: All three statements are correct: the 1995 Act recognised seven disabilities, the 2016 Act recognises 21, and the Census 2027 categories are criticised as narrower than the Act’s 21 categories.
140.tq: Compare the two Acts first, then test the separate criticism concerning Census 2027 categories.

141.s: Under the National Policy on Older Persons, 1999, an ‘older person’ is one who is:
141.x: The National Policy on Older Persons, 1999 defines an older person as an individual aged 60 years or above.
141.tq: Identify the policy definition rather than using a general retirement-age assumption.

141.s: Which of the following is NOT among the principal areas of intervention identified under the National Policy on Older Persons, 1999?
o: Compulsory military service for older persons
141.x: Compulsory military service for older persons is not part of NPOP 1999. Its 14 principal areas of intervention include health care and nutrition, and its approach relies on self-provision for old age, family care, NGO support and geriatric training.
141.tq: Reject the option that is unrelated to the policy’s welfare and care orientation.

141.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Policy for Senior Citizens, 2011:
1. It envisages harsh punishment for elder abuse.
2. It gives importance to income security, homecare and health insurance.
3. It focuses on ageing in place.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
141.x: All three statements reflect the focus of the National Policy for Senior Citizens, 2011.
141.tq: Recognise the complete policy package instead of selecting only one welfare objective.

141.s: The National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly (NPHCE) was launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in:
141.x: NPHCE was launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in 2010–11.
141.tq: Match the programme with its ministry and launch period.

141.s: The National Policy on Older Persons, 1999 identified how many areas of intervention?
141.x: The National Policy on Older Persons identified 14 areas of intervention.
141.tq: Use the exact policy figure rather than an approximate count.

141.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Policy on Older Persons, 1999 was framed by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
2. The National Policy for Senior Citizens, 2011 gives special focus to elderly women.
3. The National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly was launched by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
141.x: Statement 1 is correct: NPOP 1999 is a MoSJE policy. Statement 2 is correct: NPSC 2011 focuses on elderly women and ageing in place. Statement 3 is wrong: NPHCE was launched by MoHFW in 2010-11. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
141.tq: NPOP = MoSJE; NPHCE = MoHFW.

141.s: Under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, the obligation to maintain parents extends to:
o: Only biological sons above 18 years of age
Biological, adopted and step-children, and legal heirs in the relevant circumstances
141.x: The Act places obligations on biological, adopted and step-children, and also on legal heirs in relation to senior citizens who cannot maintain themselves.
141.tq: Watch for the restrictive word ‘only’ in the options on legal obligation.

141.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the Maintenance Tribunal under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 is headed at the sub-divisional level by the:
141.x: In Andhra Pradesh, the Maintenance Tribunal functions at the sub-division level and is headed by the Revenue Divisional Officer or Sub-Collector.
141.tq: Use the level of the tribunal to identify the appropriate administrative authority.

141.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the appellate mechanism under the Act in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The Appellate Tribunal is at State level and headed by the Governor.
The Appellate Tribunal is at sub-division level and headed by the RDO.
The Appellate Tribunal is at district level and headed by the District Collector.
The Appellate Tribunal is at national level and headed by the Union Minister.
141.x: The Appellate Tribunal is constituted at the district level in Andhra Pradesh and is headed by the District Collector.
141.tq: Distinguish the maintenance tribunal from the appellate tribunal by level and authority.

141.s: Section 20 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 deals with:
141.x: Section 20 concerns the provision of medical care for senior citizens and forms the basis of the National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly.
141.tq: Use section-number matching and reject provisions belonging to Sections 23 or other parts of the Act.

141.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007:
