1. At least one old-age home is contemplated in every district.
2. Abandoning a senior citizen may attract imprisonment up to three months and/or a fine up to ₹5,000.
3. The Act is administered by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
141.x: All three statements are correct. The Act provides for old-age homes, penalises abandonment and is administered by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
141.tq: Combine institutional, penal and administrative provisions without confusing them with pension schemes.

141.s: An elderly person transfers property to another person on the condition that the transferee will provide basic physical needs and care, but the transferee fails to do so. Under which provision can the transfer be cancelled by the Tribunal?
o: Section 32 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
Section 23 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
Section 12 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
Section 18 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
141.x: Section 23 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 permits the Tribunal to declare such a property transfer void when the promised care is not provided.
141.tq: Identify the statutory provision from the facts of conditional property transfer and failure of care.

141.s: Which one of the following is a correct provision of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007?
o: The Maintenance Tribunal can decide only cases relating to property transfer.
The Maintenance Tribunal has no power to permit an appeal.
The Maintenance Tribunal may award up to Rs 20,000 per month and should decide the case within 30 days.
The Maintenance Tribunal may award up to Rs 10,000 per month and should decide the case within 90 days.
141.x: The Act prescribed a maximum maintenance of Rs 10,000 per month, required disposal within 90 days and allowed an appeal.
141.tq: Combine the amount, time limit and appeal feature to distinguish the statutory tribunal provision.

141.s: The Himachal Pradesh Maintenance of Parents and Dependents Act was enacted in which year?
141.x: The earlier State legislation referred to is the Himachal Pradesh Maintenance of Parents and Dependents Act, 2001.
141.tq: Use the date-based distinction between the earlier State law and the later central Act.

141.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens (Amendment) Bill, 2019:
1. It proposed removing the Rs 10,000 ceiling on maintenance.
2. It proposed covering in-laws and grandchildren.
3. It was enacted as an Act of Parliament.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
141.x: The Bill proposed removing the maintenance cap and extending coverage to in-laws and grandchildren, but it was not passed.
141.tq: The enacted-versus-proposed distinction is the key trap in the third statement.

141.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding laws, policies and programmes for senior citizens.

List-I
 a. Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act
 b. National Policy on Older Persons
 c. National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly
 d. National Policy for Senior Citizens

List-II
 i. 2011
 ii. 2007
 iii. 2010–11
 iv. 1999

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
141.x: The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act was enacted in 2007; NPOP was issued in 1999; NPHCE began in 2010–11; and NPSC dates to 2011.
141.tq: Start with the statutory Act–year pair and then complete the policy and programme matches.

141.s: Under the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS), the central assistance is payable at which of the following rates?
o: ₹300 per month for 60–79 years and ₹500 per month for 80 years and above
₹500 per month for 60–79 years and ₹1,000 per month for 80 years and above
₹100 per month for 60–79 years and ₹200 per month for 80 years and above
₹200 per month for 60–79 years and ₹500 per month for 80 years and above
141.x: IGNOAPS provides ₹200 per month to persons aged 60–79 years and ₹500 per month to those aged 80 years and above. It is meant for elderly persons belonging to BPL households.
141.tq: Split the age groups and match each with its corresponding amount.

141.s: Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana was launched on 1 April 2017 at which place?
141.x: Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana was launched at Nellore in Andhra Pradesh on 1 April 2017.
141.tq: Discriminate between closely related locations within the same State.

141.s: Which one of the following is NOT provided as a free physical aid under the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana?
141.x: The scheme provides aids such as walking sticks, wheelchairs, hearing aids and dentures to BPL senior citizens. Motorised agricultural pumps are not covered.
141.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the same beneficiary-support group.

141.s: Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana is implemented through which combination?
141.x: Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana is associated with the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and ALIMCO.
141.tq: Identify the implementing agency by separating the ministry from the delivery corporation.

141.s:
Consider the following statements about the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana:
1. It is funded from the Senior Citizens’ Welfare Fund.
2. At least 30 per cent beneficiaries in each district are required to be women.
3. It is intended for BPL senior citizens.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
141.x: The scheme is funded from the Senior Citizens’ Welfare Fund, targets BPL senior citizens and requires at least 30 per cent women beneficiaries in each district.
141.tq: Check whether the beneficiary, funding and gender-target details all belong to the same scheme.

141.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the components of Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana?
141.x: The four components of AVYAY are the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens, State Action Plan, Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana and Elder Line. The National Family Benefit Scheme is an NSAP component.
141.tq: Use the programme-family distinction to reject an NSAP component.

141.s: Under the Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana, which of the following combinations is correct?
o: 10% assured pension for 10 years; maximum purchase price ₹7.5 lakh; maximum pension ₹10,000 per month
8% assured pension for 5 years; maximum purchase price ₹10 lakh; maximum pension ₹7,500 per month
8% assured pension for 10 years; maximum purchase price ₹7.5 lakh; maximum pension ₹5,000 per month
7% assured pension for 15 years; maximum purchase price ₹5 lakh; maximum pension ₹3,000 per month
141.x: PMVVY offered an assured pension at 8 per cent for 10 years, with a maximum purchase price of ₹7.5 lakh and maximum pension of ₹5,000 per month.
141.tq: Match the three numerical limits without confusing duration, purchase price and pension ceiling.

141.s: Which one of the following statements regarding PMVVY is correct?
o: It is administered by MoSJE through ALIMCO and is funded by the Senior Citizens’ Welfare Fund.
It is administered by MoRD through India Post and is available only to BPL persons.
It is administered by MoHFW through the National Health Authority and provides medical insurance.
It is administered by the Ministry of Finance through LIC and is GST-exempt.
141.x: PMVVY is associated with the Ministry of Finance and LIC, and the scheme is GST-exempt. It is a pension product rather than a medical-insurance scheme.
141.tq: Apply the ‘who would administer this product?’ method to separate pension, welfare and health schemes.

141.s: The Senior Citizen Savings Scheme primarily provides:
o: Free medical devices to BPL elderly persons
Equity funding for elderly self-help groups
Food grains to destitute elderly persons
Safe fixed-interest savings for senior citizens
141.x: The Senior Citizen Savings Scheme, available through India Post and banks, provides a safe fixed-interest savings avenue for senior citizens.
141.tq: Match the financial product with its core benefit rather than with welfare or health benefits.

141.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPOP):
1. It may provide up to 90 per cent of project cost to eligible NGOs.
2. It supports old-age homes, day-care centres and mobile medicare units.
3. It is a component of AVYAY.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
141.x: IPOP can support up to 90 per cent of project cost for NGOs and covers old-age homes, day-care centres and mobile medicare units. It is included under AVYAY.
141.tq: Verify the funding, service and programme-hierarchy statements together.

141.s: Which of the following initiatives is associated with the promotion of the silver economy under AVYAY?
141.x: SAGE promotes innovations and enterprises in the senior-care sector and supports the silver economy. AGRASR is another AVYAY-related initiative involving elderly self-help groups.
141.tq: Separate innovation and enterprise initiatives from NSAP assistance components.

141.s:
Consider the following statements about IGNOAPS:
1. It is a component of the National Social Assistance Programme.
2. It is administered by the Ministry of Rural Development.
3. Its assistance has remained frozen at Rs 200 since 2007 and it covers about 2.2 crore people.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
141.x: All three statements are correct. IGNOAPS is under NSAP and the Ministry of Rural Development; the stated figure records Rs 200 as frozen since 2007 and coverage of about 2.2 crore people.
141.tq: Combine institutional, administrative and numerical features in one coded question.

141.s: Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana was renamed from which earlier programme?
o: National Action Plan for Senior Citizens
National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly
141.x: Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana, introduced in April 2021, was renamed from the National Action Plan for Senior Citizens.
141.tq: Match the renamed scheme with its previous title.

141.s: What is the primary purpose of the SACRED portal?
o: To link senior citizens with employment opportunities
To distribute assistive devices to persons with disabilities
To provide old-age pensions through banks
141.x: SACRED stands for Senior Able Citizens for Re-Employment in Dignity and links elderly persons with jobs.
141.tq: Expand the acronym conceptually and identify the service it provides.

141.s: The Ayushman Vay Vandana card under AB-PMJAY is meant for:
o: Children below 10 years from SECC households
Only women aged 70 years and above
All persons aged 60 years and above subject to an income ceiling
All persons aged 70 years and above irrespective of income
141.x: All senior citizens aged 70 years and above are eligible for the Ayushman Vay Vandana card irrespective of income.
141.tq: Test the age threshold together with the important income-related exception.

141.s: Elder Line 14567 is:
o: A national helpline for senior citizens and a component of AVYAY
A legal-aid helpline exclusively for women
A medical-insurance registration number for children
141.x: Elder Line 14567 is the National Helpline for Senior Citizens and forms part of AVYAY.
141.tq: Use the number and programme association together to identify the helpline.

141.s: Which organisation provides technical support to Elder Line along with State emergency response centres?
141.x: Elder Line is run by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment with State emergency response centres and technical support from Tata Trusts and NSE Foundation.
141.tq: Match the helpline’s technical-support partners rather than its administering ministry.

141.s:
Consider the following statements about Elder Line:
1. It operates under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
2. Its helpline number is 14567.
3. It is limited to pension disbursement and does not provide broader senior-citizen support.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
141.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Elder Line is a National Helpline for Senior Citizens and is not limited merely to pension disbursement.
141.tq: Find the negative overstatement that narrows a broad public-service helpline to one function.

141.s: Which organisation is associated with elderly-care services and the release of elder-abuse surveys in India?
141.x: HelpAge India runs elderly-care services and releases surveys relating to elder abuse.
141.tq: Match the organisation with its distinctive activity rather than with a general human-rights function.

141.s: In Andhra Pradesh, senior citizens facing abuse or cyber fraud while living alone may approach which authority for assistance?
141.x: Such victims may approach the Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO).
141.tq: Use the situation-based clue and ask which local administrative authority would receive the grievance.

141.s: The UN Decade of Healthy Ageing covers which period?
141.x: The UN Decade of Healthy Ageing covers the period 2021–2030.
141.tq: Distinguish the decade framework from the earlier Madrid International Plan of Action on Ageing.

141.s: The International Day of Older Persons is observed on
141.x: The International Day of Older Persons is observed on 1 October.
141.tq: Use direct date recall while distinguishing it from World Elder Abuse Awareness Day.

141.s: World Elder Abuse Awareness Day is observed on
141.x: World Elder Abuse Awareness Day is observed on 15 June.
141.tq: Apply confusable-date discrimination between the two observances relating to older persons.

141.s: The Madrid International Plan of Action on Ageing was adopted in which year?
141.x: The Madrid International Plan of Action on Ageing dates to 2002. 1999 is India's NPOP, 2011 is India's NPSC, and 2021 is the start of the UN Decade of Healthy Ageing (2021-2030).
141.tq: Madrid Plan 2002; UN Decade 2021-30.

141.s:
Consider the following statements regarding elderly welfare:
1. Calls have been made for an inflation-indexed minimum pension floor under the National Social Assistance Programme.
2. Pension erosion is identified as a current concern affecting elderly welfare.
3. The proposed pension floor is intended to remain unrelated to inflation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
141.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the proposed floor is specifically intended to be indexed to inflation.
141.tq: Reject the reversed meaning in statement 3 and select the two statements that express the stated policy concern.

141.s: In Andhra Pradesh, weekly geriatric outpatient departments are functioning in how many Primary Health Centres, while daily geriatric outpatient departments are functioning in how many Community Health Centres?
141.x: Weekly geriatric OPDs function in 1,684 PHCs and daily geriatric OPDs in 177 CHCs in Andhra Pradesh.
141.tq: Keep the two facility types and their corresponding figures paired; the main trap is reversing the numbers.

141.s: Which was the first State to enact a law for the maintenance of parents, before the central Act of 2007?
141.x: Himachal Pradesh enacted the Maintenance of Parents and Dependents Act, 2001, the first such State law. Kerala is first with a Senior Citizens' Welfare Department; Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka are not cited as first.
141.tq: HP 2001 = first parents-maintenance law.

142.s:
Consider the following statements about Census 2011:
1. India's population was about 121.09 crore.
2. About 68.9% of the population was rural.
3. The decadal growth rate was 27.7%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: Statement 1 is correct: 121.09 crore. Statement 2 is correct: 68.9% rural. Statement 3 is wrong: decadal growth in 2001-11 was 17.7%, not 27.7%. So '1 and 2 only' is right; options containing 3 are wrong.
142.tq: Census 2011: 121 crore, about 69% rural, 17.7% growth - growth was slowing.

142.s: India’s next Census is scheduled to be conducted in:
142.x: The next Census of India is scheduled for 2027.
142.tq: Use the stated schedule rather than the previous decennial reference point.

142.s:
Arrange the following phases of India’s population growth in chronological order:
A. High but slowing growth
B. Great Divide
C. Population explosion
D. Decline during 1911–1921
142.x: The correct sequence is decline during 1911–1921, the Great Divide in 1921, population explosion during 1961–1971, and high but slowing growth during 1981–2011.
142.tq: Fix the dated turning points first, then place the broad later phase.

142.s: Which sequence correctly represents the stages of demographic transition?
o: Both rates low → birth rate falls → death rate falls → high rates
High birth and death rates → death rate falls → birth rate falls → both rates low
High birth and death rates → birth rate falls → death rate rises → both rates high
Death rate falls → both rates low → birth rate rises → high death rate
142.x: The demographic transition proceeds from high birth and death rates, to falling death rates, then falling birth rates, and finally low birth and death rates.
142.tq: Track the sequence of mortality decline before fertility decline.

142.s: India is presently described, in demographic-transition terms, as being in the:
142.x: India is described as being in the youth-bulge stage of demographic transition.
142.tq: Identify the current demographic-stage label rather than a general population condition.

142.s: According to NFHS-5, which of the following correctly represents the total fertility rate of India and Andhra Pradesh?
142.x: NFHS-5 recorded India’s total fertility rate at 2.0 and Andhra Pradesh’s at 1.7.
142.tq: Compare the national and State figures without reversing their order.

142.s: Which State recorded the highest total fertility rate in NFHS-5?
142.x: Bihar recorded the highest total fertility rate in NFHS-5, at 3.0.
142.tq: Identify the highest value from the fertility-rate comparison.

142.s: According to SRS 2024, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: India’s TFR was 2.4, with rural and urban rates equal.
India’s TFR was 2.1 and urban TFR was higher than rural TFR.
India’s TFR was 1.5, with rural TFR at 1.9 and urban TFR at 2.1.
India’s TFR was 1.9, with rural TFR at 2.1 and urban TFR at 1.5.
142.x: SRS 2024 reported India’s TFR at 1.9, rural TFR at 2.1 and urban TFR at 1.5.
142.tq: Check both the national figure and the rural–urban direction of difference.

142.s: The dependency ratio is calculated by which of the following formulas?
142.x: The dependency ratio is calculated as the population aged 0–14 plus the population aged 65 and above, divided by the population aged 15–64.
142.tq: Separate the dependent-age groups in the numerator from the working-age denominator.

142.s: According to SRS 2024, which of the following correctly represents the shares of the working-age population and children, respectively?
142.x: SRS 2024 gives the working-age population share as 66.4% and the children’s share as 24%.
142.tq: Read the paired percentages in the order asked.

142.s:
Consider the following statements about the SRS 2024 fertility data:
1. India's TFR has stayed below the replacement level of 2.1 for the fifth year.
2. Only six States have a TFR above 2.1.
3. Bihar recorded the lowest TFR among States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: Statement 1 is correct: India's TFR (1.9) is below 2.1 for the fifth year. Statement 2 is correct: only six States are above 2.1. Statement 3 is wrong: Delhi is lowest (1.2); Bihar is the highest-fertility State (3.0 in NFHS-5). Hence '1 and 2 only'.
142.tq: SRS 2024: 1.9; Delhi lowest 1.2; Bihar highest.

142.s: A large working-age population yields an economic dividend only when it is:
142.x: A large workforce pays off economically only if it is employed productively.
142.tq: Apply the condition that converts demographic size into an economic benefit.

142.s: Which one of the following is an environmental effect of population growth?
o: Reduction in demand for land and water
142.x: Population growth can lead to overuse of resources, creating environmental stress.
142.tq: Select the direct resource-pressure consequence rather than its reversal.

142.s: Repeated subdivision and fragmentation of land holdings is associated with:
142.x: Population growth contributes to repeated subdivision and fragmentation of land holdings.
142.tq: Link the demographic cause with its stated agrarian consequence.

142.s: India needs jobs for approximately how many new working-age people every year, a figure cited in debates on the demographic dividend?
142.x: About 9.7 million new working-age people enter each year, and a large workforce pays off only if employed. The other figures are not the cited estimate.
142.tq: ~9.7 million new workers/year.

142.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the debate on population control:
1. Population control is considered necessary for environmental protection.
2. Southern States that controlled population may lose relative representation and financial advantages.
3. Population carries 15–25% weight in Finance Commission formulas.
4. Delimitation could cost the southern States 8–10 seats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: All four statements reflect the environmental case for population control and the counter-debate concerning the possible demographic and fiscal disadvantage of southern States.
142.tq: Test the environmental argument and the representation–finance counter-debate together.

142.s: The draft Population Management Policy of Andhra Pradesh represents a shift from which approach to which approach?
o: From population control to population management
From population management to population control
From ageing management to migration control
From rural development to urban planning
142.x: The draft policy marks an Andhra Pradesh shift from population control towards population management.
142.tq: Test the direction of policy change by separating control from management.

142.s: Which one of the following correctly states the legal position in Javed v. State of Haryana (2003)?
o: The Supreme Court struck down Haryana’s two-child norm as unconstitutional.
The case abolished two-child norms for local elections throughout India.
The Supreme Court upheld Haryana’s two-child norm.
The case concerned only the calculation of the dependency ratio.
142.x: In Javed v. State of Haryana (2003), the Supreme Court upheld Haryana’s two-child norm.
142.tq: Use the case name and year to identify the precise judicial outcome.

142.s: Which of the following is a feature of Andhra Pradesh's draft Population Management Policy (March 2026)?
o: A two-child norm for contesting local body elections
An incentive of Rs 25,000 for a second or third child and removal of the two-child norm for local elections
A cash penalty on families with more than two children
Compulsory sterilisation after the second child
142.x: The draft policy moves from population control to management, offers Rs 25,000 for a second or third child and removes the two-child norm for local elections. Imposing a two-child norm, penalties or sterilisation would be control measures, the opposite of the policy.
142.tq: AP U-turn: pro-natalist, Rs 25,000, two-child norm removed.

142.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the problems of the elderly is NOT correct?
o: Persons aged 80 years and above commonly face chronic diseases.
The elderly account for approximately 30–35% of hospitalisation spending.
Insurance policies may impose age caps on the elderly.
Ageing generally eliminates the need for long-term health expenditure.
142.x: Ageing does not eliminate health expenditure; persons aged 80 and above face chronic disease, insurance may have age caps, and the elderly account for about 30–35% of hospitalisation spending.
142.tq: Find the reversal of the stated health and expenditure effects.

142.s: Which of the following correctly represents the dependency and pension situation of the elderly?
o: 70% have pensions and 78% are financially independent
78% depend on others and 70% have no pension
70% depend on others and 78% have no pension
30% depend on others and 35% have no pension
142.x: About 70% of elderly persons depend on others and 78% have no pension.
142.tq: Keep the two percentages attached to their correct indicators.

142.s: Children’s migration can contribute to loneliness among the elderly because it:
o: reduces the need for social support
142.x: Children’s migration may leave parents behind, increasing loneliness and weakening traditional support systems.
142.tq: Apply the social consequence to the family-migration scenario.

142.s: Which of the following is associated with the social problems of ageing?
142.x: Ageism and abuse are recognised social problems faced by elderly persons; loneliness and feminisation of ageing are also important concerns.
142.tq: Select the recognised vulnerability rather than an absolute positive claim.

142.s:
Consider the following statements regarding family support for the elderly:
1. Care inside the joint family is weakening.
2. More than half of the elderly now live in nuclear households.
3. The weakening of joint-family care is associated with the growing importance of living arrangements outside the traditional joint family.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: All three statements are correct. Care within joint families is weakening, while over 55% of the elderly live in nuclear households, highlighting changing family support arrangements.
142.tq: Link the demographic figure with its stated social consequence.

142.s: Under which programme can NGOs receive support of up to 90% of the cost of old age homes?
o: National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly
142.x: The Integrated Programme for Older Persons provides NGOs with support of up to 90% of the costs of old age homes.
142.tq: Match the welfare intervention with the exact programme responsible for it.

142.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the position associated with NPSC 2011?
o: It supported ageing in place and drew attention to destitution among rural elderly persons.
It restricted elderly welfare exclusively to persons living in joint families.
It recommended abolishing NGO support for old age homes.
It favoured institutionalisation of all elderly persons in urban old age homes.
142.x: NPSC 2011 backed the concept of ‘ageing in place’ and highlighted destitution among the rural elderly.
142.tq: Distinguish community-based ageing support from compulsory institutional care.

142.s: Which State is the first in India to have a Senior Citizens’ Welfare Department, a Commission and an Elderly Budget?
142.x: Kerala is the first State to establish all three: a Senior Citizens’ Welfare Department, a Commission and an Elderly Budget.
142.tq: Identify the State associated with the complete institutional framework for senior citizens.

142.s: AVYAY’s SAGE component provides equity support of up to what amount for senior-care start-ups?
142.x: Under AVYAY, the SAGE component provides equity support of up to ₹1 crore for senior-care start-ups.
142.tq: Identify the exact financial ceiling associated with the scheme component.

142.s: The National Policy on Older Persons (NPOP) was announced in:
142.x: The National Policy on Older Persons was announced in 1999. NPSC came in 2011, while 2007 is the year of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act.
142.tq: 1999 was the International Year of Older Persons: NPOP 1999.

142.s: The National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly (NPHCE) was launched in:
142.x: NPHCE was launched in 2010-11, after the National Policy on Older Persons of 1999 and before the National Policy on Senior Citizens of 2011.
142.tq: Sequence: NPOP 1999, NPHCE 2010-11, NPSC 2011.

142.s: Andhra Pradesh’s population is given as approximately 495.77 lakh. This represents what share of India’s population and what rank?
142.x: Andhra Pradesh’s population is stated as 495.77 lakh, accounting for 4.09% of India’s population and placing it 10th.
142.tq: Treat the population figure, percentage and rank as a linked numerical set.

142.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

List-I                  List-II
A. India                 1. First Senior Citizens’ Welfare Department
B. Kerala                2. First national family planning programme
C. Andhra Pradesh       3. Draft Population Management Policy

Select the correct answer using the code below.
142.x: India introduced the first national family planning programme in 1952, Kerala was first with the senior-citizens institutional framework, and Andhra Pradesh is associated with the draft Population Management Policy.
142.tq: Start with the sure pair India–first national family planning programme and eliminate the codes.

143.s:
Consider the following statements about NALSA v. Union of India:
1. It was delivered on 15 April 2014.
2. It was delivered by Justices K.S. Radhakrishnan and A.K. Sikri.
3. It held that gender identity must be decided by biological examination and State verification.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
143.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the judgment came on 15 April 2014 from Justices K.S. Radhakrishnan and A.K. Sikri. Statement 3 is wrong: NALSA held gender identity is self-determined, not decided by biology or State verification. Hence C; A omits the bench, B and D wrongly include statement 3.
143.tq: NALSA = 2014, Radhakrishnan-Sikri, self-identification.

143.s: Which one of the following was NOT a direction associated with the NALSA judgment?
o: Provision of separate public toilets, health facilities and welfare schemes
Compulsory determination of gender solely through biological examination
Treatment of transgender persons as socially and educationally backward for reservation
143.x: NALSA rejected compulsory biological determination and recognised self-identified gender. It directed legal recognition, reservation-related treatment and separate public facilities and welfare measures.
143.tq: Find the option that reverses the judgment’s self-determination principle.

143.s:
Consider the following statements regarding NALSA v. Union of India:
1. The judgment recognised transgender persons as the third gender.
2. It held that gender identity is self-determined rather than dependent on biology or State verification.
3. It extended the protection of Articles 14, 15, 16, 19(1)(a) and 21 to transgender persons.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
143.x: All three statements are correct. NALSA recognised the third gender, affirmed self-determined gender identity and applied the listed fundamental-rights provisions to transgender persons.
143.tq: Check whether each statement reflects recognition, self-identification or constitutional protection before choosing the combination.

143.s:
Assertion (A): The NALSA judgment directed that transgender persons be treated as socially and educationally backward for reservation purposes.
Reason (R): The judgment required governments to extend reservation in education and employment to transgender persons on that basis.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
143.x: Both statements are true, and the direction to extend reservation in education and employment explains the treatment of transgender persons as socially and educationally backward.
143.tq: Check whether the reason states the operative consequence of the asserted constitutional direction.

143.s: Who moved the Rights of Transgender Persons Bill, 2014 as a private member's Bill?
143.x: The Rights of Transgender Persons Bill, 2014 was moved as a private member's Bill by Tiruchi Siva of the DMK.
143.tq: Match the legislative initiative with its mover and party.

143.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Rights of Transgender Persons Bill, 2014:
1. It was passed by the Rajya Sabha in April 2015.
2. It was the first private member's Bill passed by the Rajya Sabha in over four decades.
3. It was subsequently passed by the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
143.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Bill was not passed by the Lok Sabha.
143.tq: Use the legislative-stage trap by distinguishing passage in one House from passage in both Houses.

143.s:
Under the 2019 Act, a transgender person is defined as a person whose gender does not match the gender assigned at birth. Which of the following are included within this definition?
1. Trans men and trans women
2. Persons with intersex variations
3. Genderqueer persons
4. Socio-cultural identities such as kinner, hijra, aravani and jogta
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
143.x: The 2019 definition includes trans men and women, intersex variations, genderqueer persons and specified socio-cultural identities including kinner, hijra, aravani and jogta.
143.tq: Read the statutory definition inclusively and check every category listed before selecting the code.

143.s:
Under the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, consider the following statements:
1. The certificate of identity is issued by the District Magistrate.
2. A revised certificate may be issued after surgery.
3. The certificate of identity is issued by the National Council for Transgender Persons.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
143.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the District Magistrate issues the certificate of identity, and a revised certificate may be issued after surgery. Statement 3 is wrong: the National Council advises and monitors policy; it does not issue certificates. Hence B; A omits statement 2, C and D wrongly include statement 3.
143.tq: Certificate = District Magistrate (in 2026, on a medical board's advice).

143.s: For offences such as forced or bonded labour, denial of access to public places, removal from a household and abuse, the punishment under the 2019 Act is:
o: Imprisonment from three months to one year only
Imprisonment from two years to seven years without fine
Imprisonment from six months to two years and fine
143.x: The punishment is imprisonment ranging from six months to two years along with a fine.
143.tq: Test the statutory punishment range and distinguish it from heavier penalties under other laws.

143.s: Which of the following was a criticism of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019?
o: It prescribed heavier penalties than those for comparable crimes against women.
It completely abolished the role of the District Magistrate in identity certification.
It provided no reservation for transgender persons.
It excluded all socio-cultural transgender identities from its definition.
143.x: Criticisms included lighter penalties than for similar crimes against women, District Magistrate gatekeeping of identity and the absence of reservation. The Act did include several socio-cultural identities.
143.tq: Select the genuine criticism while rejecting options that reverse the Act’s provisions.

143.s: The National Council for Transgender Persons is constituted as a statutory body under which legislation?
o: The National Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993
The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019
143.x: The National Council for Transgender Persons is a statutory body constituted under the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019.
143.tq: Identify the parent legislation of the statutory body.

143.s: The Transgender Persons Rules, 2020 primarily prescribe the procedure for applying through the national portal for obtaining which document?
o: A certificate of identity as a transgender person
143.x: The Transgender Persons Rules, 2020 prescribe the application procedure through the national portal for obtaining the certificate of identity.
143.tq: Link the procedural rule with the document for which the procedure is prescribed.

143.s:
Consider the following statements about the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019:
1. It came into force on 10 January 2020.
2. It is administered by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
3. The National Council for Transgender Persons under it is chaired by the Union Social Justice Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
143.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Act came into force on 10 January 2020. Statement 2 is wrong: it is administered by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MoSJE). Statement 3 is correct: the National Council is chaired by the Union Social Justice Minister. So B; A misses statement 3, C and D wrongly accept statement 2.
143.tq: Transgender law = MoSJE throughout (Act, Council, SMILE).

143.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Council for Transgender Persons:
1. It includes representatives from ministries such as Health, Home Affairs and Minority Affairs.
2. It includes experts and representatives of the transgender community.
3. It advises and monitors policies relating to transgender persons.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
143.x: All three statements are correct. The Council has governmental, expert and community representation and performs advisory and monitoring functions.
143.tq: Test the composition and functions together through an all-correct combination.

143.s: Under the 2026 amendment relating to the National Council for Transgender Persons, State or Union Territory representation is to be provided by rotation from which arrangement?
o: One representative each from coastal, Himalayan, plateau, desert and island regions
One representative from each of the six geographical zones
Two representatives each from North, South, East, West and Central India
One representative each from North, South, East, West and North-East
143.x: The 2026 amendment provides for one State or Union Territory representative each from the North, South, East, West and North-East, by rotation.
143.tq: Distinguish the exact geographical rotation pattern from similar regional classifications.

143.s:
Consider the following statements about the 2026 amendment:
1. The District Magistrate issues the certificate on the recommendation of a designated medical board.
2. The definition is limited to specified socio-cultural identities, intersex or congenital variations and persons forced to present as transgender.
3. Kidnapping and forcing a person to present as transgender were added as offences.
4. Self-perceived identity continues to be expressly included without restriction.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
143.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the amendment excludes self-perceived identity and omits Section 4(2).
143.tq: Find the statement that reverses the amendment’s central change concerning self-perceived identity.

143.s: The 2026 amendment to the transgender persons law was challenged in the Supreme Court by:
o: Madhu Bai Kinnar and Shabnam Mausi
Laxmi Narayan Tripathi and Zainab Javid Patel
143.x: Laxmi Narayan Tripathi and Zainab Javid Patel challenged the amendment as contrary to the principles laid down in NALSA.
143.tq: Separate the petitioners challenging the amendment from the legislator and the NALSA Bench.

143.s: Which of the following statements correctly reflects the position regarding identity cards issued before the 2026 Act?
o: They were replaced by certificates issued by the National Human Rights Commission.
They remain valid according to the assurance given by the Centre before the Supreme Court.
They remain valid only after fresh approval by a State medical board.
They automatically became invalid on the date of assent.
143.x: In August 2026, the Centre assured the Supreme Court that identity cards issued before the 2026 Act would remain valid.
143.tq: Apply the effect of a government assurance to a concrete identity-card situation.

143.s: The NHRC Advisory 2.0 of May 2026 recommended that Census categories should include which of the following?
o: Only sexual minorities and senior citizens
Intersex persons, trans men and trans women
Only transgender persons and persons with disabilities
143.x: The NHRC Advisory 2.0 recommended Census categories for intersex persons, trans men and trans women.
143.tq: Identify the exact categories proposed in the advisory.

143.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the nature of reservation sought by transgender persons in the context of the NALSA judgment?
o: A separate vertical reservation restricted to the General category
Reservation exclusively under the women’s quota
Horizontal reservation cutting across SC, ST, OBC and General categories
143.x: The transgender community has sought horizontal reservation, which would cut across the SC, ST, OBC and General categories. NALSA had directed treatment as socially and educationally backward, resembling a vertical OBC-type approach.
143.tq: Distinguish the two commonly confused forms of reservation by asking whether the quota cuts across existing categories.

143.s: The issue of reservation for transgender persons resurfaced in June 2023 in connection with which State?
143.x: The issue resurfaced through a Mumbai protest against Maharashtra’s reply to the Bombay High Court in June 2023.
143.tq: Use the place of the protest and the State involved to separate a current issue from nearby State measures.

143.s: Which State was the first to provide one per cent reservation for transgender persons in all government jobs?
143.x: Karnataka became the first State to provide one per cent reservation for transgender persons in all government jobs in July 2021.
143.tq: Discriminate between nearby States associated with transgender welfare measures.

143.s:
Consider the following statements about the SMILE scheme:
1. It was launched in 2022 by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
2. It is an umbrella Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
3. Its goal is 'Bhiksha Vritti Mukt Bharat'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
143.x: Statement 1 is correct: SMILE was launched in 2022 by MoSJE. Statement 2 is wrong: it is an umbrella Central Sector scheme (Rs 365 crore), not Centrally Sponsored. Statement 3 is correct: its goal is a begging-free India, 'Bhiksha Vritti Mukt Bharat'. Hence D; A omits statement 3, B and C wrongly include statement 2.
143.tq: SMILE: MoSJE, 2022, Central Sector, begging-free India.

143.s: What is the expanded form of SMILE in the context of welfare schemes?
o: Social Mission for Inclusive Livelihood and Employment
Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise
Scheme for Marginalised Inclusion, Livelihood and Education
Support Mission for Independent Living and Empowerment
143.x: SMILE stands for Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise.
143.tq: Test the exact official expansion of the scheme acronym.

143.s: Which of the following is NOT a component or intervention associated with the transgender-persons component of SMILE?
o: Compulsory recruitment through the Union Public Service Commission
Scholarship of Rs 13,500 per year from Class IX to postgraduate level
143.x: The transgender component includes scholarships, PM-DAKSH skilling and a PM-JAY-linked health package. Compulsory UPSC recruitment is not an identified intervention.
143.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the listed scheme interventions.

143.s: Garima Greh under SMILE is primarily associated with which service?
143.x: Garima Greh provides shelter homes for transgender persons.
143.tq: Match the named sub-scheme with its core service.

143.s: Which of the following services is provided through the National Portal for Transgender Persons?
o: Online ration card and voter card only
Automatic allotment of housing under PMAY
143.x: The National Portal for Transgender Persons provides online applications for a certificate and identity card. The certificate is mandatory for accessing benefits.
143.tq: Identify the actual digital service rather than an unrelated entitlement.

143.s: Which State was the first to formulate a transgender policy?
143.x: Kerala was the first State to formulate a transgender policy, in 2015.
143.tq: Test a first-in-the-country fact against neighbouring States associated with other transgender measures.

143.s: According to Census 2011, approximately how many transgender persons were counted in India?
143.x: Census 2011 counted approximately 4.88 lakh transgender persons in India.
143.tq: Test the precise census estimate using close numerical distractors.

143.s: Which of the following correctly represents the order of States by the number of transgender persons counted in Census 2011, beginning with the highest?
o: Uttar Pradesh, undivided Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar
Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, undivided Andhra Pradesh
Undivided Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra
Bihar, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, undivided Andhra Pradesh
143.x: The order was Uttar Pradesh, followed by undivided Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Bihar.
143.tq: Apply sequence-based recall to a ranked geographical list.

143.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Transgender Welfare Board (2008) - Tamil Nadu
2. Thirunangaigal app for ID registration - Kerala
3. Sthree Suraksha scheme for EWS women and transgender persons - Kerala
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
143.x: Pair 1 is correct: Tamil Nadu set up the Transgender Welfare Board in 2008. Pair 2 is wrong: the Thirunangaigal app (2021) is a Tamil Nadu measure. Pair 3 is correct: Sthree Suraksha is a Kerala scheme. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
143.tq: TN: Welfare Board 2008, Thirunangaigal app; Kerala: first policy, Sthree Suraksha.

143.s: Invalidity and old-age pensions are placed under which entry of the Constitution?
143.x: Invalidity and old-age pensions are included in Concurrent List Entry 24.
143.tq: Match the subject with the correct List and entry number.

143.s: Under the NTR Bharosa Pension scheme in Andhra Pradesh, the monthly pension for elderly persons aged 60 years and above, widows and transgender persons is:
143.x: NTR Bharosa provides Rs 4,000 per month to elderly persons aged 60 years and above, widows and transgender persons.
143.tq: Discriminate between the common-category rate and the higher rates for specified disabilities or diseases.

143.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched under the Andhra Pradesh pension rates cited?
143.x: The cited rates are Rs 6,000 for persons with disabilities, Rs 10,000 for chronic diseases, Rs 15,000 for fully disabled persons and Rs 4,000 for transgender persons.
143.tq: Start with the distinctive highest rate and check the category-rate pairing.

143.s: Which institutional measure concerning transgender welfare was reported for Andhra Pradesh in June 2026?
o: A medical board was abolished statewide.
A council for transgender welfare was set up.
A separate Constitutional List was created.
143.x: Andhra Pradesh was reported to have set up a council for transgender welfare in June 2026.
143.tq: Identify the State-level institutional initiative from among unrelated legal alternatives.

143.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 41 of the Constitution refers to public assistance in old age.
2. The National Social Assistance Programme rests on Articles 41 and 42.
3. Invalidity and old-age pensions are included in State List Entry 9.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
143.x: Article 41 concerns public assistance in old age, and NSAP rests on Articles 41 and 42. Invalidity and old-age pensions are in Concurrent List Entry 24, not State List Entry 9.
143.tq: The trap is the reversal of the State List and Concurrent List entries.

143.s: Who among the following was the first transgender judge in India?
143.x: Joyita Mondal of West Bengal became India’s first transgender judge in a Lok Adalat in 2017.
143.tq: Discriminate among first-person achievements by matching the person with the exact post.

143.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. K. Prithika Yashini — First transgender police sub-inspector
2. Manabi Bandyopadhyay — First transgender college principal
3. Joyita Mondal — First transgender mayor
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
143.x: Pair 1 is correct: K. Prithika Yashini (Tamil Nadu) was the first transgender police sub-inspector. Pair 2 is correct: Manabi Bandyopadhyay (West Bengal) became the first transgender college principal in 2015. Pair 3 is wrong: Joyita Mondal was the first transgender judge (Lok Adalat, 2017); the first transgender mayor was Madhu Bai Kinnar (Raigarh, 2015). So only 1 and 2 (B); A misses pair 2, C and D wrongly accept pair 3.
143.tq: Learn the 'firsts' as person-post pairs; the trap swaps judge and mayor.

143.s: Laxmi Narayan Tripathi was the first transgender person from the Asia-Pacific region to address which body?
143.x: Laxmi Narayan Tripathi was the first transgender person from the Asia-Pacific region to address the United Nations General Assembly.
143.tq: Identify the exact international forum instead of selecting a related United Nations body.

143.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Shabnam Mausi — First transgender MLA
2. Madhu Bai Kinnar — First transgender mayor
3. Karnataka — State with a 1% transgender job quota
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
143.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Shabnam Mausi became the first transgender MLA in Madhya Pradesh in 1998, Madhu Bai Kinnar the first transgender mayor in 2015, and Karnataka introduced the 1% job quota in 2021.
143.tq: Verify each first-person or State association separately, paying attention to the office and year.

143.s: The 2026 amendment concerning transgender persons has been criticised primarily because it is viewed as:
o: Removing the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court over identity matters
Extending the NALSA principle to old-age pensions
Reversing the self-identification principle recognised in NALSA
Strengthening the self-identification principle of NALSA
143.x: The principal criticism is that medical certification reverses the self-identification principle associated with the NALSA judgment.
143.tq: Contrast the two competing legal principles: self-identification and medical certification.

143.s:
Which of the following was included in NHRC Advisory 2.0 concerning transgender and intersex persons?
1. Admission by self-identified gender
2. Ban on non-consensual intersex surgery on children
3. More Garima Grehs
Which of the statements given above are correct?
143.x: NHRC Advisory 2.0 included admission by self-identified gender, a ban on non-consensual intersex surgery on children and more Garima Grehs.
143.tq: Treat each listed recommendation as a separate statement before choosing the combined code.

143.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: NTR Bharosa — medical-board certification of gender
143.x: RVY was launched at Nellore. The central IGNOAPS pension was reported as frozen at Rs 200, while NTR Bharosa pays Rs 4,000 to transgender persons; NALSA is associated with self-identification.
143.tq: Use the direct programme-location pair and reject reversals of legal and pension facts.

144.s: For determining whether a community is a minority under Article 30, the relevant unit is ordinarily the:
144.x: In T.M.A. Pai Foundation, the State was treated as the unit for determining minority status, rather than the whole of India.
144.tq: Use the unit-of-determination distinction to avoid the national-level trap.

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka:
1. The case was decided by an 11-judge Bench.
2. The State is the unit for determining minority status.
3. The State may regulate, but not control, the administration of minority institutions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: All three statements are correct. The 2002 decision was delivered by an 11-judge Bench and adopted a State-wise approach to minority status while permitting regulation without administrative control.
144.tq: Combine bench strength, territorial unit and the distinction between regulation and control.

144.s: The Constitution refers to the term ‘minority’ in which of the following Articles, without defining it?
144.x: The Constitution uses the term ‘minority’ in Articles 29, 30, 350A and 350B, but does not provide a general definition of the term.
144.tq: Recall the exact Article group rather than selecting a familiar Fundamental Rights cluster.

144.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Commission for Minorities Act does not define the term 'minority'.
2. A community notified by the Centre is treated as a minority for the purposes of the Act.
3. States cannot notify minorities of their own for State purposes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. States can also notify their own minorities for State purposes, making statement 3 incorrect.
144.tq: Watch for the absolute word 'cannot' when comparing Union and State roles.

144.s: Which one of the following statements regarding State designation of minorities is correct?
o: Jains were declared a minority simultaneously by all States in 2014.
Only the Union Government can designate a community as a minority.
States can designate their own minorities, and 11 States had declared Jains a minority before 2014.
States cannot designate minorities unless authorised by the Supreme Court.
144.x: States have the power to designate their own minorities. Before 2014, 11 States had declared Jains a minority.
144.tq: Test the distinction between Union-level notification and State-level designation.

144.s:
With reference to minority rights in India, consider the following statements:
1. Whether a community is a minority is decided with reference to its population position in the State concerned.
2. The rights of minorities under the Constitution are absolute and cannot be regulated by the State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: Statement 1 is correct: after T.M.A. Pai Foundation (2002), the State, not the whole of India, is the unit for deciding minority status. Statement 2 is wrong: minority rights are not absolute; the State may regulate standards, though it cannot take away management (APPSC G2 2017 treated 'absolute' as the untrue statement). Hence 1 only; options B, C and D wrongly accept statement 2 or reject statement 1.
144.tq: Minority rights are NOT absolute; the State is the unit (T.M.A. Pai).

144.s: Which one of the following grounds is NOT expressly included in Article 29(2) as a basis for denying admission to a State-maintained or State-aided educational institution?
144.x: Article 29(2) prohibits denial of admission on grounds only of religion, race, caste or language. Sex and place of birth are not included in this list.
144.tq: Find the omitted ground rather than selecting one of the four expressly listed grounds.

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 29:
1. Article 29(1) is available to any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture.
2. Article 29(2) protects admission to State-maintained or State-aided institutions.
3. The protection under Article 29 is available to non-citizens also.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Article 29 is available only to citizens, so statement 3 is false.
144.tq: Test both the substantive protection and the class of persons entitled to it.

144.s: A political promise to conserve the language of a particular section of citizens is, by itself, treated under the Representation of the People Act, 1951 as—
o: An electoral offence in every case
144.x: A political promise to conserve a section's language is not treated as a corrupt practice under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
144.tq: Distinguish a cultural or linguistic promise from a legally defined corrupt electoral practice.

144.s:
With reference to Article 29 of the Constitution of India, consider the following statements:
1. Any section of citizens having a distinct language, script or culture has the right to conserve it.
2. Article 29 is confined exclusively to religious and linguistic minorities.
3. No citizen can be denied admission to a State-maintained or State-aided educational institution on grounds only of religion, race, caste or language.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: Article 29(1) protects the language, script or culture of any distinct section of citizens, and Article 29(2) prohibits denial of admission on the specified grounds. Article 29 is not confined exclusively to minorities.
144.tq: Separate the broad protection under Article 29 from the minority-specific protection under Article 30.

144.s: A State seeks to deny aid to an educational institution solely because it is managed by a linguistic minority. Which constitutional provision is most directly attracted?
144.x: Article 30(2) provides that the State shall not discriminate in granting aid to an educational institution on the ground that it is under the management of a minority, whether religious or linguistic.
144.tq: Apply the factual situation to the specific clause dealing with State aid to minority-managed institutions.

144.s:
Consider the following statements about Article 30:
1. The State shall not discriminate against minority institutions in granting aid.
2. The right to administer a minority institution is completely immune from State regulation.
3. The State may regulate standards of education without destroying the minority character of the institution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The right under Article 30 is not absolute; the State may regulate educational standards, but it cannot destroy the minority character of the institution.
144.tq: Reject the absolute statement while retaining the distinction between regulation of standards and destruction of minority character.

144.s: Clause (1A) of Article 30, which protects the right of minorities to establish educational institutions when their property is compulsorily acquired, was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment?
144.x: The 44th Amendment, which removed the right to property, added Article 30(1A) so that removal of that right does not affect minorities' right to establish institutions and compensation is ensured on acquisition. The 7th Amendment (1956) inserted Articles 350A and 350B; the 93rd Amendment inserted Article 15(5) after P.A. Inamdar; the 42nd Amendment did not add Article 30(1A).
144.tq: 30(1A) = 44th Amendment (right to property removed).

144.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List-I (Case)
A. In re Kerala Education Bill
B. St. Stephen's College v. University of Delhi
C. T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka
D. P.A. Inamdar v. State of Maharashtra

List-II (Holding)
1. State is the unit for determining a linguistic or religious minority
2. Aided minority college may prefer its own community up to 50 per cent of seats
3. State cannot impose reservation on unaided minority or non-minority professional institutions
4. State may regulate standards without destroying minority character

Select the correct answer.
144.x: A-4, B-2, C-1, D-3. In re Kerala Education Bill held the Article 30 right is not absolute and the State may impose reasonable conditions (regulating standards); St. Stephen's (1992) let an aided minority college prefer its own community up to about 50%; T.M.A. Pai (2002) made the State the unit for minority status; P.A. Inamdar (2005) barred State reservation quotas in unaided institutions, minority or non-minority.
144.tq: Start from the distinctive case holdings and then verify the remaining pairs.

144.s: The reference made by the President to the Supreme Court in the matter of the Kerala Education Bill, 1957, was under
144.x: The Kerala Education Bill, 1957 was considered by the Supreme Court pursuant to a Presidential reference under Article 143.
144.tq: Distinguish the advisory jurisdiction under Article 143 from the Court's original and appellate jurisdictions.

144.s:
With reference to the decision in In re Kerala Education Bill, 1957, consider the following statements:
1. Minorities were recognised as having the right to establish educational institutions.
2. The State could attach reasonable conditions to the grant of aid.
3. The judgment held that minority institutions could never be regulated by the State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: The decision recognised the right of minorities to establish institutions and accepted reasonable conditions attached to State aid. It did not grant immunity from every form of State regulation.
144.tq: Reject the absolute word “never” while retaining the two propositions supported by the case.

144.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: P.A. Inamdar (2005) — Presidential reference under Article 143
In re Kerala Education Bill (1957) — 11-judge Bench and State-wise minority status
St. Xavier's College v. Gujarat (1974) — right to administer protected, subject to standards and excellence regulations
T.M.A. Pai Foundation (2002) — seven-judge Bench and no State quota in unaided institutions
144.x: C is correct: St. Xavier's College v. Gujarat (1974) protected the right to administer, allowing regulation only for standards and excellence. The others are mismatched: the Article 143 Presidential reference was the Kerala Education Bill case, not P.A. Inamdar; the 11-judge Bench and State-wise minority status belong to T.M.A. Pai; the seven-judge Bench barring State quotas in unaided institutions was P.A. Inamdar.
144.tq: Find the correctly matched case and holding by separating the four landmark decisions.

144.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the decision in P.A. Inamdar (2005)?
o: A seven-judge Bench held that the State could impose its quota in unaided institutions without limitation.
A seven-judge Bench held that there could be no State quota or reservation in unaided institutions, contributing to the subsequent 93rd Amendment framework.
An 11-judge Bench abolished the distinction between aided and unaided institutions.
The Court held that minority status must be determined at the national level.
144.x: P.A. Inamdar was decided by a seven-judge Bench and held that the State could not impose its quota or reservation in unaided institutions. The decision was followed by the constitutional development associated with Article 15(5) through the 93rd Amendment.
144.tq: Combine bench strength, holding and constitutional consequence without confusing it with T.M.A. Pai.

144.s: With reference to St. Stephen's College v. University of Delhi (1992), which one of the following statements is correct?
o: An aided minority college may prefer students of its own community up to about 50 percent
An aided minority college cannot admit students from its own community
Only unaided minority colleges may prefer their own community students
The State may reserve all seats in an aided minority college
144.x: The decision recognised that an aided minority college may prefer students belonging to its own community up to about 50 percent.
144.tq: Use the case-specific numerical limit to distinguish the ruling from broader Article 30 claims.

144.s: The decision in Bal Patil v. Union of India (2005) is associated with which of the following?
o: Directing the Centre to notify Jains as a national minority
Imposing reservation quotas on unaided minority institutions
Declaring that minority status must be determined nationally
Declining to direct the Centre to notify Jains as a national minority and leaving the matter to the States
144.x: The Court declined to direct the Centre to notify Jains as a national minority, leaving the matter to the States and cautioning against the multiplication of minority claims.
144.tq: Discriminate between a judicial direction and a refusal to issue that direction.

144.s:
Arrange the following cases in chronological order:
A. Kerala Education Bill
B. T.M.A. Pai Foundation
C. Bal Patil v. Union of India
D. St. Stephen's College
144.x: The correct sequence is Kerala Education Bill (1958), St. Stephen's College (1992), T.M.A. Pai Foundation (2002), and Bal Patil (2005).
144.tq: Fix the earliest and latest cases first, then place the 1992 and 2002 decisions.

144.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is correct?
o: The officer is appointed by the President and reports to the President.
The officer is appointed by the Chief Minister and reports to the Governor.
The officer is appointed by the Parliament and reports to the Prime Minister.
The officer is appointed by the Governor and reports to the State Legislature.
144.x: Under Article 350B, the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is appointed by the President and submits reports to the President.
144.tq: Apply the authority trap by matching appointment and reporting powers with the President.

144.s: The headquarters of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities is located at
144.x: The office styled as the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities has its headquarters at Prayagraj, formerly Allahabad.
144.tq: Test the exact headquarters rather than the more obvious national-capital location.

144.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Articles 350A and 350B were inserted by the 7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956.
2. The amendment was associated with the reorganisation of States.
3. The office under Article 350B is styled as the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: All three statements are correct. The 7th Constitutional Amendment, 1956, linked to the reorganisation of States, inserted Articles 350A and 350B; the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B is styled the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities (office set up in 1957).
144.tq: Combine amendment, context and official designation; all three details refer to the same constitutional arrangement.

144.s: The Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities launched a programme consisting of
o: a twelve-point programme for tribal development
a ten-point programme to preserve language and culture
a five-point programme to promote official-language use
a seven-point programme for State reorganisation
144.x: The Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities launched a 10-point programme aimed at preserving the language and culture of linguistic minorities.
144.tq: Treat the numerical feature as decisive and avoid substituting the nearby States Reorganisation or tribal-development figures.

144.s: In January 2026, concerns regarding Kannada speakers in Kasaragod were associated with which development?
o: A report of the Kundu Committee
A new Central Sector scholarship scheme
144.x: A language Bill in Kerala raised concerns for Kannada speakers in Kasaragod. Kerala stated that Clause 7 protected linguistic minorities.
144.tq: Link the reported concern to the State and legislative development, not to an older committee or constitutional amendment.

144.s: The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities was established in:
144.x: The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities was set up in 1957.
144.tq: Distinguish the office’s establishment year from the constitutional amendment year.

144.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Article)
 a. Article 347
 b. Article 350
 c. Article 350A
 d. Article 350B

List-II (Provision)
 i. Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
 ii. Representation for grievances in any language used in the Union or a State
 iii. Recognition of a language spoken by a substantial part of a State
 iv. Mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage for linguistic-minority children

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
144.x: Article 347 concerns recognition of a language spoken by a substantial part of a State; Article 350 concerns language for grievances; Article 350A concerns mother-tongue instruction; and Article 350B provides for the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.
144.tq: Start with the sure Article–provision pair and eliminate codes that disturb the remaining relationships.

144.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes religious and linguistic minorities in India?
o: Religious minorities are associated with the National Commission for Minorities, while linguistic minorities are considered State-wise and linked with the Article 350B officer
Religious minorities are identified only by States, while linguistic minorities are identified by the Union
Both categories are determined exclusively on an all-India basis
Neither category is recognised under the Constitution
144.x: Religious minorities are dealt with through the National Commission for Minorities and the Ministry of Minority Affairs. Linguistic minorities are identified State-wise, with the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B.
144.tq: Split the comparison by authority and territorial basis.

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Commission for Minorities:
1. It is a statutory body under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992.
2. The first statutory National Commission for Minorities was constituted in 1993.
3. The Chairperson and members are appointed by the President of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: the Chairperson and members of the NCM are appointed by the Central Government, not by the President.
144.tq: Apply the ‘who appoints?’ trap, especially where a constitutional President may be confused with the Central Government.

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis:
1. It was created by the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis Act, 1993.
2. The Act lapsed in 2004.
3. The Commission continues as a non-statutory body with its tenure extended by resolution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: All three statements are correct. The NCSK was created under the 1993 Act; after the Act lapsed in 2004, it continued as a non-statutory body through tenure extensions by resolution.
144.tq: Track the transition from statutory creation to present non-statutory continuation.

144.s: The Minorities Commission was initially established in 1978 by means of which of the following?
o: A resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs
144.x: The Minorities Commission was initially set up in 1978 through a resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs. It was non-statutory at that stage.
144.tq: Distinguish the original administrative arrangement from the later statutory status.

144.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the National Commission for Minorities?
o: Conducting elections to minority educational institutions
Looking into specific complaints relating to deprivation of minority safeguards
Monitoring constitutional and legal safeguards for minorities
144.x: The Commission evaluates development, monitors safeguards, examines complaints and recommends measures; conducting elections to minority educational institutions is not one of its stated functions.
144.tq: Find the option that assigns an unrelated administrative function to the Commission.

144.s:
While inquiring into complaints, the National Commission for Minorities may exercise powers similar to those of a civil court, including:
1. Summoning witnesses.
2. Requisitioning or calling for records.
3. Imposing criminal sentences.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: The Commission may summon witnesses and call for records while conducting an inquiry. It does not possess the power to impose criminal sentences.
144.tq: Separate inquiry powers from the power to impose judicial punishment.

144.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
 a. 1978
 b. 1992
 c. 1993
 d. 1995

List-II
 i. First statutory Commission constituted
 ii. Vice-Chairperson added
 iii. Non-statutory Minorities Commission formed
 iv. NCM Act made the body statutory

Select the correct answer using the code below.
144.x: The milestones are correctly matched as 1978–non-statutory Commission, 1992–statutory NCM Act, 1993–first statutory Commission and 1995–addition of Vice-Chairperson.
144.tq: Start from the sure year-event pair and eliminate codes with mismatched milestones.

144.s:
With reference to the composition of the National Commission for Minorities, consider the following statements:
1. It consists of a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and five Members.
2. All seven members must belong to minority communities.
3. Five of the seven members, including the Chairperson, must be from minority communities.
4. The term of office is three years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: The Commission has seven members: a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and five Members. Five, including the Chairperson, must be from minority communities, and the term is three years; it is not required that all seven belong to minority communities.
144.tq: Test composition, qualification and tenure separately to catch the overstatement in ‘all’.

144.s: The Ministry of Minority Affairs was set up in 2006. Haj management was added to its work from:
144.x: The Ministry of Minority Affairs was established in 2006, and Haj management was added to its responsibilities from October 2016.
144.tq: Match an institutional milestone with the precise year and month given.

144.s: In July 2026, who was appointed Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities, a post vacant since April 2025?
144.x: Harjit Singh Grewal was appointed NCM Chairperson in July 2026. Iqbal Singh Lalpura was the previous Chairperson, after whom the post fell vacant in April 2025; Munawari Begum was appointed Vice-Chairperson; Amitabh Kundu chaired the Post-Sachar Evaluation Committee.
144.tq: NCM 2026: Grewal Chair, Munawari Begum Vice-Chair; 4 of 7 posts filled.

144.s: Which of the following pairs of communities is NOT included among the notified minority communities?
144.x: The notified minority communities are Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains. Jews are not included in this listed group.
144.tq: Find the outsider in a recognised statutory list rather than choosing a community from memory alone.

144.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Parsis were notified as minority communities in 1993.
2. Jains were notified as a minority community in 2014.
3. Linguistic minorities are notified under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: The first five communities were notified in 1993 and Jains were added in 2014. Linguistic minorities are not notified under this Act.
144.tq: Check the notified-community list against the separate constitutional mechanism for linguistic minorities.

144.s: Which one of the following communities was added to India's nationally notified minority communities on 27 January 2014?
144.x: Jains were added on 27 January 2014, increasing the number of nationally notified minority communities from five to six.
144.tq: Use the exact date and the addition rather than the original five-community list.

144.s: The six nationally notified minority communities together constitute approximately what share of India's population?
144.x: The six nationally notified minority communities together account for approximately 19 percent of India's population.
144.tq: Use the approximate share rather than confusing it with an individual community's population.

144.s: Under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992, a 'minority' means a community notified as such by the Central Government under which provision?
144.x: The Act does not define minority; under Section 2(c) a minority is any community notified by the Central Government. Section 3(2) requires five members including the Chairperson to be from minority communities; Article 29(1) protects the language, script or culture of any section of citizens; Section 9(1) of the Waqf Act, 1995 concerns the Central Waqf Council.
144.tq: Sec 2(c) = Centre notifies minorities (criticised as 'unbridled power').

144.s: Which one of the following is NOT a function or power of the National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions?
o: Determining the minority status of an educational institution
Adjudicating disputes relating to affiliation with universities
Amending the Constitution to define the term minority
144.x: The Commission can determine minority status, decide affiliation disputes and issue minority certificates, and it has civil court powers. It has no power to amend the Constitution.
144.tq: Find the option outside the statutory and quasi-judicial jurisdiction of the body.

144.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding institutions related to minority affairs?
1. The National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions was established under an Act of 2004.
2. Statutory State Minority Commissions exist in 19 States/Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
144.x: Both statements are correct. The National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions is associated with the 2004 Act, and statutory State Minority Commissions exist in 19 States/Union Territories including Andhra Pradesh.
144.tq: Combine two independently verifiable institutional facts and test the ‘both’ option.

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Sachar Committee:
1. It was set up in 2005 by the Prime Minister.
2. It was chaired by Justice Rajinder Sachar.
3. Its report was submitted in November 2006.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: All three statements are correct. The committee was set up in 2005, chaired by Justice Rajinder Sachar, and submitted its report in November 2006.
144.tq: Check the committee’s establishment, chair and report date separately before selecting the coded combination.

144.s: Which Muslim group was identified as requiring attention similar to that given to Hindu Other Backward Classes?
o: All Muslim groups equally under the same classification
144.x: The Ajlaf, described as backward Muslims or commoners and lower-caste converts, were identified as requiring attention similar to Hindu OBCs.
144.tq: Separate Ajlaf from Arzal by matching the group with the specific policy concern.

144.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ashraf — upper or claimed foreign origin
Ajlaf — the most deprived Dalit Muslim group
144.x: Arzal, rather than Ajlaf, was described as the Dalit Muslim group and the most deprived category. Ajlaf was identified as a backward group requiring attention similar to Hindu OBCs.
144.tq: Use the confusable-pair trap by checking the precise description of each group.

144.s: Which of the following was NOT a proposal associated with the Sachar Committee?
144.x: The Sachar Committee proposed an Equal Opportunity Commission, National Data Bank and Assessment and Monitoring Authority. A National Linguistic Minorities Commission was not listed among its proposals.
144.tq: Eliminate the option belonging to a different institutional theme.

144.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Committee)
A. Sachar Committee
